path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 1. Rights of life, liberty, worship, pursuit of safety and happiness, free speech, acquiring and protecting property, peaceable assembly, redress of grievances, bearing arms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 1. Rights of life, liberty, worship, pursuit of safety and happiness, free speech, acquiring and protecting property, peaceable assembly, redress of grievances, bearing arms
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 1. Rights of life, liberty, worship, pursuit of safety and happiness, free speech, acquiring and protecting property, peaceable assembly, redress of grievances, bearing arms (2023)
content:
All men are, by nature, free and equal, and have certain inherent and inalienable
   rights, among which may be reckoned:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 5. Right of religious freedom
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 5. Right of religious freedom
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 5. Right of religious freedom (2023)
content:
No preference shall ever be given by law to any religious sect, society or denomination;
   nor to any particular creed, mode of worship or system of ecclesiastical polity; 
   nor shall any person be compelled to attend any place of worship, to contribute to
   the erection or maintenance of any such place, or to the salary or support of any
   minister of religion;  nor shall any man be compelled to send his child to any school
   to which he may be conscientiously opposed;  and the civil rights, privileges or capacities
   of no person shall be taken away, or in anywise diminished or enlarged, on account
   of his belief or disbelief of any religious tenet, dogma or teaching.  No human authority shall, in any case whatever, control or interfere with the rights
   of conscience.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 6. Elections to be free and equal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 6. Elections to be free and equal
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 6. Elections to be free and equal (2023)
content: All elections shall be free and equal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 11. Rights of accused in criminal prosecution; change of venue
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 11. Rights of accused in criminal prosecution; change of venue
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 11. Rights of accused in criminal prosecution; change of venue (2023)
content:
In all criminal prosecutions the accused has the right to be heard by himself and
   counsel;  to demand the nature and cause of the accusation against him;  to meet the
   witnesses face to face, and to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in
   his favor.  He cannot be compelled to give evidence against himself, nor can he be deprived
   of his life, liberty or property, unless by the judgment of his peers or the law of
   the land;  and in prosecutions by indictment or information, he shall have a speedy
   public trial by an impartial jury of the vicinage;  but the General Assembly may provide
   by a general law for a change of venue in such prosecutions for both the defendant
   and the Commonwealth, the change to be made to the most convenient county in which
   a fair trial can be obtained.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 14. Right of judicial remedy for injury; speedy trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 14. Right of judicial remedy for injury; speedy trial
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 14. Right of judicial remedy for injury; speedy trial (2023)
content:
All courts shall be open, and every person for an injury done him in his lands, goods,
   person or reputation, shall have remedy by due course of law, and right and justice
   administered without sale, denial or delay.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 13. Double jeopardy; property not to be taken for public use without compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 13. Double jeopardy; property not to be taken for public use without compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 13. Double jeopardy; property not to be taken for public use without compensation (2023)
content:
No person shall, for the same offense, be twice put in jeopardy of his life or limb,
   nor shall any man's property be taken or applied to public use without the consent
   of his representatives, and without just compensation being previously made to him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST Bill of Rights Preamble
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST Bill of Rights Preamble
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST Bill of Rights Preamble (2023)
content:
That the great and essential principles of liberty and free government may be recognized
   and established, we declare that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 9. Truth may be given in evidence in prosecution for publishing matters proper for public information; jury to try law and facts in libel prosecutions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 9. Truth may be given in evidence in prosecution for publishing matters proper for public information; jury to try law and facts in libel prosecutions
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 9. Truth may be given in evidence in prosecution for publishing matters proper for public information; jury to try law and facts in libel prosecutions (2023)
content:
In prosecutions for the publication of papers investigating the official conduct of
   officers or men in a public capacity, or where the matter published is proper for
   public information, the truth thereof may be given in evidence;  and in all indictments
   for libel the jury shall have the right to determine the law and the facts, under
   the direction of the court, as in other cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 12. Indictable offense not to be prosecuted by information; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 12. Indictable offense not to be prosecuted by information; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 12. Indictable offense not to be prosecuted by information; exceptions (2023)
content:
No person, for an indictable offense, shall be proceeded against criminally by information,
   except in cases arising in the land or naval forces, or in the militia, when in actual
   service in time of war or public danger, or by leave of court for oppression or misdemeanor
   in office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 15. Laws to be suspended only by General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 15. Laws to be suspended only by General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 15. Laws to be suspended only by General Assembly (2023)
content:
No power to suspend laws shall be exercised unless by the General Assembly or its
   authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 2. Absolute and arbitrary power denied
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 2. Absolute and arbitrary power denied
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 2. Absolute and arbitrary power denied (2023)
content:
Absolute and arbitrary power over the lives, liberty and property of freemen exists
   nowhere in a republic, not even in the largest majority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 10. Security from search and seizure; conditions of issuance of warrant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 10. Security from search and seizure; conditions of issuance of warrant
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 10. Security from search and seizure; conditions of issuance of warrant (2023)
content:
The people shall be secure in their persons, houses, papers and possessions, from
   unreasonable search and seizure;  and no warrant shall issue to search any place,
   or seize any person or thing, without describing them as nearly as may be, nor without
   probable cause supported by oath or affirmation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 7. Right of trial by jury
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 7. Right of trial by jury
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 7. Right of trial by jury (2023)
content:
The ancient mode of trial by jury shall be held sacred, and the right thereof remain
   inviolate, subject to such modifications as may be authorized by this Constitution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 23. No office of nobility or hereditary distinction, or for longer than a term of years
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 23. No office of nobility or hereditary distinction, or for longer than a term of years
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 23. No office of nobility or hereditary distinction, or for longer than a term of years (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall not grant any title of nobility or hereditary distinction,
   nor create any office the appointment of which shall be for a longer time than a term
   of years.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 3. Men are equal; no exclusive grant except for public services; property not to be exempted from taxation; grants revocable
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 3. Men are equal; no exclusive grant except for public services; property not to be exempted from taxation; grants revocable
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 3. Men are equal; no exclusive grant except for public services; property not to be exempted from taxation; grants revocable (2023)
content:
All men, when they form a social compact, are equal;  and no grant of exclusive, separate
   public emoluments or privileges shall be made to any man or set of men, except in
   consideration of public services;  but no property shall be exempt from taxation except
   as provided in this Constitution;  and every grant of a franchise, privilege or exemption,
   shall remain subject to revocation, alteration or amendment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 4. Power inherent in the people; right to alter, reform, or abolish government
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 4. Power inherent in the people; right to alter, reform, or abolish government
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 4. Power inherent in the people; right to alter, reform, or abolish government (2023)
content:
All power is inherent in the people, and all free governments are founded on their
   authority and instituted for their peace, safety, happiness and the protection of
   property.  For the advancement of these ends, they have at all times an inalienable and indefeasible
   right to alter, reform or abolish their government in such manner as they may deem
   proper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 8. Freedom of speech and of the press
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 8. Freedom of speech and of the press
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 8. Freedom of speech and of the press (2023)
content:
Printing presses shall be free to every person who undertakes to examine the proceedings
   of the General Assembly or any branch of government, and no law shall ever be made
   to restrain the right thereof.  Every person may freely and fully speak, write and print on any subject, being responsible
   for the abuse of that liberty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Distribution of the Powers of Government›KY CONST § 28. One department not to exercise power belonging to another
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Distribution of the Powers of Government › KY CONST § 28. One department not to exercise power belonging to another
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 28. One department not to exercise power belonging to another (2023)
content:
No person or collection of persons, being of one of those departments, shall exercise
   any power properly belonging to either of the others, except in the instances hereinafter
   expressly directed or permitted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 17. Excessive bail or fine, or cruel punishment, prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 17. Excessive bail or fine, or cruel punishment, prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 17. Excessive bail or fine, or cruel punishment, prohibited (2023)
content:
Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel punishment
   inflicted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 18. Imprisonment for debt restricted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 18. Imprisonment for debt restricted
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 18. Imprisonment for debt restricted (2023)
content:
The person of a debtor, where there is not strong presumption of fraud, shall not
   be continued in prison after delivering up his estate for the benefit of his creditors
   in such manner as shall be prescribed by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 16. Right to bail; habeas corpus
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 16. Right to bail; habeas corpus
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 16. Right to bail; habeas corpus (2023)
content:
All prisoners shall be bailable by sufficient securities, unless for capital offenses
   when the proof is evident or the presumption great;  and the privilege of the writ
   of habeas corpus shall not be suspended unless when, in case of rebellion or invasion,
   the public safety may require it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 30. Term of office of Senators and Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 30. Term of office of Senators and Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 30. Term of office of Senators and Representatives (2023)
content:
Members of the House of Representatives and Senators shall be elected at the general
   election in even-numbered years for terms of four years for Senators and two years
   for members of the House of Representatives.  The term of office of Representatives and Senators shall begin upon the first day
   of January of the year succeeding their election.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 20. Attainder, operation of restricted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 20. Attainder, operation of restricted
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 20. Attainder, operation of restricted (2023)
content:
No person shall be attainted of treason or felony by the General Assembly, and no
   attainder shall work corruption of blood, nor, except during the life of the offender,
   forfeiture of estate to the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 36. Time and place of meetings of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 36. Time and place of meetings of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 36. Time and place of meetings of General Assembly (2023)
content:
(1) The General Assembly, in odd-numbered years, shall meet in regular session for
      a period not to exceed a total of thirty (30) legislative days divided as follows:
      The General Assembly shall convene for the first part of the session on the first
      Tuesday after the first Monday in January in odd-numbered years for the purposes of
      electing legislative leaders, adopting rules of procedure, organizing committees,
      and introducing and considering legislation.  The General Assembly shall then adjourn.  The General Assembly shall convene for the second part of the session on the first
      Tuesday in February of that year.  Any legislation introduced but not enacted in the first part of the session shall
      be carried over into the second part of the session.  In any part of the session in an odd-numbered year, no bill raising revenue or appropriating
      funds shall become a law unless it shall be agreed to by three-fifths of all the members
      elected to each House.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 19. Ex post facto law or law impairing contract forbidden; rules of construction for mineral deeds relating to coal extraction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 19. Ex post facto law or law impairing contract forbidden; rules of construction for mineral deeds relating to coal extraction
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 19. Ex post facto law or law impairing contract forbidden; rules of construction for mineral deeds relating to coal extraction (2023)
content:
(1) No ex post facto law, nor any law impairing the obligation of contracts, shall
      be enacted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 21. Descent in case of suicide or casualty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 21. Descent in case of suicide or casualty
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 21. Descent in case of suicide or casualty (2023)
content:
The estate of such persons as shall destroy their own lives shall descend or vest
   as in cases of natural death;  and if any person shall be killed by casualty, there
   shall be no forfeiture by reason thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 24. Emigration to be free
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 24. Emigration to be free
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 24. Emigration to be free (2023)
content: Emigration from the State shall not be prohibited.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 22. Standing armies restricted; military subordinate to civil; quartering soldiers restricted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 22. Standing armies restricted; military subordinate to civil; quartering soldiers restricted
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 22. Standing armies restricted; military subordinate to civil; quartering soldiers restricted (2023)
content:
No standing army shall, in time of peace, be maintained without the consent of the
   General Assembly;  and the military shall, in all cases and at all times, be in strict
   subordination to the civil power;  nor shall any soldier, in time of peace, be quartered
   in any house without the consent of the owner, nor in time of war, except in a manner
   prescribed by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 25. Slavery and involuntary servitude forbidden
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 25. Slavery and involuntary servitude forbidden
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 25. Slavery and involuntary servitude forbidden (2023)
content:
Slavery and involuntary servitude in this State are forbidden, except as a punishment
   for crime, whereof the party shall have been duly convicted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Rights of Victims of Crime›KY CONST § 26A Rights of victims of crime
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Rights of Victims of Crime › KY CONST § 26A Rights of victims of crime
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 26A Rights of victims of crime (2023)
content:
To secure for victims of criminal acts or public offenses justice and due process
   and to ensure crime victims a meaningful role throughout the criminal and juvenile
   justice systems, a victim, as defined by law which takes effect upon the enactment
   of this section and which may be expanded by the General Assembly, shall have the
   following rights, which shall be respected and protected by law in a manner no less
   vigorous than the protections afforded to the accused in the criminal and juvenile
   justice systems: victims shall have the reasonable right, upon request, to timely
   notice of all proceedings and to be heard in any proceeding involving a release, plea,
   sentencing, or in the consideration of any pardon, commutation of sentence, granting
   of a reprieve, or other matter involving the right of a victim other than grand jury
   proceedings; the right to be present at the trial and all other proceedings, other
   than grand jury proceedings, on the same basis as the accused; the right to proceedings
   free from unreasonable delay; the right to consult with the attorney for the Commonwealth
   or the attorney's designee; the right to reasonable protection from the accused and
   those acting on behalf of the accused throughout the criminal and juvenile justice
   process; the right to timely notice, upon request, of release or escape of the accused;
   the right to have the safety of the victim and the victim’s family considered in setting
   bail, determining whether to release the defendant, and setting conditions of release
   after arrest and conviction; the right to full restitution to be paid by the convicted
   or adjudicated party in a manner to be determined by the court, except that in the
   case of a juvenile offender the court shall determine the amount and manner of paying
   the restitution taking into consideration the best interests of the juvenile offender
   and the victim; the right to fairness and due consideration of the crime victim's
   safety, dignity, and privacy; and the right to be informed of these enumerated rights,
   and shall have standing to assert these rights. The victim, the victim's attorney or other lawful representative, or the attorney
   for the Commonwealth upon request of the victim may seek enforcement of the rights
   enumerated in this section and any other right afforded to the victim by law in any
   trial or appellate court with jurisdiction over the case. The court shall act promptly on such a request and afford a remedy for the violation
   of any right. Nothing in this section shall afford the victim party status, or be construed as altering
   the presumption of innocence in the criminal justice system. The accused shall not have standing to assert the rights of a victim. Nothing in this section shall be construed to alter the powers, duties, and responsibilities
   of the prosecuting attorney. Nothing in this section or any law enacted under this section creates a cause of action
   for compensation, attorney's fees, or damages against the Commonwealth, a county,
   city, municipal corporation, or other political subdivision of the Commonwealth, an
   officer, employee, or agent of the Commonwealth, a county, city, municipal corporation,
   or any political subdivision of the Commonwealth, or an officer or employee of the
   court. Nothing in this section or any law enacted under this section shall be construed as
   creating:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Bill of Rights›KY CONST § 26. General powers subordinate to Bill of Rights; laws contrary thereto are void
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Bill of Rights › KY CONST § 26. General powers subordinate to Bill of Rights; laws contrary thereto are void
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 26. General powers subordinate to Bill of Rights; laws contrary thereto are void (2023)
content:
To guard against transgression of the high powers which we have delegated, We Declare
   that every thing in this Bill of Rights is excepted out of the general powers of government,
   and shall forever remain inviolate;  and all laws contrary thereto, or contrary to
   this Constitution, shall be void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 33. Senatorial and Representative districts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 33. Senatorial and Representative districts
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 33. Senatorial and Representative districts (2023)
content:
The first General Assembly after the adoption of this Constitution shall divide the
   State into thirty-eight Senatorial Districts, and one hundred Representative Districts,
   as nearly equal in population as may be without dividing any county, except where
   a county may include more than one district, which districts shall constitute the
   Senatorial and Representative Districts for ten years.  Not more than two counties shall be joined together to form a Representative District:
   Provided, In doing so the principle requiring every district to be as nearly equal
   in population as may be shall not be violated.  At the expiration of that time, the General Assembly shall then, and every ten years
   thereafter, redistrict the State according to this rule, and for the purposes expressed
   in this section.  If, in making said districts, inequality of population should be unavoidable, any
   advantage resulting therefrom shall be given to districts having the largest territory.  No part of a county shall be added to another county to make a district, and the
   counties forming a district shall be contiguous.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 34. Officers of Houses of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 34. Officers of Houses of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 34. Officers of Houses of General Assembly (2023)
content:
The House of Representatives shall choose its Speaker and other officers, and the
   Senate shall have power to choose its officers biennially.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 31. Time of election and term of office of Senators and Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 31. Time of election and term of office of Senators and Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 31. Time of election and term of office of Senators and Representatives (2023)
content:
At the general election to be held in November, 1984, and every two years thereafter,
   there shall be elected for four years one Senator in each Senatorial District in which
   the term of his predecessor in office will then expire and in every Representative
   District one Representative for two years.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 32. Qualifications of Senators and Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 32. Qualifications of Senators and Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 32. Qualifications of Senators and Representatives (2023)
content:
No person shall be a Representative who, at the time of his election, is not a citizen
   of Kentucky, has not attained the age of twenty-four years, and who has not resided
   in this State two years next preceding his election, and the last year thereof in
   the county, town or city for which he may be chosen.  No person shall be a Senator who, at the time of his election, is not a citizen
   of Kentucky, has not attained the age of thirty years, and has not resided in this
   State six years next preceding his election, and the last year thereof in the district
   for which he may be chosen.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 29. Legislative power vested in General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 29. Legislative power vested in General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 29. Legislative power vested in General Assembly (2023)
content:
The legislative power shall be vested in a House of Representatives and a Senate,
   which, together, shall be styled the “General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›Distribution of the Powers of Government›KY CONST § 27. Powers of government divided among legislative, executive, and judicial departments
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › Distribution of the Powers of Government › KY CONST § 27. Powers of government divided among legislative, executive, and judicial departments
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 27. Powers of government divided among legislative, executive, and judicial departments (2023)
content:
The powers of the government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky shall be divided into
   three distinct departments, and each of them be confined to a separate body of magistracy,
   to wit:  Those which are legislative, to one;  those which are executive, to another;
   and those which are judicial, to another.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 46. Bills must be reported by committee, printed, and read; how bill called from committee; votes required for passage
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 46. Bills must be reported by committee, printed, and read; how bill called from committee; votes required for passage
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 46. Bills must be reported by committee, printed, and read; how bill called from committee; votes required for passage (2023)
content:
No bill shall be considered for final passage unless the same has been reported by
   a committee and printed for the use of the members.  Every bill shall be read at length on three different days in each House, but the
   second and third readings may be dispensed with by a majority of all the members elected
   to the House in which the bill is pending.  But whenever a committee refuses or fails to report a bill submitted to it in a
   reasonable time, the same may be called up by any member, and be considered in the
   same manner it would have been considered if it had been reported.  No bill shall become a law unless, on its final passage, it receives the votes of
   at least two-fifths of the members elected to each House, and a majority of the members
   voting, the vote to be taken by yeas and nays and entered in the journal:  Provided,
   Any act or resolution for the appropriation of money or the creation of debt shall,
   on its final passage, receive the votes of a majority of all the members elected to
   each House.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 35. Number of Senators and Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 35. Number of Senators and Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 35. Number of Senators and Representatives (2023)
content: The number of Representatives shall be one hundred, and the number of Senators thirty-eight.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 41. Adjournment during session
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 41. Adjournment during session
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 41. Adjournment during session (2023)
content:
Neither House, during the session of the General Assembly, shall, without the consent
   of the other, adjourn for more than three days, nor to any other place than that in
   which it may be sitting.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 39. Powers of each House as to rules and conduct of members; contempt; bribery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 39. Powers of each House as to rules and conduct of members; contempt; bribery
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 39. Powers of each House as to rules and conduct of members; contempt; bribery (2023)
content:
Each House of the General Assembly may determine the rules of its proceedings, punish
   a member for disorderly behavior, and, with the concurrence of two-thirds, expel a
   member, but not a second time for the same cause, and may punish for contempt any
   person who refuses to attend as a witness, or to bring any paper proper to be used
   as evidence before the General Assembly, or either House thereof, or a Committee of
   either, or to testify concerning any matter which may be a proper subject of inquiry
   by the General Assembly, or offers or gives a bribe to a member of the General Assembly,
   or attempts by other corrupt means or device to control or influence a member to cast
   his vote or withhold the same.  The punishment and mode of proceeding for contempt in such cases shall be prescribed
   by law, but the term of imprisonment in any such case shall not extend beyond the
   session of the General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 37. Majority constitutes quorum; powers of less than a quorum
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 37. Majority constitutes quorum; powers of less than a quorum
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 37. Majority constitutes quorum; powers of less than a quorum (2023)
content:
Not less than a majority of the members of each House of the General Assembly shall
   constitute a quorum to do business, but a smaller number may adjourn from day to day,
   and shall be authorized by law to compel the attendance of absent members in such
   manner and under such penalties as may be prescribed by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 40. Journals; when vote to be entered
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 40. Journals; when vote to be entered
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 40. Journals; when vote to be entered (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 38. Each House to judge qualifications, elections, and returns of its members; contests
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 38. Each House to judge qualifications, elections, and returns of its members; contests
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 38. Each House to judge qualifications, elections, and returns of its members; contests (2023)
content:
Each House of the General Assembly shall judge of the qualifications, elections and
   returns of its members, but a contested election shall be determined in such manner
   as shall be directed by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 50. Purposes for which debt may be contracted; tax to discharge; public vote
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 50. Purposes for which debt may be contracted; tax to discharge; public vote
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 50. Purposes for which debt may be contracted; tax to discharge; public vote (2023)
content:
No act of the General Assembly shall authorize any debt to be contracted on behalf
   of the Commonwealth except for the purposes mentioned in Section 49, unless provision
   be made therein to levy and collect an annual tax sufficient to pay the interest stipulated,
   and to discharge the debt within thirty years;  nor shall such act take effect until
   it shall have been submitted to the people at a general election, and shall have received
   a majority of all the votes cast for and against it:  Provided, The General Assembly
   may contract debts by borrowing money to pay any part of the debt of the State, without
   submission to the people, and without making provision in the act authorizing the
   same for a tax to discharge the debt so contracted, or the interest thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 51. Law may not relate to more than one subject, to be expressed in title; amendments must be at length
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 51. Law may not relate to more than one subject, to be expressed in title; amendments must be at length
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 51. Law may not relate to more than one subject, to be expressed in title; amendments must be at length (2023)
content:
No law enacted by the General Assembly shall relate to more than one subject, and
   that shall be expressed in the title, and no law shall be revised, amended, or the
   provisions thereof extended or conferred by reference to its title only, but so much
   thereof as is revised, amended, extended or conferred, shall be reenacted and published
   at length.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 52. General Assembly may not release debt to State or to county or city
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 52. General Assembly may not release debt to State or to county or city
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 52. General Assembly may not release debt to State or to county or city (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall have no power to release, extinguish or authorize the releasing
   or extinguishing, in whole or in part, the indebtedness or liability of any corporation
   or individual to this Commonwealth, or to any county or municipality thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 42. Compensation of members; length of sessions; legislative day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 42. Compensation of members; length of sessions; legislative day
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 42. Compensation of members; length of sessions; legislative day (2023)
content:
The members of the General Assembly shall severally receive from the State Treasury
   compensation for their services:  Provided, No change shall take effect during the
   session at which it is made;  nor shall a session occurring in odd-numbered years
   extend beyond March 30;  nor shall a session of the General Assembly occurring in
   even-numbered years continue beyond sixty legislative days, nor shall it extend beyond
   April 15;  these limitations as to length of sessions shall not apply to the Senate
   when sitting as a court of impeachment.  A legislative day shall be construed to mean a calendar day, exclusive of Sundays,
   legal holidays, or any day on which neither House meets.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 55. When laws to take effect; emergency legislation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 55. When laws to take effect; emergency legislation
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 55. When laws to take effect; emergency legislation (2023)
content:
No act, except general appropriation bills, shall become a law until ninety days after
   the adjournment of the session at which it was passed, except in cases of emergency,
   when, by the concurrence of a majority of the members elected to each House of the
   General Assembly, by a yea and nay vote, entered upon their journals, an act may become
   a law when approved by the Governor;  but the reasons for the emergency that justifies
   this action must be set out at length in the journal of each House.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 57. Member having personal interest to make disclosure and not vote
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 57. Member having personal interest to make disclosure and not vote
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 57. Member having personal interest to make disclosure and not vote (2023)
content:
A member who has a personal or private interest in any measure or bill proposed or
   pending before the General Assembly, shall disclose the fact to the House of which
   he is a member, and shall not vote thereon upon pain of expulsion.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 43. Privileges from arrest and from questioning as to speech or debate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 43. Privileges from arrest and from questioning as to speech or debate
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 43. Privileges from arrest and from questioning as to speech or debate (2023)
content:
The members of the General Assembly shall, in all cases except treason, felony, breach
   or surety of the peace, be privileged from arrest during their attendance on the sessions
   of their respective Houses, and in going to and returning from the same;  and for
   any speech or debate in either House they shall not be questioned in any other place.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 56. Signing of bills; enrollment; presentation to Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 56. Signing of bills; enrollment; presentation to Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 56. Signing of bills; enrollment; presentation to Governor (2023)
content:
No bill shall become a law until the same shall have been signed by the presiding
   officer of each of the two Houses in open session;  and before such officer shall
   have affixed his signature to any bill, he shall suspend all other business, declare
   that such bill will now be read, and that he will sign the same to the end that it
   may become a law.  The bill shall then be read at length and compared;  and, if correctly enrolled,
   he shall, in the presence of the House in open session, and before any other business
   is entertained, affix his signature, which fact shall be noted in the journal, and
   the bill immediately sent to the other House.  When it reaches the other House, the presiding officer thereof shall immediately
   suspend all other business, announce the reception of the bill, and the same proceeding
   shall thereupon be observed in every respect as in the House in which it was first
   signed.  And thereupon the Clerk of the latter House shall immediately present the same to
   the Governor for his signature and approval.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 60. General law not to be made special or local by amendment; no special powers or privileges; law not to take effect on approval of other authority than General Assembly; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 60. General law not to be made special or local by amendment; no special powers or privileges; law not to take effect on approval of other authority than General Assembly; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 60. General law not to be made special or local by amendment; no special powers or privileges; law not to take effect on approval of other authority than General Assembly; exceptions (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall not indirectly enact any special or local act by the repeal
   in part of a general act, or by exempting from the operation of a general act any
   city, town, district or county;  but laws repealing local or special acts may be enacted.  No law shall be enacted granting powers or privileges in any case where the granting
   of such powers or privileges shall have been provided for by a general law, nor where
   the courts have jurisdiction to grant the same or to give the relief asked for.  No law, except such as relates to the sale, loan or gift of vinous, spirituous or
   malt liquors, bridges, turnpikes or other public roads, public buildings or improvements,
   fencing, running at large of stock, matters pertaining to common schools, paupers,
   and the regulation by counties, cities, towns or other municipalities of their local
   affairs, shall be enacted to take effect upon the approval of any other authority
   than the General Assembly, unless otherwise expressly provided in this Constitution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 47. Bills to raise revenue must originate in House of Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 47. Bills to raise revenue must originate in House of Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 47. Bills to raise revenue must originate in House of Representatives (2023)
content:
All bills for raising revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives, but
   the Senate may propose amendments thereto:  Provided, No new matter shall be introduced,
   under color of amendment, which does not relate to raising revenue.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 61. Provision to be made for local option on sale of liquor; time of elections
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 61. Provision to be made for local option on sale of liquor; time of elections
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 61. Provision to be made for local option on sale of liquor; time of elections (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall, by general law, provide a means whereby the sense of the
   people of any county, city, town, district or precinct may be taken, as to whether
   or not spirituous, vinous or malt liquors shall be sold, bartered or loaned therein,
   or the sale thereof regulated.  But nothing herein shall be construed to interfere with or to repeal any law in
   force relating to the sale or gift of such liquors.  All elections on this question may be held on a day other than the regular election
   days.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 44. Ineligibility of members to civil office created or given increased compensation during term
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 44. Ineligibility of members to civil office created or given increased compensation during term
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 44. Ineligibility of members to civil office created or given increased compensation during term (2023)
content:
No Senator or Representative shall, during the term for which he was elected, nor
   for one year thereafter, be appointed or elected to any civil office of profit in
   this Commonwealth, which shall have been created, or the emoluments of which shall
   have been increased, during the said term, except to such offices as may be filled
   by the election of the people.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 45. Collector of public money ineligible unless he has quietus
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 45. Collector of public money ineligible unless he has quietus
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 45. Collector of public money ineligible unless he has quietus (2023)
content:
No person who may have been a collector of taxes or public moneys for the Commonwealth,
   or for any county, city, town or district, or the assistant or deputy of such collector,
   shall be eligible to the General Assembly, unless he shall have obtained a quietus
   six months before the election for the amount of such collection, and for all public
   moneys for which he may have been responsible.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 53. Investigation of accounts of Treasurer and Auditor; report, publication, submission to Governor and General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 53. Investigation of accounts of Treasurer and Auditor; report, publication, submission to Governor and General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 53. Investigation of accounts of Treasurer and Auditor; report, publication, submission to Governor and General Assembly (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall provide by law for monthly investigations into the accounts
   of the Treasurer and Auditor of Public Accounts, and the result of these investigations
   shall be reported to the Governor, and these reports shall be semiannually published
   in two newspapers of general circulation in the State.  The reports received by the Governor shall, at the beginning of each session, be
   transmitted by him to the General Assembly for scrutiny and appropriate action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 71. Gubernatorial succession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 71. Gubernatorial succession
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 71. Gubernatorial succession (2023)
content:
The Governor shall be ineligible for the succeeding four years after the expiration
   of any second consecutive term for which he shall have been elected.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 54. No restriction on recovery for injury or death
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 54. No restriction on recovery for injury or death
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 54. No restriction on recovery for injury or death (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall have no power to limit the amount to be recovered for injuries
   resulting in death, or for injuries to person or property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 49. Power to contract debts; limit
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 49. Power to contract debts; limit
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 49. Power to contract debts; limit (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may contract debts to meet casual deficits or failures in the
   revenue;  but such debts, direct or contingent, singly or in the aggregate, shall
   not at any time exceed five hundred thousand dollars, and the moneys arising from
   loans creating such debts shall be applied only to the purpose or purposes for which
   they were obtained, or to repay such debts:  Provided, The General Assembly may contract
   debts to repel invasion, suppress insurrection, or, if hostilities are threatened,
   provide for the public defense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 48. Resources of Sinking Fund not to be diminished; preservation of fund
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 48. Resources of Sinking Fund not to be diminished; preservation of fund
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 48. Resources of Sinking Fund not to be diminished; preservation of fund (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall have no power to enact laws to diminish the resources of
   the Sinking Fund as now established by law until the debt of the Commonwealth be paid,
   but may enact laws to increase them;  and the whole resources of said fund, from year
   to year, shall be sacredly set apart and applied to the payment of the interest and
   principal of the State debt, and to no other use or purpose, until the whole debt
   of the State is fully satisfied.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 78. Governor may require information from state officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 78. Governor may require information from state officers
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 78. Governor may require information from state officers (2023)
content:
He may require information in writing from the officers of the Executive Department
   upon any subject relating to the duties of their respective offices.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 80. Governor may call extraordinary session of General Assembly; adjourn General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 80. Governor may call extraordinary session of General Assembly; adjourn General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 80. Governor may call extraordinary session of General Assembly; adjourn General Assembly (2023)
content:
He may, on extraordinary occasions, convene the General Assembly at the seat of government,
   or at a different place, if that should have become dangerous from an enemy or from
   contagious diseases.  In case of disagreement between the two Houses with respect to the time of adjournment,
   he may adjourn them to such time as he shall think proper, not exceeding four months.  When he shall convene the General Assembly it shall be by proclamation, stating
   the subjects to be considered, and no other shall be considered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 81. Governor to enforce laws
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 81. Governor to enforce laws
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 81. Governor to enforce laws (2023)
content: He shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 70. Election of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; term; tie vote
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 70. Election of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; term; tie vote
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 70. Election of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; term; tie vote (2023)
content:
The Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall be elected for the term of four years by
   the qualified voters of the State.  They shall be elected jointly by the casting by each voter of a single vote applicable
   to both offices, as shall be provided by law.  The slate of candidates having the highest number of votes cast jointly for them
   for Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall be elected;  but if two or more slates
   of candidates shall be equal and highest in votes, the election shall be determined
   by lot in such manner as the General Assembly may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 62. Style of laws
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 62. Style of laws
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 62. Style of laws (2023)
content:
The style of the laws of this Commonwealth shall be as follows:  “Be it enacted by
   the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 59. Local and special legislation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 59. Local and special legislation
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 59. Local and special legislation (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall not pass local or special acts concerning any of the following
   subjects, or for any of the following purposes, namely:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 69. Executive power vested in Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 69. Executive power vested in Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 69. Executive power vested in Governor (2023)
content:
The supreme executive power of the Commonwealth shall be vested in a Chief Magistrate,
   who shall be styled the “Governor of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Legislative Department›KY CONST § 58. General Assembly not to audit nor allow private claim; exception; appropriations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Legislative Department › KY CONST § 58. General Assembly not to audit nor allow private claim; exception; appropriations
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 58. General Assembly not to audit nor allow private claim; exception; appropriations (2023)
content:
The General Assembly shall neither audit nor allow any private claim against the Commonwealth,
   except for expenses incurred during the session at which the same was allowed;  but
   may appropriate money to pay such claim as shall have been audited and allowed according
   to law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 72. Qualifications of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; duties of Lieutenant Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 72. Qualifications of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; duties of Lieutenant Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 72. Qualifications of Governor and Lieutenant Governor; duties of Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
The Governor and the Lieutenant Governor shall be at least thirty years of age, and
   have been citizens and residents of Kentucky for at least six years next preceding
   their election.  The duties of the Lieutenant Governor shall be prescribed by law, and he shall have
   such other duties as delegated by the Governor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 74. Compensation of Governor and Lieutenant Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 74. Compensation of Governor and Lieutenant Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 74. Compensation of Governor and Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
The Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall at stated times receive for the performance
   of the duties of their respective offices compensation to be fixed by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 79. Reports and recommendations to General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 79. Reports and recommendations to General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 79. Reports and recommendations to General Assembly (2023)
content:
He shall, from time to time, give to the General Assembly information of the state
   of the Commonwealth, and recommend to their consideration such measures as he may
   deem expedient.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 82. Succession of Lieutenant Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 82. Succession of Lieutenant Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 82. Succession of Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
The Lieutenant Governor shall be ineligible to the office of Lieutenant Governor for
   the succeeding four (4) years after the expiration of any second consecutive term
   for which he shall have been elected.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 84. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor; President of the Senate not to preside at impeachment of Governor; certification of disability of Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 84. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor; President of the Senate not to preside at impeachment of Governor; certification of disability of Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 84. When Lieutenant Governor to act as Governor; President of the Senate not to preside at impeachment of Governor; certification of disability of Governor (2023)
content:
Should the Governor be impeached and removed from office, die, refuse to qualify,
   resign, certify by entry on his Journal that he is unable to discharge the duties
   of his office, or be, from any cause, unable to discharge the duties of his office,
   the Lieutenant Governor shall exercise all the power and authority appertaining to
   the office of Governor until another be duly elected and qualified, or the Governor
   shall be able to discharge the duties of his office.  On the trial of the Governor, the President of the Senate shall not preside over
   the proceedings, but the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall preside during the
   trial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 73. When terms of Governor and Lieutenant Governor begin
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 73. When terms of Governor and Lieutenant Governor begin
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 73. When terms of Governor and Lieutenant Governor begin (2023)
content:
The Governor and the Lieutenant Governor shall commence the execution of the duties
   of their offices on the fifth Tuesday succeeding their election, and shall continue
   in the execution thereof until a successor shall have qualified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 75. Governor is Commander-in-Chief of army, navy, and militia
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 75. Governor is Commander-in-Chief of army, navy, and militia
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 75. Governor is Commander-in-Chief of army, navy, and militia (2023)
content:
He shall be Commander-in-Chief of the army and navy of this Commonwealth, and of the
   militia thereof, except when they shall be called into the service of the United States;
   but he shall not command personally in the field, unless advised so to do by a resolution
   of the General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 77. Power of Governor to remit fines and forfeitures, grant reprieves and pardons; no power to remit fees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 77. Power of Governor to remit fines and forfeitures, grant reprieves and pardons; no power to remit fees
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 77. Power of Governor to remit fines and forfeitures, grant reprieves and pardons; no power to remit fees (2023)
content:
He shall have power to remit fines and forfeitures, commute sentences, grant reprieves
   and pardons, except in case of impeachment, and he shall file with each application
   therefor a statement of the reasons for his decision thereon, which application and
   statement shall always be open to public inspection.  In cases of treason, he shall have power to grant reprieves until the end of the
   next session of the General Assembly, in which the power of pardoning shall be vested;
   but he shall have no power to remit the fees of the Clerk, Sheriff or Commonwealth's
   Attorney in penal or criminal cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 76. Power of Governor to fill vacancies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 76. Power of Governor to fill vacancies
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 76. Power of Governor to fill vacancies (2023)
content:
He shall have the power, except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, to fill
   vacancies by granting commissions, which shall expire when such vacancies shall have
   been filled according to the provisions of this Constitution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 87. Who to act as Governor in absence of Lieutenant Governor and President of the Senate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 87. Who to act as Governor in absence of Lieutenant Governor and President of the Senate
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 87. Who to act as Governor in absence of Lieutenant Governor and President of the Senate (2023)
content:
If the Lieutenant Governor shall be called upon to administer the government in place
   of the Governor, and shall, while in such administration, resign, or die during the
   recess of the General Assembly, if there be no President of the Senate, it shall be
   the duty of the Attorney General, for the time being, to convene the Senate for the
   purpose of choosing a President;  and until a President is chosen, the Attorney General
   shall administer the government.  If there be no Attorney General to perform the duties devolved upon him by this
   section, then the Auditor, for the time being, shall convene the Senate for the purpose
   of choosing a President, and shall administer the government until a President is
   chosen.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 86. Compensation of President of the Senate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 86. Compensation of President of the Senate
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 86. Compensation of President of the Senate (2023)
content:
The President of the Senate shall receive for his services the same compensation which
   shall, for the same period, be allowed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
   and during the time he administers the government as Governor, he shall receive the
   same compensation which the Governor would have received had he been employed in the
   duties of his office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 85. President of Senate; election; powers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 85. President of Senate; election; powers
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 85. President of Senate; election; powers (2023)
content:
A President of the Senate shall be elected by each Senate as soon after its organization
   as possible and as often as there is a vacancy in the office of President, another
   President of the Senate shall be elected by the Senate, if in session.  And if, during the vacancy of the office of Governor, the Lieutenant Governor shall
   be impeached and removed from office, refuse to qualify, resign, or die, the President
   of the Senate shall in like manner administer the government.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 91. Constitutional State officers; election; qualifications; term of office; duties; Secretary of State to record acts of Governor and report them to General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 91. Constitutional State officers; election; qualifications; term of office; duties; Secretary of State to record acts of Governor and report them to General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 91. Constitutional State officers; election; qualifications; term of office; duties; Secretary of State to record acts of Governor and report them to General Assembly (2023)
content:
A Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Commissioner of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics,
   Secretary of State, and Attorney-General, shall be elected by the qualified voters
   of the State at the same time the Governor and Lieutenant Governor are elected, for
   the term of four years, each of whom shall be at least thirty years of age at the
   time of his election, and shall have been a resident citizen of the State at least
   two years next before his election.  The duties of all these officers shall be such as may be prescribed by law, and
   the Secretary of State shall keep a fair register of and attest all the official acts
   of the Governor, and shall, when required, lay the same and all papers, minutes and
   vouchers relative thereto before either House of the General Assembly.  The officers named in this section shall enter upon the discharge of their duties
   the first Monday in January after their election, and shall hold their offices until
   their successors are elected and qualified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 88. Signature of bills by Governor; veto; passage over veto; partial veto
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 88. Signature of bills by Governor; veto; passage over veto; partial veto
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 88. Signature of bills by Governor; veto; passage over veto; partial veto (2023)
content:
Every bill which shall have passed the two Houses shall be presented to the Governor.  If he approve, he shall sign it;  but if not, he shall return it, with his objections,
   to the House in which it originated, which shall enter the objections in full upon
   its journal, and proceed to reconsider it.  If, after such reconsideration, a majority of all the members elected to that House
   shall agree to pass the bill, it shall be sent, with the objections, to the other
   House, by which it shall likewise be considered, and if approved by a majority of
   all the members elected to that House, it shall be a law;  but in such case the votes
   of both Houses shall be determined by yeas and nays, and the names of the members
   voting for and against the bill shall be entered upon the journal of each House respectively.  If any bill shall not be returned by the Governor within ten days (Sundays excepted)
   after it shall have been presented to him, it shall be a law in like manner as if
   he had signed it, unless the General Assembly, by their adjournment, prevent its return,
   in which case it shall be a law, unless disapproved by him within ten days after the
   adjournment, in which case his veto message shall be spread upon the register kept
   by the Secretary of State.  The Governor shall have the power to disapprove any part or parts of appropriation
   bills embracing distinct items, and the part or parts disapproved shall not become
   a law unless reconsidered and passed, as in case of a bill.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 92. Qualifications of Attorney General
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 92. Qualifications of Attorney General
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 92. Qualifications of Attorney General (2023)
content: The Attorney-General shall have been a practicing lawyer eight years before his election.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 93. Succession of elected Constitutional State Officers; duties; inferior officers and members of boards and commissions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 93. Succession of elected Constitutional State Officers; duties; inferior officers and members of boards and commissions
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 93. Succession of elected Constitutional State Officers; duties; inferior officers and members of boards and commissions (2023)
content:
The Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Secretary of State, Commissioner of Agriculture,
   Labor and Statistics, and Attorney General shall be ineligible to reelection for the
   succeeding four years after the expiration of any second consecutive term for which
   they shall have been elected.  The duties and responsibilities of these officers shall be prescribed by law, and
   all fees collected by any of said officers shall be covered into the treasury.  Inferior State officers and members of boards and commissions, not specifically
   provided for in this Constitution, may be appointed or elected, in such manner as
   may be prescribed by law, which may include a requirement of consent by the Senate,
   for a term not exceeding four years, and until their successors are appointed or elected
   and qualified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 89. Concurrent orders and resolutions on same footing as bill
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 89. Concurrent orders and resolutions on same footing as bill
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 89. Concurrent orders and resolutions on same footing as bill (2023)
content:
Every order, resolution or vote, in which the concurrence of both Houses may be necessary,
   except on a question of adjournment, or as otherwise provided in this Constitution,
   shall be presented to the Governor, and, before it shall take effect, be approved
   by him;  or, being disapproved, shall be repassed by a majority of the members elected
   to both Houses, according to the rules and limitations prescribed in case of a bill.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for the State at Large›KY CONST § 90. Contest of election for Governor or Lieutenant Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for the State at Large › KY CONST § 90. Contest of election for Governor or Lieutenant Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 90. Contest of election for Governor or Lieutenant Governor (2023)
content:
Contested elections for Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall be determined by both
   Houses of the General Assembly, according to such regulations as may be established
   by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for Districts and Counties›KY CONST § 105. Consolidation of offices of sheriff and jailer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Executive Department › Officers for Districts and Counties › KY CONST § 105. Consolidation of offices of sheriff and jailer
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 105. Consolidation of offices of sheriff and jailer (2023)
content:
The General Assembly may, at any time, consolidate the offices of Jailer and Sheriff
   in any county or counties, as it shall deem most expedient;  but in the event such
   consolidation be made, the office of Sheriff shall be retained, and the Sheriff shall
   be required to perform the duties of Jailer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Judicial Department›KY CONST § 109. The judicial power; unified system; impeachment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Kentucky Constitution › The Judicial Department › KY CONST § 109. The judicial power; unified system; impeachment
citation: KY Stat § KY CONST § 109. The judicial power; unified system; impeachment (2023)
content:
The judicial power of the Commonwealth shall be vested exclusively in one Court of
   Justice which shall be divided into a Supreme Court, a Court of Appeals, a trial court
   of general jurisdiction known as the Circuit Court and a trial court of limited jurisdiction
   known as the District Court.  The court shall constitute a unified judicial system for operation and administration.  The impeachment powers of the General Assembly shall remain inviolate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Kentucky Constitution›The Executive Department›Officers for Districts and Counties›KY CONST § 100. Qualifications of officers for counties and districts
