title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.135. Barrier Awareness Day; Disability Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.135. Barrier Awareness Day; Disability Day (2023)
content:
(1)  May 7 of each year is named and declared to be “Barrier Awareness Day” throughout
      the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.1095. Kentucky Museum of African American History
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.1095. Kentucky Museum of African American History
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.1095. Kentucky Museum of African American History (2023)
content:
Jackson Hall at Kentucky State University is designated the Kentucky Museum of African
   American History.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.148. A Day of Prayer for Kentucky’s Students
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.148. A Day of Prayer for Kentucky’s Students
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.148. A Day of Prayer for Kentucky’s Students (2023)
content:
(1)  The General Assembly recognizes that the students of the Commonwealth are the
      state's single greatest resource and designates the last Wednesday in September of
      each year as A Day of Prayer for Kentucky's Students.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.149. Farmer Suicide Prevention Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.149. Farmer Suicide Prevention Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.149. Farmer Suicide Prevention Day (2023)
content:
(1)  The Wednesday of National Farm Safety Week, which is the third week of September,
      shall be observed in Kentucky as “Farmer Suicide Prevention Day.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.153. Tuskegee Airmen Commemoration Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.153. Tuskegee Airmen Commemoration Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.153. Tuskegee Airmen Commemoration Day (2023)
content:
The fourth Thursday in March of each year is designated as Tuskegee Airmen Commemoration
   Day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.155. Kentucky National Guard Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.155. Kentucky National Guard Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.155. Kentucky National Guard Day (2023)
content:
The twenty-fourth day of June of each year is designated as Kentucky National Guard
   Day in the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.112. Dates of recognition

content: (1)  The following months are designated with honor in Kentucky:

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.156. State gun (2023)
content:
The Kentucky Long Rifle is named and designated the official gun of the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.159. Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.159. Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.159. Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans Day (2023)
content:
The thirtieth day of March each year is designated as Welcome Home Vietnam Veterans
   Day in the Commonwealth of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.190. Presidential election day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.190. Presidential election day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.190. Presidential election day (2023)
content:
The Tuesday after the first Monday in November in Presidential election years shall
   be a state holiday on which all state offices, all schools and all state universities
   and colleges shall be closed.  Any employee who is required to work on said state holiday shall receive compensatory
   pay or time off.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.110. Public holidays
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.110. Public holidays
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.110. Public holidays (2023)
content:
(1)  The first day of January (New Year's Day), the third Monday of January (Birthday
      of Martin Luther King, Jr.), the nineteenth day of January (Robert E. Lee Day), the
      thirtieth day of January (Franklin D. Roosevelt Day), the twelfth day of February
      (Lincoln's Birthday), the third Monday in February (Washington's Birthday), the last
      Monday in May (Memorial Day), the third day of June (Confederate Memorial Day, and
      Jefferson Davis Day), the fourth day of July (Independence Day), the first Monday
      in September (Labor Day), the second Monday in October (Columbus Day), the eleventh
      day of November (Veterans Day), the twenty-fifth day of December (Christmas Day) of
      each year, and all days appointed by the President of the United States or by the
      Governor as days of thanksgiving, are holidays, on which all the public offices of
      this Commonwealth may be closed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.233. Diffuse intrinsic Pontine Glioma Awareness Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.233. Diffuse intrinsic Pontine Glioma Awareness Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.233. Diffuse intrinsic Pontine Glioma Awareness Day (2023)
content:
(1)  May 17 of each year is designated as “Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma Awareness
      Day” throughout the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.145. Kentucky Harvest Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.145. Kentucky Harvest Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.145. Kentucky Harvest Day (2023)
content: November 15 is designated as “Kentucky Harvest Day.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.152. 9/11. First Responders Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.152. 9/11. First Responders Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.152. 9/11. First Responders Day (2023)
content:
(1)  The eleventh day of September each year shall be observed in Kentucky as “9/11
      First Responders Day.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.130. Mother's Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.130. Mother's Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.130. Mother's Day (2023)
content:
The Governor is authorized and requested to issue annually a proclamation calling
   upon the state officials to display the United States flag on all state and school
   buildings and the people of the state to display the flag at their homes, lodges,
   churches, and places of business and other suitable places, on the second Sunday in
   May, known as Mother's Day, as a public expression of love and reverence for the mothers
   of our state and other women serving it and as an inspiration for better homes and
   closer ties between the home and our Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.235. Mesothelioma Awareness Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.235. Mesothelioma Awareness Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.235. Mesothelioma Awareness Day (2023)
content:
(1)  September 26 of each year is designated “Mesothelioma Awareness Day” throughout
      the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.157. Kentucky Retired Veterans Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.157. Kentucky Retired Veterans Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.157. Kentucky Retired Veterans Day (2023)
content: July 1 of each year is designated as Kentucky Retired Veterans Day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.250. Garden week
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.250. Garden week
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.250. Garden week (2023)
content: The first week of June of each year is “Garden Week.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.245. Retired Teachers' Week
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.245. Retired Teachers' Week
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.245. Retired Teachers' Week (2023)
content:
The fourth week of May of each year is designated as Retired Teachers' Week.  The Governor may annually issue a proclamation designating the fourth week of May
   as Retired Teachers' Week and calling upon public schools and citizens of the state
   to observe the occasion and honor the retired teachers of the state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.227. Anti-Bullying Month
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.227. Anti-Bullying Month
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.227. Anti-Bullying Month (2023)
content:
(1)  The General Assembly recognizes its responsibility to secure the environment
      for all Kentucky students.  Thus, October of each year shall be designated as Anti-Bullying Month in the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.230. Native American Indian Month
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.230. Native American Indian Month
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.230. Native American Indian Month (2023)
content:
(1)  The month of November of each year shall be observed in Kentucky as “Native American
      Indian Month” and during this month schools, clubs, and civic and religious organizations
      are encouraged to recognize the contributions of Native American Indians with suitable
      ceremony and fellowship designed to promote greater understanding and brotherhood
      between Native American Indians and the non-Native American Indian people of the Commonwealth
      of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.225. State amphitheater
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.225. State amphitheater
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.225. State amphitheater (2023)
content:
The Iroquois Amphitheater, located in Iroquois Park in Louisville, Kentucky, is named
   and designated as the state amphitheater.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.220. Kentucky Commonwealth Theatre
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.220. Kentucky Commonwealth Theatre
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.220. Kentucky Commonwealth Theatre (2023)
content:
Devou Park Summer Classics Theatre of Covington shall be designated as the Kentucky
   Commonwealth Theatre.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.200. Declaration of day of mourning
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.200. Declaration of day of mourning
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.200. Declaration of day of mourning (2023)
content:
The Governor is authorized to declare a day of mourning in the Commonwealth of Kentucky
   on suitable and appropriate occasions.  Such declaration of a day of mourning shall in no way affect the operation of banks
   and trust companies, public schools, public offices, state agencies or any other segment
   of public or private endeavor in the state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.158. Korean War Armistice Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.158. Korean War Armistice Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.158. Korean War Armistice Day (2023)
content:
(1)  To recognize Armed Forces members who courageously served during the Korean War,
      July 27, the date of the military armistice agreement that ended the war, shall be
      observed in Kentucky as “Korean War Armistice Day.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.300. State silverware pattern
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.300. State silverware pattern
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.300. State silverware pattern (2023)
content:
Old Kentucky Blue Grass-The Georgetown Pattern is named and designated as the official
   state silverware pattern.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.210. Kentucky Shakespeare Festival
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.210. Kentucky Shakespeare Festival
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.210. Kentucky Shakespeare Festival (2023)
content:
Shakespeare in Central Park of Louisville, Kentucky, is hereby designated as the Kentucky
   Shakespeare Festival.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.237. Coal Miners Appreciation Week; Coal Truck Driver Appreciation Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.237. Coal Miners Appreciation Week; Coal Truck Driver Appreciation Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.237. Coal Miners Appreciation Week; Coal Truck Driver Appreciation Day (2023)
content:
The third week of August of each year shall be designated as Coal Miners Appreciation
   Week, and the Monday of the fourth week shall be designated as Coal Truck Driver Appreciation
   Day.  The Governor may annually issue a proclamation designating the third week of August
   as Coal Miners Appreciation Week and the Monday of the fourth week as Coal Truck Driver
   Appreciation Day, and calling upon coal mining businesses and all citizens of the
   Commonwealth to observe the occasion and honor the coal miners and coal truck drivers
   of the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.234. ALS Awareness Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.234. ALS Awareness Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.234. ALS Awareness Day (2023)
content:
(1)  February 21 of each year is designated as “ALS Awareness Day” throughout the
      Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.280. Official steam locomotive of Kentucky
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.280. Official steam locomotive of Kentucky
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.280. Official steam locomotive of Kentucky (2023)
content:
Steam locomotive #152, a 4-6-2 Light Pacific, formerly of the Louisville and Nashville
   Railroad and restored to operation by the volunteer members of the Kentucky Railway
   Museum, is named and designated as the official steam locomotive of the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.236. Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita Awareness Day
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.236. Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita Awareness Day
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.236. Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita Awareness Day (2023)
content:
The thirtieth day of June of each year is designated and shall be observed in Kentucky
   as “Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita Awareness Day.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.240. Organ Donor Awareness Week
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.240. Organ Donor Awareness Week
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.240. Organ Donor Awareness Week (2023)
content:
(1)  The fourth week of April of each year is designated as Organ Donor Awareness
      Week, and the Governor shall annually issue a proclamation inviting and urging the
      people of the Commonwealth to be involved with appropriate activities.  This observance is created to educate the citizens of the Commonwealth about the
      importance of organ donation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.255. “Commonwealth Cleanup” week; Environmental Education Month
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.255. “Commonwealth Cleanup” week; Environmental Education Month
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.255. “Commonwealth Cleanup” week; Environmental Education Month (2023)
content:
(1)  The fourth week of March each year shall be “Commonwealth Cleanup” week, culminating
      with a statewide cleanup day on the Saturday of that week.  This week shall provide an opportunity for Kentucky communities, in partnership
      with local, regional, and state entities, to clean and display the natural beauty
      of the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.400. State bourbon festival
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.400. State bourbon festival

content:
The Kentucky Bourbon Festival, Incorporated, of Bardstown, Kentucky, is named and

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.010. Consent of state to acquisition of lands
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.010. Consent of state to acquisition of lands
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.010. Consent of state to acquisition of lands (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth of Kentucky consents to the acquisition by the United States of all
   lands and appurtenances in this state, by condemnation, gift or purchase, which are
   needful to their constitutional purposes, but said acquisition shall not be deemed
   to result in a cession of jurisdiction by this Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.020. Jurisdiction retained for execution of process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.020. Jurisdiction retained for execution of process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.020. Jurisdiction retained for execution of process (2023)
content:
Kentucky retains jurisdiction for the execution of process, issued under its authority,
   over all lands in Kentucky heretofore or hereafter ceded to or acquired by the United
   States for the erection or establishment of post offices, custom houses, courthouses,
   locks, dams, canals, parks, cemeteries, or forest reserves.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.026. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Fayette County ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.026. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Fayette County ceded (2023)
content:
Kentucky cedes to the United States jurisdiction over the area embraced by the federal
   correctional institution at Fayette County.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.030. Jurisdiction over military post (Fort Knox) at West Point ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.030. Jurisdiction over military post (Fort Knox) at West Point ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.030. Jurisdiction over military post (Fort Knox) at West Point ceded (2023)
content:
Kentucky cedes to the United States all the rights and jurisdiction which she now
   possesses over the land and premises in the vicinity of West Point, Kentucky, conveyed
   or to be conveyed to the United States for the purpose of establishing a permanent
   camp of instruction and military post, so long as the same shall remain the property
   of the United States.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time›KY REV ST 2.990. Penalty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 2. Citizenship, Emblems, Holidays, and Time › KY REV ST 2.990. Penalty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 2.990. Penalty (2023)
content:
Any person violating any of the provisions ofKRS 2.060shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100) or imprisoned for not more
   than thirty (30) days, or both.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.028. Jurisdiction over federal correctional facilities in McCreary and Martin Counties ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.028. Jurisdiction over federal correctional facilities in McCreary and Martin Counties ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.028. Jurisdiction over federal correctional facilities in McCreary and Martin Counties ceded (2023)
content:
(1)  Kentucky cedes to the United States concurrent civil and criminal jurisdiction
      over all of the lands acquired by the United States in McCreary County and Martin
      County acquired for a United States penitentiary and ancillary correctional facilities,
      including lands now owned and adjacent lands that may be acquired by the United States
      in the future as part of said correctional facilities.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.027. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Manchester ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.027. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Manchester ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.027. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Manchester ceded (2023)
content:
Kentucky cedes to the United States concurrent civil and criminal jurisdiction over
   all of the land and premises acquired by the United States in Clay County constituting
   the federal correctional institution at Manchester.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.040. Jurisdiction of military park at Perryville ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.040. Jurisdiction of military park at Perryville ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.040. Jurisdiction of military park at Perryville ceded (2023)
content:
Kentucky cedes its jurisdiction to the United States over so much of any lands, not
   exceeding three thousand (3,000) acres, as may be selected in Boyle County, near Perryville,
   for the purpose of establishing, maintaining, beautifying and protecting a national
   military park at the battlefield of Perryville.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.025. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Ashland ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.025. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Ashland ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.025. Jurisdiction over federal correctional institution at Ashland ceded (2023)
content:
Kentucky cedes to the United States jurisdiction over the area embraced by the federal

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.090. General Assembly to be furnished request for cession of jurisdiction of land to United States
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.090. General Assembly to be furnished request for cession of jurisdiction of land to United States
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.090. General Assembly to be furnished request for cession of jurisdiction of land to United States (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided inKRS 3.255to3.275, whenever the United States, or any agency thereof, shall request the Commonwealth
   to cede jurisdiction over any area, it shall be the duty of the Governor to transmit
   such request to the next session of the General Assembly for such action as it may
   deem proper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.060. Zachary Taylor burial grounds ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.060. Zachary Taylor burial grounds ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.060. Zachary Taylor burial grounds ceded (2023)
content:
(1)  Kentucky cedes its jurisdiction to the United States over all that portion of
      the Zachary Taylor burial grounds and appurtenances in Jefferson County which were
      conveyed by Kentucky to the United States for national cemetery purposes, so long
      as the United States shall own the land.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.050. Perryville battlefield to be conveyed to the United States
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.050. Perryville battlefield to be conveyed to the United States
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.050. Perryville battlefield to be conveyed to the United States (2023)
content:
(1)  Whenever the United States Congress enacts a law authorizing the United States
      to take over the Perryville battlefield, now in the hands of the Division of Parks,
      the Governor shall appoint a commissioner who shall make and execute on behalf of
      Kentucky, a deed conveying fee simple title to the United States for national cemetery
      or park purposes, in conformity with the provisions of the Act of Congress when enacted,
      seventeen and three-fourths (17.75) acres of land, more or less, in Boyle County,
      Kentucky, now owned and held by the Commonwealth of Kentucky, together with all improvements
      thereon and appurtenances thereunto belonging.  The conveyance shall be made free of any cost or charge to the United States for
      the property conveyed.  The commissioner may ascertain by survey or otherwise the metes and bounds of the
      land conveyed and include in the deed an appropriate description of the land.  The deed shall contain a clause to the effect that, when the United States shall
      cease to use or maintain the land conveyed as a national cemetery or park, upon demand
      of the Governor of Kentucky, it shall revert to Kentucky, and complete jurisdiction
      over it shall be again vested in Kentucky.  The deed shall be in a form agreeable to the provisions of the Act of Congress,
      when enacted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.100. Letter accepting jurisdiction by United States to be entered upon executive journal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.100. Letter accepting jurisdiction by United States to be entered upon executive journal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.100. Letter accepting jurisdiction by United States to be entered upon executive journal (2023)
content:
Whenever the United States accepts the cession of jurisdiction over any area, the
   letter of acceptance shall be entered upon the executive journal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.070. Jurisdiction of land for Mammoth Cave National Park ceded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.070. Jurisdiction of land for Mammoth Cave National Park ceded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.070. Jurisdiction of land for Mammoth Cave National Park ceded (2023)
content:
(1)  The United States is authorized to acquire, pursuant to the provisions of this
      section, as well as in pursuance toKRS 148.111,148.121,148.141and148.151, the lands, including the caves and caverns underlying the same, within the area
      hereinafter referred to, as well as any lands contiguous or adjacent thereto which
      may hereafter be duly authorized for acquisition for national park purposes, for the
      purpose of converting same into, and for the establishment and maintenance thereon
      of, a national park as contemplated and provided for by the Act of Congress entitled
      “An Act to provide for the establishment of the Mammoth Cave National Park in the
      State of Kentucky, and for other purposes,” approved May 25, 1926 (44 Stat. 635),
      and any amendments thereto.  The lands, consisting of approximately 70,618 acres, are situated in the counties
      of Edmonson, Barren and Hart, in Kentucky.  The general boundaries thereof are set forth in the report of the Southern Appalachian
      National Park Commission to the Secretary of the Interior, under the date of April
      8, 1926.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.080. Consent to acquisition of national forest reserves; jurisdiction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.080. Consent to acquisition of national forest reserves; jurisdiction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.080. Consent to acquisition of national forest reserves; jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(1)  Kentucky consents to the acquisition by the United States, by purchase or gift,
      or by condemnation, of such lands within the boundaries of Kentucky as in the opinion
      of the United States are needed for the establishment of national forest reserves
      within prescribed areas.  Before such establishment the written approval and consent of the Governor of Kentucky,
      recorded in his office, shall be given as to the area of lands acquired by the United
      States.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth›Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire›KY REV ST 3.110. Consent to retrocession of jurisdiction by United States
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title I. Sovereignty and Jurisdiction of the Commonwealth › Chapter 3. Grants to United States of Lands and Rights to Acquire › KY REV ST 3.110. Consent to retrocession of jurisdiction by United States
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 3.110. Consent to retrocession of jurisdiction by United States (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided inKRS 3.255to3.275, the Commonwealth consents to any retrocession by the United States of lands within
   its geographical boundaries whenever the United States shall have ceased to exercise
   exclusive or special jurisdiction over such lands.  Inter alia, the conveyance of lands to private owners shall be deemed to constitute
   a retrocession of jurisdiction.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 5. Legislative Districts›Generalities›KY REV ST 5.031. Review and redrawing of precinct boundaries for legislative districts following 1996. Regular Session redistricting
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 5. Legislative Districts › Generalities › KY REV ST 5.031. Review and redrawing of precinct boundaries for legislative districts following 1996. Regular Session redistricting
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 5.031. Review and redrawing of precinct boundaries for legislative districts following 1996. Regular Session redistricting (2023)
content:
County boards of elections shall meet, immediately following January 11, 1996, for
   the purpose of reviewing the changes made to legislative district boundaries.  The county boards of elections shall redraw precinct boundaries so as to conform
   to state legislative district boundaries established by the General Assembly in its
   1996 Regular Session in order to minimize the number of split precincts.  Any redrawing of precinct boundaries required as a result of this redistricting
   shall be completed no later than forty-five (45) days after January 11, 1996, the
   provisions ofKRS 117.055(3)notwithstanding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.080. Disobedient witnesses; attempt to corrupt legislator; penalty; enforcement by Attorney General
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.080. Disobedient witnesses; attempt to corrupt legislator; penalty; enforcement by Attorney General
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.080. Disobedient witnesses; attempt to corrupt legislator; penalty; enforcement by Attorney General (2023)
content:
Any person who, after being lawfully summoned by the General Assembly, either house
   or a committee of either, refuses to attend as a witness, or bring any paper proper
   to be used as evidence or who, being present, refuses to testify concerning any matter
   which may be a proper subject of inquiry, and any person who offers or gives a bribe
   to a member of the General Assembly, or attempts, by other corrupt means, to influence
   a member to cast or withhold his vote, shall, on conviction as provided byKRS 6.090to6.131, be fined not more than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) or imprisoned in the county
   jail any time during the then current session of the General Assembly, or both.  The Attorney General, upon request of any committee of the General Assembly or a
   co-chair of the Commission, shall enforce this section in the county of residence
   of the accused person or in Franklin County underKRS 15.210.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.072. Witnesses before General Assembly; privileges and compensation; oath
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.072. Witnesses before General Assembly; privileges and compensation; oath
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.072. Witnesses before General Assembly; privileges and compensation; oath (2023)
content:
(1)  Witnesses attending the General Assembly, either house or a legislative committee
      are entitled to the same privileges and immunities, and the same compensation, as
      witnesses in other cases.  When summoned by the Commonwealth, they shall be paid out of the State Treasury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.131. Resolutions and orders; how enforced
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.131. Resolutions and orders; how enforced
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.131. Resolutions and orders; how enforced (2023)
content:
Resolutions of imprisonment and orders of either house shall be executed by the sergeant-at-arms
   of that house, or by any sheriff to whom the order is directed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.150. Officers and employees; number elected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.150. Officers and employees; number elected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.150. Officers and employees; number elected (2023)
content:
At the beginning of each regular session of the General Assembly, each house shall
   elect one (1) chief clerk, one (1) assistant clerk, one (1) enrolling clerk, one (1)
   sergeant-at-arms, one (1) doorkeeper and one (1) janitor;  the Senate shall elect
   one (1) cloakroom keeper and three (3) pages and the House of Representatives shall
   elect two (2) cloakroom keepers and four (4) pages.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.130. Collection of fine
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.130. Collection of fine
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.130. Collection of fine (2023)
content:
If a fine is imposed underKRS 6.080, it may be collected by action in the Franklin Circuit Court by the Attorney General,
   in the name of the Commonwealth, and the proceedings shall be the same as in civil
   cases instituted by the Commonwealth for the collection of debt.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 5. Legislative Districts›Representative Districts›KY REV ST 5.300. One Hundredth Representative District
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 5. Legislative Districts › Representative Districts › KY REV ST 5.300. One Hundredth Representative District
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 5.300. One Hundredth Representative District (2023)
content: The One Hundredth Representative District shall consist of the following territory:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.162. Expenses of preparing journals; how paid
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.162. Expenses of preparing journals; how paid
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.162. Expenses of preparing journals; how paid (2023)
content:
The expenses of preparing, indexing, and editing the journals of the General Assembly
   shall be paid from the appropriation for legislative journals and acts upon requisition
   of the co-chairmen of the Legislative Research Commission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Apportionment›KY REV ST 6.020. New counties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Apportionment › KY REV ST 6.020. New counties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.020. New counties (2023)
content:
Any new county created before the next apportionment of representation shall, for
   the purpose of representation, be considered as part of the district from which the
   greater part of its territory was taken.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 5. Legislative Districts›Representative Districts›KY REV ST 5.299. Ninety-ninth Representative District
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 5. Legislative Districts › Representative Districts › KY REV ST 5.299. Ninety-ninth Representative District
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 5.299. Ninety-ninth Representative District (2023)
content: The Ninety-ninth Representative District shall consist of the following territory:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.071. Collection and disposition of fines imposed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.071. Collection and disposition of fines imposed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.071. Collection and disposition of fines imposed (2023)
content:
All fines imposed underKRS 6.050or6.070shall be collected by the sheriff of the county where the offender or his estate
   is found, under the mandate of the house imposing the fine, signed by its presiding
   officer and shall be paid into the State Treasury by the sheriff, and accounted for
   as other public moneys collected by him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.090. Charge; what to contain
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.090. Charge; what to contain
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.090. Charge; what to contain (2023)
content:
Any member of the General Assembly may make the charge against the offender in writing,
   and shall specify the offense in ordinary and concise language, and in such manner
   as to enable a person of common understanding to know what is intended, and with such
   degree of certainty as to enable the General Assembly, or either house, to pronounce
   judgment on the charge.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.070. Contempt or breach of privilege, punishment for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.070. Contempt or breach of privilege, punishment for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.070. Contempt or breach of privilege, punishment for (2023)
content:
Either house of the General Assembly may punish anyone by fine not exceeding five
   hundred dollars ($500) or by imprisonment not exceeding six (6) months, or both, for
   a breach of privilege, or for any contempt except the offenses described inKRS 6.080, which shall be punished as provided inKRS 6.080to6.131.  Contempts and breaches of privilege shall be inquired into first by a special committee,
   before which the accused shall have the right to be heard by himself and counsel,
   and have compulsory process to procure the attendance of his witnesses.  The committee shall report all matters of fact specially, with its opinion, for
   the final action of the house.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.050. Privilege from arrest or civil suit; censure; fine or expulsion
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.050. Privilege from arrest or civil suit; censure; fine or expulsion
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.050. Privilege from arrest or civil suit; censure; fine or expulsion (2023)
content:
(1)  A member of the General Assembly, while going to, attending or returning from
      any session of the house to which he belongs shall not be arrested, menaced or disturbed
      at any place in the Commonwealth of Kentucky except on legal process for treason,
      felony, or breach or surety of the peace.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.145. Resignation of member
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.145. Resignation of member
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.145. Resignation of member (2023)
content:
A member of the General Assembly who desires to resign his office shall submit a letter
   of resignation to the officer required to issue a writ of special election to fill
   such vacancy, pursuant toKRS 118.730.  Upon receiving such letter of resignation such officer immediately shall notify
   the director of the Legislative Research Commission of the fact of such resignation
   and its effective date.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.100. Procedure on charge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.100. Procedure on charge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.100. Procedure on charge (2023)
content:
If the offense was against the General Assembly, or a joint committee, the house in
   which the charge is filed may adopt a resolution providing for an investigation.  If the resolution is concurred in by the other house, the President of the Senate
   shall appoint two (2) of its members and the Speaker of the House three (3) of its
   members, who shall constitute a joint committee of investigation.  If the offense was against the house in which the charge is filed or one (1) of
   its committees, the President or Speaker shall appoint five (5) of its members as
   a committee of investigation.  The committee of investigation shall select one (1) of its number chairman, who
   may summon and swear witnesses and require the production of papers to be used as
   evidence.  The committee shall summon the accused to appear before it and answer the charge,
   and, after reasonable notice to him of the time and place of trial, shall hear testimony,
   and cause the testimony or its substance to be reduced to writing, and report its
   conclusions, with the testimony taken and its recommendations, to the house in which
   the charge is pending, or to the Senate if the committee is a joint committee.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses›KY REV ST 6.110. Judgment on report of committee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Privileges and Discipline; Witnesses › KY REV ST 6.110. Judgment on report of committee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.110. Judgment on report of committee (2023)
content:
(1)  On the report of a joint committee, the Senate shall, by resolution, fix the
      penalty or discharge the accused, as the testimony authorizes.  If the accused is found guilty and the resolution is concurred in by the House,
      he shall be punished accordingly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.212. Payment of allowances authorized by KRS § 6.211
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.212. Payment of allowances authorized by KRS § 6.211
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.212. Payment of allowances authorized by KRS § 6.211 (2023)
content:
The secretary of the Finance and Administration Cabinet shall, on the first and fifteenth
   day of each month, during the time the General Assembly is in regular or extraordinary
   session, draw his warrant on the Treasurer in favor of each member of the General
   Assembly for the sums set forth inKRS 6.211.  These sums shall be paid from the general fund.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.180. Employees to attend sessions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.180. Employees to attend sessions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.180. Employees to attend sessions (2023)
content:
Each employee of the General Assembly shall attend the daily sessions of the house
   by which he is employed and shall not be absent from the seat of government during
   the session of the General Assembly without a leave of absence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.237. Group life and group hospitalization insurance for members of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.237. Group life and group hospitalization insurance for members of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.237. Group life and group hospitalization insurance for members of General Assembly (2023)
content:
(1)  The secretary of the Finance and Administration Cabinet, upon the recommendation
      of the director of the Legislative Research Commission shall procure from one (1)
      or more life insurance companies, and from one (1) or more hospitalization insurance
      companies, authorized to do business in this state, a policy or policies of group
      life insurance insuring the lives of all members of the General Assembly and shall
      procure a policy or policies of group hospitalization insurance covering all members
      of the General Assembly.  The policy or policies shall be approved by the commissioner of the Department of
      Insurance and may contain such provisions as he approves whether or not otherwise
      permitted by the insurance laws.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Form of Acts›KY REV ST 6.240. Date of approval or passage to be stated at end of act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Form of Acts › KY REV ST 6.240. Date of approval or passage to be stated at end of act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.240. Date of approval or passage to be stated at end of act (2023)
content:
The date of the approval of an act by the Governor, or the day it passes against his
   objections, shall be stated at the end of the act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.160. Duties of chief clerk, assistant clerk and enrolling clerk of each house
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.160. Duties of chief clerk, assistant clerk and enrolling clerk of each house
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.160. Duties of chief clerk, assistant clerk and enrolling clerk of each house (2023)
content:
(1)  The chief clerk of each house shall file and preserve in the office of his house
      a correct copy of the journal of its proceedings.  At the close of each session of the General Assembly, he shall make an inventory
      of all the books, stationery and furniture belonging to his house, box up all the
      books, and deliver the books, stationery and furniture to the co-chairmen of the Legislative
      Research Commission and take a receipt for them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.161. Journals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.161. Journals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.161. Journals (2023)
content:
The chief clerk of each house shall furnish a correct journal of its proceedings for
   each day to the Legislative Research Commission as soon as the journal is approved
   by the house.  The Legislative Research Commission shall carefully compare or have compared the
   proofs of the journals.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.170. Duties of sergeant-at-arms, doorkeeper, janitor, cloakroom keeper and pages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.170. Duties of sergeant-at-arms, doorkeeper, janitor, cloakroom keeper and pages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.170. Duties of sergeant-at-arms, doorkeeper, janitor, cloakroom keeper and pages (2023)
content:
(1)  The sergeant-at-arms shall direct and superintend the pages and the delivery
      of the mail, and perform the duties of the doorkeeper in his absence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.185. Funds appropriated for legislative sessions; payment of compensation of members and employees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.185. Funds appropriated for legislative sessions; payment of compensation of members and employees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.185. Funds appropriated for legislative sessions; payment of compensation of members and employees (2023)
content:
All funds appropriated for legislative sessions shall be placed in a legislative session
   fund.  All compensation of members and employees and all contingent expenses of the General
   Assembly shall be paid from this fund on vouchers approved by the co-chairmen of the
   Legislative Research Commission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.210. Certification for payment of compensation and travel allowance of members of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.210. Certification for payment of compensation and travel allowance of members of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.210. Certification for payment of compensation and travel allowance of members of General Assembly (2023)
content:
The compensation and travel allowance of the President of the Senate, Speaker of the
   House of Representatives, and members of both houses of the General Assembly shall
   be paid on the certificate of the co-chairmen of the Legislative Research Commission
   of the amount due.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.213. Interim expense allowances for members
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.213. Interim expense allowances for members
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.213. Interim expense allowances for members (2023)
content:
(1)  In addition to the per diem and all allowances provided by law to members of
      the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, each member of the Legislature
      is hereby granted an expense allowance of nine hundred fifty dollars ($950) per month
      for secretarial assistance, books and periodicals, other reports or publications,
      conduct of small-scale studies related to governmental activity, postage, telephone
      service, or any other expense incident to performance of the legislator's duties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.190. Compensation; travel expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.190. Compensation; travel expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.190. Compensation; travel expenses (2023)
content:
Beginning as of January 1, 1984, the members of the General Assembly, other than the
   Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President of the Senate, the Speaker
   Pro Tempore of the House of Representatives, President Pro Tempore of the Senate,
   and the majority and minority leadership of each house of the General Assembly, shall
   each receive as compensation one hundred dollars ($100) per day, the President of
   the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives shall each receive as compensation
   one hundred twenty-five dollars ($125) per day, the majority and minority floor leaders
   of each house of the General Assembly shall each receive as compensation one hundred
   twenty dollars ($120) per day, and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate, the Speaker
   Pro Tempore, and the majority and minority caucus chairmen and whips of each house
   of the General Assembly shall each receive as compensation one hundred fifteen dollars
   ($115) per day, during the session of the General Assembly.  In addition to his compensation as a member of the General Assembly, each chairman
   of a standing committee of the House of Representatives or the Senate shall receive
   compensation of ten dollars ($10) for each regularly scheduled meeting of the standing
   committee which he chairs during sessions of the General Assembly.  Beginning as of July 1, 1980, each member of the General Assembly shall receive
   mileage and reimbursement of road tolls for one (1) round trip for each week of the
   session between his home and the State Capitol during regular sessions and extraordinary
   sessions of the General Assembly and the necessary travel in going to and returning
   from the sessions of their respective houses.  The mileage allowance under this section shall be equal to the maximum mileage allowance
   permitted by the federal government, to be increased as federal mileage allowance
   is increased.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.220. Allowance in lieu of stationery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.220. Allowance in lieu of stationery
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.220. Allowance in lieu of stationery (2023)
content:
In lieu of stationery, there shall be allowed to each member of the General Assembly
   the sum of fifty dollars ($50).  This allowance shall be paid out of the State Treasury at the beginning of the session.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.211. Additional allowances for members of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.211. Additional allowances for members of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.211. Additional allowances for members of General Assembly (2023)
content:
Effective January 1, 1994, in addition to any and all sums, compensation, or expenses
   now paid the members of the General Assembly, each shall receive an expense allowance
   of one hundred ten percent (110%) of the expense allowance paid federal employees
   traveling in the Frankfort, Kentucky area for each calendar day.  This sum shall be paid whether the General Assembly is in regular or extraordinary
   session and shall be in full recompense of any additional expenses incurred in excess
   of that now received by them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.230. Compensation of employees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.230. Compensation of employees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.230. Compensation of employees (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Members, Officers, and Employees›KY REV ST 6.225. Offices for President of Senate and Speaker of House of Representatives; interim per diem and expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Members, Officers, and Employees › KY REV ST 6.225. Offices for President of Senate and Speaker of House of Representatives; interim per diem and expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.225. Offices for President of Senate and Speaker of House of Representatives; interim per diem and expenses (2023)
content:
Between sessions of the General Assembly offices shall be maintained in the State
   Capitol building for the use and benefit of the President of the Senate and the Speaker
   of the House of Representatives.  Except when the General Assembly is in session the President of the Senate and the
   Speaker of the House of Representatives shall each receive an amount per day equal
   to the per diem compensation they receive during sessions of the General Assembly
   for each day they are engaged in the duties of their offices and shall be reimbursed
   for necessary traveling expenses.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Filing of Bills›KY REV ST 6.247. Bill request files
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Filing of Bills › KY REV ST 6.247. Bill request files
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.247. Bill request files (2023)
content:
The Legislative Research Commission shall maintain separate bill request files as
   follows:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Display of Motto›KY REV ST 6.330. “In God We Trust” to be displayed above dais of Speaker of the House of Representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Display of Motto › KY REV ST 6.330. “In God We Trust” to be displayed above dais of Speaker of the House of Representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.330. “In God We Trust” to be displayed above dais of Speaker of the House of Representatives (2023)
content:
In commemoration of the fiftieth anniversary of the resolution which passed through
   the 84th United States Congress and subsequently was signed by President Dwight D.
   Eisenhower on July 30, 1956, thereby making “In God We Trust” the national motto of
   the United States, the General Assembly hereby directs the Legislative Research Commission
   to display the national motto “In God We Trust” on the wall directly above and behind
   the dais of the Speaker of the Kentucky House of Representatives.  The display shall be consistent with the historic and patriotic display of the national
   motto located directly above and behind the dais of the Speaker of the United States
   House of Representatives.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Legislators' Retirement Plan›KY REV ST 6.500. Legislators' Retirement Plan; creation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Legislators' Retirement Plan › KY REV ST 6.500. Legislators' Retirement Plan; creation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.500. Legislators' Retirement Plan; creation (2023)
content:
There hereby is created a retirement plan for the members of the General Assembly
   (hereinafter “legislators”). Each legislator in office on July 1, 1980, and each legislator thereafter taking
   office, may acquire membership in the plan in accordance with the provisions ofKRS 6.505.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Filing of Bills›KY REV ST 6.248. Authorization of joint primary and cosponsorship of similar bills in opposite chambers; petition; approval; withdrawal; forms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Filing of Bills › KY REV ST 6.248. Authorization of joint primary and cosponsorship of similar bills in opposite chambers; petition; approval; withdrawal; forms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.248. Authorization of joint primary and cosponsorship of similar bills in opposite chambers; petition; approval; withdrawal; forms (2023)
content:
(1)  If a bill is introduced in the Senate or the House of Representatives, and a
      substantially similar bill is introduced in the opposite chamber, the primary sponsors
      of each of the bills may jointly petition the Committee on Committees in each chamber
      to authorize joint primary and cosponsorship by members of both chambers of one or
      both bills.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Actuarial Analysis›KY REV ST 6.350. Actuarial analysis required for bill before General Assembly to increase benefits or participation in state-administered retirement system
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Actuarial Analysis › KY REV ST 6.350. Actuarial analysis required for bill before General Assembly to increase benefits or participation in state-administered retirement system
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.350. Actuarial analysis required for bill before General Assembly to increase benefits or participation in state-administered retirement system (2023)
content:
(1)  A bill which would increase or decrease the benefits or increase or decrease
      participation in the benefits or change the actuarial accrued liability of any state-administered
      retirement system shall not be reported from a legislative committee of either house
      of the General Assembly for consideration by the full membership of that house unless
      the bill is accompanied by an actuarial analysis.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Security›KY REV ST 6.420. Department of Kentucky State Police to provide certified officers to protect property, facilities, and meetings of General Assembly and Legislative Research Commission; briefings on security matters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Security › KY REV ST 6.420. Department of Kentucky State Police to provide certified officers to protect property, facilities, and meetings of General Assembly and Legislative Research Commission; briefings on security matters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.420. Department of Kentucky State Police to provide certified officers to protect property, facilities, and meetings of General Assembly and Legislative Research Commission; briefings on security matters (2023)
content:
The Department of Kentucky State Police shall provide certified officers for the protection
   of the property, facilities, and the meetings of the General Assembly and the Legislative
   Research Commission, including off-site protection, both during and between sessions
   of the General Assembly, and shall render such additional security services as may
   be required by the co-chairmen of the Legislative Research Commission.  Notwithstanding any other law to the contrary, the Department of Kentucky State
   Police shall brief the leadership of the General Assembly and the Legislative Research
   Commission on security matters relating to the Capitol campus when requested to do
   so.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title II. Legislative Branch›Chapter 6. The General Assembly›Legislators' Retirement Plan›KY REV ST 6.520. Retirement benefits for members who began participating before January 1, § 2014
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title II. Legislative Branch › Chapter 6. The General Assembly › Legislators' Retirement Plan › KY REV ST 6.520. Retirement benefits for members who began participating before January 1, § 2014
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 6.520. Retirement benefits for members who began participating before January 1, § 2014 (2023)
content:
(1)  A member of the Legislators' Retirement Plan who retires on or after his or her
      normal retirement date shall receive a service retirement allowance, payable monthly
      during his or her lifetime, in an amount per month equal to three and fifty one-hundredths
      percent (3.50%) of his or her final compensation multiplied by the number of years
      of his or her service, but in no event to exceed one hundred percent (100%) of final
      compensation.  For this purpose, “final compensation” means the average monthly creditable compensation as determined inKRS 61.510(13)of the member for services as a legislator for the three (3) years during which the
      member had the highest creditable legislative compensation.
