citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-010. Authority to transact business required; certificate of authority required for award of state contract; exception for foreign insurer (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity shall not transact business in this Commonwealth until it obtains
      a certificate of authority from the Secretary of State.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-060. Withdrawal of foreign entity
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-060. Withdrawal of foreign entity
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-060. Withdrawal of foreign entity (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity authorized to transact business in this Commonwealth shall not
      withdraw from this Commonwealth until there has been filed with the Secretary of State
      a certificate of withdrawal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-020. Consequences of transacting business without authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-020. Consequences of transacting business without authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-020. Consequences of transacting business without authority (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity transacting business in this Commonwealth without a certificate
      of authority may not maintain a proceeding in any court in this Commonwealth until
      it obtains a certificate of authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-070. Grounds for revocation

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-050. Effect of certificate of authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-050. Effect of certificate of authority

content:
(1)  A certificate of authority shall authorize the foreign entity to which it is
      issued the authority to transact business in this Commonwealth subject, however, to
      the right of the Commonwealth to revoke the certificate as provided in this chapter.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-030. Application for certificate of authority (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity may apply for a certificate of authority to transact business

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-040. Amended certificate of authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-040. Amended certificate of authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-040. Amended certificate of authority (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity authorized to transact business in this Commonwealth shall obtain
      an amended certificate of authority from the Secretary of State if it changes any
      information required byKRS 14A.9-030(1).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-090. Appeal from revocation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-090. Appeal from revocation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-090. Appeal from revocation (2023)
content:
(1)  A foreign entity may appeal the Secretary of State's revocation of its certificate
      of authority to the Franklin Circuit Court within thirty (30) days after service of
      the certificate of revocation.  The foreign entity may appeal by petitioning the court to set aside the revocation
      and attaching to the petition copies of its certificate of authority and the Secretary
      of State's certificate of revocation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act›Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities›KY REV ST 14A.9-080. Procedure for an effective revocation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 14A. Kentucky Business Entity Filing Act › Subchapter 9. Foreign Business Entities › KY REV ST 14A.9-080. Procedure for an effective revocation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 14A.9-080. Procedure for an effective revocation (2023)
content:
(1)  If the Secretary of State determines that one (1) or more grounds exist underKRS 14A.9-070for revocation of a certificate of authority, the foreign entity shall be served
      with written notice of that determination by mailing the notice by first-class mail
      to the foreign entity at its principal place of business address.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.015. Practice of law prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.015. Practice of law prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.015. Practice of law prohibited (2023)
content:
The Attorney General shall not engage in the private practice of law during his term
   of office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.010. Department of Law; Attorney General as head; major organizational units (Effective March 15, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.010. Department of Law; Attorney General as head; major organizational units (Effective March 15, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.010. Department of Law; Attorney General as head; major organizational units (Effective March 15, 2024) (2023)
content: (1)  The Attorney General is the head of the Department of Law.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.025. Conditions to furnishing opinions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.025. Conditions to furnishing opinions (2023)
content: The Attorney General, when requested in writing, underKRS 15.020, shall furnish such opinions subject to the following conditions:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.020. Chief law officer and adviser; duty to attend to litigation, write opinions, draft writings; communication with Legislative Research Commission; when to appear for Commonwealth; constitutional challenge may be brought in any county
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.020. Chief law officer and adviser; duty to attend to litigation, write opinions, draft writings; communication with Legislative Research Commission; when to appear for Commonwealth; constitutional challenge may be brought in any county
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.020. Chief law officer and adviser; duty to attend to litigation, write opinions, draft writings; communication with Legislative Research Commission; when to appear for Commonwealth; constitutional challenge may be brought in any county (2023)
content:
(1)  The Attorney General is the chief law officer of the Commonwealth of Kentucky
      and all of its departments, commissions, agencies, and political subdivisions, and
      the legal adviser of all state officers, departments, commissions, and agencies, and
      when requested in writing shall furnish to them his or her written opinion touching
      any of their official duties, and shall prepare proper drafts of all instruments of
      writing required for public use, and shall exercise all common law duties and authority
      pertaining to the office of the Attorney General under the common law, except when
      modified by statutory enactment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.055. Publication of list of delinquent child support obligors; distribution of “most wanted” posters (Effective until July 1, 2025)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.055. Publication of list of delinquent child support obligors; distribution of “most wanted” posters (Effective until July 1, 2025)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.055. Publication of list of delinquent child support obligors; distribution of “most wanted” posters (Effective until July 1, 2025) (2023)
content:
(1)  The Office of the Attorney General shall receive from the Cabinet for Health
      and Family Services a list of names of delinquent obligors as defined in administrative
      regulations promulgated under this section.

content: The Attorney General may:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.070. Index book of cases; opinions to be kept on file
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.070. Index book of cases; opinions to be kept on file
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.070. Index book of cases; opinions to be kept on file (2023)
content:
(1)  The Attorney General shall keep in his office an index book, in which shall be
      entered the number and style of each case in which the Commonwealth is interested
      and the court in which it is pending, and a brief statement of the nature of the case
      and the steps taken therein.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.080. Biennial report to Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.080. Biennial report to Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.080. Biennial report to Governor (2023)
content:
The Attorney General shall biennially, on or before December 31 preceding each regular
   session of the General Assembly, report to the Governor a full statement of the business
   done in his office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.170. Expenses of Attorney General and assistants when away from capital
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.170. Expenses of Attorney General and assistants when away from capital
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.170. Expenses of Attorney General and assistants when away from capital (2023)
content:
The Attorney General and the assistant attorneys general shall be paid their actual
   and necessary expenses when called away from the state capital on business of the
   Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.100. Deputy attorney general, solicitor general, assistant deputy attorneys general, assistants, special attorneys and contract attorneys
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.100. Deputy attorney general, solicitor general, assistant deputy attorneys general, assistants, special attorneys and contract attorneys
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.100. Deputy attorney general, solicitor general, assistant deputy attorneys general, assistants, special attorneys and contract attorneys (2023)
content:
(1)  The Attorney General shall appoint a deputy attorney general, who shall have
      the same qualifications required of a Circuit Judge except for residence in a district
      and who shall receive the same salary as a Circuit Judge, to serve at the pleasure
      of the Attorney General and to perform the duties he or she may designate.  The Attorney General may appoint two (2) assistant deputy attorneys general, who
      shall have the same qualifications required of a District Judge except for residence
      in a district and who shall receive the same salary as a District Judge, to serve
      at the pleasure of the Attorney General and to perform the duties he or she may designate.  In addition thereto, he or she shall appoint a solicitor general to serve at the
      pleasure of the Attorney General and to perform the duties he or she may designate
      and shall set his or her salary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.090. Appeals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.090. Appeals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.090. Appeals (2023)
content:
The Attorney General may prosecute an appeal, without security, in any case from which
   an appeal will lie whenever, in his judgment, the interest of the Commonwealth demands
   it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.113. Attorney General may investigate certain illegal or fraudulent activity; prevention of identity theft
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.113. Attorney General may investigate certain illegal or fraudulent activity; prevention of identity theft
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.113. Attorney General may investigate certain illegal or fraudulent activity; prevention of identity theft (2023)
content:
(1)  The Attorney General may investigate the use of personal identification and financial
      information by persons for the purpose of theft, fraud, or both, or any other illegal
      or fraudulent activity that may involve electronic commerce, the use of public funds
      or property, or obtaining or attempting to obtain a benefit provided by the government.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.015. Deputy secretaries of justice and public safety
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.015. Deputy secretaries of justice and public safety
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.015. Deputy secretaries of justice and public safety (2023)
content:
Deputy secretaries of justice and public safety shall be appointed by and directly
   responsible to the secretary and shall be the principal assistants and advisors to
   the secretary for all policies, programs and operations of the cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.020. Organization of Justice and Public Safety Cabinet
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.020. Organization of Justice and Public Safety Cabinet
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.020. Organization of Justice and Public Safety Cabinet (2023)
content: (1)  The Justice and Public Safety Cabinet shall have the following departments:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.105. Assistant attorneys general for certain agencies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.105. Assistant attorneys general for certain agencies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.105. Assistant attorneys general for certain agencies (2023)
content:
(1)  The Attorney General, with the approval of the head of the cabinet involved,
      shall appoint assistant attorneys general for the Transportation Cabinet and the Finance
      and Administration Cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.150. Stenographic, investigative and clerical help
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.150. Stenographic, investigative and clerical help
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.150. Stenographic, investigative and clerical help (2023)
content:
The Attorney General may employ such stenographic, investigative and other clerical
   help for the use and benefit of his department as he deems necessary for the proper
   conduct of his office, within the limits of appropriations made for that purpose.  Investigative personnel as designated by the Attorney General shall have the power
   of peace officers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.180. Power to promulgate regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.180. Power to promulgate regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.180. Power to promulgate regulations (2023)
content:
The Attorney General may promulgate and file with the Legislative Research Commission
   those rules and regulations which will facilitate performing the duties and exercising
   the authority vested in the Attorney General and the Department of Law by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.030. Additional organizational units in cabinet
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.030. Additional organizational units in cabinet

content:
(1)  The Justice and Public Safety Cabinet, in addition to the departments, divisions,
      offices, and branches set forth inKRS 15A.020, shall consist of the following organizational units:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.011. Definitions for chapter

content: As used in this chapter, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15. Department of Law›KY REV ST 15.111. Division of Administrative Hearings (Effective July 1, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15. Department of Law › KY REV ST 15.111. Division of Administrative Hearings (Effective July 1, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15.111. Division of Administrative Hearings (Effective July 1, 2024) (2023)
content:
(1)  The Division of Administrative Hearings is created in the Office of Attorney
      General.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.040. Office of the Secretary; duties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.040. Office of the Secretary; duties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.040. Office of the Secretary; duties (2023)
content:
The Office of the Secretary of the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet shall advise
   and recommend to the secretary of the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet, the Governor,
   and the General Assembly policies and direction for long-range planning regarding
   all elements of the criminal justice system.  The office shall also:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.061. Juvenile justice data tracking system; interdepartmental collaboration for analysis of juvenile recidivism
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.061. Juvenile justice data tracking system; interdepartmental collaboration for analysis of juvenile recidivism
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.061. Juvenile justice data tracking system; interdepartmental collaboration for analysis of juvenile recidivism (2023)
content:
(1)  The cabinet shall maintain a comprehensive, centralized data tracking system
      for the Department of Juvenile Justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.060. Office of Secretary to serve as state planning agency for federal Crime Control and Safe Streets Act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.060. Office of Secretary to serve as state planning agency for federal Crime Control and Safe Streets Act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.060. Office of Secretary to serve as state planning agency for federal Crime Control and Safe Streets Act (2023)
content:
The Office of Secretary of Justice and Public Safety shall serve as the state planning
   agency for purposes of compliance with the federal Crime Control and Safe Streets
   Act of 1968, as amended1, or subsequently adopted federal criminal justice legislation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.063. Juvenile Justice Oversight Council; purpose; membership; duties; attachment to Legislative Research Commission
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.063. Juvenile Justice Oversight Council; purpose; membership; duties; attachment to Legislative Research Commission
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.063. Juvenile Justice Oversight Council; purpose; membership; duties; attachment to Legislative Research Commission (2023)
content:
(1)  The Juvenile Justice Oversight Council is created for the purpose of providing
      independent review of the state juvenile justice system and providing recommendations
      to the General Assembly.  The council shall actively review the implementation of all juvenile justice reforms
      enacted by the General Assembly, collect and review performance measurement data,
      and continue to review the juvenile justice system for changes that improve public
      safety, hold youth accountable, provide better outcomes for children and families,
      and control juvenile justice costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.065. Department of Juvenile Justice; powers and duties; advisory board
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.065. Department of Juvenile Justice; powers and duties; advisory board

content:
(1)  The Department of Juvenile Justice shall be headed by a commissioner and shall
      develop and administer programs for:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.062. Fiscal incentive program for local efforts to enhance public safety and reduce juvenile justice system costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.062. Fiscal incentive program for local efforts to enhance public safety and reduce juvenile justice system costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.062. Fiscal incentive program for local efforts to enhance public safety and reduce juvenile justice system costs (2023)
content:
(1)  It is the intent of the Commonwealth to maintain public safety and achieve savings
      through the use of evidence-based treatment programs and practices at the local level
      and to reinvest a portion of the savings achieved into community-based programs and
      services.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.067. Division of Program Services; access to educational records; screening and education of incarcerated youth; information on educational status and need
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.067. Division of Program Services; access to educational records; screening and education of incarcerated youth; information on educational status and need
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.067. Division of Program Services; access to educational records; screening and education of incarcerated youth; information on educational status and need (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “facility” means any of the facilities specified inKRS 15A.200operated by a political subdivision of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and juvenile
      detention facilities operated by the Commonwealth of Kentucky for the care of juveniles
      alleged to be delinquent or adjudicated delinquent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.0652. Juvenile justice administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.0652. Juvenile justice administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.0652. Juvenile justice administrative regulations (2023)
content:
The Department of Juvenile Justice shall promulgate administrative regulations that
   shall include:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.0651. Access to juvenile facility records; when permitted; appeal of denial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.0651. Access to juvenile facility records; when permitted; appeal of denial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.0651. Access to juvenile facility records; when permitted; appeal of denial (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “juvenile facility” means any facility wherein a juvenile or other person under the authority of the
      Department of Juvenile Justice is confined.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.0653. Liability insurance for health care professionals employed by or serving department; authority of commissioner to purchase
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.0653. Liability insurance for health care professionals employed by or serving department; authority of commissioner to purchase
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.0653. Liability insurance for health care professionals employed by or serving department; authority of commissioner to purchase (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner of the Department of Juvenile Justice may, with the approval
      of the Finance and Administration Cabinet, purchase liability insurance for the protection
      of health care professionals employed by or serving the department to protect them
      from liability for acts and claims of medical and professional malpractice arising
      in the course and scope of their employment or service to the department.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.0654. Earmarking of juvenile justice funding for evidence-based practices
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.0654. Earmarking of juvenile justice funding for evidence-based practices
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.0654. Earmarking of juvenile justice funding for evidence-based practices (2023)
content:
(1)  Beginning July 1, 2016, fifty percent (50%) of state moneys expended by the department
      on programs shall be for programs that are in accordance with evidence-based practices.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.068. Duties of department if child may be victim of human trafficking; administrative regulations

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.066. Department of Juvenile Justice employee not required to give personal attendance in out-of-county civil suit; exception for necessary witness
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.066. Department of Juvenile Justice employee not required to give personal attendance in out-of-county civil suit; exception for necessary witness
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.066. Department of Juvenile Justice employee not required to give personal attendance in out-of-county civil suit; exception for necessary witness (2023)
content:
No employee of the Department of Juvenile Justice shall be required to give personal
   attendance as a witness in any civil suit arising out of or related to his or her
   employment, out of the county of that employee's assigned work station, but his or
   her deposition shall be taken in lieu thereof;  however, if the court in which the
   civil action is pending finds that the witness is a necessary witness for trial, that
   court may order the personal attendance of the witness at trial.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.090. Internal organization
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.090. Internal organization (2023)
content:
The secretary shall establish the internal organization of the cabinet not otherwise
   established by the Governor or the General Assembly and shall organize the cabinet
   into such organizational units as the secretary deems necessary to perform the functions,
   powers, and duties of the cabinet, subject to the provisions of KRS Chapter 12.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.150. Administering of programs and grants
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.150. Administering of programs and grants
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.150. Administering of programs and grants (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by law, the cabinet shall administer all state programs
   and all state and federally funded grant programs related to criminal justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.080. Interrelationship of offices for administrative purposes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.080. Interrelationship of offices for administrative purposes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.080. Interrelationship of offices for administrative purposes (2023)
content:
The Kentucky Law Enforcement Council shall be attached to the office of the commissioner,
   Department of Criminal Justice Training for administrative purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.075. Criminal Justice Council; membership; duties; administrative support
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.075. Criminal Justice Council; membership; duties; administrative support
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.075. Criminal Justice Council; membership; duties; administrative support (2023)
content:
(1)  The Criminal Justice Council is hereby created within the Justice and Public
      Safety Cabinet.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.190. Uniform reporting forms to provide statistical information on crimes; administrative regulations

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.072. Transfer of Department of Criminal Justice Training contract employees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.072. Transfer of Department of Criminal Justice Training contract employees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.072. Transfer of Department of Criminal Justice Training contract employees (2023)
content:
(1)  Effective May 1, 2017, contract employees of Eastern Kentucky University who
      are engaged in providing instructional and support services to the mission of the
      Department of Criminal Justice Training shall be transferred to the Department of
      Criminal Justice Training within the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet along with
      the funding associated with those employees.  The Personnel Cabinet shall assist in implementing the transfer of employees.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.195. Prohibition against racial profiling; model policy; local law enforcement agencies' policies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.195. Prohibition against racial profiling; model policy; local law enforcement agencies' policies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.195. Prohibition against racial profiling; model policy; local law enforcement agencies' policies (2023)
content:
(1)  No state law enforcement agency or official shall stop, detain, or search any
      person when such action is solely motivated by consideration of race, color, or ethnicity,
      and the action would constitute a violation of the civil rights of the person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.110. Assistants to secretary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.110. Assistants to secretary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.110. Assistants to secretary (2023)
content:
All appointments to positions not in the classified service shall be made pursuant
   toKRS 12.050and such appointees shall be major assistants to the secretary and shall assist in
   the development of policy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.197. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.197. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet may provide state personnel, property, and resources to Trooper Island, the Kentucky State Police Foundation, and the Kentucky Law Enforcement Memorial Foundation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.197. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet may provide state personnel, property, and resources to Trooper Island, the Kentucky State Police Foundation, and the Kentucky Law Enforcement Memorial Foundation (2023)
content:
The Justice and Public Safety Cabinet and its agencies may provide state personnel,
   state property, and state resources to Trooper Island Incorporated, the Kentucky State
   Police Foundation, and the Kentucky Law Enforcement Memorial Foundation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.100. Power and authority of secretary in performing functions of cabinet; deputy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.100. Power and authority of secretary in performing functions of cabinet; deputy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.100. Power and authority of secretary in performing functions of cabinet; deputy (2023)
content:
The secretary shall have any and all necessary power and authority, subject to appropriate
   provisions of the statutes, to create such positions and to employ the necessary personnel
   in such positions to enable the secretary to perform the functions of the cabinet.  The secretary shall designate a person to act as deputy for him in the exercise
   of his duties in his absence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet›KY REV ST 15A.160. Promulgation of administrative regulations; administration of laws and cabinet functions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 15A. Justice and Public Safety Cabinet › KY REV ST 15A.160. Promulgation of administrative regulations; administration of laws and cabinet functions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 15A.160. Promulgation of administrative regulations; administration of laws and cabinet functions (2023)
content:
The secretary may promulgate administrative regulations in accordance with KRS Chapter
   13A and direct proceedings and actions for the administration of all laws and functions
   which are vested in the cabinet, except laws and functions vested in the Department
   of Public Advocacy.

content: As used inKRS 16.010to16.199, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.040. Organization of department; qualifications of officers; investigation of applicants
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.040. Organization of department; qualifications of officers; investigation of applicants
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.040. Organization of department; qualifications of officers; investigation of applicants (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall consist of the commissioner and the number of officers,
      individuals employed as a Trooper R Class, CVE R Class, and civilians, and shall be
      organized in the manner as the commissioner from time to time determines.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.030. Qualifications of commissioner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.030. Qualifications of commissioner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.030. Qualifications of commissioner (2023)
content:
The commissioner shall be more than twenty-eight (28) years of age;  shall be a citizen
   of the United States;  and shall be selected on the basis of training, experience
   and qualifications for this position and preferably shall have at least five (5) years
   experience in public or police administration.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.045. Appointment of deputy commissioner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.045. Appointment of deputy commissioner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.045. Appointment of deputy commissioner (2023)
content:
The commissioner may appoint a deputy commissioner.  The appointee shall have peace officer authority only if that appointee is a current
   or honorably retired member of the Kentucky State Police.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.050. Appointment and compensation of personnel; Department of Kentucky State Police Personnel Board; organization, duties, and compensation; repayment of training costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.050. Appointment and compensation of personnel; Department of Kentucky State Police Personnel Board; organization, duties, and compensation; repayment of training costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.050. Appointment and compensation of personnel; Department of Kentucky State Police Personnel Board; organization, duties, and compensation; repayment of training costs (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner shall appoint or promote to the ranks and grades and positions
      of the department such officers as are considered by him or her to be necessary for
      the efficient administration of the department.  The Kentucky State Police shall conduct a biennial salary survey, and the findings
      of the salary survey shall be included in the department's budget request submitted
      to the Kentucky General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.052. Salary schedules for Kentucky State officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.052. Salary schedules for Kentucky State officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.052. Salary schedules for Kentucky State officers (2023)
content:
(1)  The base compensation of troopers and commercial vehicle enforcement officers
      shall be determined based on years of service and rank, as provided in this section.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.062. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.062. Prohibition against requesting or requiring victim of alleged sexual offense to submit to polygraph or other examination; other prohibitions (2023)
content: No officer of the Kentucky State Police shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.060. Powers and duties of commissioner and officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.060. Powers and duties of commissioner and officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.060. Powers and duties of commissioner and officers (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the commissioner, each officer of the department, and each
   individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class to detect and prevent crime,
   apprehend criminals, maintain law and order throughout the state, to collect, classify
   and maintain information useful for the detection of crime and the identification,
   apprehension and conviction of criminals and to enforce the criminal, as well as the
   motor vehicle and traffic laws of the Commonwealth.  To this end the commissioner, each officer of the department, and each individual
   employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class is individually vested with the powers
   of a peace officer and shall have in all parts of the state the same powers with respect
   to criminal matters and enforcement of the laws relating thereto as sheriffs, constables
   granted peace officer powers and police officers in their respective jurisdictions,
   and shall possess all the immunities and matters of defense now available or hereafter
   made available to sheriffs, constables granted peace officer powers and police officers
   in any suit brought against them in consequence of acts done in the course of their
   employment.  Any warrant of arrest may be executed by the commissioner, any officer of the department,
   and each individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class.

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.066. Design and availability of forms relating to purchases of metals and objects containing metal; charges for copies; copyright; use of other facsimiles
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.066. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.066. Design and availability of forms relating to purchases of metals and objects containing metal; charges for copies; copyright; use of other facsimiles (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police shall design the electronic and paper
      forms utilized inKRS 433.890(1)and any other forms and instructions necessary to implementKRS 433.890.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.065. Additional duties of department
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.065. Additional duties of department (2023)
content:
In addition to the performance of all duties relating to the Department of Kentucky
   State Police, the department shall perform the following functions:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.080. Administrative regulations governing officers and department; bonds of employees; oaths; acquisition of real estate; reduction of sick leave balances
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.080. Administrative regulations governing officers and department; bonds of employees; oaths; acquisition of real estate; reduction of sick leave balances
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.080. Administrative regulations governing officers and department; bonds of employees; oaths; acquisition of real estate; reduction of sick leave balances (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner shall promulgate administrative regulations for the enlistment,
      training, code of ethics, discipline, and conduct of officers of the department and
      individuals employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class, and the commissioner may
      promulgate administrative regulations for the governing and operation of the department
      as appear to him or her reasonably necessary to carry out the provisions ofKRS 16.010to16.170.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.090. Training school
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.090. Training school
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.090. Training school (2023)
content:
The commissioner is authorized to organize and maintain a training school or schools
   for officers of the department, and in connection therewith to provide by administrative
   regulation the course and conduct of such training and the period of time for which
   any officer, or any applicant therefor, shall attend such school.  The commissioner, under such administrative regulations as he or she may promulgate,
   is further authorized, but shall not be required, to make such training facilities
   available to any local governing unit within this Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.068. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.068. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.068. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police may charge a fee of ten dollars ($10)
      per set of fingerprint impressions taken and five dollars ($5) per photograph taken
      or copied when those services are requested by a person for professional, trade, or
      commercial purposes or for personal use.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.075. Automobile liability insurance for State Police
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.075. Automobile liability insurance for State Police
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.075. Automobile liability insurance for State Police (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police shall secure, or reimburse members of
      the State Police who purchase a rider on their personal motor vehicle insurance policy
      to secure, such automobile liability insurance and uninsured and underinsured motorist
      coverage as will reasonably protect the interest of members of the State Police when
      in the conduct of official business.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.095. Officers required to take educational course on AIDS
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.095. Officers required to take educational course on AIDS
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.095. Officers required to take educational course on AIDS (2023)
content:
(1)  The Justice and Public Safety Cabinet shall require all officers employed by
      them to complete an educational course approved by the Cabinet for Health and Family
      Services on human immunodeficiency virus infection and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome.  The Justice and Public Safety Cabinet shall develop literature on the human immunodeficiency
      virus infection and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and a training curriculum of
      not more than four (4) hours for the instruction of officers.  The literature and training curriculum shall include information of known modes
      of transmission and methods of controlling and preventing these diseases with an emphasis
      on appropriate behavior and attitude change.  This training may be part of any other training required and for which law enforcement
      officers receive an allowance to attend.  However, nonreceipt of allowance does not exclude a law enforcement officer from
      the training required in this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.070. Uniforms, equipment, and facilities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.070. Uniforms, equipment, and facilities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.070. Uniforms, equipment, and facilities (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner is the head and chief executive officer of the department.  He or she shall provide for himself or herself, each officer of the department,
      and each individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class, under the provisions
      ofKRS 45A.045to45A.650, such uniforms, equipment, and facilities, including motor vehicles, necessary to
      the performance of their respective duties, but all uniforms, equipment, and facilities,
      including motor vehicles, shall remain the property of the Commonwealth.  The commissioner may sell through the Finance and Administration Cabinet, under
      the provisions ofKRS 45A.045to45A.650, such uniforms, equipment, and facilities, including motor vehicles, as become unfit
      for use, and all moneys received therefrom shall be paid into the State Treasury and
      credited to a revolving fund to be used by the department.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.100. Travel expenses and per diem allowances
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.100. Travel expenses and per diem allowances
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.100. Travel expenses and per diem allowances (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner may approve vouchers in payment of expenses, including travel,
      lodging and meals incurred by officers, individuals employed as a Trooper R Class
      or CVE R Class, and civilians of the department in the discharge of their duties,
      and such vouchers shall be audited and paid out of the department's appropriation
      in the manner required by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.128. The Department of Kentucky State Police is encouraged to receive training on issues pertaining to school and student safety, to meet with local superintendents, and to collaborate with local school districts on policies and procedures for communicating any instances of trauma-exposed students
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.128. The Department of Kentucky State Police is encouraged to receive training on issues pertaining to school and student safety, to meet with local superintendents, and to collaborate with local school districts on policies and procedures for communicating any instances of trauma-exposed students
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.128. The Department of Kentucky State Police is encouraged to receive training on issues pertaining to school and student safety, to meet with local superintendents, and to collaborate with local school districts on policies and procedures for communicating any instances of trauma-exposed students (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police is encouraged to receive training on
      issues pertaining to school and student safety and shall be invited to meet annually
      with local superintendents to discuss emergency response plans and emergency response
      concerns.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.110. Fees or rewards
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.110. Fees or rewards
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.110. Fees or rewards (2023)
content:
No fee for the performance of an act in line of duty, and no reward offered for the
   apprehension and conviction of any person or for the recovery of any property may
   be accepted by any officer, individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class,
   or employee of the department, but any fee or reward to which such officer, individual
   employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class, or civilian would be entitled, apart
   from the foregoing provision, shall be paid into the State Treasury and credited to
   a revolving fund, to be used by the department.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.130. Cooperation with other agencies, local officers; other states and federal government
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.130. Cooperation with other agencies, local officers; other states and federal government
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.130. Cooperation with other agencies, local officers; other states and federal government (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner shall cooperate and exchange information with any other department
      or agency of this Commonwealth, or with other police forces, both within and without
      this Commonwealth and with the federal government.  The commissioner may, when authorized by the Governor, negotiate with the appropriate
      officials of other states in the preparation of interstate compacts for police protection
      as authorized by the Federal Congress, and such compacts as negotiated shall be submitted
      to the Governor and the General Assembly for approval.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.132. Collection of statistical data concerning sexual offenses and sexual assault evidence kits; tracking process for evidence kits; public portal for victims to access the system
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.132. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.132. Collection of statistical data concerning sexual offenses and sexual assault evidence kits; tracking process for evidence kits; public portal for victims to access the system (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police shall request from other law enforcement
      agencies, pursuant toKRS 17.150, and shall collect statistical data regarding the reporting and investigation of
      any person charged with committing, attempting to commit, or complicity to a sexual
      offense as defined byKRS 510.040,510.050,510.060,510.070,510.080,510.090,510.110,510.120,510.130,510.140,530.020,530.064(1)(a), and531.310, and on the number of sexual assault evidence kits, as defined inKRS 216B.400, which are submitted to law enforcement agencies, the number of such kits submitted
      to the Department of Kentucky State Police forensic laboratory, and the number of
      kits tested.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.140. Discipline and removal of officers; grounds and procedure; removal of civilian employees; probationary period
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.140. Discipline and removal of officers; grounds and procedure; removal of civilian employees; probationary period
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.140. Discipline and removal of officers; grounds and procedure; removal of civilian employees; probationary period (2023)
content:
(1)  With the exceptions specified in this section,KRS 16.150,16.160, and16.196to16.199, no officer of the department shall be removed, suspended, reduced in grade or pay
      for any reason except inefficiency, misconduct, insubordination, or violation of law
      or of any administrative regulation promulgated by the commissioner.  Any person may prefer charges in writing against any officer or individual employed
      as a Trooper R Class, which shall be filed in the Office of Internal Affairs, which
      shall be designated by the commissioner as the recipient of charges and shall be administratively
      responsible for the maintenance of good order within the department through the collection
      and investigation of charges and the retention of their dispositions.  The charges shall be signed by the person making the same, and shall set out with
      clarity and distinction each and every charge.  The commissioner, whenever probable cause appears, shall prefer charges against
      any officer whom he believes to have been guilty of conduct justifying his removal
      or punishment, in the interest of public order.  Within five (5) days after the filing of charges, the Office of Internal Affairs
      shall deliver a copy thereof, personally, by certified mail, return receipt requested
      to the officer offending.  Within five (5) days after the receipt thereof, the officer may demand public hearing,
      or may admit the truth of the charges in whole or in part.  If the officer admits the truthfulness of the charges, the commissioner shall remove,
      suspend, reduce in rank or pay the officer so offending, in proportion to the seriousness
      of the charges.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.150. Appeal from disciplinary action or removal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.150. Appeal from disciplinary action or removal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.150. Appeal from disciplinary action or removal (2023)
content:
(1)  Any officer of the department who shall be found guilty by the trial board of
      any charge as provided inKRS 16.140shall have the right, within ten (10) days from the date of judgment of the trial
      board, to appeal to the Franklin Circuit Court, provided the punishment be a suspension
      of more than twenty (20) days or his pay be reduced more than ten percent (10%), or
      if he is reduced in grade, if his classification so warrants, or is removed or dismissed
      from the department;  provided, however, the enforcement of the judgment of the trial
      board upon said charges shall not be suspended during said appeal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.170. Political activity forbidden
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.170. Political activity forbidden
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.170. Political activity forbidden (2023)
content:
No officer of the department or individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R
   Class shall, directly or indirectly, give, solicit or receive, or be in any manner
   concerned in giving, soliciting or receiving, any assessment, subscription or contribution
   for any political party or political purpose whatever.  No officer or individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE R Class shall, orally
   or by letter, solicit or be in any manner concerned in soliciting any assessment,
   subscription or contribution for any political party or purpose whatever from any
   person holding a position in the department.  No officer of the department or individual employed as a Trooper R Class or CVE
   R Class shall take any part in political management or affairs or in political campaigns
   further than to cast his vote and to express privately his opinion.  Violation of the provisions hereof shall be grounds for removal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.175. Abduction of children; Kentucky Amber alert system; department to operate in cooperation with other agencies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.175. Abduction of children; Kentucky Amber alert system; department to operate in cooperation with other agencies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.175. Abduction of children; Kentucky Amber alert system; department to operate in cooperation with other agencies (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Kentucky State Police, in cooperation with the Transportation
      Cabinet, the Division of Emergency Management, the Kentucky Broadcasters Association,
      and the Kentucky Press Association, shall operate a system to notify the public when
      a child has been abducted and the department determines that public notification might
      aid in the recovery of the child.  The system shall be known as the Kentucky Amber alert system.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.167. Election of benefits by disabled officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.167. Election of benefits by disabled officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.167. Election of benefits by disabled officer (2023)
content:
Prior to his or her retirement underKRS 16.510to16.652, any Department of Kentucky State Police officer, as defined inKRS 16.010, who became disabled on or before July 1, 1977, as a result of an injury or disease
   arising out of the performance of a hazardous duty in the course of his or her employment
   with the department may elect benefits underKRS 16.165, if he or she qualifies therefor, or he or she may elect to continue receiving preretirement
   benefits otherwise available to him or her due to the disability.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.160. Restrictions on discipline or removal; reduction of force
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.160. Restrictions on discipline or removal; reduction of force
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.160. Restrictions on discipline or removal; reduction of force (2023)
content:
No officer shall be suspended, reduced in rank or pay, or be discharged or dismissed,
   except as provided inKRS 16.140and16.150, and with the further exception that when insufficient funds require a reduction
   in expenditures, the officer or officers junior in point of service shall be first
   discharged.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›Department of Kentucky State Police›KY REV ST 16.173. Unit of department to receive and investigate complaints of human trafficking
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › Department of Kentucky State Police › KY REV ST 16.173. Unit of department to receive and investigate complaints of human trafficking
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.173. Unit of department to receive and investigate complaints of human trafficking (2023)
content:
The Department of Kentucky State Police shall designate a unit within the department
   to receive and investigate complaints of human trafficking.  The unit shall cooperate with and assist prosecutorial agencies and local and federal
   law enforcement, as well as law enforcement from other states, in the receipt and
   investigation of complaints of human trafficking.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›State Police Retirement System›KY REV ST 16.543. Determination of service credit; picked-up employee contributions; service earned while on leave; refund
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › State Police Retirement System › KY REV ST 16.543. Determination of service credit; picked-up employee contributions; service earned while on leave; refund
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.543. Determination of service credit; picked-up employee contributions; service earned while on leave; refund (2023)
content:
(1)  Employee contributions shall be deducted from the creditable compensation of
      each member of the retirement system in the active employment of the Department of
      Kentucky State Police of the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet as an officer as defined
      inKRS 16.520.  After August 1, 1982, employee contributions shall be picked up by the employer
      pursuant toKRS 16.545(4).  Service credit shall be allowed for each month such member receives creditable compensation
      for an average of one hundred (100) hours or more of work per month.  If the average number of hours of work is less than one hundred (100) per month,

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 16. State Police›State Police Retirement System›KY REV ST 16.530. Membership statements and certificates
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 16. State Police › State Police Retirement System › KY REV ST 16.530. Membership statements and certificates
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 16.530. Membership statements and certificates (2023)
content:
Under such rules and regulations as are adopted by the board, each employee becoming
   a member on July 1, 1958, shall have on file at the retirement office, on such forms
   as the board may prescribe, a statement of the facts pertaining to his status as a
   member which shall include a detailed description of all service rendered prior to
   July 1, 1958.  Until such statement is filed, no member shall be entitled to receive any benefits
   underKRS 16.505to16.652.  As soon as practicable after said statement is filed, the system shall ascertain
   the amount of prior service, if any, to which each member is entitled and shall issue

content:

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 17. Public Safety›Criminal Records and Statistics›KY REV ST 17.143. Qualified person to administer system; personnel

content:
The commissioner shall appoint a qualified person to administer the centralized criminal

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 17.110. Report of offense under penal code to department (2023)
content:
(1)  All city and county law enforcement agencies shall cause a photograph, a set
      of fingerprints, and a general description report of all persons arrested on a felony
      charge to be made and two (2) copies of each item forwarded within thirty (30) days
      after the arrest to the Department of Kentucky State Police of the Justice and Public
      Safety Cabinet, in accordance with administrative regulations of the cabinet.  Unless the charges are dismissed or withdrawn at that appearance, the judge shall
      require any adult person appearing before any Circuit Court in the Commonwealth on
      a felony charge, who has not been arrested, to, if this has not already been done
      in the case before the court, be photographed and fingerprinted, and have a general
      description made following his arraignment.  Agencies specified above shall furnish any other information involving offenses
      or in their possession relative to law enforcement upon request by the cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 17. Public Safety›Criminal Records and Statistics›KY REV ST 17.131. Kentucky Unified Criminal Justice Information System; committee to design and implement system; uniform policy; duties; automated warrant system; denial of funds upon failure of agency or officer to participate in system
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 17. Public Safety › Criminal Records and Statistics › KY REV ST 17.131. Kentucky Unified Criminal Justice Information System; committee to design and implement system; uniform policy; duties; automated warrant system; denial of funds upon failure of agency or officer to participate in system
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 17.131. Kentucky Unified Criminal Justice Information System; committee to design and implement system; uniform policy; duties; automated warrant system; denial of funds upon failure of agency or officer to participate in system (2023)
content:
(1)  There is hereby established the Kentucky Unified Criminal Justice Information
      System, referred to in this chapter as the “system.”  The system shall be a joint effort of the criminal justice agencies, the Courts of
      Justice, and the Office of Homeland Security.  Notwithstanding any statutes, administrative regulations, and policies to the contrary,
      if standards and technologies other than those set by the Commonwealth Office of Technology
      are required, the executive director of the Commonwealth Office of Technology shall
      review, expedite, and grant appropriate exemptions to effectuate the purposes of the
      unified criminal justice information system.  Nothing in this section shall be construed to hamper any public officer or official,
      agency, or organization of state or local government from furnishing information or
      data that they are required or requested to furnish and which they are allowed to
      procure by law, to the General Assembly, the Legislative Research Commission, or a
      committee of either.  For the purposes of this section, “criminal justice agencies” include all departments of the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet except the Department
      of Public Advocacy, the Unified Prosecutorial System, Commonwealth's attorneys, county
      attorneys, the Transportation Cabinet, the Cabinet for Health and Family Services,
      and any agency with the authority to issue a citation or make an arrest.

      Justice and Public Safety Cabinet or the Administrative Office of the Courts, or both,
      records of all available convictions involving any felony offense, any misdemeanor
      offense in KRS Chapter 531 or KRS Chapter 510, any misdemeanor offense under KRS Chapter
      218A committed within the five (5) years immediately preceding the application, or
      any conviction for violating KRS Chapter 189A committed within the five (5) years
      immediately preceding the application of a person who applies for employment or volunteers
      for a position in which he or she would have supervisory or disciplinary power over
      a minor.  The cabinet or the Administrative Office of the Courts, as appropriate, shall furnish
      the information to the requesting employer and shall also send a copy of the information
      to the applicant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 17. Public Safety›Criminal Records and Statistics›KY REV ST 17.157. Funds withheld for failure to comply
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 17. Public Safety › Criminal Records and Statistics › KY REV ST 17.157. Funds withheld for failure to comply
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 17.157. Funds withheld for failure to comply (2023)
content:
If any public official or employee, except justices, judges, circuit clerks, and employees
   of the Court of Justice, required to report to the department neglects or refuses
   to comply with the requests of the department, or its rules governing record systems
   and their maintenance, the department chief shall give written notice thereof to the
   person or persons authorized by law to disburse funds of the governmental agency to
   the public official or employee involved.  No funds of the governmental agency shall thereafter be paid to the public official
   or employee, whether in the form of salary, fees, expenses, compensation, or otherwise,
   until the department chief notifies the disbursing authority that performance of the
   required duty has been completed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 17. Public Safety›Criminal Records and Statistics›KY REV ST 17.170. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 17. Public Safety › Criminal Records and Statistics › KY REV ST 17.170. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 17.170. Maintenance of DNA samples collected before March 27, 2009; persons required to provide DNA sample; persons and procedures authorized for DNA sample collection; administrative regulation; penalties for refusing to provide DNA sample or tampering with samples or containers (2023)
content:
(1)  Any DNA sample collected pursuant to the law in effect prior to March 27, 2009,
      shall be maintained and used pursuant to this section andKRS 17.175and17.510.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title III. Executive Branch›Chapter 17. Public Safety›Criminal Records and Statistics›KY REV ST 17.175. Centralized database for DNA identification records; analysis and classification of evidence; exemption from KRS 61.870. to 61.884; expungement of information and destruction of DNA sample; penalty for unlawful use of DNA database identification system
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title III. Executive Branch › Chapter 17. Public Safety › Criminal Records and Statistics › KY REV ST 17.175. Centralized database for DNA identification records; analysis and classification of evidence; exemption from KRS 61.870. to 61.884; expungement of information and destruction of DNA sample; penalty for unlawful use of DNA database identification system
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 17.175. Centralized database for DNA identification records; analysis and classification of evidence; exemption from KRS 61.870. to 61.884; expungement of information and destruction of DNA sample; penalty for unlawful use of DNA database identification system (2023)
content:
(1)  A centralized database of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) identification records
      for convicted or adjudicated offenders, crime scene specimens, unidentified human
      remains, missing persons, and close biological relatives of missing persons shall
      be established in the Department of Kentucky State Police under the direction, control,
      and supervision of the Department of Kentucky State Police forensic laboratory.  The established system shall be compatible with the procedures set forth in a national
      DNA identification index to ensure data exchange on a national level.
