path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement›Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners›KY REV ST 21.470. Exemption from taxation, execution; taxability after December 31, § 1997
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement › Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners › KY REV ST 21.470. Exemption from taxation, execution; taxability after December 31, § 1997
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21.470. Exemption from taxation, execution; taxability after December 31, § 1997 (2023)
content:
All retirement allowances and other benefits accrued or accruing to any person under
   the provisions ofKRS 21.350to21.510are hereby exempted from any state, county or municipal tax, and shall not be subject
   to execution, attachment, garnishment or any other process whatsoever, nor shall any
   assignment thereof be enforceable in any court.  Except retirement benefits accrued or accruing to any person under the provisions
   ofKRS 21.350to21.510on or after January 1, 1998, shall be subject to the tax imposed byKRS 141.020, to the extent provided inKRS 141.010and141.0215.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement›Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners›KY REV ST 21.550. Investments, judicial retirement fund
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement › Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners › KY REV ST 21.550. Investments, judicial retirement fund
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21.550. Investments, judicial retirement fund (2023)
content:
(1)  Those members of the board of trustees of the Judicial Form Retirement System
      who are appointed by the Supreme Court, together with the members appointed by the
      Governor, shall constitute an investment committee for the Judicial Retirement Plan,
      and as such shall have full and sole authority over the judicial retirement fund and
      the investment thereof, including the prescribing of funding standards, the adoption
      of actuarial methods and assumptions, and the making of employments or contracts for
      required personal services, including administrative, actuarial and investment counseling
      services.  The committee shall be considered trustee of the judicial retirement fund and shall
      have the sole authority to make investment transactions or obtain insurance contracts
      for funding purposes.  The fund shall be invested in securities which, at the time of making the investment,
      are by law permitted for the investment of funds by fiduciaries in this state, or
      funding may be accomplished in part by contract with a reputable life insurance company
      authorized to do business in this state.  To the extent that funding is provided through insurance contract, no contributions,
      payments or premiums shall be subject to any tax on insurance premiums or annuity
      considerations.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement›Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners›KY REV ST 21.560. Investments; legislative retirement fund
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21. Judicial Retirement › Judicial Retirement System for Judges and Commissioners › KY REV ST 21.560. Investments; legislative retirement fund
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21.560. Investments; legislative retirement fund (2023)
content:
The members of the board of trustees of the Judicial Form Retirement System who are
   appointed by the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives,
   singly or jointly, together with the members of the board who are appointed by the
   Governor, shall constitute an investment committee for the Legislators' Retirement
   Plan, and as such shall have all the powers and duties with respect to the legislators'
   retirement fund as are given byKRS 21.440(1)and21.550to the investment committee of the Judicial Retirement Plan with respect to the judicial
   retirement fund.  The committee provided for by this section may, with the concurrence of the investment
   committee for the Judicial Retirement Plan, arrange for the legislators' retirement
   fund and the judicial retirement fund to constitute a common fund for investment purposes
   only, to be under the management of the investment committee for the Judicial Retirement
   Plan, each fund sharing in the common fund in proportion to the value of its assets
   contributed to the common fund.

content:
The records of the Court of Appeals involving proceedings before that court, prior
   to January 1, 1976, shall become part of the permanent records of the Supreme Court.  Such records shall be given the same faith and credit as are records of the Supreme
   Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.050. Reversal or modification of judgments; procedures for appeal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.050. Reversal or modification of judgments; procedures for appeal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.050. Reversal or modification of judgments; procedures for appeal (2023)
content:
(1)  A judgment, order or decree of a lower court may be reversed, modified or set
      aside by the Supreme Court for errors appearing in the record.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.060. Effect of equal division of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.060. Effect of equal division of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.060. Effect of equal division of court (2023)
content:
If the Supreme Court is equally divided in the decision of a case, the judgment, order
   or decree of the lower court shall stand affirmed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.070. Publication of opinions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.070. Publication of opinions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.070. Publication of opinions (2023)
content: (1)  All opinions of the Supreme Court shall be published.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.080. Process, to whom directed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.080. Process, to whom directed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.080. Process, to whom directed (2023)
content:
The original or final process of the Supreme Court may be directed to the sheriff
   of any county.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.110. Retired justice or judge serving as special judge; compensation; expenses

content: Any retired justice or judge assigned to active judicial service pursuant toSection 110(5)(b) of the Constitutionshall be compensated for his or her service as follows:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.120. Special justice of Supreme Court; qualifications; compensation; expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.120. Special justice of Supreme Court; qualifications; compensation; expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.120. Special justice of Supreme Court; qualifications; compensation; expenses (2023)
content:
(1)  If it becomes necessary for the Governor to appoint a justice to the Supreme
      Court pursuant toSection 110(3) of the Constitution, a person so appointed shall possess the qualifications of a Supreme Court Justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.140. Disposition of fees paid for admission to practice of law
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.140. Disposition of fees paid for admission to practice of law
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.140. Disposition of fees paid for admission to practice of law (2023)
content:
Any fees fixed by the Supreme Court to be paid by applicants for admission to the
   practice of law and for the issuance of a license to practice law shall be promptly
   paid into the State Treasury by the person, officer, or agency designated by the Supreme
   Court to receive or collect the fees.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.130. Board of Bar Examiners; compensation and expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.130. Board of Bar Examiners; compensation and expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.130. Board of Bar Examiners; compensation and expenses (2023)
content:
(1)  To assist in the evaluation of applicants for admission to the practice of law,
      the Supreme Court may appoint a Board of Bar Examiners.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.170. In-service training for judges, domestic relations commissioners, and trial commissioners on child sexual abuse, domestic violence, and crimes against the elderly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.170. In-service training for judges, domestic relations commissioners, and trial commissioners on child sexual abuse, domestic violence, and crimes against the elderly (2023)
content:
The Supreme Court shall provide, at least once every two (2) years, in- service training
   programs for Circuit Judges, District Judges, and domestic relations and trial commissioners
   in:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.090. Security personnel and services for Court of Justice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.090. Security personnel and services for Court of Justice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.090. Security personnel and services for Court of Justice (2023)
content:
(1)  At the request of the Chief Justice, the Governor may provide through the Department
      of Kentucky State Police such security personnel and services for the Supreme Court
      and Court of Appeals as shall be necessary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.180. Training for judges, domestic relations commissioners, and trial commissioners on adult abuse, neglect, and exploitation investigations and prosecutions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.180. Training for judges, domestic relations commissioners, and trial commissioners on adult abuse, neglect, and exploitation investigations and prosecutions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.180. Training for judges, domestic relations commissioners, and trial commissioners on adult abuse, neglect, and exploitation investigations and prosecutions (2023)
content:
The Administrative Office of the Courts, under the direction of the Supreme Court,
   shall develop training for Circuit Judges, District Judges, and domestic relations
   and trial commissioners on investigation and prosecution of cases of adult abuse,
   neglect, and exploitation and on the investigation and services provided under KRS
   Chapter 209.  This multidisciplinary training shall specify the roles and responsibilities of
   Circuit Judges, District Judges, and domestic relations and trial commissioners, and
   employees in their respective offices, with respect to the investigations and prosecutions
   of these cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.160. Organization and control of state bar vested in Supreme Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.160. Organization and control of state bar vested in Supreme Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.160. Organization and control of state bar vested in Supreme Court (2023)
content:
The Supreme Court has power to provide for the organization, government and membership
   of the state bar of Kentucky and to adopt rules and regulations to govern conduct
   and activity of the state bar and its members.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.150. Powers of Kentucky Bar Association in disciplinary proceedings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.150. Powers of Kentucky Bar Association in disciplinary proceedings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.150. Powers of Kentucky Bar Association in disciplinary proceedings (2023)
content:
As deemed necessary in the exercise of its power to discipline attorneys, as granted
   bySection 116 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court may authorize the Kentucky Bar Association to conduct hearings,
   administer necessary oaths, take testimony under oath, compel the attendance of witnesses,
   and compel the production of records and other evidence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.190. Pilot project to study the feasibility and desirability of conducting some open juvenile proceedings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.190. Pilot project to study the feasibility and desirability of conducting some open juvenile proceedings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.190. Pilot project to study the feasibility and desirability of conducting some open juvenile proceedings (2023)
content:
(1)  The General Assembly respectfully requests that the Supreme Court of Kentucky
      institute a pilot project to study the feasibility and desirability of the opening
      or limited opening of court proceedings, except for proceedings related to sexual
      abuse, to the public which are related to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.300. Prohibition against solicitation of professional employment from victim or relative of victim of accident or disaster
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.300. Prohibition against solicitation of professional employment from victim or relative of victim of accident or disaster
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.300. Prohibition against solicitation of professional employment from victim or relative of victim of accident or disaster (2023)
content:
(1)  NotwithstandingKRS 21A.160, for a period of thirty (30) days following the filing of a criminal or civil action,
      or claim for damages, or a traffic citation, injury, accident, or disaster, an attorney
      or an attorney referral service shall be subject to the following prohibition.  An attorney or an attorney referral service shall not directly solicit, or knowingly
      permit another person to directly solicit on his or its behalf, a victim of the accident
      or disaster, or a relative of the victim, for the purpose of obtaining professional
      employment relating to a criminal or civil action, or claim for damages, arising out
      of the traffic citation, injury, accident, or disaster.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals›KY REV ST 22A.010. Numbers of judges; districts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals › KY REV ST 22A.010. Numbers of judges; districts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 22A.010. Numbers of judges; districts (2023)
content:
(1)  The Court of Appeals shall consist of fourteen (14) judges, with two (2) judges
      from each of seven (7) Court of Appeals districts.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.310. Penalties for violation of KRS § 21A.300
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.310. Penalties for violation of KRS § 21A.300
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.310. Penalties for violation of KRS § 21A.300 (2023)
content: (1)  NotwithstandingKRS 21A.160, any person violating any provision ofKRS 21A.300shall, upon conviction, be guilty of a Class A misdemeanor.

content: (1)  A court chosen for the pilot project authorized byKRS 21A.190shall, subject to written authorization by the Chief Justice:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky›KY REV ST 21A.350. Weighted caseload analysis of need to increase, decrease, or rearrange circuits or districts or reallocate judges; certification of necessity
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.350. Weighted caseload analysis of need to increase, decrease, or rearrange circuits or districts or reallocate judges; certification of necessity
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 21A.350. Weighted caseload analysis of need to increase, decrease, or rearrange circuits or districts or reallocate judges; certification of necessity (2023)
content:
(1)  Beginning in 2020 and every eight (8) years thereafter, the Supreme Court may
      direct the Administrative Office of the Courts to perform a weighted caseload analysis
      to determine the need to reduce, increase, or rearrange the Commonwealth's judicial
      circuits and districts, to reallocate the assignment of judges, or to modify the number
      of judges relative to their respective populations or caseloads.  This analysis shall include caseload totals by case type and case weight and the
      total number of judges necessary for the Commonwealth's judicial circuits and districts.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 21A. Supreme Court of Kentucky › KY REV ST 21A.320. Permissible types of solicitation

content: Nothing contained inKRS 21A.300and21A.310shall prohibit an attorney or attorney referral service from:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals›KY REV ST 22A.020. Jurisdiction; appeal procedures
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals › KY REV ST 22A.020. Jurisdiction; appeal procedures
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 22A.020. Jurisdiction; appeal procedures (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided inSection 110 of the Constitution, an appeal may be taken as a matter of right to the Court of Appeals from any conviction,
      final judgment, order, or decree in any case in Circuit Court, including a family
      court division of Circuit Court, unless such conviction, final judgment, order, or
      decree was rendered on an appeal from a court inferior to Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals›KY REV ST 22A.030. Facilities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals › KY REV ST 22A.030. Facilities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 22A.030. Facilities (2023)
content:
(1)  The administrative director of the courts shall provide for such physical facilities
      as are available for the operation of the Court of Appeals, and may utilize the services
      of the Finance and Administration Cabinet in securing such facilities.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals›KY REV ST 22A.040. Clerk; appointment; compensation; oath; bond; assistants; fee schedule; seal; annual audit
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals › KY REV ST 22A.040. Clerk; appointment; compensation; oath; bond; assistants; fee schedule; seal; annual audit
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 22A.040. Clerk; appointment; compensation; oath; bond; assistants; fee schedule; seal; annual audit (2023)
content:
(1)  The clerk of the Court of Appeals shall be appointed by the court to serve at
      its pleasure.  The annual salary of the clerk shall be fixed by the Supreme Court not to exceed
      twenty-two thousand dollars ($22,000).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 23A. Circuit Court›KY REV ST 23A.010. Jurisdiction of Circuit Court; court of record and of continuous session
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 23A. Circuit Court › KY REV ST 23A.010. Jurisdiction of Circuit Court; court of record and of continuous session
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 23A.010. Jurisdiction of Circuit Court; court of record and of continuous session (2023)
content:
(1)  The Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction;  it has original jurisdiction
      of all justiciable causes not exclusively vested in some other court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals›KY REV ST 22A.050. Enforcement of mandates
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 22A. Court of Appeals › KY REV ST 22A.050. Enforcement of mandates
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 22A.050. Enforcement of mandates (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 23A. Circuit Court›KY REV ST 23A.070. Thirtieth Judicial Circuit; family court; funds from previously created campaign accounts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 23A. Circuit Court › KY REV ST 23A.070. Thirtieth Judicial Circuit; family court; funds from previously created campaign accounts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 23A.070. Thirtieth Judicial Circuit; family court; funds from previously created campaign accounts (2023)
content:
(1)  The Thirtieth Judicial Circuit is entitled to twenty-three (23) judges and shall
      have twenty-three (23) numbered divisions of the Circuit Court.  The Circuit Court divisions designated for family court shall be consecutively numbered
      beginning with the Thirtieth Judicial Circuit, First Division, Family Court.  All other Circuit Court divisions shall be consecutively numbered beginning with
      the Thirtieth Judicial Circuit, First Division, and shall appear on the ballot prior
      to the designated family court divisions.  These designations shall apply for election purposes and all other purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 23A. Circuit Court›KY REV ST 23A.080. Appeals from District Court; issuance of writs by Circuit Court

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 23A. Circuit Court›KY REV ST 23A.090. Security services provided by sheriff; compensation

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 23A. Circuit Court›KY REV ST 23A.120. Position of domestic relations commissioner abolished in family court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 23A. Circuit Court › KY REV ST 23A.120. Position of domestic relations commissioner abolished in family court

content:
In any judicial circuit where a family court is established or has been established,
   the position of domestic relations commissioner is abolished, and no commissioner

   family court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 24A. District Court›KY REV ST 24A.020. Exclusive jurisdiction granted District Court by statute; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 24A. District Court › KY REV ST 24A.020. Exclusive jurisdiction granted District Court by statute; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 24A.020. Exclusive jurisdiction granted District Court by statute; exception (2023)
content:
When jurisdiction over any matter is granted to District Court by statute, such jurisdiction
   shall be deemed to be exclusive unless the statute specifically states that the jurisdiction
   shall be concurrent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 27A. Judicial Support Agencies and Personnel›KY REV ST 27A.050. Administrative Office of the Courts; appointment of director; compensation; prohibition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 27A. Judicial Support Agencies and Personnel › KY REV ST 27A.050. Administrative Office of the Courts; appointment of director; compensation; prohibition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 27A.050. Administrative Office of the Courts; appointment of director; compensation; prohibition (2023)
content:
The Administrative Office of the Courts is created to serve as the staff for the Chief
   Justice in executing the policies and programs of the Court of Justice.  The director of the Administrative Office of the Courts, employees thereof, and
   administrative assistants of the Chief Justice shall serve at the pleasure of the
   Chief Justice.  Provided, however, the director shall be appointed or reappointed at least every
   four (4) years with the advice and consent of the Senate;  but if the Senate is not
   in session when a term expires or a vacancy occurs, the Chief Justice shall make the
   appointment to take effect at once, subject to the approval of the Senate when convened.  The salaries of the director, employees thereof, and administrative assistants of
   the Chief Justice shall be fixed by order of the Chief Justice and paid monthly or
   at such other periods as may be consonant with the policy applicable to payment of
   salaries of state employees out of the State Treasury.  While holding their positions the director, employees of the office and administrative
   assistants shall not practice law in any court of this Commonwealth.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 24A. District Court › KY REV ST 24A.197. Position of domestic relations commissioner abolished in family court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 24A.197. Position of domestic relations commissioner abolished in family court (2023)
content:

   family court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 27A. Judicial Support Agencies and Personnel›KY REV ST 27A.095. Standard power of attorney regarding medical treatment and school-related decisions for a minor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 27A. Judicial Support Agencies and Personnel › KY REV ST 27A.095. Standard power of attorney regarding medical treatment and school-related decisions for a minor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 27A.095. Standard power of attorney regarding medical treatment and school-related decisions for a minor (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “medical treatment” means any medical, chiropractic, optometric, or dental examination, diagnostic procedure,
      and treatment, including but not limited to hospitalization, developmental screening,
      mental health screening and treatment, preventive care, pharmacy services, immunizations
      recommended by the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee
      on Immunization Practices, well-child care, and blood testing, except that “medical
      treatment” shall not include HIV/AIDS testing, controlled substance testing, or any
      other testing for which a separate court order or informed consent is required under
      other applicable law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 27A. Judicial Support Agencies and Personnel›KY REV ST 27A.096. Judicial guidelines for pretrial release of moderate-risk or high-risk defendants

      risk assessments indicate that they are moderate or high risk and would otherwise

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.080. Disqualifications for jury service; permanent exemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.080. Disqualifications for jury service; permanent exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.080. Disqualifications for jury service; permanent exemption (2023)
content:
(1)  The Chief Circuit Judge or one (1) or more judges of the court, the court's clerk,
      a deputy clerk, the court's administrator, or a deputy court administrator so designated
      by the Chief Circuit Judge shall determine on the basis of the information provided
      on the juror qualification form whether the prospective juror is disqualified for
      jury service for any of the reasons listed in subsection (2) of this section.  This determination shall be entered in the space provided on the juror qualification
      form.  The Chief Circuit Judge shall cause each disqualified juror to be immediately notified
      of the juror's disqualification.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.180. Responsibility for needs of jurors, transportation to view scene, security personnel, equipment, and services
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.180. Responsibility for needs of jurors, transportation to view scene, security personnel, equipment, and services (2023)
content:

      and other incidental needs of grand jurors and petit jurors in Circuit Court and in
      District Court when the jurors are kept overnight or otherwise sequestered when ordered
      to do so by the judge of the court for which the jurors were summoned.  The expenses for these services shall be borne by the Finance and Administration
      Cabinet and the officer shall be reimbursed in accordance with administrative regulations
      issued by the Finance and Administration Cabinet, pursuant to KRS Chapter 13A.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.170. Compensation of jurors

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.170. Compensation of jurors (2023)

      day for jury service.  In addition thereto, they shall be paid seven dollars and fifty cents ($7.50) per
      day as reimbursement of expenses incurred, which sum is hereby determined to be the
      equivalent of the minimum daily expenses reasonably to be incurred by such juror.

content: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.060. Assignment of jurors by Chief Circuit Judge; service of summons; selection of additional jurors; summonsing jurors from adjoining counties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.060. Assignment of jurors by Chief Circuit Judge; service of summons; selection of additional jurors; summonsing jurors from adjoining counties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.060. Assignment of jurors by Chief Circuit Judge; service of summons; selection of additional jurors; summonsing jurors from adjoining counties (2023)
content:
(1)  Each Circuit or District Judge shall inform the Chief Circuit Judge or the Chief
      Circuit Judge's designee of the need for qualified jurors.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.020. Procedural rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.020. Procedural rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.020. Procedural rules (2023)
content:
The Supreme Court may make and amend such procedural rules as may be necessary to
   implement the provisions of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.070. Juror qualification forms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.070. Juror qualification forms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.070. Juror qualification forms (2023)
content:
(1)  The Chief Circuit Judge shall cause to be mailed or delivered with the summons
      to each juror a juror qualification form accompanied by instructions to fill out and
      return the form by mail or hand delivery to the clerk within five (5) days after its
      receipt, or to be completed as otherwise directed.  The juror qualification form shall be provided by the Administrative Office of the
      Courts and subject to approval by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.240. Oath to grand jury
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.240. Oath to grand jury
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.240. Oath to grand jury (2023)
content:
The court shall swear the grand jury using substantially the following oath:  “Do
   you swear or affirm that you will hear and weigh carefully all the evidence presented
   to you, and that you will do your duty as prescribed by law, and that you will carry
   out carefully any investigations which you are requested to make?”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.090. Automatic exemptions prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.090. Automatic exemptions prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.090. Automatic exemptions prohibited (2023)
content: There shall be no automatic exemptions from jury service.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.130. Limitation on jury service within a twenty-four-month period
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.130. Limitation on jury service within a twenty-four-month period
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.130. Limitation on jury service within a twenty-four-month period (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as set out in this section, in any twenty-four (24) month period, a person
      shall not be required to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.100. Postponement of service or excusing of juror; breastfeeding mothers to be excused
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.100. Postponement of service or excusing of juror; breastfeeding mothers to be excused
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.100. Postponement of service or excusing of juror; breastfeeding mothers to be excused (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon the request of a prospective juror prior to assignment to a trial court,
      the Chief Circuit Judge, or after the juror's assignment to a trial court, the trial
      judge may excuse such juror upon a showing of undue hardship, extreme inconvenience,
      or public necessity.  On the day on which the prospective jurors are summonsed to appear, any person not
      previously excused who desires to be excused shall be heard.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.110. Disclosure of records or papers used in selection process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.110. Disclosure of records or papers used in selection process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.110. Disclosure of records or papers used in selection process (2023)
content:
The contents of any records or papers used by the Administrative Office of the Courts
   or the clerk in connection with the selection process and not required to be made
   public under this chapter shall not be disclosed, except in connection with the preparation
   or presentation of a motion under the Rules of Civil Procedure or the Rules of Criminal
   Procedure or upon order of the Chief Justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.160. Employer's duties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.160. Employer's duties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.160. Employer's duties (2023)
content:
(1)  An employer shall not deprive an employee of his employment, or threaten or otherwise
      coerce him with respect thereto, because the employee receives a summons, responds
      thereto, serves as a juror, or attends court for prospective jury service.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.140. Discharge of juror
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.140. Discharge of juror
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.140. Discharge of juror (2023)
content:
At the conclusion of his period of service as required by this chapter, each juror
   shall be discharged.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.150. Contempt; failure to perform jury service
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.150. Contempt; failure to perform jury service
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.150. Contempt; failure to perform jury service (2023)
content:
(1)  A person summoned for jury service who fails to appear as directed shall be ordered
      by the court to appear forthwith and show cause for his failure to comply with the
      summons.  If he fails to show good cause for noncompliance with the summons, he may be punished
      for contempt.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.200. Number of grand jurors; number required to find indictment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.200. Number of grand jurors; number required to find indictment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.200. Number of grand jurors; number required to find indictment (2023)
content:
A grand jury shall consist of twelve (12) persons, nine (9) of whom concurring may
   find an indictment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.290. Examination of petit jurors; challenges; alternate jurors
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.290. Examination of petit jurors; challenges; alternate jurors
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.290. Examination of petit jurors; challenges; alternate jurors (2023)
content:
(1)  The voir dire examination of petit jurors shall be conducted in the manner prescribed
      by the Supreme Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.190. Adjournment of juries
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.190. Adjournment of juries
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.190. Adjournment of juries (2023)
content:
The court may adjourn the whole or part of the petit jury to any day of their required
   periods of service, but they shall not be paid for the time they stand adjourned.  The grand jury may be adjourned in like manner without pay.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.320. Duty of jury and officer after submission; causes for discharge of jury; procedure for rendering verdict
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.320. Duty of jury and officer after submission; causes for discharge of jury; procedure for rendering verdict
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.320. Duty of jury and officer after submission; causes for discharge of jury; procedure for rendering verdict (2023)
content:
(1)  When the case is finally submitted to the jury, they shall retire for deliberation.  When they retire, they shall be kept together in some convenient place, under the
      charge of an officer, until they agree upon a verdict or are discharged by the court,
      subject to the Supreme Court rules permitting them to separate temporarily at night
      and for their meals.  The officer having them under his charge shall not allow any communications to be
      made to them, nor make any himself, except to ask them if they have agreed upon their
      verdict, unless by order of the court;  and he shall not, before their verdict is
      rendered, communicate to any person the state of their deliberations, or the verdict
      agreed upon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.230. Release of juror from grand jury service and retention as petit juror
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.230. Release of juror from grand jury service and retention as petit juror
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.230. Release of juror from grand jury service and retention as petit juror (2023)
content:
If a juror selected is incapable of serving as a grand juror but capable of serving
   as a petit juror, the judge may, for good cause shown, release the juror from grand
   jury service and retain him as a petit juror.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.210. Summoning and convening of regular grand juries; sessions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.210. Summoning and convening of regular grand juries; sessions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.210. Summoning and convening of regular grand juries; sessions (2023)
content:
(1)  A regular grand jury shall be summoned upon the order of the Chief Circuit Judge.  The grand jury shall be convened at least once every four (4) months at such time
      as may be designated by the Circuit Court.  The court may require the grand jury to convene more often if the ends of justice
      or the needs of the county so require.  The court may require the grand jury to convene if the Commonwealth's or county
      attorney certifies to the court that there are defendants who have been bound over
      to the grand jury and that there is a need for the grand jury to consider the return
      of any indictments.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.220. Special grand juries; sessions; extension of sessions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.220. Special grand juries; sessions; extension of sessions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.220. Special grand juries; sessions; extension of sessions (2023)
content:
(1)  Any Chief Circuit Judge may summon for cause a special grand jury to deal with
      a situation requiring lengthy investigation which cannot be adequately handled during
      the term of the regular grand jury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.260. Replacement of grand juror who is excused
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.260. Replacement of grand juror who is excused
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.260. Replacement of grand juror who is excused (2023)
content:
At any time for cause shown, the court may excuse a grand juror either temporarily
   or permanently and may swear another grand juror from a current jury panel in place
   of the one excused.  The discharge of any such grand juror shall in no way or manner affect any indictment
   found by the grand jury as it was composed either before or after such discharge.  If it is impossible to fill the vacancy on the grand jury from a current jury panel,
   the Chief Circuit Judge may summon, using the procedure inKRS 29A.060(5), such number of prospective jurors as deemed necessary for the purpose.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.280. Number of jurors in Circuit and District Courts; number required for verdict
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.280. Number of jurors in Circuit and District Courts; number required for verdict
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.280. Number of jurors in Circuit and District Courts; number required for verdict (2023)
content: (1)  Juries for all trials in Circuit Court shall be composed of twelve (12) persons.  Juries for all trials in District Court shall be composed of six (6) persons.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.250. Foreman of grand jury; oath to witnesses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.250. Foreman of grand jury; oath to witnesses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.250. Foreman of grand jury; oath to witnesses (2023)
content:
The grand jurors shall elect one (1) of their members to be foreman.  The foreman shall administer an oath to each witness who testifies before the grand
   jury, substantially as follows:  “Do you swear or affirm that you will tell the truth,
   the whole truth, and nothing but the truth?”.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.270. Right to jury trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.270. Right to jury trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.270. Right to jury trial (2023)
content:
(1)  Defendants shall have the right to a jury trial in all criminal prosecutions,
      including prosecutions for violations of traffic laws, in the Circuit and District
      Courts.  The defendant may request a jury trial at any time prior to the time his case is
      called for trial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.310. Admonition to jury upon separation; view of property or place
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.310. Admonition to jury upon separation; view of property or place
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.310. Admonition to jury upon separation; view of property or place (2023)
content:
(1)  If the jury is permitted to separate, either during the trial or after the case
      is submitted to them, they shall be admonished by the court that it is their duty
      not to converse with, nor allow themselves to be addressed by, any other person on
      any subject of the trial;  and that, during the trial, it is their duty not to form
      or express an opinion thereon, until the case is finally submitted to them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.020. Oath of clerk and deputies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.020. Oath of clerk and deputies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.020. Oath of clerk and deputies (2023)
content:
Every clerk and deputy, in addition to the oath prescribed bySection 228 of the Constitution, shall, before entering on the duties of his office, take the following oath in presence
   of the Circuit Court:  “I, ․․․․․․․․․․, do swear that I will well and truly discharge the duties of the office of ․․․․․․․․․․ County Circuit Court clerk, according to the best of my skill and judgment, making
   the due entries and records of all orders, judgments, decrees, opinions and proceedings
   of the court, and carefully filing and preserving in my office all books and papers
   which come to my possession by virtue of my office;  and that I will not knowingly
   or willingly commit any malfeasance of office, and will faithfully execute the duties
   of my office without favor, affection or partiality, so help me God.” The fact that the oath has been administered shall be entered on the record of the
   Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.990. Penalties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.990. Penalties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.990. Penalties (2023)
content: (1)  Any employer who violates subsection (1) or (2) ofKRS 29A.160is guilty of a Class B misdemeanor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.010. Clerk defined; duties coextensive with Commonwealth; subject to administrative control of Chief Justice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.010. Clerk defined; duties coextensive with Commonwealth; subject to administrative control of Chief Justice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.010. Clerk defined; duties coextensive with Commonwealth; subject to administrative control of Chief Justice (2023)
content:
(1)  For the purpose ofKRS 30A.010to30A.190, “clerk” means the Circuit Court clerk serving in his capacity as clerk of both the Circuit
      Court and the District Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.300. Oath to petit jury
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.300. Oath to petit jury
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.300. Oath to petit jury (2023)
content:
The court shall swear the petit jurors using substantially the following oath:  “Do
   you swear or affirm that you will impartially try the case between the parties and
   give a true verdict according to the evidence and the law, unless dismissed by the
   court?”.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 29A. Juries›KY REV ST 29A.330. Jury fee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 29A. Juries › KY REV ST 29A.330. Jury fee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 29A.330. Jury fee (2023)
content:
(1)  The jury fee for a civil trial in Circuit Court and District Court shall be set
      in accordance withKRS 48.195.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.040. Office in each county; branch offices; office hours
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.040. Office in each county; branch offices; office hours
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.040. Office in each county; branch offices; office hours (2023)
content:
Every Circuit Court and every District Court shall have a clerk's office in each county,
   and shall have such branch offices within the county as are approved by the Supreme
   Court.  Minimum office hours of the clerk's offices shall be determined by the Supreme Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.050. Number and qualifications of deputy clerks and employees; power of deputy clerks; compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.050. Number and qualifications of deputy clerks and employees; power of deputy clerks; compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.050. Number and qualifications of deputy clerks and employees; power of deputy clerks; compensation (2023)
content:
(1)  The number and qualifications of deputy clerks and other employees in the office
      of each clerk shall be determined by the Administrative Office of the Courts after
      consultation with the clerk concerned.  All deputies and employees of the clerk's office shall be employees of the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.015. Domestic violence training for circuit clerks and deputy clerks
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.015. Domestic violence training for circuit clerks and deputy clerks
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.015. Domestic violence training for circuit clerks and deputy clerks (2023)
content:
(1)  The Administrative Office of the Courts, under the direction of the Supreme Court,
      shall provide initial training courses and, at least once every two (2) years, continuing
      education courses for circuit clerks and deputy clerks concerning the dynamics of
      domestic violence, effects of domestic violence on adult and child victims, legal
      remedies for protection, lethality and risk issues, model protocols for addressing
      domestic violence, available community resources and victims services, and reporting
      requirements.  The training shall be developed in consultation with legal, victims services, victim
      advocacy, and mental health professionals with an expertise in domestic violence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.030. Bond of clerks, deputies, and other personnel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.030. Bond of clerks, deputies, and other personnel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.030. Bond of clerks, deputies, and other personnel (2023)
content:
(1)  All clerks, deputy clerks, and other persons employed in the office of the clerk
      shall be bonded to the Commonwealth for the faithful performance of their duties and
      for the accounting of all funds which may come into their hands by virtue of their
      office.  They shall be covered by the blanket bond for all elected or appointed state officials.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.060. Clerk to prepare bonds and to refuse insufficient surety; authorization for preparation and acceptance of bail bonds by other public officers or employees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.060. Clerk to prepare bonds and to refuse insufficient surety; authorization for preparation and acceptance of bail bonds by other public officers or employees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.060. Clerk to prepare bonds and to refuse insufficient surety; authorization for preparation and acceptance of bail bonds by other public officers or employees (2023)
content:
(1)  Each clerk shall prepare in a proper manner every bond to be taken by or given
      before him or his court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.070. Clerk may administer oaths and take affidavits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.070. Clerk may administer oaths and take affidavits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.070. Clerk may administer oaths and take affidavits (2023)
content:
Every clerk may administer oaths, in or out of court, touching any matter in which
   an oath may be legally administered, and may take any affidavit requested or permitted
   in the progress of a proceeding in his court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.090. Collection of fees or charges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.090. Collection of fees or charges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.090. Collection of fees or charges (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless the plaintiff has established his right to prosecute as a poor person
      as provided by statute or rule, each clerk shall, when a proceeding is filed in his
      court, collect the filing fee fixed by law.  He shall also collect any charges which have accrued during the progress of the
      action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.080. Maintenance of records; removal from county; transfer by rule or order of Supreme Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.080. Maintenance of records; removal from county; transfer by rule or order of Supreme Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.080. Maintenance of records; removal from county; transfer by rule or order of Supreme Court (2023)
content:
(1)  Every clerk shall maintain all records, files, dockets, and indexes as are prescribed
      by statute or rule.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.100. Assessment of costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.100. Assessment of costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.100. Assessment of costs (2023)
content:
At the termination of an action, every clerk shall assess the costs of each party
   and file it with the case.  The assessment shall be subject to correction by the court by motion upon notice
   given.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.110. Payment of jurors and witnesses; clerk's liability for advancements; reports to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; penalty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.110. Payment of jurors and witnesses; clerk's liability for advancements; reports to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; penalty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.110. Payment of jurors and witnesses; clerk's liability for advancements; reports to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; penalty (2023)
content:
(1)  Each clerk shall pay to each juror and to each witness the compensation allowed
      to him by law, under appropriations provided by the General Assembly and in accordance
      with procedures governing expenditures from appropriations.  The clerk shall take a receipt for each payment made by him showing the date on
      which payment is made.  A canceled check shall be the equivalent of a receipt.  For the purpose of providing for such payments, the State Treasurer, on direction
      of the Finance and Administration Cabinet, shall advance to each clerk two (2) imprest
      funds:  one for the payment of jurors which shall be sufficient for the period of
      service of each grand or petit jury panel, or both, but not to exceed a period of
      sixty (60) days;  the other for the payment of Commonwealth witnesses, which shall
      be sufficient for a period of time not to exceed sixty (60) days.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.120. Collection of fines and forfeitures; semimonthly reports and payments to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; delinquency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.120. Collection of fines and forfeitures; semimonthly reports and payments to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; delinquency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.120. Collection of fines and forfeitures; semimonthly reports and payments to the Finance and Administration Cabinet; delinquency (2023)
content:
(1)  Every clerk shall collect all fines and forfeitures imposed in District and Circuit
      Court, and shall issue receipts therefor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.140. Additional duties of clerk
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.140. Additional duties of clerk
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.140. Additional duties of clerk (2023)
content:
Every clerk shall perform such additional duties as may be prescribed by statute or
   court rule.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.125. Circuit clerk to report final disposition of criminal case to Administrative Office of the Courts; update of database within ninety days of disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.125. Circuit clerk to report final disposition of criminal case to Administrative Office of the Courts; update of database within ninety days of disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.125. Circuit clerk to report final disposition of criminal case to Administrative Office of the Courts; update of database within ninety days of disposition (2023)
content:
Each circuit clerk shall submit to the Administrative Office of the Courts, in a manner
   prescribed by the Administrative Office of the Courts, the final court disposition.  Said disposition shall be inclusive of regulatory violations and traffic cases which
   are not subject to prepayment.  The Administrative Office of the Courts shall update their database within ninety
   (90) days of the disposition.  The update shall include information from the:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.150. Vacancy in office of clerk; appointment of successor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.150. Vacancy in office of clerk; appointment of successor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.150. Vacancy in office of clerk; appointment of successor (2023)
content:
Whenever a vacancy occurs in the office of the clerk, the chief judge of the judicial
   circuit shall within thirty (30) days appoint a qualified successor to the office
   who shall serve until replaced as provided bySection 152 of the Constitution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.145. Clerks to send notices to State Board of Elections on incompetency determinations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.145. Clerks to send notices to State Board of Elections on incompetency determinations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.145. Clerks to send notices to State Board of Elections on incompetency determinations (2023)
content:
Each circuit clerk shall send certified notices of incompetency to the State Board
   of Elections within ten (10) days after the determination has become final with regard
   to any person before the courts of the county.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.200. Moneys deposited with court clerks and payable to a third person
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.200. Moneys deposited with court clerks and payable to a third person
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.200. Moneys deposited with court clerks and payable to a third person (2023)
content:
All moneys which are deposited with the clerk and which are payable to a third person,
   not the Commonwealth, or which may become payable to such third person as a result
   of court action or otherwise shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.180. Assignment as special circuit clerk to fill vacancy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.180. Assignment as special circuit clerk to fill vacancy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.180. Assignment as special circuit clerk to fill vacancy (2023)
content:
In the event of a vacancy in the office of circuit clerk in any county, the Chief
   Justice may assign any other circuit clerk in the Commonwealth as special circuit
   clerk to fill the vacancy for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days, or until a
   person is appointed to fill the vacancy as provided by law, whichever occurs first.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.130. Certification of copies of documents and records
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.130. Certification of copies of documents and records
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.130. Certification of copies of documents and records (2023)
content:
Every clerk shall prepare, attest and certify copies of all documents and records
   in his office upon payment of the charge established by statute.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.250. Expenditure of funds for liability insurance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.250. Expenditure of funds for liability insurance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.250. Expenditure of funds for liability insurance (2023)
content:
The Court of Justice may expend funds necessary to insure circuit clerks and their
   deputies against any liability arising out of an act or omission committed in the
   scope and course of performing legal duties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.210. Rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.210. Rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.210. Rules (2023)
content:
The Supreme Court shall issue rules relating to the receipt, handling, deposit, and
   disbursal of moneys by the circuit clerk which are held in accounts covered byKRS 30A.200.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.170. Clerk ex officio a special circuit clerk of Commonwealth
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.170. Clerk ex officio a special circuit clerk of Commonwealth
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.170. Clerk ex officio a special circuit clerk of Commonwealth (2023)
content:
Each circuit clerk shall be, ex officio, a special circuit clerk of the Commonwealth,
   and as such shall perform the duties and services required byKRS 30A.180, at such time and places, coextensive with the Commonwealth, as required by the Chief
   Justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.260. Payment to clerk by debit or credit card account; imposition of fee if check or sight order dishonored
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.260. Payment to clerk by debit or credit card account; imposition of fee if check or sight order dishonored
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.260. Payment to clerk by debit or credit card account; imposition of fee if check or sight order dishonored (2023)
content:
(1)  A clerk may, but shall not be required to, accept payment of any fine, forfeiture,
      tax, or fee by debit or credit card account.  If an individual chooses to pay a fine, forfeiture, tax, or fee by debit or credit
      card account, the clerk may recover the transaction fee charged by the issuer or acquirer
      of the account as part of and in addition to the original amount of the fine, forfeiture,
      tax, or fee.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.190. Accounting by circuit clerk for all fines, fees, forfeitures, and costs collected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.190. Accounting by circuit clerk for all fines, fees, forfeitures, and costs collected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.190. Accounting by circuit clerk for all fines, fees, forfeitures, and costs collected (2023)
content:
All fees, fines, forfeitures, and costs in any District Court or Circuit Court case
   shall be collected and accounted for by the Circuit Court clerk and paid into the
   State Treasury, except that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.205. Interest on deposits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.205. Interest on deposits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.205. Interest on deposits (2023)
content:
(1)  The bank accounts of the circuit clerk authorized byKRS 30A.200shall accrue interest at such rate per annum upon the average daily deposit on hand
      at the close of banking hours as may be agreed upon by the bank and the Chief Justice
      or his designee.  Interest accrued shall not be at a rate less than the interest paid on similar accounts
      of the Commonwealth in that bank.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Additional Personnel›KY REV ST 30A.310. Authorization for appointment or employment of court personnel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Additional Personnel › KY REV ST 30A.310. Authorization for appointment or employment of court personnel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.310. Authorization for appointment or employment of court personnel (2023)
content:
The Chief Justice, through the Administrative Office of the Courts, may authorize
   the appointment or employment by the chief judge of such secretaries, court reporters,
   interpreters, court administrators, friends of the court, and other personnel demonstrated
   as being necessary to the proper and efficient operation of the Court of Justice or
   any court which is a component thereof.  Persons so authorized to be employed or appointed shall be compensated and classified
   according to the Judicial Personnel System.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.435. Use of equipment by interpreter or disabled person; approval required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.435. Use of equipment by interpreter or disabled person; approval required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.435. Use of equipment by interpreter or disabled person; approval required (2023)
content:
(1)  In the performance of his duties the interpreter may utilize electronic recording,
      foreign language translation, and other equipment.  A person who is deaf, hard of hearing, or speech impaired may elect to use assistive
      technology in lieu of or in addition to the services of an interpreter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Additional Personnel›KY REV ST 30A.300. Secretaries for Circuit Courts and District Courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Additional Personnel › KY REV ST 30A.300. Secretaries for Circuit Courts and District Courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.300. Secretaries for Circuit Courts and District Courts (2023)
content: (1)  Each Circuit Judge may appoint a secretary for his circuit.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.430. Interpreter not to be examined as witness; other privileged communications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.430. Interpreter not to be examined as witness; other privileged communications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.430. Interpreter not to be examined as witness; other privileged communications (2023)
content:
Every person who acts as an interpreter in circumstances involving the arrest, police
   custody or other stage in a criminal, civil, or other matter of a person coming underKRS 30A.410shall not be examined as a witness regarding conversations between that person and
   his attorney, when the conversations would otherwise be subject to the attorney-client
   privilege, without the consent of that person.  Interpreters shall not be required to testify regarding any other privileged communications
   without the consent of the person for whom they are interpreting.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.010. Department of Public Advocacy; establishment; functions; independent agency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.010. Department of Public Advocacy; establishment; functions; independent agency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.010. Department of Public Advocacy; establishment; functions; independent agency (2023)
content:
There is hereby established as an independent agency of state government, attached
   for administrative purposes to the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet, the Department
   of Public Advocacy, in order to provide for the establishment, maintenance, and operation
   of a state-sponsored and controlled system for:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Circuit Clerks›KY REV ST 30A.160. Delivery of books and records to successor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Circuit Clerks › KY REV ST 30A.160. Delivery of books and records to successor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.160. Delivery of books and records to successor (2023)
content:
Upon the resignation, removal from office or expiration of the term of office of a
   clerk, he shall immediately deliver to his successor, or such other person as the
   court orders, all books, records, and other papers belonging to his office.  For failure to do so he shall be guilty of a Class A misdemeanor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.400. Interpreters; appointment; hearing to determine need
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.400. Interpreters; appointment; hearing to determine need
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.400. Interpreters; appointment; hearing to determine need (2023)
content:
(1)  If a person has been detained in police custody or has been arrested, an interpreter
      shall be provided prior to any interrogation or taking of a statement from the person
      if the court determines he meets the criteria set forth inKRS 30A.410.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.405. Qualifications of interpreter; standards
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.405. Qualifications of interpreter; standards
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.405. Qualifications of interpreter; standards (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person appointed as interpreter pursuant to this chapter shall be qualified
      by training or experience to interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, both
      receptively and expressively, using any necessary specialized vocabulary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.410. When interpreter shall be provided; removal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.410. When interpreter shall be provided; removal

content:
(1)  The court in any matter, criminal or civil, shall appoint a qualified interpreter
      or interpreters, to be paid out of the State Treasury, for the following categories
      of persons, whether they are parties, jurors, or witnesses:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.030. Authority and duties of department (Effective July 1, 2024)

content:
The authority and duties of the Department of Public Advocacy shall include but are
