path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.415. Responsibility for payment for interpreter's services
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.415. Responsibility for payment for interpreter's services
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.415. Responsibility for payment for interpreter's services (2023)
content:
(1)  In criminal or civil cases, the Court of Justice shall be responsible for payment,
      including ordinary and reasonable expenses, for interpretive services for court appearances.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.420. Payment out of State Treasury
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.420. Payment out of State Treasury
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.420. Payment out of State Treasury (2023)
content:
In cases where compensation by the state is required or permitted interpreters' fees
   and ordinary and reasonable expenses shall be paid out of the State Treasury according
   to the pay schedule of the Judicial Personnel System.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 30A. Court Personnel›Interpreters›KY REV ST 30A.425. Duties of interpreter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 30A. Court Personnel › Interpreters › KY REV ST 30A.425. Duties of interpreter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 30A.425. Duties of interpreter (2023)
content: The duties of the interpreter may include:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.020. Public advocate; qualifications; selection; term; salary; staff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.020. Public advocate; qualifications; selection; term; salary; staff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.020. Public advocate; qualifications; selection; term; salary; staff (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Public Advocacy shall consist of the public advocate, deputy
      public advocate, general counsel, such assistant public advocates as the public advocate
      shall deem necessary, and such secretarial and other personnel as the public advocate
      shall deem necessary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.050. Public advocacy plans; review and approval or denial by public advocate; funding by department and governmental unit; recordkeeping; annual report
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.050. Public advocacy plans; review and approval or denial by public advocate; funding by department and governmental unit; recordkeeping; annual report
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.050. Public advocacy plans; review and approval or denial by public advocate; funding by department and governmental unit; recordkeeping; annual report (2023)
content:
(1)  The public advocate shall review and approve or deny or suggest modifications
      to all plans which are submitted to the Department of Public Advocacy for defense
      of indigent persons.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.035. Advisory boards for protection and advocacy division; appointment; number; terms; compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.035. Advisory boards for protection and advocacy division; appointment; number; terms; compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.035. Advisory boards for protection and advocacy division; appointment; number; terms; compensation (2023)
content:
(1)  There shall be advisory boards for the Protection and Advocacy Division of the
      Department of Public Advocacy as set forth inPublic Laws 99-319and 106-402 and their implementing regulations.  Each shall be comprised of not more than seventeen (17) citizen members appointed
      for terms of not less than two (2) years by the Protection and Advocacy Division director.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.085. Plans must comply with department's rules and regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.085. Plans must comply with department's rules and regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.085. Plans must comply with department's rules and regulations (2023)
content:
All plans authorized by this chapter shall conform to all rules and regulations promulgated
   by the Department of Public Advocacy.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.100. Definitions

content:
The following terms and standards shall apply, subject to further definition and regulation

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.060. Local office in jurisdiction with ten or more Circuit Judges required; funding by governmental unit required in amount set by department
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.060. Local office in jurisdiction with ten or more Circuit Judges required; funding by governmental unit required in amount set by department
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.060. Local office in jurisdiction with ten or more Circuit Judges required; funding by governmental unit required in amount set by department (2023)
content:
(1)  Each county, urban-county, charter county, and consolidated local government
      with a judicial circuit containing ten (10) or more Circuit Judges, excluding judges
      of family court divisions as designated by the Supreme Court, shall establish and
      maintain an office of public advocacy and submit a plan for the operation thereof
      to the Department of Public Advocacy.  If the plan submitted is approved by the Department of Public Advocacy, the public
      advocate shall grant to the county, urban-county, charter county, or consolidated
      local government the amount to which it would be entitled underKRS 31.050(2)which shall be used as the Commonwealth's share in defraying the expenses of the
      program in that county, urban-county, charter county, or consolidated local government.

content: (1)  A master commissioner may be appointed for each county within a judicial circuit.

content:
(1)  A needy person who is being detained by a law enforcement officer, on suspicion

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.120. Determination of whether person needy; factors for determination; affidavit of indigency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.120. Determination of whether person needy; factors for determination; affidavit of indigency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.120. Determination of whether person needy; factors for determination; affidavit of indigency (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) The determination of whether a person covered byKRS 31.110is a needy person shall be deferred no later than his or her first appearance in
         court or in a suit for payment or reimbursement underKRS 31.211, whichever occurs earlier.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.211. Determination of ability to pay partial fee for representation and services at arraignment; collection of unpaid partial fee by civil judgment; funds placed in special trust and agency account (Effective July 1, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.211. Determination of ability to pay partial fee for representation and services at arraignment; collection of unpaid partial fee by civil judgment; funds placed in special trust and agency account (Effective July 1, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.211. Determination of ability to pay partial fee for representation and services at arraignment; collection of unpaid partial fee by civil judgment; funds placed in special trust and agency account (Effective July 1, 2024) (2023)
content:
(1)  At arraignment, the court shall conduct a nonadversarial hearing to determine
      whether a person who has requested a public defender is able to pay a partial fee
      for legal representation, the other necessary services and facilities of representation,
      and court costs.  The court shall order payment in an amount determined by the court and may order
      that the payment be made in a lump sum or by installment payments to recover money
      for representation provided under this chapter.  This partial fee determination shall be made at each stage of the proceedings.
