title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.185. Facilities available to department; ex parte request for funds for representation; funding responsibility; Finance and Administration special account and payment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.185. Facilities available to department; ex parte request for funds for representation; funding responsibility; Finance and Administration special account and payment (2023)
content:
(1)  Any defending attorney operating under the provisions of this chapter is entitled
      to use the same state facilities for the evaluation of evidence as are available to
      the attorney representing the Commonwealth.  If he or she considers their use impractical, the court of competent jurisdiction
      in which the case is pending may authorize the use of private facilities to be paid
      for on court order from the special account of the Finance and Administration Cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.140. Waiver of right to counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.140. Waiver of right to counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.140. Waiver of right to counsel (2023)
content:
A person who has been appropriately informed underKRS 31.120may waive in writing, or by other record, any right provided by this chapter, if
   the court concerned, at the time of or after waiver, finds of record that he has acted
   with full awareness of his rights and of the consequences of a waiver and if the waiver
   is otherwise according to law.  The court shall consider such factors as the person's age, education, and familiarity
   with English, and the complexity of the crime involved.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.235. Payment for representation upon failure of department to provide attorney; decision of public advocate final (Effective July 1, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.235. Payment for representation upon failure of department to provide attorney; decision of public advocate final (Effective July 1, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.235. Payment for representation upon failure of department to provide attorney; decision of public advocate final (Effective July 1, 2024) (2023)
content:
If a court, after finding that the Department of Public Advocacy fails to provide
   an attorney to a person eligible for representation under KRS Chapter 31, appoints,
   under the court's inherent authority, an attorney to provide representation to the
   needy person, the public advocate is hereby authorized to pay reasonable and necessary
   fees and expenses subject to the following limitations:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.215. Acceptance of fees by public advocacy attorneys prohibited; exceptions (Effective July 1, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.215. Acceptance of fees by public advocacy attorneys prohibited; exceptions (Effective July 1, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.215. Acceptance of fees by public advocacy attorneys prohibited; exceptions (Effective July 1, 2024) (2023)
content:
(1)  Except for attorneys appointed pursuant toKRS 620.100,625.041,625.080, and31.120, no attorney employed by the Department of Public Advocacy shall accept any fees
      for the representation of any needy person as defined in this chapter from that person
      or anyone for his or her benefit and the fees for representation of that person shall
      be limited to the fees provided in this chapter.  “Fees” shall include cash, property, or other pecuniary benefits of any kind.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.220. When chapter applies to United States courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.220. When chapter applies to United States courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.220. When chapter applies to United States courts (2023)
content:
This chapter applies only to representation in the courts of this state, except that
   it does not prohibit a defending attorney from representing a needy person in a federal
   court of the United States, if:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.219. Appeal by public advocacy attorney (Effective July 1, 2024)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.219. Appeal by public advocacy attorney (Effective July 1, 2024)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.219. Appeal by public advocacy attorney (Effective July 1, 2024) (2023)
content:
(1)  It shall be the duty of the attorney employed by the Department of Public Advocacy
      representing a client at trial to file a notice of appeal if his or her client requests
      an appeal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy›KY REV ST 31.241. Protections; sanctions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31. Department of Public Advocacy › KY REV ST 31.241. Protections; sanctions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31.241. Protections; sanctions (2023)
content:
The protections provided by this chapter do not exclude any protection or sanction
   that the law otherwise provides.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.990. Penalties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.990. Penalties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.990. Penalties (2023)
content:
(1)  If any master commissioner or receiver fails to comply with his duties as defined
      by appropriate court order, he shall be guilty of a violation, and, upon conviction,
      shall be removed from office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.040. Special commissioner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.040. Special commissioner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.040. Special commissioner (2023)
content: (1)  When the master commissioner is interested as an attorney or party;  or

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.080. Receivers; persons not to be appointed receivers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.080. Receivers; persons not to be appointed receivers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.080. Receivers; persons not to be appointed receivers (2023)
content:
(1)  Receivers, except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, may be appointed
      under the same terms and conditions as a master commissioner.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.030. Oath
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.030. Oath
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.030. Oath (2023)
content:
The master commissioner shall take an oath that he will faithfully and honestly discharge
   the duties of his office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.120. Use of proof of and performance of duties of predecessor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.120. Use of proof of and performance of duties of predecessor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.120. Use of proof of and performance of duties of predecessor (2023)
content:
The master commissioner or receiver may use any proof reduced to writing and signed
   by his predecessor, and may execute any order or judgment which it was the duty of
   his predecessor to have executed, and which remains unexecuted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers›KY REV ST 31A.020. Bond; special bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 31A. Master Commissioners and Receivers › KY REV ST 31A.020. Bond; special bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 31A.020. Bond; special bond (2023)
content:
The master commissioner shall execute a bond, with surety approved by the court.  The bond shall be recorded in court.  He shall execute a special bond when required by the court and no action shall be
   maintained on his general bond for matters covered by a special bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System›KY REV ST 32.031. Secretaries for Circuit Judges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System › KY REV ST 32.031. Secretaries for Circuit Judges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 32.031. Secretaries for Circuit Judges (2023)
content:
Each Circuit Judge may employ a secretary.  The secretary shall be appointed by and shall hold office at the pleasure of the
   judge.  The salary for the secretary, payable out of the State Treasury, shall be commensurate
   with the secretary's education, training, and experience based upon the guidelines
   established by the classification and compensation plan for comparable positions maintained
   by the state Personnel Cabinet pursuant toKRS 64.640.  Persons employed as secretaries to Circuit Judges shall be members of the Kentucky
   Employees Retirement System in accordance with the provisions ofKRS 61.510to61.692.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System›KY REV ST 32.011. Construction of law
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System › KY REV ST 32.011. Construction of law
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 32.011. Construction of law (2023)
content:
Nothing contained inKRS 32.011to32.070shall be construed as limiting, restricting, or terminating the authority of local
   governmental units, including cities, counties, and urban-county governments, to provide
   financial support for the court system and the offices of the Commonwealth's attorneys
   which are serving that local community, and all such units of local government are
   further authorized to supplement the financial support provided thereto by the state
   underKRS 32.011to32.070.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Nominating Commissions›KY REV ST 34.010. Terms; appointments
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Nominating Commissions › KY REV ST 34.010. Terms; appointments
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.010. Terms; appointments (2023)
content:
(1)  Members of judicial nominating commissions, both statewide and local, shall hold
      office for a term of four (4) years and until such time as their successors shall
      be appointed or elected, except as provided in subsection (2).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.033. Military judges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.033. Military judges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.033. Military judges (2023)
content:
Procedures pertaining to the selection and regulation of military judges shall be
   promulgated by the adjutant general and approved by the Governor of the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.045. Imposition of restraint
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.045. Imposition of restraint
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.045. Imposition of restraint (2023)
content:
(1)  Arrest is the restraint of a person by an order not imposed as a punishment for
      an offense, directing the person to remain within certain specified limits.  Confinement is the physical restraint of a person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System›KY REV ST 32.070. Expense allowances for grand jurors, petit jurors, and persons summoned for jury service
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 32. Financing of Unified State Court System › KY REV ST 32.070. Expense allowances for grand jurors, petit jurors, and persons summoned for jury service
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 32.070. Expense allowances for grand jurors, petit jurors, and persons summoned for jury service (2023)
content:
Beginning July 1, 1976, or at such earlier date as may be fixed as hereinafter provided,
   grand jurors, petit jurors and persons summoned for jury service in Circuit Court
   eligible for payment of the compensation designated inKRS 29A.170(1)shall be paid, in addition thereto, the sum of seven dollars and fifty cents ($7.50)
   per day as reimbursement of expenses incurred, which sum is hereby determined to be
   the equivalent of the minimum daily expenses reasonably to be incurred by such juror
   or person.  Payment of such reimbursement for expenses may be made beginning as of such date
   prior to July 1, 1976, but not prior to July 1, 1974, as may be fixed by the Governor
   upon recommendation of the secretary of justice and public safety if and to the extent
   that prior to July 1, 1976, the Commonwealth of Kentucky is awarded grant funds by
   the Law Enforcement Assistance Administration of the United States Department of Justice
   on a matching basis of not less than ninety percent (90%) federal funds and ten percent
   (10%) state funds which grant funds are sufficient to pay the full cost of the reimbursement
   of expenses, and of the administrative expenses related thereto, authorized by this
   section from the date so fixed through June 30, 1976.  Eligible state funds appropriated for the 1974-1976 biennium may be used for matching
   purposes so long as such use does not reduce the level of services provided in the
   executive budget for that biennium.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission›KY REV ST 34.320. Compensation; expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission › KY REV ST 34.320. Compensation; expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.320. Compensation; expenses (2023)
content:
Members of the Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission who do not otherwise receive
   a salary from the State Treasury shall receive sixty dollars ($60) for each day they
   are in session or on official duty.  All members shall be reimbursed for their necessary expenses for each day they are
   in session or on official duty.  All claims shall be approved by the Chief Justice or his designee and shall be paid
   out of the State Treasury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Nominating Commissions›KY REV ST 34.020. Compensation of members
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Nominating Commissions › KY REV ST 34.020. Compensation of members
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.020. Compensation of members (2023)
content:
Members of judicial nominating commissions shall receive no compensation for their
   services but shall be paid their necessary expenses for each day spent in the performance
   of their duties.  All claims for expenses shall be approved by the Chief Justice or his designee and
   shall be paid out of the State Treasury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission›KY REV ST 34.330. Oaths; testimony; evidence; contempt proceedings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission › KY REV ST 34.330. Oaths; testimony; evidence; contempt proceedings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.330. Oaths; testimony; evidence; contempt proceedings (2023)
content:
In the exercise of its powers and duties, the Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission
   may administer necessary oaths, take testimony under oath, compel the attendance of
   witnesses, and compel the production of records and other evidence.  If any witness refuses to testify concerning any matter on which he may lawfully
   be interrogated, any Circuit Judge, on application of the commission may compel obedience
   by proceedings for contempt as in the case of disobedience of a subpoena issued from
   the Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.010. Definitions for chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.010. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.010. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission›KY REV ST 34.310. Membership
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission › KY REV ST 34.310. Membership
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.310. Membership (2023)
content:
(1)  The members of the Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission to be selected
      from among the Judges of the Court of Appeals, the Circuit Judges, and the District
      Judges, shall be selected according to rules promulgated by the Supreme Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Nominating Commissions›KY REV ST 34.030. Administrative services; records
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Nominating Commissions › KY REV ST 34.030. Administrative services; records
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.030. Administrative services; records (2023)
content:
The Administrative Office of the Courts shall provide administrative support for,
   and maintain the records of, judicial nominating commissions.  The director of the Administrative Office of the Courts shall certify the costs
   for these services to the Chief Justice who, upon verification, shall certify the
   expenses for payment out of the State Treasury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IV. Judicial Branch›Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions›Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission›KY REV ST 34.340. Majority vote required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IV. Judicial Branch › Chapter 34. Judicial Commissions › Judicial Retirement and Removal Commission › KY REV ST 34.340. Majority vote required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 34.340. Majority vote required (2023)
content:
No justice or judge shall be retired for disability or suspended without pay or removed
   for good cause except upon a majority vote of members of the Judicial Retirement and
   Removal Commission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.057. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.057. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.057. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited (2023)
content:
No member of the state military forces may be placed in confinement in immediate association
   with enemy prisoners or other foreign nationals not members of the Armed Forces.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.060. Punishment prohibited before trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.060. Punishment prohibited before trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.060. Punishment prohibited before trial (2023)
content:
No person, while being held for trial or awaiting a verdict, shall be subjected to
   punishment or penalty other than arrest or confinement upon the charges pending against
   the person, nor shall the arrest or confinement imposed upon the person be any more
   rigorous than the circumstances require to insure the person's presence, but the person
   may be subjected to minor punishment during that period for infractions of discipline.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.015. Persons subject to this code; jurisdiction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.015. Persons subject to this code; jurisdiction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.015. Persons subject to this code; jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(1)  This code applies to all members of the state military forces at all times and
      in all places.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.031. Judge advocates
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.031. Judge advocates
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.031. Judge advocates (2023)
content:
(1)  The senior force judge advocates in each of the state's military forces or that
      judge advocate's delegates shall make frequent inspections in the field of supervision
      of the administration of military justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.020. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.020. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.020. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel (2023)
content:
(1)  Each person discharged from the state military forces who is later charged with
      having fraudulently obtained a discharge is, subject toKRS 35.215, subject to trial by court-martial on that charge and is, after apprehension, subject
      to this code while in custody under the direction of the state military forces for
      that trial.  Upon conviction of that charge that person is subject to trial by court-martial
      for all offenses under this code committed prior to the fraudulent discharge.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.030. Territorial applicability of the code
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.030. Territorial applicability of the code
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.030. Territorial applicability of the code (2023)
content:
(1)  This code has applicability at all times and in all places subject to the personal
      jurisdiction as provided inKRS 35.015, or, if not in a duty status, that there is a nexus between the act or omission constituting
      the offense and the efficient functioning of the state military forces;  however,
      this grant of military jurisdiction shall neither preclude nor limit civilian jurisdiction
      over an offense, which is limited only by the prohibition of double jeopardy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.075. Classification of courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.075. Classification of courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.075. Classification of courts-martial (2023)
content: The two (2) kinds of courts-martial in the state military forces are:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.035. Apprehension
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.035. Apprehension
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.035. Apprehension (2023)
content: (1)  Apprehension is the taking of a person into custody.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.120. Who may serve on courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.120. Who may serve on courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.120. Who may serve on courts-martial (2023)
content:
(1)  Any commissioned officer of the state military forces is eligible to serve on
      all courts-martial for the trial of any person subject to this code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.105. Who may convene general courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.105. Who may convene general courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.105. Who may convene general courts-martial (2023)
content: (1)  General courts-martial may be convened by:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.130. Detail of trial counsel and defense counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.130. Detail of trial counsel and defense counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.130. Detail of trial counsel and defense counsel (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) For each general and special court-martial the authority convening the court
         shall detail trial counsel, defense counsel, and assistants as are appropriate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.050. Restraint of person charged with offenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.050. Restraint of person charged with offenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.050. Restraint of person charged with offenses (2023)
content:
Any subject person charged with an offense under this code may be ordered into arrest
   or confinement, as circumstances may require.  When any person subject to this code is placed in arrest or confinement prior to
   trial, immediate steps shall be taken to inform the person of the specific wrong of
   which the person is accused and diligent steps shall be taken to try the person or
   to dismiss the charges and release the person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.150. Charges and specifications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.150. Charges and specifications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.150. Charges and specifications (2023)
content:
(1)  Charges and specifications shall be signed by a person subject to this code under
      oath before a commissioned officer authorized by this chapter to administer oaths
      and shall state:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.055. Place of confinement; reports and receiving of prisoners
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.055. Place of confinement; reports and receiving of prisoners
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.055. Place of confinement; reports and receiving of prisoners (2023)
content:
(1)  If a person subject to this code is confined before, during, or after trial,
      confinement shall be in a civilian or military confinement facility.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.065. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.065. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.065. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities (2023)
content:
(1)  A person subject to this code accused of an offense against civil authority may
      be delivered, upon request, to the civil authority for trial or confinement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.170. Advice of judge advocate and reference for trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.170. Advice of judge advocate and reference for trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.170. Advice of judge advocate and reference for trial (2023)
content:
(1)  Before directing the trial of any charge by general court-martial, the convening
      authority shall refer it to a judge advocate for consideration and advice.  The convening authority may not refer a specification under a charge to a general
      court-martial for trial unless the convening authority has been advised in writing
      by a judge advocate that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.070. Commanding officer's nonjudicial punishment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.070. Commanding officer's nonjudicial punishment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.070. Commanding officer's nonjudicial punishment (2023)
content:
(1)  Under such regulations as prescribed, any commanding officer, and for purposes
      of this section, officers-in-charge, may impose disciplinary punishments for minor
      offenses without the intervention of a court-martial pursuant to this section.  The Governor, the adjutant general, or an officer of a general or flag rank in command
      may delegate the powers under this section to a principal assistant who is a member
      of the state military forces.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.085. Jurisdiction of general courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.085. Jurisdiction of general courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.085. Jurisdiction of general courts-martial (2023)
content:
Subject toKRS 35.080, general courts-martial have jurisdiction to try persons subject to this code for
   any offense made punishable by this code, and may, under those limitations as the
   Governor may prescribe, adjudge any punishment not forbidden by this code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.090. Jurisdiction of special courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.090. Jurisdiction of special courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.090. Jurisdiction of special courts-martial (2023)
content:
Subject toKRS 35.080, special courts-martial have jurisdiction to try persons subject to this code for
   any offense made punishable by this code, and may, under those limitations as the
   Governor may prescribe, adjudge any punishment not forbidden by this code except dishonorable
   discharge, dismissal, confinement for more than one (1) year, forfeiture of pay exceeding
   two-thirds (2/3) pay per month, or forfeiture of pay for more than one (1) year.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.185. Unlawfully influencing action of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.185. Unlawfully influencing action of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.185. Unlawfully influencing action of court (2023)
content:
(1)  No authority convening a general or special court-martial, nor any other commanding
      officer, or officer serving on the staff thereof, may censure, reprimand, or admonish
      the court or any member, military judge, or counsel thereof, with respect to the findings
      or sentence adjudged by the court, or with respect to any other exercise of its or
      their functions in the conduct of the proceeding.  No person subject to this code may attempt to coerce or, by unauthorized means,
      influence the action of a court-martial or court of inquiry or any member thereof
      in reaching the findings or sentence in any case, or the action of any convening,
      approving or reviewing authority with respect to their judicial acts.  The foregoing provisions shall not apply to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.125. Military judge of a general or special court-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.125. Military judge of a general or special court-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.125. Military judge of a general or special court-martial (2023)
content:
(1)  A military judge shall be detailed to each general and special court-martial.  The military judge shall preside over each open session of the court-martial to
      which the military judge has been detailed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.080. Court-martial jurisdiction of National Guard or active militia; rules and regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.080. Court-martial jurisdiction of National Guard or active militia; rules and regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.080. Court-martial jurisdiction of National Guard or active militia; rules and regulations (2023)
content:
Each component of the state military forces has court-martial jurisdiction over all
   members of the particular component who are subject to this code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.110. Who may convene special courts-martial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.110. Who may convene special courts-martial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.110. Who may convene special courts-martial (2023)
content: (1)  Special courts-martial may be convened by:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.175. Service of charges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.175. Service of charges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.175. Service of charges (2023)
content:
The trial counsel shall serve or cause to be served upon the accused a copy of the
   charges.  No person may, against the person's objection, be brought to trial before a general
   court-martial case within a period of five (5) days after the service of charges upon
   the person, or in a special court-martial, within a period of three (3) days after
   the service of the charges upon the accused.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.145. Absent and additional members
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.145. Absent and additional members
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.145. Absent and additional members (2023)
content:
(1)  No member of a general or special court-martial shall be absent or excused after
      the court has been assembled for the trial of the accused unless excused as a result
      of a challenge, excused by the military judge for physical disability or other good
      cause, or excused by order of the convening authority for good cause.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.155. Compulsory self-incrimination prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.155. Compulsory self-incrimination prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.155. Compulsory self-incrimination prohibited (2023)
content:
(1)  No person subject to this code may compel any person to incriminate himself or
      herself or to answer any question the answer to which may tend to incriminate him
      or her.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.180. Governor or the adjutant general may prescribe rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.180. Governor or the adjutant general may prescribe rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.180. Governor or the adjutant general may prescribe rules (2023)
content:
Pretrial, trial, and post-trial procedures, including modes of proof, for courts-martial
   cases arising under this code, and for courts of inquiry, may be prescribed by the
   Governor or adjutant general by regulations, or as otherwise provided by law, which
   shall apply the principles of law and the rules of evidence generally recognized in
   military criminal cases in the courts of the Armed Forces but which may not be contrary
   to or inconsistent with this code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.140. Detail or employment of reporters and interpreters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.140. Detail or employment of reporters and interpreters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.140. Detail or employment of reporters and interpreters (2023)
content:
Under such regulations as may be prescribed, the convening authority of a general
   or special court-martial or court of inquiry shall detail or employ qualified court
   reporters, who shall record the proceedings of and testimony taken before that court
   and may detail or employ interpreters who shall interpret for the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.160. Investigation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.160. Investigation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.160. Investigation (2023)
content:
(1)  No charge or specification shall be referred to a general court-martial for trial
      until a thorough and impartial investigation of all the matters set forth therein
      has been made.  This investigation shall include inquiry as to the truth of the matter set forth
      in the charges, consideration of the form of charges, and a recommendation as to the
      disposition which should be made of the case in the interest of justice and discipline.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.165. Forwarding of charges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.165. Forwarding of charges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.165. Forwarding of charges (2023)
content:
When a person is held for trial by general court-martial, the commanding officer shall,
   within eight (8) days after the accused is ordered into arrest or confinement, if
   practicable, forward the charges, together with the investigation and allied papers,
   to the person exercising general court-martial jurisdiction.  If that is not practicable, the commanding officer shall report in writing to that
   person the reasons for delay.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.195. Sessions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.195. Sessions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.195. Sessions (2023)
content:
(1)  At any time after the service of charges which have been referred for trial to
      a court-martial composed of a military judge and members, the military judge may,
      subject toKRS 35.175, call the court into session without the presence of the members for the purpose
      of:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.190. Duties of trial counsel and defense counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.190. Duties of trial counsel and defense counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.190. Duties of trial counsel and defense counsel (2023)
content:
(1)  The trial counsel of a general or special court-martial shall be a member in
      good standing of the state bar and shall prosecute in the name of the state, and shall,
      under the direction of the court, prepare the record of the proceedings.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.200. Continuances
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.200. Continuances
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.200. Continuances (2023)
content:
The military judge of a court-martial may, for reasonable cause, grant a continuance
   to any party for such time and as often as appears to be just.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.210. Oaths or affirmations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.210. Oaths or affirmations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.210. Oaths or affirmations (2023)
content:
(1)  Before performing their respective duties, military judges, general and special
      courts-martial members, trial counsel, defense counsel, reporters and interpreters
      shall take an oath or affirmation in the presence of the accused to perform their
      duties faithfully. The form of the oath or affirmation, the time and place of the taking thereof, the
      manner of recording the same, and whether the oath or affirmation shall be taken for
      all cases in which these duties are to be performed or for a particular case, shall
      be as prescribed in regulation or as provided by law.  These regulations may provide that an oath or affirmation to perform faithfully
      the duties as a military judge, trial counsel, or defense counsel may be taken at
      any time by any judge advocate or other person certified or designated to be qualified
      or competent for the duty, and if such an oath or affirmation is taken, it need not
      again be taken at the time the judge advocate or other person is detailed to that
      duty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.220. Former jeopardy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.220. Former jeopardy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.220. Former jeopardy (2023)
content: (1)  No person may, without his consent, be tried a second time for the same offense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.250. Admissibility of records of courts of inquiry
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.250. Admissibility of records of courts of inquiry
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.250. Admissibility of records of courts of inquiry (2023)
content:
(1)  In any case not extending to the dismissal of a commissioned officer, the sworn
      testimony, contained in the duly authenticated record of proceedings of a court of
      inquiry, of a person whose oral testimony cannot be obtained, may, if otherwise admissible
      under the rules of evidence, be read in evidence by any party before a court-martial
      if the accused was a party before the court of inquiry and if the same issue was involved
      or if the accused consents to the introduction of such evidence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.205. Challenges
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.205. Challenges
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.205. Challenges (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) The military judge and members of a general or special court-martial may
         be challenged by the accused or the trial counsel for cause stated to the court.  The military judge or the court shall determine the relevancy and validity of challenges
         for cause, and may not receive a challenge to more than one (1) person at a time.  Challenges by the trial counsel shall ordinarily be presented and decided before
         those by the accused are offered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.225. Pleas of the accused
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.225. Pleas of the accused
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.225. Pleas of the accused (2023)
content:
(1)  If an accused after arraignment makes any irregular pleading, or, after a plea
      of guilty, sets up matter inconsistent with the plea, or if it appears that the accused
      has entered the plea of guilty improvidently or through lack of understanding of its
      meaning and effect, or if the accused fails or refuses to plead, a plea of not guilty
      shall be entered in the record and the court shall proceed as though he had pleaded
      not guilty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.215. Statute of limitations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.215. Statute of limitations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.215. Statute of limitations (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this section, a person charged with any offense
      is not liable to be tried by court-martial or punished underKRS 35.070if the offense was committed more than three (3) years before the receipt of sworn
      charges and specifications by an officer exercising court-martial jurisdiction over
      the command or before the imposition of punishment underKRS 35.070.  There shall be no statute of limitations for the crimes set forth inKRS 35.678to35.690.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.230. Opportunity to obtain witnesses and other evidence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.230. Opportunity to obtain witnesses and other evidence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.230. Opportunity to obtain witnesses and other evidence (2023)
content:
The trial counsel, defense counsel, and the court-martial shall have equal opportunity
   to obtain witnesses and other evidence as prescribed by regulations and provided by
   law.  Process issued in court-martial cases to compel witnesses to appear and testify
   and to compel the production of other evidence shall apply the principles of law and
   the rules of courts-martial generally recognized in military criminal cases in the
   courts of the Armed Forces of the United States, but which may not be contrary to
   or inconsistent with this code.  Process shall run to any part of the United States, or the Territories, Commonwealths,
   and possessions, and may be executed by civil officers as prescribed by the laws of
   the place where the witness or evidence is located or of the United States.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.240. Contempt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.240. Contempt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.240. Contempt (2023)
content:
(1)  A military judge may punish for contempt any person who uses any disrespectful
      word, sign, or gesture in its presence, or who disturbs its proceedings by any riot
      or disorder.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.282. Deferment of sentences
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.282. Deferment of sentences
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.282. Deferment of sentences (2023)
content:
(1)  On application by an accused who is under sentence to confinement that has not
      been ordered executed, the convening authority or, if the accused is no longer under
      that person's jurisdiction, the person exercising general court-martial jurisdiction
      over the command to which the accused is currently assigned, may in that person's
      sole discretion defer service of the sentence of confinement.  The deferment shall terminate when the sentence is ordered executed.  The deferment may be rescinded at any time by the person who granted it or, if the
      accused is no longer under that person's jurisdiction, by the person exercising general
      court-martial jurisdiction over the command to which the accused is currently assigned.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.245. Depositions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.245. Depositions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.245. Depositions (2023)
content:
(1)  At any time after charges have been signed as provided inKRS 35.150, any party may take oral or written depositions unless the military judge hearing
      the case, or, if the case is not being heard, an authority competent to convene a
      court-martial for the trial of those charges forbids it for good cause.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.326. Action by the convening authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.326. Action by the convening authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.326. Action by the convening authority (2023)
content:
(1)  The findings and sentence of a court-martial shall be reported promptly to the
      convening authority after the announcement of the sentence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.235. Refusal to appear or testify
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.235. Refusal to appear or testify
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.235. Refusal to appear or testify (2023)
content: (1)  Any person not subject to this code, who:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.255. Voting and rulings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.255. Voting and rulings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.255. Voting and rulings (2023)
content:
(1)  Voting by members of a general or special court-martial on the findings and on
      the sentence shall be by secret written ballot.  The junior member of the court shall count the votes.  The count shall be checked by the president, who shall forthwith announce the result
      of the ballot to the members of the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.252. Defense of lack of mental responsibility
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.252. Defense of lack of mental responsibility
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.252. Defense of lack of mental responsibility (2023)
content:
(1)  It is an affirmative defense in a trial by court-martial that, at the time of
      the commission of the acts constituting the offense, the accused, as a result of severe
      mental disease or defect, was unable to appreciate the nature and quality or the wrongfulness
      of the acts.  Mental disease or defect does not otherwise constitute a defense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.260. Number of votes required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.260. Number of votes required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.260. Number of votes required (2023)
content:
(1)  No person may be convicted of an offense except as provided inKRS 35.225(2)or by the concurrence of two-thirds (2/3) of the members present at the time the
      vote is taken.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.280. Effective date of sentences
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.280. Effective date of sentences
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.280. Effective date of sentences (2023)
content:
(1)  Whenever a sentence of a court-martial, as lawfully adjudged and approved, includes
      a forfeiture of pay or allowances in addition to confinement not suspended, the forfeiture
      may apply to pay or allowances becoming due on or after the date the sentence is approved
      by the convening authority.  No forfeiture may extend to any pay or allowances accrued before that date.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.270. Record of trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.270. Record of trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.270. Record of trial (2023)
content:
(1)  Each general and special court-martial shall keep a separate record of the proceedings
      in each case before it, and the record shall be authenticated by the signature of
      the military judge.  If the record cannot be authenticated by the military judge by reason of his death,
      disability or absence, it shall be authenticated by the signature of the trial counsel
      or by that of a member, if the trial counsel is unable to authenticate it by reason
      of his or her death, disability, or absence.  In a court-martial consisting of only a military judge, the record shall be authenticated
      by the court reporter under the same conditions which would impose such a duty on
      a member under this subsection.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.277. Maximum limits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.277. Maximum limits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.277. Maximum limits (2023)
content:
(1)  The punishment which a court-martial may direct for an offense may not exceed
      such limits as prescribed by this code, but in no instance may a sentence exceed more
      than ten (10) years for a military offense, nor shall a sentence of death be adjudged.  A conviction by general court-martial of any military offense for which an accused
      may receive a sentence of confinement for more than one (1) year is a felony offense.  All other military offenses are misdemeanors.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.265. Court to announce action
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.265. Court to announce action
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.265. Court to announce action (2023)
content:
A court-martial shall announce its findings and sentence to the parties as soon as
   determined.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.275. Cruel and unusual punishments prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.275. Cruel and unusual punishments prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.275. Cruel and unusual punishments prohibited (2023)
content:
Punishment by flogging, or by branding, marking, or tattooing on the body, or any
   other cruel or unusual punishment may not be adjudged by a court-martial or inflicted
   upon any person subject to this code.  The use of irons, single or double, except for the purpose of safe custody, is prohibited.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.285. Execution of confinement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.285. Execution of confinement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.285. Execution of confinement (2023)
content:
(1)  A sentence of confinement adjudged by a court-martial, whether or not the sentence
      includes discharge or dismissal, and whether or not the discharge or dismissal has
      been executed, may be carried into execution by confinement in any place authorized
      by this code.  Persons so confined are subject to the same discipline and treatment as persons
      regularly confined or committed to that place.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.289. Sentences: reduction in enlisted grade upon approval
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.289. Sentences: reduction in enlisted grade upon approval
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.289. Sentences: reduction in enlisted grade upon approval (2023)
content:
(1)  A court-martial sentence of an enlisted member in a pay grade above E-1, as approved
      by the convening authority, shall reduce that member to pay grade E-1, effective on
      the date of that approval, when it includes:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.328. Appeal by the state
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.328. Appeal by the state
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.328. Appeal by the state (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) In a trial by court-martial in which a punitive discharge may be adjudged,
         the state may appeal the following, other than a finding of not guilty with respect
         to the charge or specification by the members of the court-martial, or by a judge
         in a bench trial so long as it is not made in reconsideration:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.325. Error of law; lesser included offense
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.325. Error of law; lesser included offense
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.325. Error of law; lesser included offense (2023)
content:
(1)  A finding or sentence of a court-martial may not be held incorrect on the ground
      of an error of law unless the error materially prejudices the substantial rights of
      the accused.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.327. Withdrawal of appeal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.327. Withdrawal of appeal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.327. Withdrawal of appeal (2023)
content:
(1)  In each case subject to appellate review under this code, the accused may file
      with the convening authority a statement expressly withdrawing the right of the accused
      to an appeal.  A withdrawal shall be signed by both the accused and his defense counsel and must
      be filed in accordance with appellate procedures as provided by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.294. Sentences: forfeiture of pay and allowances during confinement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.294. Sentences: forfeiture of pay and allowances during confinement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.294. Sentences: forfeiture of pay and allowances during confinement (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) A court-martial sentence described in paragraph (b) of this subsection shall
         result in the forfeiture of pay, or of pay and allowances, due that member during
         any period of confinement or parole.  The forfeiture pursuant to this article shall take effect on the date determined
         underKRS 35.282and may be deferred as provided by that section.  The pay and allowances forfeited, in the case of a general court-martial, shall
         be all pay and allowances due that member during that period and, in the case of a
         special court-martial, shall be two-thirds (2/3) of all pay due that member during
         that period.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.329. Rehearings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.329. Rehearings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.329. Rehearings (2023)
content:
Each rehearing under this code shall take place before a court-martial composed of
   members who were not members of the court-martial which first heard the case.  Upon a rehearing the accused may not be tried for any offense of which the accused
   was found not guilty by the first court-martial, and no sentence in excess of or more
   severe than the original sentence may be approved, unless the sentence is based upon
   a finding of guilty of an offense not considered upon the merits in the original proceedings,
   or unless the sentence prescribed for the offense is mandatory.  If the sentence approved after the first court-martial was in accordance with a
   pretrial agreement and the accused at the rehearing changes a plea with respect to
   the charges or specifications upon which the pretrial agreement was based, or otherwise
   does not comply with the pretrial agreement, the approved sentence as to those charges
   or specifications may include any punishment not in excess of that lawfully adjudged
   at the first court-martial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.355. Restoration
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.355. Restoration
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.355. Restoration (2023)
content:
(1)  Under such regulations as may be prescribed, all rights, privileges, and property
      affected by an executed part of a court-martial sentence which has been set aside
      or disapproved, except an executed dismissal or discharge, shall be restored unless
      a new trial or rehearing is ordered and such executed part is included in a sentence
      imposed upon the new trial or rehearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.336. Execution of sentence; suspension of sentence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.336. Execution of sentence; suspension of sentence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.336. Execution of sentence; suspension of sentence (2023)
content:
(1)  If the sentence of the court-martial extends to dismissal or a dishonorable or
      bad-conduct discharge and if the right of the accused to appellate review is not waived,
      and an appeal is not withdrawn underKRS 35.327, that part of the sentence extending to dismissal or a dishonorable or bad-conduct
      discharge may not be executed until there is a final judgment as to the legality of
      the proceedings.  A judgment as to the legality of the proceedings is final in such cases when review
      is completed by an appellate court prescribed inKRS 35.333, and is deemed final by the law of the state where the judgment was had.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.331. Review by the senior force judge advocate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.331. Review by the senior force judge advocate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.331. Review by the senior force judge advocate (2023)
content:
(1)  Each general and special court-martial case in which there has been a finding
      of guilty shall be reviewed by the senior force judge advocate, or a designee.  The senior force judge advocate or designee may not review a case under this subsection
      if that person has acted in the same case as an accuser, investigating officer, member
      of the court, military judge, or counsel or has otherwise acted on behalf of the prosecution
      or defense.  The senior force judge advocate's review shall be in writing and shall contain the
      following:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.332. Disposition of records after review by the convening authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.332. Disposition of records after review by the convening authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.332. Disposition of records after review by the convening authority (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise required by this code, all records of trial and related documents
   shall be transmitted and disposed of as prescribed by regulation and provided by law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.333. Review by state appellate authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.333. Review by state appellate authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.333. Review by state appellate authority (2023)
content:
Final decisions of a court-martial shall be deemed the statutory equivalent of a Circuit
   Court decision.  The appellate procedures to be followed shall be those provided by law for the appeal
   of criminal cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.350. Remission and suspension
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.350. Remission and suspension
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.350. Remission and suspension (2023)
content:
(1)  Any authority competent to convene, for the command in which the accused is serving
      or assigned, a court of the kind that imposed the sentence may remit or suspend any
      part or amount of the unexecuted part of any sentence, including all uncollected forfeitures
      other than a sentence approved by the Governor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.334. Appellate counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.334. Appellate counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.334. Appellate counsel (2023)
content:
(1)  The senior force judge advocate shall detail a judge advocate as appellate government
      counsel to represent the state in the review or appeal of cases specified inKRS 35.333and before any federal court when requested to do so by the state Attorney General.  Appellate government counsel must be a member in good standing of the bar of the
      highest court of the state to which the appeal is taken.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.345. Petition for a new trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.345. Petition for a new trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.345. Petition for a new trial (2023)
content:
At any time within two (2) years after approval by the convening authority of a court-martial
   sentence the accused may petition the adjutant general for a new trial on grounds
   of newly discovered evidence or fraud in the court-martial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.340. Vacation of suspension
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.340. Vacation of suspension
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.340. Vacation of suspension (2023)
content:
(1)  Before the vacation of the suspension of a special court-martial sentence, which
      as approved includes a bad-conduct discharge, or of any general court-martial sentence,
      the officer having special court-martial jurisdiction over the probationer shall hold
      a hearing on the alleged violation of probation. The probationer shall be represented at the hearing by military counsel if the probationer
      so desires.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.364. Leave required to be taken pending review of certain court-martial convictions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.364. Leave required to be taken pending review of certain court-martial convictions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.364. Leave required to be taken pending review of certain court-martial convictions (2023)
content:
Under regulations prescribed, an accused who has been sentenced by a court-martial
   may be required to take leave pending completion of action under this section if the
   sentence, as approved underKRS 35.326, includes an unsuspended dismissal or an unsuspended dishonorable or bad-conduct
   discharge.  The accused may be required to begin that leave on the date on which the sentence
   is approved underKRS 35.326or at any time after that date, and the leave may be continued until the date on
   which action under this section is completed or may be terminated at an earlier time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.367. Determination of lack of mental capacity or mental responsibility
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.367. Determination of lack of mental capacity or mental responsibility
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.367. Determination of lack of mental capacity or mental responsibility (2023)
content:
The determination of lack of mental capacity or mental responsibility shall be determined
   pursuant to Kentucky state law as well as regulations of the Department of Defense
   of the United States and the laws of the United States governing the Armed Forces
   of the United States as required under the Kentucky Constitution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.360. Finality of proceedings, findings, and sentences
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.360. Finality of proceedings, findings, and sentences
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.360. Finality of proceedings, findings, and sentences (2023)
content:
The appellate review of records of trial provided by this code, the proceedings, findings,
   and sentences of courts-martial as approved, reviewed, or affirmed as required by
   this code, and all dismissals and discharges carried into execution under sentences
   by courts-martial following the approval, review, or affirmation as required by this
   code, are final and conclusive.  Orders publishing the proceedings of courts-martial and all action taken pursuant
   to those proceedings are binding upon all departments, courts, agencies, and officers
   of the United States and the several states, subject only to action upon a petition
   for a new trial as provided inKRS 35.345and to action underKRS 35.350.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.440. Principals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.440. Principals

content: Any subject person is a principal who:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.445. Conviction of lesser included offense
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.445. Conviction of lesser included offense
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.445. Conviction of lesser included offense (2023)
content:
An accused may be found guilty of an offense necessarily included in the offense charged
   or of an attempt to commit either the offense charged or an offense necessarily included
   therein.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.442. Accessory after the fact
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.442. Accessory after the fact
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.442. Accessory after the fact (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who, knowing that an offense punishable by this code
   has been committed, receives, comforts, or assists the offender in order to hinder
   or prevent the person's apprehension, trial, or punishment shall be punished as a
   court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.474. Absence without leave
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.474. Absence without leave
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.474. Absence without leave (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code shall be punished as a court-martial directs who,

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.580. Resistance, flight, breach of arrest, and escape

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.471. Fraudulent enlistment, appointment, or separation
