path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.450. Attempts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.450. Attempts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.450. Attempts (2023)
content:
(1)  An act, done with specific intent to commit an offense under this code, amounting
      to more than mere preparation and tending, even though failing, to effect its commission,
      is an attempt to commit that offense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.451. Conspiracy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.451. Conspiracy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.451. Conspiracy (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who conspires with any other person to commit an offense
   under this code shall, if one or more of the conspirators does an act to effect the
   object of the conspiracy, be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.470. Solicitation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.470. Solicitation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.470. Solicitation (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person subject to this code who solicits or advises another or others to
      desert in violation ofKRS 35.473, or mutiny in violation ofKRS 35.577, shall, if the offense solicited or advised is attempted or committed, be punished
      with the punishment provided for the commission of the offense, but, if the offense
      solicited or advised is not committed or attempted, the person shall be punished as
      a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.472. Unlawful enlistment, appointment, or separation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.472. Unlawful enlistment, appointment, or separation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.472. Unlawful enlistment, appointment, or separation (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who effects an enlistment or appointment in or a separation
   from the state military forces of any person who is known to him or her to be ineligible
   for that enlistment, appointment, or separation because it is prohibited by law, regulation
   or order shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.4751. Missing movement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.4751. Missing movement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.4751. Missing movement (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who through neglect or design misses the movement
   of a ship, aircraft, or unit with which the person is required in the course of duty
   to move shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.481. Assaulting or willfully disobeying superior commissioned officer

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.486. Insubordinate conduct toward warrant officer, noncommissioned officer, or petty officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.486. Insubordinate conduct toward warrant officer, noncommissioned officer, or petty officer (2023)
content:
Any warrant officer or enlisted member is guilty of any of the following offenses

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.478. Disrespect toward superior commissioned officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.478. Disrespect toward superior commissioned officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.478. Disrespect toward superior commissioned officer (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who behaves with disrespect toward the person's superior
   commissioned officer shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.476. Contempt toward officials
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.476. Contempt toward officials
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.476. Contempt toward officials (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who uses contemptuous words against the President
   or the Governor which may detrimentally affect the morale or effectiveness of any
   unit of the state military forces shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.605. Subordinate compelling surrender
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.605. Subordinate compelling surrender
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.605. Subordinate compelling surrender (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who compels or attempts to compel the commander of
   the state military forces of the state, or of any other state, place, vessel, aircraft,
   or other military property, or of any body of members of the Armed Forces, to give
   it up to an enemy or to abandon it, or who strikes the colors or flag to an enemy
   without proper authority, shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.585. Releasing prisoner without proper authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.585. Releasing prisoner without proper authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.585. Releasing prisoner without proper authority (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who, without proper authority, releases any prisoner
   committed to his or her charge, or who through neglect or design suffers any such
   prisoner to escape, shall be punished as a court-martial may direct, whether or not
   the prisoner was committed in strict compliance with law.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.625. Aiding the enemy

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.575. Cruelty and maltreatment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.575. Cruelty and maltreatment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.575. Cruelty and maltreatment (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who is guilty of cruelty toward, or oppression or
   maltreatment of, any person subject to the person's orders shall be punished as a
   court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.491. Failure to obey order or regulation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.491. Failure to obey order or regulation

content: Any person subject to this code shall be punished as a court-martial may direct who:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.635. False official statements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.635. False official statements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.635. False official statements (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who, with intent to deceive, signs any false record,
   return, regulation, order, or other official document made in the line of duty, knowing
   it to be false, or makes any other false official statement made in the line of duty,
   knowing it to be false, shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.637. Military property; loss, damage, destruction, or wrongful disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.637. Military property; loss, damage, destruction, or wrongful disposition

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.630. Misconduct as prisoner

content:
Any person subject to this code shall be punished as a court-martial may direct who,

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.645. Driving under the influence or reckless driving
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.645. Driving under the influence or reckless driving
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.645. Driving under the influence or reckless driving (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who operates or is in physical control of any vehicle
   while under the influence of alcohol or any other substances or combination of substances
   which impair one's driving ability, or in a reckless or wanton manner, shall be punished
   as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.595. Noncompliance with procedural rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.595. Noncompliance with procedural rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.595. Noncompliance with procedural rules (2023)
content: Any person subject to this code shall be punished as a court-martial may direct who:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.600. Misbehavior before the enemy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.600. Misbehavior before the enemy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.600. Misbehavior before the enemy (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code shall be punished as a court-martial may direct who,

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.590. Unlawful detention
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.590. Unlawful detention
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.590. Unlawful detention (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who, except as provided by law or regulation, apprehends,
   arrests, or confines any person shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.654. Misbehavior of sentinel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.654. Misbehavior of sentinel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.654. Misbehavior of sentinel (2023)
content:
Any sentinel or lookout who is found drunk or sleeping upon his or her post or leaves
   it before being regularly relieved, shall be punished, if the offense is committed
   in a time of war, by confinement of not more than ten (10) years or other punishment
   as a court-martial may direct, but if the offense is committed at any other time,
   by such punishment as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.657. Dueling
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.657. Dueling
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.657. Dueling (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who fights or promotes, or is concerned in or connives
   at fighting a duel, or who, having knowledge of a challenge sent or about to be sent,
   fails to report the fact promptly to the proper authority, shall be punished as a
   court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.650. Drunk on duty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.650. Drunk on duty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.650. Drunk on duty (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code other than a sentinel or lookout, who is found drunk
   on duty, shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.620. Captured or abandoned property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.620. Captured or abandoned property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.620. Captured or abandoned property (2023)
content:
(1)  All persons subject to this code shall secure all property taken for the service
      of the United States or the state, and shall give notice and turn over to the proper
      authority without delay all captured or abandoned property in their possession, custody,
      or control.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.665. Riot or breach of peace
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.665. Riot or breach of peace
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.665. Riot or breach of peace (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who causes or participates in any riot or breach of
   the peace shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.614. Forcing a safeguard
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.614. Forcing a safeguard
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.614. Forcing a safeguard (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who forces a safeguard shall be punished as a court-martial
   may direct.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.609. Improper use of countersign
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.609. Improper use of countersign
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.609. Improper use of countersign (2023)
content:
Any person subject to this code who in time of war discloses the parole or countersign

   to receive and use the parole or countersign, a different parole or countersign from

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.810. Redress of injuries to property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.810. Redress of injuries to property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.810. Redress of injuries to property (2023)
content:
(1)  Whenever complaint is made to any commanding officer that willful damage has
      been done to the property of any person or that the person's property has been wrongfully
      taken by members of the state military forces, that person may, under such regulations
      prescribed, convene a board to investigate the complaint.  The board shall consist of from one (1) to three (3) commissioned officers and,
      for the purpose of that investigation, it has power to summon witnesses and examine
      them upon oath, to receive depositions or other documentary evidence, and to assess
      the damages sustained against the responsible parties.  The assessment of damages made by the board is subject to the approval of the commanding
      officer, and in the amount approved by that officer shall be charged against the pay
      of the offenders.  The order of such commanding officer directing charges herein authorized is conclusive
      on any disbursing officer for the payment to the injured parties of the damages so
      assessed and approved.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.815. Payment of fees, costs, and expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.815. Payment of fees, costs, and expenses

      reporters, and interpreters, fees for the service of process, the costs of collection,
      apprehension, detention and confinement, and all other necessary expenses of prosecution
      and the administration of military justice, not otherwise payable by any other source,
      shall be paid out of the military justice fund.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.807. Complaints of wrongs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.807. Complaints of wrongs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.807. Complaints of wrongs (2023)
content:
Any member of the state military forces who believes himself or herself wronged by
   his or her commanding officer, and, upon due application to that commander, is refused
   redress, may complain to any superior commissioned officer who shall forward the complaint
   to the officer exercising general court-martial jurisdiction over the officer against
   whom it is made.  The officer exercising general court-martial jurisdiction shall examine into the
   complaint and take proper measures for redressing the wrong complained of, and shall,
   as soon as possible, send to the adjutant general a true statement of that complaint,
   with the proceedings thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.730. General article
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.730. General article
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.730. General article (2023)
content:
Though not specifically mentioned in this code, all disorders and neglects to the
   prejudice of good order and discipline in the state military forces and all conduct
   of a nature to bring discredit upon the state military forces shall be taken cognizance
   of by a court-martial and punished at the discretion of a military court.  However, where a crime constitutes an offense that violates both this code and the
   criminal laws of the state where the offense occurs or criminal laws of the United
   States, jurisdiction of the military court must be determined in accordance withKRS 35.015(2).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 35. Military Justice›KY REV ST 35.822. Immunity for action of military courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 35. Military Justice › KY REV ST 35.822. Immunity for action of military courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 35.822. Immunity for action of military courts (2023)
content:
All persons acting under the provisions of this code, whether as a member of the military
   or as a civilian, shall be immune from any personal liability for any of the acts
   or omissions which they did or failed to do as part of their duties under this code.

   declared invalid for any reason, such declaration shall not affect the validity of
   the remaining portions of this code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs›KY REV ST 36.025. Deputy and assistant adjutant general for Army National Guard; Assistant adjutant general and chief-of-staff for Air National Guard; appointment, qualifications; compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs › KY REV ST 36.025. Deputy and assistant adjutant general for Army National Guard; Assistant adjutant general and chief-of-staff for Air National Guard; appointment, qualifications; compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 36.025. Deputy and assistant adjutant general for Army National Guard; Assistant adjutant general and chief-of-staff for Air National Guard; appointment, qualifications; compensation (2023)
content:
(1)  For the Army National Guard, the Governor, with the recommendation of the adjutant
      general, may appoint a deputy adjutant general and an assistant adjutant general,
      who at the time of appointment shall be at least thirty (30) years of age and shall
      be serving as a commissioned officer in the Kentucky National Guard.  The Governor shall issue a commission to each such deputy adjutant general and assistant
      adjutant general in the grade of brigadier general, provided such individual is qualified
      for federal recognition in that grade.  The adjutant general, in his or her discretion, may require either the deputy or
      assistant adjutant general to serve as a full-time employee in the Department of Military
      Affairs. The deputy adjutant general or assistant adjutant general who serves as an employee
      of the department may be compensated at the base rate of pay, not including subsistence
      and quarters allowances, as provided inKRS 38.205, or as prescribed inKRS 64.640.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs›KY REV ST 36.030. Adjutant general, deputy adjutant general, chief-of-staff, and assistant adjutant general; compatibility of office
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs › KY REV ST 36.030. Adjutant general, deputy adjutant general, chief-of-staff, and assistant adjutant general; compatibility of office
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 36.030. Adjutant general, deputy adjutant general, chief-of-staff, and assistant adjutant general; compatibility of office (2023)
content:
The office of the adjutant general, deputy adjutant general, chief-of-staff, or assistant
   adjutants general shall not necessarily be incompatible with or serve to vacate the
   commission in the Kentucky National Guard held by the officer appointed as the adjutant
   general, deputy adjutant general, chief-of-staff, or assistant adjutant general at
   the time of his or her appointment, nor shall it be incompatible with any office of
   the National Guard to which he or she might be promoted or appointed, nor interfere
   with or prevent his or her attending to the duties of the office held at the time
   or to which he or she may thereafter be promoted or appointed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title V. Military Affairs›Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs›KY REV ST 36.068. Bluegrass Station Division
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title V. Military Affairs › Chapter 36. Department of Military Affairs › KY REV ST 36.068. Bluegrass Station Division
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 36.068. Bluegrass Station Division (2023)

   and homeland security agencies, contractors, and associated and compatible operations,
   including the jobs which they bring to Kentucky.  Agency contracts, leases, and accounting procedures may additionally reflect the
   needs of these customers.  The Bluegrass Station Division shall be headed by a director experienced with federal
   contracts, construction, and installation operations, and maintenance funding requirements.
