title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Consolidation of Local Governments in Counties Containing Cities of the First Class › KY REV ST 67C.147. Taxes and services in area of former city of the first class; imposition of different tax rates; urban service tax district; modification of boundaries; reporting requirements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.147. Taxes and services in area of former city of the first class; imposition of different tax rates; urban service tax district; modification of boundaries; reporting requirements (2023)
content:
(1)  In order to maintain the tax structure, tax rates, or level of services in the
      area of the consolidated local government formerly comprising the city of the first
      class, the legislative council of a consolidated local government may provide in the
      manner described in this chapter for taxes and services within the area comprising
      the former city of the first class which are different from the taxes and services
      which are applicable in the remainder of the county.  These differences may include differences in tax rates upon the class of property
      which includes the surface of the land, differences in ad valorem tax rates upon personal
      property, and differences in tax rates upon insurance premiums.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.313. Police officers deemed qualified to continue duties and to be permanent employees; probationary officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.313. Police officers deemed qualified to continue duties and to be permanent employees; probationary officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.313. Police officers deemed qualified to continue duties and to be permanent employees; probationary officers (2023)
content:
(1)  All police officers of whatever rank and title of a consolidated local government
      police force shall be covered by the provisions of this section, except probationary
      officers.  All officers of a consolidated local government police force on active duty or service
      as of the effective date of an ordinance creating a consolidated local government
      police merit system and board, shall be deemed fit and qualified to continue their
      respective duties of employment on or for the consolidated local government police
      force without examination or further qualification.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.315. Application to chief, assistant chief, and officers above the rank of captain
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.315. Application to chief, assistant chief, and officers above the rank of captain
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.315. Application to chief, assistant chief, and officers above the rank of captain (2023)
content:
(1)  The provisions ofKRS 67C.303,67C.305,67C.307,67C.309, and67C.319shall not apply to the chief of police, assistant chief, and any officers above the
      rank of captain of the consolidated local government police force.  These officers shall be appointed by the mayor and shall not be considered covered
      under the employment protections of the merit board, except as provided in subsection
      (2) of this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.309. Meetings of board; secretary; minutes; records
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.309. Meetings of board; secretary; minutes; records
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.309. Meetings of board; secretary; minutes; records (2023)
content:
(1)  The board shall meet at least once every two (2) calendar months and minutes
      of each meeting shall be kept.

Soliciting and receiving political contributions; appointment or promotion for political service; discipline for failure to make political contribution; opinions and beliefs; political or religious controversies; political activity prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.317. Soliciting and receiving political contributions; appointment or promotion for political service; discipline for failure to make political contribution; opinions and beliefs; political or religious controversies; political activity prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.317. Soliciting and receiving political contributions; appointment or promotion for political service; discipline for failure to make political contribution; opinions and beliefs; political or religious controversies; political activity prohibited (2023)
content:
(1)  No officer while on duty or in uniform covered by the provisions ofKRS 67C.301to67C.327shall directly or indirectly solicit or receive or be in any manner concerned in
      receiving, soliciting, or publicizing any assessment, gift, subscription, or contribution
      to or for any political party or candidate for public office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.321. Actions taken by chief against officers; written statement; answer; citizen charges of misconduct
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.321. Actions taken by chief against officers; written statement; answer; citizen charges of misconduct
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.321. Actions taken by chief against officers; written statement; answer; citizen charges of misconduct (2023)
content:
(1)  Any officer may be removed, suspended for a period not to exceed thirty (30)
      days, laid-off, or reduced in grade by the chief for any cause which promotes the
      efficiency of the services, but before any such action is taken by the chief against
      any officer, the chief shall furnish the officer concerned with a written statement
      of the reasons why the described action is being taken.  The officer may be reduced, removed, suspended for a period not to exceed thirty
      (30) days, or laid-off from the date the written statement of reasons is served upon
      her or him.  Each officer removed, suspended for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days, laid-off,
      or reduced in grade shall be allowed a period of ten (10) days within which the officer
      may file a written answer to the charges and the reasons which caused her or his suspension,
      removal, or reduction.  This answer shall be made a part of the official records of the police department.  No trial or examination of witnesses shall be required in any such case except at
      the discretion of the chief.  The chief shall likewise furnish a copy of the written charges and reasons for her
      or his action to the board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.311. Mayor's certification of information on police officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.311. Mayor's certification of information on police officers (2023)
content:
Within thirty (30) days after the creation of a merit board underKRS 67C.301to67C.327, the mayor shall certify to the board the names, rank, rate of pay, and the seniority
   of every officer on the police force as of the effective date of the ordinance creating
   the board.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.319. Rules for qualification, appointment, and discipline of officers; chief examiner; promotional examinations; review of results; filling promotional vacancies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.319. Rules for qualification, appointment, and discipline of officers; chief examiner; promotional examinations; review of results; filling promotional vacancies (2023)
content:
(1)  Every consolidated local government police force merit system board created shall
      make, promulgate, and when necessary, amend rules for the qualifications, original
      appointment, probation, promotion, demotion, transfer, lay-off, reinstatement, suspension,
      and removal of the officers covered byKRS 67C.303,67C.305,67C.307, and67C.309.  No rule or regulation made, promulgated, or amended by any consolidated local government
      police force merit system board shall be inconsistent with the express provisions
      of this chapter.  The board shall publish its rules and any amendments and shall supply certified
      copies to the mayor, legislative council, and the police chief and shall post a copy
      conspicuously in the office or place where the headquarters of the consolidated local
      government police is maintained.  The copies of the rules and amendments shall be distributed and posted in the manner
      prescribed within three (3) days after adoption.

content:

      officers of consolidated local governments of this Commonwealth, the following standards
      of conduct are stated as the intention of the General Assembly to deal fairly and
      set administrative due process rights for police officers of the consolidated local
      government and at the same time providing a means for redress by the citizens of the
      Commonwealth for wrongs allegedly done to them by police officers covered by this
      section:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.325. Rights of officer brought before board; subpoenas
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.325. Rights of officer brought before board; subpoenas
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.325. Rights of officer brought before board; subpoenas (2023)
content:
Procedural due process shall be afforded to any police officer brought before the
   board.  The officer shall be given a prompt hearing by the board, have an opportunity to
   confront his or her accusers, and have the privilege of presenting the board with
   evidence.  The board shall have the power to issue subpoenas attested in the name of its chairman,
   to compel the attendance of witnesses, to compel the production of documents and other
   documentary evidence, and so far as practicable, conduct the hearing within the Kentucky
   Rules of Civil Procedure.  Upon a showing of proper need, the board shall issue subpoenas to compel the attendance
   of witnesses, or to compel the production of documents and other documentary evidence
   for the benefits of the officer or the chief at the request of the officer or the
   chief.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Promotional lists in existence upon establishment of consolidated local government; merit board
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.327. Promotional lists in existence upon establishment of consolidated local government; merit board (2023)
content:
Upon the establishment of a consolidated local government merit board, the existing
   or currently promulgated promotional lists of the merit and civil service boards of
   the previously existing county and city of the first class governments shall remain
   in effect until their normal expiration date, or no longer than two (2) years after
   the effective date of the ordinance required to be enacted byKRS 67C.303.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class›Police Force Merit System in Consolidated Local Government›KY REV ST 67C.329. Minimum age required to attend basic training course

Minimum age required to attend basic training course
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.329. Minimum age required to attend basic training course (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person who is at least twenty (20) years of age shall be eligible to be employed
      by a consolidated local government police force for the purpose of attending a basic
      training course as defined inKRS 15.310if he or she will be twenty-one (21) years of age at the time of becoming certified
      underKRS 15.380to15.404.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.402. Employees' right to organize for the purpose of collective bargaining; mayor to represent consolidated local government (2023)
content:
(1)  Police officers of a consolidated local government shall have, and shall be protected
      in the exercise of, the right of self-organization, to form, join, or assist any labor
      organization, to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing
      on questions of wages, hours, and other conditions of employment free from interference,
      restraint, or coercion.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.404. Duty to bargain collectively (2023)
content:
The consolidated local government and the labor organization that has been designated
   as the exclusive representative of police officers in an appropriate unit, through
   appropriate officials or their representatives, shall have the authority and the duty
   to bargain collectively.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 67C. Restructure of Local Government in County Containing City of First Class › Collective Bargaining for Police Officers in Consolidated Local Government › KY REV ST 67C.416. Consolidated local government to withhold dues and deliver to bargaining unit
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.416. Consolidated local government to withhold dues and deliver to bargaining unit (2023)
content:
Subject to the requirements set forth inKRS 336.135, upon the written authorization of any police officers within a bargaining unit,
   the consolidated local government shall deduct from the payroll of the police officer
   the monthly amount of dues as certified by the secretary of the exclusive bargaining
   representative and shall deliver the same to the treasurer of the exclusive bargaining
   representative.

Petition for fact-finding panel upon deadlock; hearings; findings; expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.412. Petition for fact-finding panel upon deadlock; hearings; findings; expenses (2023)
content:
(1)  If, after a reasonable period, but in no event less than thirty (30) days, of
      negotiations over the terms of a new collective bargaining agreement or modifications
      in an existing agreement, the parties to the negotiations are deadlocked, either party
      or the parties jointly may petition the cabinet, by certified mail, return receipt
      requested, or by registered mail, to initiate fact-finding.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 67C.418. Police officer or labor organization not to participate in strike (2023)
content:
No police officer of a consolidated local government shall engage in, and no police
   officer labor organization shall sponsor or condone, any strike.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 68. County Finance and County Treasurer›KY REV ST 68.001. Definition of state local finance officer

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 68.001. Definition of state local finance officer (2023)
content:
As used in this chapter and other provisions of law, “state local finance officer” shall mean the commissioner of the Department for Local Government, or his agent
   designated in writing with the approval of the Governor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.010. Special oath of sheriff

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.010. Special oath of sheriff (2023)
content:
(1)  In addition to the oath prescribed in the Constitution, every sheriff shall take
      the following oath:  “I, A B, do swear that I will do right, as well to the poor as
      to the rich, in all things belonging to my office as sheriff;  that I will do no wrong
      to any one for any gift, reward or promise, nor for favor or hatred, and in all things
      I will faithfully and impartially execute the duties of my office according to the
      best of my skill and judgment, so help me God.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.040. Deputy's acts and omissions; liability for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.040. Deputy's acts and omissions; liability for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.040. Deputy's acts and omissions; liability for (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall be liable for the acts or omissions of his deputies;  except that,
   the office of sheriff, and not the individual holder thereof, shall be liable under
   this section.  When a deputy sheriff omits to act or acts in such a way as to render his principal
   responsible, and the latter discharges such responsibility, the deputy shall be liable
   to the principal for all damages and costs which are caused by the deputy's act or
   omission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.020. General bond of sheriff; minimum; record
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.020. General bond of sheriff; minimum; record
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.020. General bond of sheriff; minimum; record (2023)
content:
(1)  The sheriff shall execute a bond for the faithful performance of the duties of
      his or her office.  This bond shall be in addition to the bond required of him or her byKRS 134.230and shall be a minimum of ten thousand dollars ($10,000), with sureties approved
      by the fiscal court, which shall enter the approval in its minutes and shall record
      the bond with the county clerk.  The fiscal court shall require the sheriff to renew this bond annually, and more
      often if it deems proper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.030. Deputy sheriffs; certified court security officers; nonsworn personnel; participation in Law Enforcement Foundation Program
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.030. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.030. Deputy sheriffs; certified court security officers; nonsworn personnel; participation in Law Enforcement Foundation Program (2023)
content:
(1)  The sheriff may appoint his or her own deputies and may revoke the appointment
      at his or her pleasure, except where that revocation is prohibited by the provisions
      ofKRS 70.260to70.273.  Any law to the contrary notwithstanding, a sheriff may appoint a deputy who resides
      outside the Commonwealth.  In a county containing a consolidated local government or city of the first class
      with a deputy sheriff merit board, the term of office of a deputy shall continue from
      sheriff to sheriff unless a deputy is removed according to the provisions ofKRS 70.260to70.273.  Before any deputy executes the duties of his or her office, he or she shall take
      the oath required to be taken by the sheriff.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.036. Uniforms for sheriffs, deputies, and court security officers; use; expense, how paid (2023)
content:
(1)  Sheriffs, bonded deputy sheriffs, and certified court security officers are authorized
      to wear approved uniforms while engaged in the performance of their duties.  As used herein, “approved uniforms” means those uniforms the design and color of which are officially approved by the
      Kentucky Sheriffs' Association.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.050. Person may be empowered to execute process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.050. Person may be empowered to execute process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.050. Person may be empowered to execute process (2023)
content:
(1)  A sheriff may, by writing, empower any person to execute an original or mesne
      process.  The person so empowered shall indorse his action on the instrument empowering him,
      and shall make affidavit to the truth of the indorsement, and attach the affidavit
      to the process and deliver the indorsement and affidavit to the sheriff or his deputy,
      to be returned to the proper office.  The indorsement shall have the same validity as if made by the sheriff.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.070. Execution and return of process; territorial jurisdiction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.070. Execution and return of process; territorial jurisdiction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.070. Execution and return of process; territorial jurisdiction (2023)
content:
Each sheriff shall execute and make due return of all notices and process which come
   to him and may be lawfully executed by him against any person or property in his county,
   or upon any river or creek adjoining his county.  He shall return the time of service of each notice and process, and the time of
   the levy of each execution, what levied on, when he sold the property seized, whom
   to and what for, and all other matters touching his duty, and shall subscribe his
   own name to the return, and, if he is a deputy, the name also of his principal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.075. Duty of sheriff to attend clerk's office
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.075. Duty of sheriff to attend clerk's office
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.075. Duty of sheriff to attend clerk's office (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the sheriff, or of one (1) of his deputies, to attend at the
   clerk's office daily--Sundays excepted--to receive any process that may be issued,
   and the clerk shall deliver to him any process remaining in his office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.062. School and student safety issues training encouraged; collaboration between sheriffs and local school districts encouraged
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.062. School and student safety issues training encouraged; collaboration between sheriffs and local school districts encouraged
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.062. School and student safety issues training encouraged; collaboration between sheriffs and local school districts encouraged (2023)
content:
(1)  The sheriff in each county is encouraged to receive training on issues pertaining
      to school and student safety, and shall be invited to meet annually with local school
      superintendents to discuss emergency response plans and emergency response concerns.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.076. Sheriff to indorse time of receiving process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.076. Sheriff to indorse time of receiving process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.076. Sheriff to indorse time of receiving process (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall indorse upon every summons, order of arrest or for the delivery
   of property, or of attachment, or injunction, in his hands, the day and hour of its
   reception by him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.060. Sheriff may command power of county
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.060. Sheriff may command power of county
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.060. Sheriff may command power of county (2023)
content:
Any sheriff, deputy sheriff or other like officer may command and take with him the
   power of the county, or a part thereof, to aid him in the execution of the duties
   of his office, and may summon as many persons as he deems necessary to aid him in
   the performance thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.079. Process not to be returned “prevented by force”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.079. Process not to be returned “prevented by force”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.079. Process not to be returned “prevented by force” (2023)
content:
It shall not be a sufficient return of any process, that the officer was prevented
   by force from executing it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.078. Breaking and entering buildings to execute order of arrest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.078. Breaking and entering buildings to execute order of arrest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.078. Breaking and entering buildings to execute order of arrest (2023)
content:
A sheriff having an order of arrest may enter any house or inclosure in which the
   party to be arrested may be, to arrest him;  and, if necessary for this purpose, may
   break the house or inclosure, having informed any person therein of his object;  or,
   if no person appear to whom such information can be given, after having publicly demanded
   the person to be arrested;  and, in either case, after having given sufficient time
   for the house or inclosure to be opened.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.080. Return of “not found”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.080. Return of “not found”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.080. Return of “not found” (2023)
content:
No officer shall return on any process that the defendant is not found within his
   county, unless he has actually been to the defendant's residence.  If the defendant is not found by the officer, or is not a resident of the county,
   the officer shall so return.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.077. Breaking and entering buildings to execute process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.077. Breaking and entering buildings to execute process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.077. Breaking and entering buildings to execute process (2023)
content:
A sheriff having an order of attachment, or for the delivery of property, may enter
   any building or inclosure containing the property, to take it;  and, if necessary
   for this purpose, may break the building or inclosure, having first publicly demanded
   the property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.085. Summons, return of; amendment if erroneous; penalty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.085. Summons, return of; amendment if erroneous; penalty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.085. Summons, return of; amendment if erroneous; penalty (2023)
content:
The return on a summons by an officer must state when and how the summons was served,
   and, if erroneous, may, with leave of the court, be amended according to the truth.  An officer who makes an erroneous return may be fined by the court not exceeding
   ten dollars ($10), and is liable to the person aggrieved for any injury caused by
   the error.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.090. Fines, forfeitures and fees; sheriff to collect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.090. Fines, forfeitures and fees; sheriff to collect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.090. Fines, forfeitures and fees; sheriff to collect (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall collect and account for all fines and forfeitures, and all officers'
   fees listed with him, and payable in his county, during his term of office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.100. Distrainable fee-bills; time allowed for collection
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.100. Distrainable fee-bills; time allowed for collection
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.100. Distrainable fee-bills; time allowed for collection (2023)
content:
Except as provided in subsection (1) ofKRS 64.050which is hereby made applicable to sheriffs, for two (2) years after the expiration
   of his term of office a sheriff and his deputies may collect his distrainable fee-bills,
   or those of any other officer, placed in his hands for collection during his term
   of office, and may make distress for the same within the time during which the fee
   retains its distrainable force, and, with his sureties, shall be liable to the person
   entitled to such fees.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.105. Money unpaid pending litigation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.105. Money unpaid pending litigation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.105. Money unpaid pending litigation (2023)
content:
Any money due an outgoing sheriff, other than compensation for the collection of taxes,
   remaining unpaid because of pending litigation shall be paid to the outgoing sheriff
   at the conclusion of the litigation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.092. Sheriff to negotiate collection fee with governing body for special tax, license, fee, or other charge collected with tax bill; limitation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.092. Sheriff to negotiate collection fee with governing body for special tax, license, fee, or other charge collected with tax bill; limitation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.092. Sheriff to negotiate collection fee with governing body for special tax, license, fee, or other charge collected with tax bill; limitation (2023)
content:
If the governing body of a city, county, urban-county government, consolidated local
   government, charter county, or unified local government levies or imposes a special
   tax, license, fee, or other charge to be collected as part of a tax bill by the sheriff,
   the sheriff shall negotiate a collection fee with the governing body.  The local government then shall set the negotiated collection fee, and the sheriff
   shall retain an amount not to exceed four and one-fourth percent (4.25%) of the special
   tax, license, fee, or other charge collected, if no other compensation is otherwise
   authorized.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.095. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.095. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.095. Fees for fingerprint impressions or photograph requested for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or personal use (2023)
content:
(1)  Sheriffs may charge a fee of ten dollars ($10) per set of fingerprint impressions
      taken and five dollars ($5) per photograph taken or copied when those services are
      requested by a person for professional, trade, or commercial purposes or for personal
      use.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.110. Execution of process after leaving office; rights of sureties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.110. Execution of process after leaving office; rights of sureties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.110. Execution of process after leaving office; rights of sureties (2023)
content:
(1)  When a sheriff dies or otherwise vacates his office, his deputies shall complete
      the execution of any process in his or their hands.  The sureties on the bond of the sheriff may require indemnity from the deputies
      in the manner prescribed for sureties in official or other bonds inKRS 62.090to62.120.  If the deputies fail to give the indemnity which the court requires, their powers
      to act as deputy shall be revoked by the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.140. Sheriff to attend and keep order in fiscal and Court of Justice courts; court security officers limited to Court of Justice courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.140. Sheriff to attend and keep order in fiscal and Court of Justice courts; court security officers limited to Court of Justice courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.140. Sheriff to attend and keep order in fiscal and Court of Justice courts; court security officers limited to Court of Justice courts (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall, by himself or deputy, attend and keep order in the fiscal court
   and any court of the Court of Justice and shall obey the orders of said courts, but
   a certified court security officer may only attend and keep order in any court of
   the Court of Justice and shall obey the orders of said court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.120. Money collected by sheriff; demand for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.120. Money collected by sheriff; demand for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.120. Money collected by sheriff; demand for (2023)
content:
A person entitled to money collected by a sheriff may demand it from the sheriff,
   by himself, his attorney, or any other person having his written authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.130. Sheriff to execute sentences of court and convey prisoners; coroner or jailer may act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.130. Sheriff to execute sentences of court and convey prisoners; coroner or jailer may act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.130. Sheriff to execute sentences of court and convey prisoners; coroner or jailer may act (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall, by himself or deputy, convey all persons to the penitentiary or
   juvenile facility condemned to confinement therein, and execute the sentence of the
   court in other criminal and penal cases.  But the court may order the coroner or jailer to act in the place of the sheriff
   in the discharge of those duties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.150. Sheriff to patrol roads; record of accidents
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.150. Sheriff to patrol roads; record of accidents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.150. Sheriff to patrol roads; record of accidents (2023)
content:
(1)  The sheriff of each county and his deputies shall patrol all public roads in
      his county, and direct, regulate and control the traffic on such roads so as to maintain
      a maximum degree of safety.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.170. Salary for services under KRS § 70.150
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.170. Salary for services under KRS § 70.150
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.170. Salary for services under KRS § 70.150 (2023)
content:
(1)  Each sheriff performing the duties required under the provisions ofKRS 70.150shall be allowed the amount of thirty-six hundred dollars ($3,600) annually payable
      out of the State Treasury at the rate of three hundred dollars ($300) per month for
      such services.  The first such monthly payment shall be for the month of July, 1966, and the check
      therefor shall be forwarded to the sheriff concerned on or about the last working
      day of that month and each month thereafter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.280. Court security officers; duties; prohibited conduct

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.280. Court security officers; duties; prohibited conduct (2023)
content: (1)  A certified court security officer shall be charged with the following duties:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.190. Obligations taken by officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.190. Obligations taken by officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.190. Obligations taken by officers (2023)
content:
Every obligation taken by any officer, by color of his office, from a person in his
   custody, in any manner or form other than that especially provided by law, shall be
   void, but unnecessary conditions in the obligations shall not vitiate it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.180. Breaking and entering for purpose of executing writs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.180. Breaking and entering for purpose of executing writs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.180. Breaking and entering for purpose of executing writs (2023)
content:
(1)  A sheriff or other officer may, in the execution of a writ of habere facias possessionem,
      or writ of seizin, break open either the outer or inner door of a dwelling or any
      other house on the premises, during the daytime.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.200. Elisor; how appointed; term of office; powers; compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.200. Elisor; how appointed; term of office; powers; compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.200. Elisor; how appointed; term of office; powers; compensation (2023)
content:
(1)  If the office of sheriff is vacant in any county, the Circuit Judge may appoint
      a citizen of the county to act as elisor.  The elisor shall hold his office for one (1) year or until a sheriff is qualified,
      unless removed by the Circuit Judge.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.260. Option for county to create deputy sheriff merit board; expenses; membership; meetings; exclusion of certain deputy sheriffs who serve in policy-making positions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.260. Option for county to create deputy sheriff merit board; expenses; membership; meetings; exclusion of certain deputy sheriffs who serve in policy-making positions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.260. Option for county to create deputy sheriff merit board; expenses; membership; meetings; exclusion of certain deputy sheriffs who serve in policy-making positions (2023)
content:
(1)  The primary legislative body of each county may enact an ordinance creating a
      deputy sheriff merit board, which shall be charged with the duty of holding hearings,
      public and executive, in disciplinary matters concerning deputy sheriffs.  For the purpose ofKRS 70.260to70.273, the primary legislative body of each county that does not have an urban-county,
      consolidated local government, or charter county government shall be the fiscal court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.261. Adoption of rules; certified copies; subjects addressed; issuance of additional rules; repeal or amendment of existing rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.261. Adoption of rules; certified copies; subjects addressed; issuance of additional rules; repeal or amendment of existing rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.261. Adoption of rules; certified copies; subjects addressed; issuance of additional rules; repeal or amendment of existing rules (2023)
content:
(1)  When a county creates a deputy sheriff merit board, the board shall issue, and
      publish within forty-eight (48) hours after their adoption, rules that are not inconsistent
      with the provisions ofKRS 70.260to70.273.  The board shall provide a certified copy of the rules to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.263. Training requirements for counties having deputy sheriff merit board; training for deputy sheriff providing security service to the courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.263. Training requirements for counties having deputy sheriff merit board; training for deputy sheriff providing security service to the courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.263. Training requirements for counties having deputy sheriff merit board; training for deputy sheriff providing security service to the courts (2023)
content:
(1)  Each person serving as a covered deputy sheriff on the effective date of an ordinance
      that creates a deputy sheriff merit board for the county in which he serves shall
      have successfully completed, within one (1) year following the effective date of that
      ordinance, a basic training course as established byKRS 15.440at a school certified or recognized by the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council.  Training approved by the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council received before the effective
      date of the ordinance may be used to satisfy all or part of this requirement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.210. Mobile radio communication equipment for sheriffs and deputies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.210. Mobile radio communication equipment for sheriffs and deputies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.210. Mobile radio communication equipment for sheriffs and deputies (2023)
content:
The fiscal court of any county may purchase mobile radio communication equipment for
   the use of the sheriff and deputies of that county if it deems the purchase of such
   equipment to be to the best interest of the county, considering the county finances
   and other permissible expenditures.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Sheriffs›KY REV ST 70.155. Motor vehicle impoundment; handling and storage fees; challenge to validity of impoundment; hearing; appeal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Sheriffs › KY REV ST 70.155. Motor vehicle impoundment; handling and storage fees; challenge to validity of impoundment; hearing; appeal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.155. Motor vehicle impoundment; handling and storage fees; challenge to validity of impoundment; hearing; appeal (2023)
content: (1)  As used in this section, “hearing board” or “board” means a body:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.262. Collective bargaining for deputy sheriffs in merit system in county containing a consolidated local government or a city of first class; prohibition against strikes; employment contract with sheriff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.262. Collective bargaining for deputy sheriffs in merit system in county containing a consolidated local government or a city of first class; prohibition against strikes; employment contract with sheriff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.262. Collective bargaining for deputy sheriffs in merit system in county containing a consolidated local government or a city of first class; prohibition against strikes; employment contract with sheriff (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided inKRS 336.130, in any county containing a consolidated local government or city of the first class
      that has adopted a merit system underKRS 70.260to70.273, deputies subject to the merit system may organize, form, join, or participate in
      organizations in order to engage in lawful concerted activities for the purpose of
      collective bargaining or other mutual aid and protection, and to bargain collectively
      through a representative of their own free choice.  Deputies shall also have the right to refrain from any or all of these activities
      but shall be subject to the lawful provisions of any collective bargaining agreement
      entered into under this section.  Strikes by deputies of any collective bargaining unit shall be prohibited at any
      time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Employment Contracts›KY REV ST 70.292. Sheriff may employ retired police officer; qualifications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Employment Contracts › KY REV ST 70.292. Sheriff may employ retired police officer; qualifications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.292. Sheriff may employ retired police officer; qualifications (2023)
content:
(1)  A county police department or county sheriff's office in the Commonwealth of
      Kentucky may employ police officers who have retired under the State Police Retirement
      System, Kentucky Employees Retirement System, or the County Employees Retirement System
      as provided byKRS 70.291to70.293.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.265. Deputy sheriff merit boards to employ chief examiner; duties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.265. Deputy sheriff merit boards to employ chief examiner; duties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.265. Deputy sheriff merit boards to employ chief examiner; duties (2023)
content:
(1)  Deputy sheriff merit boards shall employ a chief examiner who shall operate under
      the board's sole supervision.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Employment Contracts›KY REV ST 70.291. Definition of “police officer” for KRS 70.291. to § 70.293
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Employment Contracts › KY REV ST 70.291. Definition of “police officer” for KRS 70.291. to § 70.293
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.291. Definition of “police officer” for KRS 70.291. to § 70.293 (2023)
content: As used inKRS 70.291to70.293, “police officer” shall have the same meaning as “police officer” inKRS 15.420and as “officer” inKRS 16.010.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.267. Prohibited conduct; construction of section; probationary period
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.267. Prohibited conduct; construction of section; probationary period
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.267. Prohibited conduct; construction of section; probationary period (2023)
content:
(1)  No deputy sheriff covered by the provisions ofKRS 70.260to70.273shall directly or indirectly solicit, receive, or be in any manner concerned in receiving,
      soliciting, or publicizing any assessment, gift, subscription, or contribution to
      or for any political party or candidate for public office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.270. Disciplinary and removal procedures by sheriff; charges by citizen
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.270. Disciplinary and removal procedures by sheriff; charges by citizen
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.270. Disciplinary and removal procedures by sheriff; charges by citizen (2023)
content:
(1)  Any deputy sheriff may be removed, suspended, or laid-off by the sheriff for
      any cause which will promote the efficiency of the department.  Except when an appointment is revoked during the probationary period described inKRS 70.267(5), the sheriff shall furnish a covered deputy with a written statement of the reason
      why the action was taken.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.273. Disciplinary and removal procedures by board; hearing; appeals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.273. Disciplinary and removal procedures by board; hearing; appeals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.273. Disciplinary and removal procedures by board; hearing; appeals (2023)
content:
(1)  The board may remove, suspend, lay off or discipline any deputy sheriff covered
      by the provisions ofKRS 70.260to70.273on written charges of misconduct preferred on its own initiative or the initiative
      of any citizen, but only after reasonable notice to the accused and after a complete
      public hearing at which the deputy accused shall have the right to be present, represented
      by counsel, and confronted by all of the witnesses preferring charges against him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.370. Precedence of levying and satisfying writs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.370. Precedence of levying and satisfying writs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.370. Precedence of levying and satisfying writs (2023)
content:
Executions, fee-bills, orders of witnesses' attendance, distress warrants and attachments,
   shall be levied and satisfied by the constable according to the priority of time in
   which they are placed in his hands.  The constable shall, in every case, indorse the time of reception.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.284. Failure or refusal of sheriff to provide court security services; contracts with units of local government
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.284. Failure or refusal of sheriff to provide court security services; contracts with units of local government
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.284. Failure or refusal of sheriff to provide court security services; contracts with units of local government (2023)
content:
(1)  In any county, if the sheriff fails or refuses to provide certified peace officers
      or certified security officers for the provision of security services to any court
      of the Court of Justice, then the Administrative Office of the Courts shall contract
      with a county, urban-county, charter county, consolidated local government, combined
      local government agency, or an agency of a city government to provide security services
      to any court of the Court of Justice in the county where the sheriff has failed or
      refused to provide such services.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Employment Contracts›KY REV ST 70.290. Employment contract for deputy sheriff or peace officer; reimbursement of law enforcement agency when deputy or peace officer accepts employment with another agency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Employment Contracts › KY REV ST 70.290. Employment contract for deputy sheriff or peace officer; reimbursement of law enforcement agency when deputy or peace officer accepts employment with another agency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.290. Employment contract for deputy sheriff or peace officer; reimbursement of law enforcement agency when deputy or peace officer accepts employment with another agency (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) City and county law enforcement agencies, including sheriff's offices, may,
         as a condition of employment, require a newly appointed deputy sheriff or peace officer
         who will participate in the Kentucky Law Enforcement Foundation Fund Program, authorized
         byKRS 15.410to15.510, to enter into an employment contract for a period of no longer than five (5) years
         from the date of graduation from the Department of Criminal Justice Training, or other
         training approved by the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards›KY REV ST 70.282. Provision of security services for Court of Justice, courthouses, and courtrooms limited to sheriff and Department of Kentucky State Police; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Deputy Sheriff Merit Boards › KY REV ST 70.282. Provision of security services for Court of Justice, courthouses, and courtrooms limited to sheriff and Department of Kentucky State Police; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.282. Provision of security services for Court of Justice, courthouses, and courtrooms limited to sheriff and Department of Kentucky State Police; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  No agency of a unit of local government, other than the sheriff, shall provide
      security services for the Court of Justice, a courthouse, or a courtroom unless the
      provision of the service is specifically authorized by the Kentucky Revised Statutes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Employment Contracts›KY REV ST 70.294. Employment contract for law enforcement telecommunicator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Employment Contracts › KY REV ST 70.294. Employment contract for law enforcement telecommunicator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.294. Employment contract for law enforcement telecommunicator (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “law enforcement agency” means a city, county, consolidated local government, urban-county government, charter
      county government, unified local government, or state law enforcement agency, and
      includes a sheriff's office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Employment Contracts›KY REV ST 70.293. Terms of employment of retired police officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Employment Contracts › KY REV ST 70.293. Terms of employment of retired police officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.293. Terms of employment of retired police officer (2023)
content: (1)  Individuals employed underKRS 70.291to70.293shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.360. Return of “not found”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.360. Return of “not found”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.360. Return of “not found” (2023)
content:
No constable shall return on any process that the defendant is not found, unless he
   has actually been to the defendant's residence and has not found him, if the defendant
   is a resident of the county.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.325. Powers and duties of constable (Effective until July 1, 2025)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.325. Powers and duties of constable (Effective until July 1, 2025)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.325. Powers and duties of constable (Effective until July 1, 2025) (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, for any constable or deputy
      constable taking office after January 1, 2023, who was not a constable or deputy constable
      in the preceding four (4) year term of office, the powers and duties of the office
      of constable shall not include the general powers of a peace officer or police officer.  The powers and duties of the office of constable shall include:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.340. Powers after leaving office
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.340. Powers after leaving office
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.340. Powers after leaving office (2023)
content:
(1)  A constable who vacates or is removed from office shall return and account for
      all claims, processes and papers in his hands, in the same manner as if he had continued
      in office, or he may be required by the county judge/executive to deliver them to
      his successor or to the county judge/executive.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›County Police Force and Auxiliary›KY REV ST 70.540. County police force authorized; jurisdiction; appointment; qualifications; term; oath; officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › County Police Force and Auxiliary › KY REV ST 70.540. County police force authorized; jurisdiction; appointment; qualifications; term; oath; officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.540. County police force authorized; jurisdiction; appointment; qualifications; term; oath; officers (2023)
content:
The county judges/executive of the respective counties shall have and are hereby given
   the power, jurisdiction and authority to establish, appoint and maintain a county
   police force within their respective counties, all of the members and officers of
   which shall have and are hereby given jurisdiction coextensive with the whole county
   for which they are appointed.  Such police force may consist of a chief and such member, rank and grade subordinate
   to the chief, and such clerical and skilled employees as the county judge/executive
   shall deem proper.  All of the members and employees of the county police force shall be appointed by
   the county judge/executive and shall serve for a term of one (1) year from the date
   of their respective appointments, unless sooner removed by the county judge/executive
   for neglect of duty or improper conduct.  All members of the force shall be citizens of the United States not less than twenty-one
   (21) years of age and residents of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.  None but discreet and sober persons shall be appointed to any position on said county
   police force.  Each of the members of the said county police force shall take an oath, before the
   county judge/executive of their county, to faithfully, impartially and diligently
   perform the duties of their respective offices.  Provided, however, that the chief officer of the county police force of any county
   may be designated, in the discretion of the county judge/executive of said county,
   as captain or any other appropriate title, and such county police force in any county
   may consist of one (1) or more commanding officers, as the county judge/executive
   of such county may deem proper or adequate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.320. Deputy constables in authorized counties; qualifications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.320. Deputy constables in authorized counties; qualifications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.320. Deputy constables in authorized counties; qualifications (2023)
content: (1)  As used in this section:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.310. Bond and oath of constable and deputy constable; minimum; record
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.310. Bond and oath of constable and deputy constable; minimum; record
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.310. Bond and oath of constable and deputy constable; minimum; record (2023)
content:
(1)  Every constable and each deputy constable appointed underKRS 70.320shall execute a bond in an amount determined sufficient by the fiscal court or the
      legislative council of the urban-county government or legislative body of a consolidated
      local government, the minimum amount of which shall be ten thousand dollars ($10,000),
      with good sureties approved by the fiscal court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.400. Claims placed in hands; not to become interested in
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.400. Claims placed in hands; not to become interested in
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.400. Claims placed in hands; not to become interested in (2023)
content:
No constable shall buy, or become interested by contract in, any claim against another
   put into his hands for collection.  Any such purchase or contract may be relied on by a defendant in bar of a suit on
   such claim, or as a ground for vacating a judgment or quashing an execution thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.350. Execution of process; jurisdiction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.350. Execution of process; jurisdiction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.350. Execution of process; jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(1)  Constables may execute warrants where specifically authorized by statute, and
      summons, subpoenas, attachments, notices, rules and orders of court in all criminal,
      penal, and civil cases, and shall return all process placed in his or her hands to
      the courts or persons issuing them, on or before the return day, noting the time of
      execution on them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Guards›KY REV ST 70.610. Guards for safekeeping prisoner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Guards › KY REV ST 70.610. Guards for safekeeping prisoner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.610. Guards for safekeeping prisoner (2023)
content:
When the circuit judge believes that the safekeeping of a prisoner confined in his
   county under a charge of felony requires that a guard be kept over him, he shall make
   the order of record to that effect, and direct the number of guards to be summoned,
   by whom, and under whose control they shall be placed.  Each guard so summoned and performing duty shall be allowed one dollar ($1) per
   day, to be paid out of the county treasury.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 71. Jailer›KY REV ST 71.010. Bond and oath of jailer; minimum; record
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 71. Jailer › KY REV ST 71.010. Bond and oath of jailer; minimum; record
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 71.010. Bond and oath of jailer; minimum; record (2023)
content:
The jailer shall take the oath prescribed by the Constitution and execute bond to
   the Commonwealth in the minimum amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000), with sureties
   approved by the fiscal court, which shall record the approval in its minutes and shall
   file the bond with the county clerk.  No coroner, sheriff, sheriff's deputy, county judge/executive or Circuit Judge,
   county or circuit clerk, or attorney shall be surety for the jailer on his official
   bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.380. Staying or delay of process; when constable excused by
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.380. Staying or delay of process; when constable excused by
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.380. Staying or delay of process; when constable excused by (2023)
content:
It shall be no defense to any action or motion against a constable or his sureties
   that the process or other authority under which he acted, or it was his duty to act,
   was stayed or in any manner delayed, unless it was done in writing signed by the plaintiff,
   his agent or attorney.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.410. Motion against constable or deputy constable; notice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.410. Motion against constable or deputy constable; notice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.410. Motion against constable or deputy constable; notice (2023)
content:
Recovery on the constable's or deputy constable's bond may be had by motion.  At least ten (10) days' notice, specifying the grounds of the motion, shall be given.  If not executed on all persons liable on the bond, the motion may proceed against
   those notified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.420. Recovery for failure to pay over money collected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.420. Recovery for failure to pay over money collected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.420. Recovery for failure to pay over money collected (2023)
content:
(1)  For constable's failure, upon proper demand, to pay over money collected by him,
      the plaintiff shall recover the amount collected by the officer, and interest from
      the time of demand, and ten percent (10%) damages thereon, and the costs of his motion
      or action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.440. False entries in books and reports
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.440. False entries in books and reports
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.440. False entries in books and reports (2023)
content:
No constable or deputy constable in any county shall make, participate in making,
   or knowingly permit another to make a false entry, or omit, or participate in or permit
   the omission of, any proper entry, in his or her official books or records, or knowingly
   make or participate in the making of any false statement or report, including reports
   required underKRS 70.430, or knowingly take any action with intent to cheat or defraud the state, the county,
   or any person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force›Constables›KY REV ST 70.390. To collect, return and receipt for claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units › Chapter 70. Sheriffs, Constables, and County Police Force › Constables › KY REV ST 70.390. To collect, return and receipt for claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 70.390. To collect, return and receipt for claim (2023)
content:
(1)  The constable shall collect all claims placed in his hands for collection, when
      by proper diligence they may be collected.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title IX. Counties, Cities, and Other Local Units›Chapter 71. Jailer›KY REV ST 71.030. Jailer to keep jail clean and warm
