content:
(1)  The corporation is hereby authorized to provide for the issuance of refunding
      obligations for the purpose of refunding any obligations then outstanding which shall
      have been issued under the provisions of this chapter, including the payment of any
      redemption premium thereon and any interest accrued or to accrue to the date of redemption
      of such obligations and, if deemed advisable by the corporation, for any corporate
      purpose of the corporation.  The issuance of such obligations, the maturities and other details thereof, the
      rights of the holders thereof, and the rights, duties and obligations of the corporation
      in respect of the same shall be governed by the provisions of this chapter which relate
      to the issuance of obligations, insofar as such provisions may be appropriate therefor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.180. Exemption from personal liability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.180. Exemption from personal liability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.180. Exemption from personal liability (2023)
content:
No member or other officer of the corporation shall be subject to any personal liability
   or accountability by reason of his execution of any obligations or the issuance thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.200. Corporation exempt from taxation; interest on bonds issued by corporation may be subject to federal income taxation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.200. Corporation exempt from taxation; interest on bonds issued by corporation may be subject to federal income taxation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.200. Corporation exempt from taxation; interest on bonds issued by corporation may be subject to federal income taxation (2023)
content:
The Kentucky Higher Education Student Loan Corporation has been duly created as an
   independent de jure municipal corporation and political subdivision of the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky.  As the corporation will in all respects be performing essential governmental and
   public functions, the corporation shall not be required to pay any taxes or assessments
   upon any of its property, real, personal, or mixed, nor upon the income therefrom;
   and bonds, notes or other obligations issued by the corporation under this chapter,
   the income thereon, and the transfer thereof, including any profit made on the sale
   thereof, shall at all times be exempt from taxation or assessment of any type by the
   Commonwealth, its agencies and departments, and by all political subdivisions within
   the state.  Nothing contained in this chapter shall preclude or prevent the authorization and
   issuance by the corporation from time to time of bonds, notes or other obligations,
   the receipt of interest on which may be subject to federal income taxation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.210. Conflicts of interest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.210. Conflicts of interest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.210. Conflicts of interest (2023)
content:
If any member, officer or employee of the corporation shall be interested either directly
   or indirectly, or shall be an officer or employee of or have an ownership interest
   in any firm or corporation interested directly or indirectly in any contract with
   the corporation, such interest shall be disclosed to the corporation and shall be
   set forth in the minutes of the corporation, and the member, officer or employee having
   such interest therein shall not participate on behalf of the corporation in the authorization
   of any such contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.230. Dissolution of corporation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.230. Dissolution of corporation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.230. Dissolution of corporation (2023)
content:
Upon termination or dissolution, all rights and properties of the corporation shall
   pass to and be vested in the Commonwealth of Kentucky, subject to the rights of lienholders
   and other creditors, unless the board of directors directs at such times that they
   be distributed among one (1) or more corporations, trusts, community chests, funds
   or foundations organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, scientific,
   literary, or educational purposes, no part of the net earnings of which inures to
   the benefit of any private shareholder, member or individual and no substantial part
   of whose activities consists of carrying on propaganda, or otherwise attempting to
   influence legislation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.260. REV STABLE Kentucky account
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.260. REV STABLE Kentucky account
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.260. REV STABLE Kentucky account (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “STABLE Kentucky account” means an account established by or for the benefit of an eligible individual, as
      that term is defined by26 U.S.C. sec. 529A, and established and maintained by the Commonwealth of Kentucky or pursuant to any
      agreement between the Commonwealth and any other state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.250. Student loan forgiveness program for graduates in energy-related fields
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.250. Student loan forgiveness program for graduates in energy-related fields
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.250. Student loan forgiveness program for graduates in energy-related fields (2023)
content:
(1)  It is the intent of the General Assembly to establish a student loan forgiveness
      program for individuals who receive a bachelor's degree or graduate degree from a
      Kentucky college or university after August 30, 2007, and who are employed in an energy-related
      field as engineers, engineering technologists, chemists, geologists, or hydrologists
      in Kentucky.  The loan forgiveness program shall be funded by the Commonwealth of Kentucky using
      state appropriations and shall be administered by the Kentucky Higher Education Student
      Loan Corporation.  All costs associated with the program shall be paid for by the Commonwealth of Kentucky,
      including the reimbursement of any expenses incurred by the corporation in its administration
      of the program.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.110. Bonds of officers to cover duties under bond issue
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.110. Bonds of officers to cover duties under bond issue
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.110. Bonds of officers to cover duties under bond issue (2023)
content:
The president and treasurer of the university shall each give bond with approved surety
   in a sum fixed by the board of aldermen of the city.  The bond shall be payable to the university and obligate the makers to perform faithfully
   the duties of their offices and faithfully account for and pay over all money or other
   thing of value that may come into their hands.  The bonds shall be kept in force during the time any money received from the bond
   issue provided for byKRS 165.080is being handled or administered by the university or its officers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.220. Chapter deemed supplemental to other laws
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.220. Chapter deemed supplemental to other laws
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.220. Chapter deemed supplemental to other laws (2023)
content:
The foregoing sections of this chapter shall be deemed to provide an additional and
   alternative method for the doing of the things authorized thereby and shall be regarded
   as supplemental and additional to powers conferred by other laws, and shall not be
   regarded as in derogation of any powers now existing;  provided, however, that the
   issuance of bonds or notes under the provisions of this chapter need not comply with
   the requirements of any other law applicable to the issuance of bonds or notes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.010. Definition of municipal university, college and junior college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.010. Definition of municipal university, college and junior college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.010. Definition of municipal university, college and junior college (2023)
content:
A municipal university, college or junior college as used in this chapter means any
   university, college or junior college established or supported in whole or in part
   by funds raised by municipal taxation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance›KY REV ST 164A.240. “Eligible borrower” defined; additional student loans permitted; garnishment; administrative regulations; bonds to finance loans; maximum annual loan amount
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 164A. Higher Education Finance › KY REV ST 164A.240. “Eligible borrower” defined; additional student loans permitted; garnishment; administrative regulations; bonds to finance loans; maximum annual loan amount
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 164A.240. “Eligible borrower” defined; additional student loans permitted; garnishment; administrative regulations; bonds to finance loans; maximum annual loan amount (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) As used in this section, the term “eligible borrower” means a student, a former student, or the parent of a dependent student or former
         student, who demonstrates an intention and capacity to repay an educational loan and
         meets the loan criteria established by the promulgation of administrative regulations
         by the corporation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.120. Employment of technical advisers and others for construction work
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.120. Employment of technical advisers and others for construction work
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.120. Employment of technical advisers and others for construction work (2023)
content:
The president and trustees of the university may employ such persons as they deem
   necessary, including architects and other technical advisers, to perform any work
   for which a bond issue has been provided.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.040. Payment of appropriation to university
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.040. Payment of appropriation to university
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.040. Payment of appropriation to university (2023)
content:
The funds appropriated by the board of aldermen of a city of the first class as provided
   inKRS 165.030may be paid to the treasurer of the university by the director of finance of the
   city in regular monthly installments.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.140. Financial and other reports concerning university
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.140. Financial and other reports concerning university
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.140. Financial and other reports concerning university (2023)
content:
The president and trustees of a municipal university in a city of the first class
   shall annually report to the mayor and the board of aldermen of the city what they
   do under the provisions ofKRS 165.080to165.130, and account for all funds received by them.  An annual report and audit of receipts and disbursements of funds received by the
   university underKRS 165.030to165.050shall be made in addition to other reports required by its charter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.050. Appropriation of funds other than taxes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.050. Appropriation of funds other than taxes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.050. Appropriation of funds other than taxes (2023)
content:
The board of aldermen of a city of the first class having a municipal university may
   devote to university purposes funds derived from other sources as well as from taxes
   levied for general city purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.015. Appropriation of city funds for postsecondary educational facilities and programs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.015. Appropriation of city funds for postsecondary educational facilities and programs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.015. Appropriation of city funds for postsecondary educational facilities and programs (2023)
content:
It shall be a public purpose for a city of any class to support postsecondary education
   through the appropriation of funds for postsecondary educational facilities located
   or to be located within the city and for postsecondary educational programs offered
   within the city.  Nothing in this section andKRS 165.160,165.165,165.180,165.190, and165.195shall create an obligation or liability for the Council on Postsecondary Education.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.080. Bond issue question may be submitted to voters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.080. Bond issue question may be submitted to voters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.080. Bond issue question may be submitted to voters (2023)
content:
The board of aldermen of any city of the first class may adopt an ordinance submitting
   to the voters of the city at any regular election held in the city the question of
   whether or not bonds of the city shall be issued for the benefit of the municipal
   university if the ordinance is filed with the county clerk not later than the second
   Tuesday in August preceding the regular election.  Authorization of the bond issue and submission of the question to the voters may
   be by one (1) ordinance and at one (1) election covering the entire amount of the
   bonds or it may be by different ordinances authorizing different elections at different
   times for parts of the total amount.  The ordinance shall provide the date and maturity of the bonds, the rate of interest
   they shall bear and the total amount to be then issued, and shall contain the necessary
   details with reference to the execution and delivery of the bonds, their denominations,
   coupons to be attached, and taxes to be levied to pay interest and to create a sinking
   fund to retire the bonds at maturity.  A failure of the voters at one (1) election to authorize a bond issue shall not
   prevent submission of the question of issuing bonds at subsequent elections.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.060. Appropriation of land for university
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.060. Appropriation of land for university
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.060. Appropriation of land for university (2023)
content:
The board of aldermen of a city of the first class may set apart or appropriate as
   a site for the buildings and grounds of its municipal university any public grounds
   of the city not specially appropriated or dedicated by ordinance to another use.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.090. Sale of bonds; disposition of proceeds
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.090. Sale of bonds; disposition of proceeds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.090. Sale of bonds; disposition of proceeds (2023)
content:
Bonds issued under authority ofKRS 165.080shall be placed under the control of the president and trustees of the university,
   who shall determine when and at what price they shall be sold, but no bonds shall
   be sold for less than par.  Any premium obtained from the bonds shall constitute a part of the sinking fund
   for their ultimate redemption.  The proceeds of the bonds shall be deposited to the credit of the university in
   the depositories that are selected for the deposit of the funds of the sinking fund
   commissioners of the city, upon the same agreement as to interest, and shall be withdrawn
   upon the checks of the treasurer of the university, countersigned by the president
   thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.030. Appropriation for university
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.030. Appropriation for university
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.030. Appropriation for university (2023)
content:
The board of aldermen of a city of the first class having a municipal university may
   make an annual appropriation from the general fund of the city for the support of
   such university.  Such appropriation shall be such sum as in the judgment of the board of aldermen
   shall, when supplemented by other income of the university, be reasonably necessary
   for such purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.175. Municipal college support district
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.175. Municipal college support district
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.175. Municipal college support district (2023)
content:
(1)  The fiscal court of a county containing a city with a population equal to or
      greater than twenty thousand (20,000) based upon the most recent federal decennial
      census that has a municipal college, having obtained the authorization of the legislative
      body of such city for the college to accept tax support from a municipal college support
      district and for appointment of three (3) members of the college board of trustees
      by the governing body of the district, may establish a municipal college support district
      consisting of the territory in the county outside the limits of the city in which
      is located the college.  The members of the fiscal court shall constitute the governing body of the district.  Subject to the provisions of subsection (2), the district may levy a tax of not
      less than five ($0.05) or more than fourteen cents ($0.14) on each one hundred dollars
      ($100) of the assessed valuation of all property in the district.  The funds raised by this tax shall be used solely to support the college.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.180. Appropriation of funds other than taxes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.180. Appropriation of funds other than taxes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.180. Appropriation of funds other than taxes (2023)
content:
Any city having a municipal college pursuant toKRS 165.160may devote to college purposes any funds or properties derived from sources other
   than taxes levied for special purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.100. Purposes for which proceeds may be used
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.100. Purposes for which proceeds may be used
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.100. Purposes for which proceeds may be used (2023)
content:
The money derived from the bonds issued under authority ofKRS 165.080shall be used to meet the needs of the university.  The authorized use includes the payment for real estate and buildings purchased
   or to be purchased, the erection and alteration of improvements, and the securing
   of proper equipment, but does not include the payment of salaries or operating expenses
   or the payment of any existing indebtedness incurred as an operating expense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.070. Condemnation, purchase or gift of land
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.070. Condemnation, purchase or gift of land
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.070. Condemnation, purchase or gift of land (2023)
content:
The board of trustees of a municipal university in a city of the first class may acquire,
   by purchase or gift, lands and improvements for the purpose of expanding the plant
   and extending the usefulness of the university, and when unable to agree with the
   owner of land and improvements necessary for the purposes of the university may proceed
   to condemn the land and improvements.  The condemnation proceedings shall be conducted in the manner provided in the Eminent
   Domain Act of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.210. Municipal junior colleges in designated cities; establishment and control of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.210. Municipal junior colleges in designated cities; establishment and control of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.210. Municipal junior colleges in designated cities; establishment and control of (2023)
content:
(1)  Boards of education of designated cities may establish or acquire by lawful conveyance
      municipal junior colleges for the purpose of promoting public education.  A college in a designated city shall not constitute a municipal junior college or
      receive support as provided inKRS 165.220to165.240unless it is controlled by the board of education of the city as a part of the public
      school system, and unless its principal work is the maintenance of courses affording
      instruction in such arts, sciences and professions and conferring such certificates
      of attainment as are authorized by other similar institutions of learning above high
      school grade.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.130. Contracts; bids for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.130. Contracts; bids for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.130. Contracts; bids for (2023)
content:
Any work for which a bond issue has been provided may be done by contract or otherwise,
   in the discretion of the president and trustees of the university.  When any contract involves the expenditure of two thousand dollars ($2,000) or more
   it shall be awarded to the lowest and best bidder.  All bids or parts of bids for any such work, or for any supplies, may be rejected
   by the president and trustees.  The president and trustees may do any part of the work by day labor when deemed
   advisable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.240. Appropriation of land for junior college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.240. Appropriation of land for junior college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.240. Appropriation of land for junior college (2023)
content:
The board of education of any city that has established or acquired a municipal junior
   college pursuant toKRS 165.210may set apart or appropriate any site or school building, or part of a school building
   and grounds, not needed for general school purposes, for the use of a municipal junior
   college.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.170. Tax levy for municipal college; amount; disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.170. Tax levy for municipal college; amount; disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.170. Tax levy for municipal college; amount; disposition (2023)
content:
The legislative body of any city with a population equal to or greater than twenty
   thousand (20,000) based upon the most recent federal decennial census that has a municipal
   college may, after an election as required bySection 184 of the Constitution, annually levy and collect, for the support of the municipal college, a tax of not
   less than five cents ($0.05) nor more than fourteen cents ($0.14) on each one hundred
   dollars' ($100) worth of property subject to taxation for city purposes.  The levy of such taxes shall be made at the same time and in the same manner as
   other levies for city purposes.  The amount levied shall be placed to the credit of the municipal college fund upon
   the completion of the assessment of property for taxation, and paid as collected,
   subject to the discount allowed on other city taxes, by the treasurer of the city
   to the treasurer or other financial officer of the college, for the purpose of establishing,
   acquiring and operating the college.  The taxes authorized by this section shall be construed to be school taxes and shall
   be in addition to all other taxes authorized by law to be used for municipal or school
   purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.165. Bond issue for municipal college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.165. Bond issue for municipal college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.165. Bond issue for municipal college (2023)
content:
The legislative body of a city which has established or acquired a municipal college
   pursuant toKRS 165.160or where a junior college exists under the provisions ofKRS 165.160to165.260may, for educational purposes, use and employ all the authority contained inKRS 165.080to165.140and162.340to162.380to issue bonds for the benefit of such college.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.150. Law school buildings for municipal university; erection of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.150. Law school buildings for municipal university; erection of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.150. Law school buildings for municipal university; erection of (2023)
content:
(1)  Any city of the first class may, if the necessary ground is conveyed to the city
      without cost and free of all liens and encumbrances, erect law school buildings, with
      necessary appurtenances, for the purpose of supplying the municipal university of
      the city with adequate buildings necessary to carry out its powers and duties.  The city shall proceed under the provisions ofKRS 162.160to162.280.  When so applied,KRS 162.160to162.280shall be so read that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.260. Existing junior colleges not affected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.260. Existing junior colleges not affected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.260. Existing junior colleges not affected (2023)
content:
KRS 165.210to165.250do not affect cities that had established and were operating, on January 27, 1937,
   municipal junior colleges other than by boards of education.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.160. Municipal colleges in cities with populations of 3,000. or more, except for cities of the first class; establishment; board of trustees; advisory board prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.160. Municipal colleges in cities with populations of 3,000. or more, except for cities of the first class; establishment; board of trustees; advisory board prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.160. Municipal colleges in cities with populations of 3,000. or more, except for cities of the first class; establishment; board of trustees; advisory board prohibited (2023)
content:
(1)  Except for cities of the first class, cities with populations equal to or greater
      than three thousand (3,000) based upon the most recent federal decennial census may
      establish or acquire by lawful conveyance municipal colleges for the purpose of promoting
      public education.  A college in a city meeting the requirements set out in this subsection shall not
      constitute a municipal college or receive support as provided inKRS 165.170to165.190unless it is controlled by a board of trustees appointed by the mayor and legislative
      body of the city, and unless its principal work is the maintenance of courses affording
      instruction in such arts, sciences, and professions and conferring such certificates
      of attainment as are authorized by other similar institutions of learning above the
      high school grade.  No advisory board shall be appointed for any college established pursuant to the
      provisions of this section, and the board of trustees of the college shall perform
      the functions of an advisory board in addition to its other functions.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.340. Kentucky Commission on Proprietary Education; membership; terms; duties of executive director; administrative regulations; meetings; powers and duties of commission; compensation; complaint committee; annual report
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.340. Kentucky Commission on Proprietary Education; membership; terms; duties of executive director; administrative regulations; meetings; powers and duties of commission; compensation; complaint committee; annual report
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.340. Kentucky Commission on Proprietary Education; membership; terms; duties of executive director; administrative regulations; meetings; powers and duties of commission; compensation; complaint committee; annual report (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.360. License; bond or other collateral; suspension or renewal; transferability; voidable student contracts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.360. License; bond or other collateral; suspension or renewal; transferability; voidable student contracts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.360. License; bond or other collateral; suspension or renewal; transferability; voidable student contracts (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) No person shall maintain or operate a proprietary school located and doing
         business within this state until the school has been issued a license by the commission
         pursuant to the provisions ofKRS 165A.310to165A.410.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.400. Rules and regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.400. Rules and regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.400. Rules and regulations (2023)
content:
The commission shall have the authority to promulgate and adopt reasonable rules and
   regulations for the administration of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.200. Financial and other reports concerning college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.200. Financial and other reports concerning college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.200. Financial and other reports concerning college (2023)
content:
An annual report and audit of receipts and disbursements of funds received by a municipal
   college underKRS 165.160to165.190shall be made in addition to such other reports on the condition of the college as
   are required by its charter or by the governing body of the city.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.450. Licensed schools to contribute to a student protection fund; purposes; minimum balance; fee structure
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.450. Licensed schools to contribute to a student protection fund; purposes; minimum balance; fee structure
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.450. Licensed schools to contribute to a student protection fund; purposes; minimum balance; fee structure (2023)
content:
All licensed schools, resident and nonresident, shall be required to contribute to
   a student protection fund.  The fund shall be used to pay off debts, including refunds to students enrolled
   or on leave of absence by not being enrolled for one (1) academic year or less from
   the school at the time of the closing, incurred due to the closing of a school, discontinuance
   of a program, loss of license, or loss of accreditation by a school or program.  The Kentucky Commission on Proprietary Education shall promulgate administrative
   regulations in accordance with KRS Chapter 13A to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.460. Proprietary schools that offer CDL training governed by this chapter; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.460. Proprietary schools that offer CDL training governed by this chapter; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.460. Proprietary schools that offer CDL training governed by this chapter; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, all proprietary schools
      located or doing business in this state that offer CDL driver training shall be governed
      by the provisions of this chapter, except for matters governing:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.195. Acquisition of property by board of trustees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.195. Acquisition of property by board of trustees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.195. Acquisition of property by board of trustees (2023)
content:
The board of trustees of a municipal college established pursuant toKRS 165.160may acquire, by purchase or gift, lands and improvements for the purpose of expanding
   the plant and extending the usefulness of the college, and when unable to agree with
   the owner of land and improvements necessary for the purposes of the college may proceed
   to condemn the land and improvements.  The condemnation proceedings shall be conducted in the manner provided in the Eminent
   Domain Act of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.190. Appropriation of land for college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.190. Appropriation of land for college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.190. Appropriation of land for college (2023)
content:
The legislative body of any city having a municipal college pursuant toKRS 165.160may appropriate as a site for the buildings and grounds for that municipal college
   any public grounds of the city not especially appropriated or dedicated to any other
   use.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.230. Tuition charged by junior college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.230. Tuition charged by junior college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.230. Tuition charged by junior college (2023)
content:
The board of education of any city that establishes or acquires a municipal junior
   college pursuant toKRS 165.210may, for the purpose of supplementing the tax provided inKRS 165.220, charge each pupil attending the college an annual tuition fee of not more than two
   hundred dollars ($200).  The tuition fee shall be collected by the treasurer of the board of education and
   placed to the credit of the board of education college fund, and shall be used for
   maintaining and operating the college.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.470. License to operate CDL driver training school; persons who may not be connected with school; requirements for school and instructors
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.470. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.470. License to operate CDL driver training school; persons who may not be connected with school; requirements for school and instructors (2023)
content:
(1)  A person shall not operate, conduct, maintain, or establish a CDL driver training
      school unless the person holds a valid current license issued by the commission.  The following persons shall not be allowed to be connected in any capacity whatsoever
      with a CDL driver training school:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.250. Financial report of junior college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.250. Financial report of junior college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.250. Financial report of junior college (2023)
content:
An annual report and an audit of receipts and disbursements of the junior college
   fund shall be made by the board of education of the city.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges›KY REV ST 165.220. Tax levy for junior college
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165. City Universities and Colleges › KY REV ST 165.220. Tax levy for junior college
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165.220. Tax levy for junior college (2023)
content:
The board of education of any city having a municipal junior college pursuant toKRS 165.210may request and the legislative body of the city shall then, after an election as
   required bySection 184 of the Constitution, annually cause to be levied and collected, for the support of a municipal junior
   college, a tax of not less than five cents ($0.05) nor more than seven cents ($0.07)
   on each one hundred dollars ($100) worth of property subject to taxation for city
   purposes.  Any election for the levy of taxes under this section shall be held at the next
   regular election if the question is filed with the county clerk not later than the
   second Tuesday in August preceding the regular election.  The levy of such taxes shall be made at the same time and in the same manner as
   other levies for public school purposes.  The amount levied shall be placed to the credit of the board of education fund upon
   completion of the assessment of property for taxation, and paid as collected, subject
   to the discounts or penalties allowed on other city taxes, by the treasurer of the
   city to the treasurer of the board of education for the purpose of establishing, acquiring
   and operating the college.  The taxes authorized by this section shall be construed to be school taxes and shall
   be in addition to all other taxes authorized by law to be used for municipal or school
   purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.330. License required; applications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.330. License required; applications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.330. License required; applications (2023)
content:
(1)  No person shall conduct, operate, maintain, or establish a proprietary school
      as herein defined or use any words which designate or tend to designate to the public
      that the operator of the school is qualified to conduct, operate, and maintain the
      school, unless he holds a valid current license from the commission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.480. License to operate school or act as instructor; posting and carrying of licenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.480. License to operate school or act as instructor; posting and carrying of licenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.480. License to operate school or act as instructor; posting and carrying of licenses (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon receipt of a satisfactory application accompanied by the prescribed fee,
      the commission shall issue a license to the applicant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.320. Applicability of KRS 165A.310. to § 165A.410
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.320. Applicability of KRS 165A.310. to § 165A.410
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.320. Applicability of KRS 165A.310. to § 165A.410 (2023)
content:
KRS 165A.310to165A.410shall not apply to any institution offering a four (4) year bachelor's degree recognized
   by the Council on Postsecondary Education, nor shall it apply to any religious institution
   exempt from taxation under the laws of this state or which is subject to the provisions
   ofKRS 164.945.KRS 165A.310to165A.410is intended to apply to and regulate for-profit and not-for-profit proprietary schools,
   including but not limited to traditional, Web-based, distance learning, or correspondence
   schools, which are operated as or are organized for a profit, or on a not-for-profit
   basis.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.350. Requirements for agent's permit; bond or other collateral; conditional license; renewal; owner's liability for actions of agents
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.350. Requirements for agent's permit; bond or other collateral; conditional license; renewal; owner's liability for actions of agents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.350. Requirements for agent's permit; bond or other collateral; conditional license; renewal; owner's liability for actions of agents (2023)
content:
(1)  No person shall solicit or perform the services of an agent in this state for
      a proprietary school, located either within or without this state, unless the school
      shall have been issued by the commission a license pursuant toKRS 165A.310to165A.410and the person shall have been issued an agent's permit for said proprietary school.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Definitions › KY REV ST 165A.310. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.310. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: As used in this chapter:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.370. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.370. Minimum standards and requirements; training requirements for administrators and instructors; records; financial statement; approval and denial of license; conditional license (2023)
content:
(1)  No proprietary school located or doing business in this state shall be issued

      the school, after a physical inspection of the premises, can be reasonably maintained
      and operated, in substantial compliance with the following minimum standards:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.390. Revocation or suspension of permits and licenses; conveyance of student records to commission prior to discontinuance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.390. Revocation or suspension of permits and licenses; conveyance of student records to commission prior to discontinuance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.390. Revocation or suspension of permits and licenses; conveyance of student records to commission prior to discontinuance (2023)
content:
(1)  An agent's permit may be revoked by the commission for fraud or misrepresentation
      in procuring or soliciting a student or prospective student for enrollment in a course
      or courses of instruction or study offered or maintained by a proprietary school located
      within or without this state.  An agent's permit may be revoked by the commission for a false or misleading written
      or oral statement in the application therefor submitted by the applicant with the
      intent to mislead or conceal the truth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.410. Enforcement of chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.410. Enforcement of chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.410. Enforcement of chapter (2023)
content:
The Attorney General may, at the request of the Kentucky Commission on Proprietary
   Education or on his own motion, bring in a Circuit Court appropriate action for the
   enforcement of the provisions of this chapter.  Any such action under this section may, at the discretion of the Attorney General,
   be brought either in the county in which the violation occurred or in the Franklin
   Circuit Court, or other appropriate court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Proprietary Education›KY REV ST 165A.380. Disposition of fees; trust and agency account
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Proprietary Education › KY REV ST 165A.380. Disposition of fees; trust and agency account
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.380. Disposition of fees; trust and agency account (2023)
content:
(1)  All fees collected pursuant to this chapter, except those collected pursuant
      toKRS 165A.450, shall be deposited in the State Treasury in a trust and agency account of the Kentucky
      Commission on Proprietary Education and shall be used by the commission to defray
      the cost of administering and enforcing this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.475. content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 167. Education of the Physically Handicapped›KY REV ST 167.035. Kentucky School for the Blind Advisory Board
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 167. Education of the Physically Handicapped › KY REV ST 167.035. Kentucky School for the Blind Advisory Board
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 167.035. Kentucky School for the Blind Advisory Board (2023)
content:
(1)  There may be established a Kentucky School for the Blind Advisory Board composed
      of five (5) members appointed by the Kentucky Board of Education upon recommendation
      by the chief state school officer for terms of four (4) years and until their successors
      are appointed.  The board shall elect from its membership a chairman.  Members of the board shall serve without compensation but shall be reimbursed for
      necessary expenses incurred in performance of their duties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.465. Criminal history background check for CDL trainers; fingerprinting; eligibility based on results; fees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.465. Criminal history background check for CDL trainers; fingerprinting; eligibility based on results; fees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.465. Criminal history background check for CDL trainers; fingerprinting; eligibility based on results; fees (2023)
content:
(1)  All persons initially applying for a license to operate a CDL driver training
      school or a license as a CDL driver training instructor shall be required to undergo
      a state and national criminal history background check conducted by the Department
      of Kentucky State Police.  Application forms for a license to operate a CDL driver training school or a license
      as a CDL driver training instructor shall conspicuously state the following:  “STATE
      LAW REQUIRES A STATE AND NATIONAL CRIMINAL HISTORY BACKGROUND CHECK AS A CONDITION
      OF APPLYING FOR THIS LICENSE. ANY PERSON WHO REFUSES TO SUBMIT TO A CRIMINAL HISTORY BACKGROUND CHECK SHALL NOT
      BE ELIGIBLE TO APPLY FOR, OR BE ISSUED, A LICENSE TO OPERATE A CDL DRIVER TRAINING
      SCHOOL OR A LICENSE FOR A CDL DRIVER TRAINING INSTRUCTOR.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.485. Expiration and renewal of licenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.485. Expiration and renewal of licenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.485. Expiration and renewal of licenses (2023)
content:
(1)  Every license issued for the operation of a CDL driver training school shall
      expire on June 30 following the date of the issuance unless revoked or canceled by
      the commission.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.495. Hearing on suspension or revocation of license; written request; appeal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.495. Hearing on suspension or revocation of license; written request; appeal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.495. Hearing on suspension or revocation of license; written request; appeal (2023)
content:
Any person whose license to conduct a CDL driver training school or any person whose
   license to give instructions in these schools has been suspended or revoked or the
   issue or renewal thereof is refused, may request a hearing.  The request shall be in writing addressed to the commission, who shall conduct a
   hearing thereon as soon as possible.  The hearing shall be conducted in accordance with KRS Chapter 13B.  Any person may appeal from the final order of the commission in the Franklin Circuit
   Court in accordance with KRS Chapter 13B.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.490. Suspension or revocation of, or refusal to issue or renew, license
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.490. Suspension or revocation of, or refusal to issue or renew, license
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.490. Suspension or revocation of, or refusal to issue or renew, license (2023)
content:
The commission shall, upon receipt of satisfactory evidence, suspend, revoke, refuse
   to issue, or refuse to renew the license of a CDL driver training school or a CDL
   driver training instructor if:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.505. Location of CDL driver training school
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.505. Location of CDL driver training school
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.505. Location of CDL driver training school (2023)
content:
A CDL driver training school shall not be located within three hundred (300) feet
   of any governmental building in which is carried on any function having to do with
   the administration of any laws relating to motor vehicles.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.515. Application of chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.515. Application of chapter

content: (1)  This chapter shall not apply to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XIII. Education›Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education›Commercial Driver's License Training›KY REV ST 165A.500. Records kept by schools and instructors; retention requirements; confidentiality
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XIII. Education › Chapter 165A. Proprietary Education › Commercial Driver's License Training › KY REV ST 165A.500. Records kept by schools and instructors; retention requirements; confidentiality
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 165A.500. Records kept by schools and instructors; retention requirements; confidentiality (2023)
content:
(1)  Every CDL driver training school and CDL driver training instructor shall maintain
      records showing the name, address, and instruction permit or operator's license number
      of each person to whom instruction is given.  The records shall also indicate the type of instruction given and the length of
      time of the instruction.

content:
