content: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202A. Hospitalization of the Mentally Ill›KY REV ST 202A.081. Court-ordered community-based outpatient treatment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202A. Hospitalization of the Mentally Ill › KY REV ST 202A.081. Court-ordered community-based outpatient treatment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202A.081. Court-ordered community-based outpatient treatment (2023)
content:
(1)  Following the preliminary hearing but prior to the completion of the final hearing,
      the court may order the person held in a hospital approved by the cabinet for such
      purpose for the committing judicial district, or released, upon application and agreement
      of the parties, for the purpose of community-based outpatient treatment.  No person held under this section shall be held in jail unless criminal charges
      are also pending.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.019. County attorney's duties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.019. County attorney's duties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.019. County attorney's duties (2023)
content:
In all proceedings under this chapter, it shall be the duty of the county attorney
   to assist the petitioner and represent the interest of the Commonwealth and to assist
   the court in its inquiry by the presentation of evidence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.021. Voluntary admission to an ICF/ID; discharge of voluntarily admitted resident; release of voluntarily admitted resident upon written request
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.021. Voluntary admission to an ICF/ID; discharge of voluntarily admitted resident; release of voluntarily admitted resident upon written request
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.021. Voluntary admission to an ICF/ID; discharge of voluntarily admitted resident; release of voluntarily admitted resident upon written request (2023)
content:
(1)  Minors and adult persons with an intellectual disability may be voluntarily admitted
      for care and treatment in an ICF/ID under the applicable provisions of this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.110. Venue for proceedings subsequent to preliminary hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.110. Venue for proceedings subsequent to preliminary hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.110. Venue for proceedings subsequent to preliminary hearing (2023)
content:
A respondent who has been ordered involuntarily admitted following the preliminary
   hearing shall have venue for all subsequent proceedings, including the final hearing,
   transferred to the court of the county where the respondent is admitted;  however,
   the court of the county where the preliminary hearing was held may, upon its own motion,
   or shall, upon motion of one (1) of the parties, retain venue over proceedings subsequent
   to the preliminary hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.120. Certificate contents; fee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.120. Certificate contents; fee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.120. Certificate contents; fee (2023)
content:
(1)  The certificate referred to in this chapter shall be in the form prescribed by
      the cabinet.  The certificate shall state that the respondent has been examined by each of the
      qualified professionals in the area of intellectual disabilities making the certificate
      within twenty-four (24) hours, excluding weekends and holidays, prior to the date
      of the certificate.  It shall state the facts and circumstances upon which the judgment of the examining
      physician is based and shall be sworn to before a notary or the clerk or judge of
      the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.040. Criteria for involuntary admission for individuals with an intellectual disability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.040. Criteria for involuntary admission for individuals with an intellectual disability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.040. Criteria for involuntary admission for individuals with an intellectual disability (2023)
content:
When a person who is alleged to be an individual with an intellectual disability is
   involuntarily admitted, there shall be a determination that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.170. Interim determination and possible dismissal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.170. Interim determination and possible dismissal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.170. Interim determination and possible dismissal (2023)
content:
(1)  Following the preliminary hearing but prior to the completion of the final hearing,
      the court may order the respondent to reside in his or her current residence, an emergency
      placement designated by the regional program for mental health and individuals with
      an intellectual disability, or an ICF/ID approved by the secretary for that purpose
      for the committing judicial district in a community program approved by the secretary
      or in a hospital.  The respondent may be released, upon application and agreement of the parties, for
      the purpose of community-based outpatient treatment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.150. Time of preliminary and final hearings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.150. Time of preliminary and final hearings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.150. Time of preliminary and final hearings (2023)
content:
(1)  The preliminary hearing shall be held not later than fifteen (15) days, excluding
      weekends and holidays, from the date of the filing of the petition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.060. Rights of residents with an intellectual disability; adoption of regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.060. Rights of residents with an intellectual disability; adoption of regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.060. Rights of residents with an intellectual disability; adoption of regulations (2023)
content:
The secretary shall adopt administrative regulations for the proper administration
   and enforcement of this chapter.  The regulations shall include, but shall not be limited to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.190. Disclosure of professional communications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.190. Disclosure of professional communications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.190. Disclosure of professional communications (2023)
content:
In proceedings under this chapter, there shall be no privilege as to any relevant
   communications between qualified professionals in the area of intellectual disabilities
   and patients.  Qualified professionals in the area of intellectual disabilities may disclose communications
   relating to diagnosis and treatment of the patient's mental condition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.025. Temporary admission by authorized staff physician at ICF/ID
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.025. Temporary admission by authorized staff physician at ICF/ID
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.025. Temporary admission by authorized staff physician at ICF/ID (2023)
content:
(1)  An authorized staff physician may order the admission of any person who is present
      at, or is presented at, an ICF/ID. Within twenty-four (24) hours, excluding weekends and holidays, of the admission under
      this section, the authorized staff physician ordering the admission of the person
      shall certify in the record of the individual that in the opinion of the physician,
      the individual should be involuntarily admitted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.180. Confidentiality of court records; expungement; disclosure by court order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.180. Confidentiality of court records; expungement; disclosure by court order
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.180. Confidentiality of court records; expungement; disclosure by court order (2023)
content:
(1)  The court records of a respondent made in all proceedings pursuant to this chapter
      shall be confidential and shall not be open to the general public for inspection except
      when the disclosure is provided inKRS 202B.190.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.080. Title of chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.080. Title of chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.080. Title of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter may be cited as the “Kentucky Admission Act for Individuals with an Intellectual
   Disability”.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.070. Exemption from personal liability; duty of individuals with direct-care responsibility for residents of ICF/ID to meet specific care needs, including supervision
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.070. Exemption from personal liability; duty of individuals with direct-care responsibility for residents of ICF/ID to meet specific care needs, including supervision
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.070. Exemption from personal liability; duty of individuals with direct-care responsibility for residents of ICF/ID to meet specific care needs, including supervision (2023)
content:
(1)  Persons carrying out duties or rendering professional opinions as provided in
      this chapter shall be free of personal liability for such actions provided that such
      activities are performed in good faith within the scope of their official duties and
      in a manner consistent with accepted professional practices.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.050. Rights guaranteed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.050. Rights guaranteed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.050. Rights guaranteed (2023)
content:
All rights guaranteed by KRS Chapter 210 to mentally ill persons shall apply to individuals
   with an intellectual disability.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.230. Appeals; manner; parties who may appeal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.230. Appeals; manner; parties who may appeal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.230. Appeals; manner; parties who may appeal (2023)
content:
Appeals from the final orders or judgments of the District Court made and entered
   in proceedings under this chapter shall be taken in the manner as other appeals from
   District Court to Circuit Court.  Appeals may be taken by the Commonwealth, the individual who is subject to the proceedings,
   or the individual's guardian, limited guardian, or other authorized representative.  This appeal shall be advanced on the Circuit Court docket without motion or notice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.140. Witnesses to examination
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.140. Witnesses to examination
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.140. Witnesses to examination (2023)
content:
A qualified professional in the area of intellectual disabilities retained by the
   respondent, or the respondent's parent or guardian, at the expense of the parent or
   guardian, shall be permitted to witness and participate in any examination of the
   respondent and may submit findings, if any, to the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.100. Proceedings for involuntary admission; petition; duties of court; disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.100. Proceedings for involuntary admission; petition; duties of court; disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.100. Proceedings for involuntary admission; petition; duties of court; disposition (2023)
content:
(1)  Proceedings for involuntary admission of a person to an ICF/ID shall be initiated
      by the filing of a verified petition in District Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.130. Number of certifications required for involuntary admission; time limit
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.130. Number of certifications required for involuntary admission; time limit
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.130. Number of certifications required for involuntary admission; time limit (2023)
content:
In any proceeding for involuntary admission under the applicable provisions of this
   chapter, if the criteria for involuntary admission are not certified by at least two
   (2) professionals as specified inKRS 202B.100(6)(c), the court shall, without taking any further action, terminate the proceedings and
   order the release of the person.  The qualified professional in the area of intellectual disabilities shall certify
   to the court, within twenty-four (24) hours of the examination, excluding weekends
   and holidays, his or her findings and opinions as to whether the person shall be involuntarily
   admitted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.200. Court to notify cabinet of admission ordered to ICF/ID; refusal to receive by ICF/ID; transport of person
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.200. Court to notify cabinet of admission ordered to ICF/ID; refusal to receive by ICF/ID; transport of person
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.200. Court to notify cabinet of admission ordered to ICF/ID; refusal to receive by ICF/ID; transport of person (2023)
content:
(1)  The court which orders any person to an ICF/ID under the provisions of this chapter,
      shall at once notify the cabinet that the order has been made, advising of the sex
      and condition of the person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.220. Right to be present
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.220. Right to be present
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.220. Right to be present (2023)
content:
The respondent shall be present at all hearings unless the respondent and the respondent's
   attorney waive the respondent's rights to be present, or unless the court makes a
   specific finding after the respondent has been brought to the place of the hearing
   that the respondent should be removed from the hearing because the person's conduct
   is so disruptive that the proceedings cannot continue in any reasonable manner.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.160. Hearing procedures; rights of guardians and immediate family members
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.160. Hearing procedures; rights of guardians and immediate family members
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.160. Hearing procedures; rights of guardians and immediate family members (2023)
content:
(1)  The preliminary hearing need not be formal and shall include the receiving of
      reports of the qualified professional in the area of intellectual disabilities as
      evidence.  The hearing may be held by the court in chambers, at an ICF/ID, or other suitable
      place.  The respondent shall be afforded an opportunity to testify, to present witnesses,
      and to cross-examine any witnesses.  The respondent and the attorney for the respondent may waive respondent's right
      to a preliminary hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.270. Convalescent leave status
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.270. Convalescent leave status
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.270. Convalescent leave status (2023)
content:
(1)  A physician may release a resident on convalescent leave status when the interdisciplinary
      team concludes that the resident would not present a danger or a threat of danger
      to self, family, or others if provided with continued medical supervision in a less
      restrictive alternative mode of treatment.  Release on convalescent leave status does not terminate a court admission order
      and shall include provisions for the development of a treatment plan jointly by the
      ICF/ID and by a provider of outpatient care for follow-up care by the provider and
      for the continual monitoring of that resident's condition by the provider.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.300. Return of Kentucky residents from other states; determination of need for further admission
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.300. Return of Kentucky residents from other states; determination of need for further admission
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.300. Return of Kentucky residents from other states; determination of need for further admission (2023)
content:
(1)  Legal residents of the state who have become public charges in other states and
      have been returned to Kentucky because they have been involuntarily admitted may be
      immediately admitted to an ICF/ID at the request of the secretary or the secretary's
      designated representative.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.210. Right to counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.210. Right to counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.210. Right to counsel (2023)
content:
Upon the filing of a petition for involuntary admission pursuant toKRS 202B.045, the court shall appoint an attorney to represent the respondent with the appointment
   and representation to continue unless the respondent retains private counsel.  The appointed attorney shall be forthwith notified by the clerk of the allegations
   in the petition and the date and purpose of the preliminary hearing.  When it is necessary to appoint counsel, the District Court shall endeavor to appoint
   private counsel, if available, to represent respondents, from a list of attorneys
   who have volunteered to represent such respondents.  The list shall be maintained by the District Court clerk.  Private counsel appointed by the court shall be compensated in the manner set forth
   inKRS 620.100.  If no other method of appointing counsel for the respondent is available, the respondent
   shall be represented by the public advocate pursuant to KRS Chapter 31.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.250. Review hearing; procedures; disposition; requested hearing by resident or certain persons
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.250. Review hearing; procedures; disposition; requested hearing by resident or certain persons
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.250. Review hearing; procedures; disposition; requested hearing by resident or certain persons (2023)
content:
(1)  No less than once in every five (5) years following the initial order for involuntary
      admission of a resident to an ICF/ID, or an order authorizing continued care and treatment
      following review pursuant to this section, the court shall hold a hearing to review
      the status of the resident and necessity for continued care and treatment in the ICF/ID.  Notice at least twenty (20) days in advance of the hearing shall be provided by
      the court to the ICF/ID, county attorney, guardian or limited guardian of the resident,
      if any, or, if none, an immediate family member as listed on the last interdisciplinary
      report filed by the ICF/ID.  The court shall appoint an attorney to represent the resident at the review hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.245. ICF/ID review committee; procedure when involuntary resident refuses to participate in treatment plan
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.245. ICF/ID review committee; procedure when involuntary resident refuses to participate in treatment plan
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.245. ICF/ID review committee; procedure when involuntary resident refuses to participate in treatment plan (2023)
content:
(1)  Every ICF/ID approved under the provisions of this chapter shall have a review
      committee of three (3) qualified professionals in the area of intellectual disabilities
      appointed by the facility director.  This review committee shall have the authority to review the appropriateness of
      a resident's individual treatment plan.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.290. Respite care
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.290. Respite care
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.290. Respite care (2023)
content:
Upon recommendation or approval of the interdisciplinary team of an ICF/ID, a physician
   may admit for respite care an individual with an intellectual disability.  Respite care provided to any individual with an intellectual disability under this
   section shall not exceed a total of thirty (30) days in any calendar year.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.280. Peace officer authorized to take absent resident into custody and return resident to ICF/ID
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.280. Peace officer authorized to take absent resident into custody and return resident to ICF/ID
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.280. Peace officer authorized to take absent resident into custody and return resident to ICF/ID (2023)
content:
If a resident undergoing involuntary treatment on an inpatient basis is absent from
   the ICF/ID without or in excess of authorization from the ICF/ID staff, the person
   in charge or that person's designee may notify the appropriate sheriff or other peace
   officers who shall take the resident into custody and return the resident to the ICF/ID.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.260. Petition for writ of habeas corpus
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.260. Petition for writ of habeas corpus
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.260. Petition for writ of habeas corpus (2023)
content:
At any time, and without notice, a person detained at a facility, or a relative, friend,
   guardian, representative, or attorney on behalf of such person, may petition for a
   writ of habeas corpus to question the cause and legality of the detention and request
   that the Circuit Court issue a writ for release.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability›KY REV ST 202B.240. Annual review; interdisciplinary evaluation report; discharge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.240. Annual review; interdisciplinary evaluation report; discharge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202B.240. Annual review; interdisciplinary evaluation report; discharge (2023)
content:
(1)  Every resident admitted under the provisions of this chapter shall have an annual
      review conducted by an interdisciplinary team of the ICF/ID to determine the appropriateness
      of and the necessity for care and treatment provided the resident in the ICF/ID.  On or before the anniversary date of an involuntary admission order entered for
      a resident pursuant toKRS 202B.190, and every year thereafter for as long as the resident resides in the ICF/ID, the
      ICF/ID shall file with the admitting court an interdisciplinary evaluation report
      on behalf of the resident whose continued placement in the ICF/ID is required.  The report shall detail the social, psychological, medical, and other considerations
      requiring continued placement of the resident in the ICF/ID, a description of the
      treatment or habilitation programs which will benefit the resident as a result of
      such placement, and a statement that the criteria for involuntary admission set forth
      inKRS 202B.040are satisfied.  The interdisciplinary report shall list the name and address of the guardian or
      limited guardian or, if none, an immediate family member of the resident.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.020. Petition for involuntary commitment proceeding; guardian ad litem; duty of Commonwealth’s attorney
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.020. Petition for involuntary commitment proceeding; guardian ad litem; duty of Commonwealth’s attorney
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.020. Petition for involuntary commitment proceeding; guardian ad litem; duty of Commonwealth’s attorney (2023)
content:
(1)  When a defendant who is charged with a qualifying offense has been found, after
      a hearing under KRS Chapter 504, to be incompetent to stand trial with no substantial
      probability that the defendant will attain competency within three hundred sixty (360)
      days, the Commonwealth's attorney's office serving the county of criminal prosecution
      shall immediately petition the Circuit Court that found the defendant incompetent
      to stand trial or, if the finding was by a District Court, the Circuit Court in the
      county of the criminal prosecution, for an involuntary commitment proceeding, to include
      an evidentiary hearing and a commitment hearing, if applicable, under this chapter.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.010. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.010. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.030. Evidentiary hearing, purposes and conduct of; when subsequent commitment hearing is required; evidence submitted by respondent inadmissible in other criminal or civil cases
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.030. Evidentiary hearing, purposes and conduct of; when subsequent commitment hearing is required; evidence submitted by respondent inadmissible in other criminal or civil cases
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.030. Evidentiary hearing, purposes and conduct of; when subsequent commitment hearing is required; evidence submitted by respondent inadmissible in other criminal or civil cases (2023)
content:
(1)  An adversarial evidentiary hearing on the record shall be held within twenty
      (20) days, excluding weekends and holidays, of the filing of a petition pursuant toKRS 202C.020.  Appropriate notice shall be served on all parties.  The court shall order the Commonwealth to provide all available discovery to the
      respondent no later than seven (7) days, excluding weekends and holidays, before the
      hearing.  No evidence may be presented at the hearing that has not been disclosed through
      discovery.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.070. Exclusion of persons unnecessary to hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.070. Exclusion of persons unnecessary to hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.070. Exclusion of persons unnecessary to hearing (2023)
content: In a hearing underKRS 202C.030,202C.040, and202C.060, the court may exclude all persons not necessary for the conduct of the hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.080. Respondent’s qualified mental health professional; right to be present and participate in any examination of respondent
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.080. Respondent’s qualified mental health professional; right to be present and participate in any examination of respondent
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.080. Respondent’s qualified mental health professional; right to be present and participate in any examination of respondent (2023)
content:
A qualified mental health professional retained by the respondent shall be permitted
   to witness and participate in any examination of the respondent under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.050. Criteria for involuntary commitment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.050. Criteria for involuntary commitment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.050. Criteria for involuntary commitment (2023)
content:
(1)  No respondent shall be involuntarily committed under this chapter unless there
      is a determination that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.100. Confidentiality of records; judge may order disclosure of information when appropriate and in best interest of respondent or public
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.100. Confidentiality of records; judge may order disclosure of information when appropriate and in best interest of respondent or public
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.100. Confidentiality of records; judge may order disclosure of information when appropriate and in best interest of respondent or public (2023)
content:
(1)  The court records of a respondent made in all proceedings under this chapter
      are hereby declared to be confidential and shall not be open to the general public
      for inspection.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.040. Commitment hearing; scheduling and conduct of; participation by Commonwealth’s attorney, respondent, and guardian ad litem; standard of proof; waiver of right to commitment hearing prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.040. Commitment hearing; scheduling and conduct of; participation by Commonwealth’s attorney, respondent, and guardian ad litem; standard of proof; waiver of right to commitment hearing prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.040. Commitment hearing; scheduling and conduct of; participation by Commonwealth’s attorney, respondent, and guardian ad litem; standard of proof; waiver of right to commitment hearing prohibited (2023)
content:
(1)  A commitment hearing shall be held within twenty (20) days, excluding weekends
      and holidays, after the court finds that the evidence presented in an evidentiary
      hearing pursuant toKRS 202C.030supports a finding that the respondent is guilty of the charged crime against him
      or her by a preponderance of the evidence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.090. Relevant communications between qualified mental health professionals; not privileged
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.090. Relevant communications between qualified mental health professionals; not privileged
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.090. Relevant communications between qualified mental health professionals; not privileged (2023)
content:
In proceedings under this chapter, there shall be no privilege as to any relevant
   communications between qualified mental health professionals.  Qualified mental health professionals may disclose communications relating to diagnosis
   and treatment of the patient's mental condition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.150. Psychiatric facility review committee; treatment plan
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.150. Psychiatric facility review committee; treatment plan
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.150. Psychiatric facility review committee; treatment plan (2023)
content:
(1)  Every forensic psychiatric facility caring for respondents involuntarily committed
      under this chapter shall have a review committee of three (3) qualified mental health
      professionals appointed by the facility director.  This review committee shall have the authority to review the appropriateness of
      a respondent's individual treatment plan.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.140. Rights of involuntarily committed patients
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.140. Rights of involuntarily committed patients
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.140. Rights of involuntarily committed patients (2023)
content:
A respondent involuntarily committed under this chapter shall have the following rights
   as a patient:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.110. Right to petition for writ of habeas corpus
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.110. Right to petition for writ of habeas corpus
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.110. Right to petition for writ of habeas corpus (2023)
content:
At any time, and without notice, a respondent detained at a forensic psychiatric facility,
   or a relative, friend, guardian, representative, or attorney on behalf of such person,
   may petition for a writ of habeas corpus to question the cause and legality of the
   detention and request that the court issue a writ for release.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.120. Notification of receiving psychiatric facility; transportation of patient
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.120. Notification of receiving psychiatric facility; transportation of patient
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.120. Notification of receiving psychiatric facility; transportation of patient (2023)
content:
(1)  The court which orders any respondent transferred to a forensic psychiatric facility
      underKRS 202C.050or504.110(3), shall at once notify the receiving hospital or psychiatric facility that such order
      has been made, advising of the sex and condition of the respondent and any other pertinent
      information.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.130. Clarification of court orders; appeals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.130. Clarification of court orders; appeals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.130. Clarification of court orders; appeals (2023)
content:
Forensic psychiatric facilities ordered to receive an involuntarily committed respondent
   shall have standing to petition the Circuit Court for any necessary clarification
   or modification of orders or judgments entered in proceedings under this chapter and
   to appeal from final judgments or orders entered in proceedings which have not complied
   with the provisions of this chapter.  A copy shall be sent to the involuntarily committed respondent, the respondent's
   guardian ad litem, and the respondent's attorney of record, of whatever pleadings
   are filed by the hospital.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance›KY REV ST 205.710. Definitions for KRS 205.712. to § 205.800
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance › KY REV ST 205.710. Definitions for KRS 205.712. to § 205.800
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 205.710. Definitions for KRS 205.712. to § 205.800 (2023)
content: As used inKRS 205.712to205.800, unless the context clearly dictates otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.160. Chapter not to apply to persons under age eighteen; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.160. Chapter not to apply to persons under age eighteen; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.160. Chapter not to apply to persons under age eighteen; exception (2023)
content:
This chapter shall not apply to persons under eighteen (18) years of age unless specifically
   authorized by the Kentucky Unified Juvenile Code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance›KY REV ST 205.690. Reports to General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance › KY REV ST 205.690. Reports to General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 205.690. Reports to General Assembly (2023)
content:
The secretary shall submit a written report to the General Assembly upon written request
   or appear in person before any joint interim committee of the General Assembly within
   thirty (30) days of a request. The following information related to the implementation ofKRS 205.2003shall be provided:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings›KY REV ST 202C.170. Administrative regulations for chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202C. Involuntary Commitment Proceedings › KY REV ST 202C.170. Administrative regulations for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 202C.170. Administrative regulations for chapter (2023)
content:
This cabinet shall promulgate administrative regulations in accordance with KRS Chapter
   13A in order to carry out the provisions of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance›KY REV ST 205.715. Debt due and owing to state by parents
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance › KY REV ST 205.715. Debt due and owing to state by parents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 205.715. Debt due and owing to state by parents (2023)
content:
The payment of public assistance to or on behalf of a dependent child shall create
   a debt due and owing the state by the parent or parents of the child.  If a court has ordered child support incident to a final divorce decree or other
   final order for child support, the debt shall be limited to the amount specified in
   the decree or order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance›KY REV ST 205.721. Title IV-A services available to individuals not receiving public assistance benefits; continuation of IV-D services; fee for services; exemption; annual fee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance › KY REV ST 205.721. Title IV-A services available to individuals not receiving public assistance benefits; continuation of IV-D services; fee for services; exemption; annual fee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 205.721. Title IV-A services available to individuals not receiving public assistance benefits; continuation of IV-D services; fee for services; exemption; annual fee (2023)
content:
(1)  All services available to individuals receiving public assistance under Title
      IV-A of the Federal Social Security Act1benefits shall also be available to individuals not receiving public assistance benefits,
      upon application by the individual with the cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare›Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance›KY REV ST 205.713. Standardized forms for entry of state case registry information
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 205. Public Assistance and Medical Assistance › KY REV ST 205.713. Standardized forms for entry of state case registry information
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 205.713. Standardized forms for entry of state case registry information (2023)
content:
All forms, child support orders, wage withholding orders, or orders amending an existing
   child support order, entered in any case in Circuit Court, District Court, or family
   court that require entry into the state case registry underKRS 205.712(4)shall be entered on forms adopted by the Administrative Office of the Courts after
   consultation with the Cabinet for Health and Family Services.  If the provisions of a child support order are contained in an order that is narrative
   in nature, the adopted forms shall be used in addition to the narrative order.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XVII. Economic Security and Public Welfare › Chapter 202B. Admission of an Individual with an Intellectual Disability › KY REV ST 202B.990. Penalties

content:
(1)  The unwarranted admission of any person under the provisions of this chapter;
      or
