   and upon the producing strata for the purpose of recovering the oil, if the introduction
   of air, gas, water, or other liquid conforms to the requirements of Section 1425 of
   the Safe Drinking Water Act (Public Law 93-523as amended)1and any regulations associated with it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.180. Requirements for plugging abandoned well; bids; remedy for possessor of adjacent land or for department
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.180. Requirements for plugging abandoned well; bids; remedy for possessor of adjacent land or for department
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.180. Requirements for plugging abandoned well; bids; remedy for possessor of adjacent land or for department (2023)
content:
(1)  No person shall abandon or remove casings from any oil or gas well, either dry
      or producing, without first plugging the well in a secure manner approved by the department
      and consistent with its administrative regulations.  Upon the department's plugging of an abandoned well in accordance with the requirements
      of this subsection, the department may sell, by sealed bid, or include as part of
      compensation in the contract for the plugging of the well, all equipment removed from
      that well and deposit the proceeds of the sale into the oil and gas well plugging
      fund, established inKRS 353.590(27).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.210. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by trustee representing contingent future interests
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.210. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by trustee representing contingent future interests
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.210. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by trustee representing contingent future interests (2023)
content:
A trustee appointed by any Circuit Court of this state in cases where contingent future
   interests in land are involved may enter into a consolidation agreement, as defined
   inKRS 353.220, subject to approval by the Circuit Judge as provided inKRS 353.230.  The detailed provisions of such agreement may be such as the court approves, consistently
   with the provisions ofKRS 353.220.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.205. Department to release production data on crude oil and natural gas
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.205. Department to release production data on crude oil and natural gas
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.205. Department to release production data on crude oil and natural gas (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Revenue shall submit to the department on or before September
      1 of each year, beginning in 1995 for 1994 production data, statistics on crude oil
      as reported to the Department of Revenue under the crude oil excise tax requirements
      of KRS Chapter 137 and statistics on natural gas production as reported to the Department
      of Revenue under the natural resources severance tax requirements of KRS Chapter 143A.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.330. Parties; representation of minors, mentally disabled, and persons not in being
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.330. Parties; representation of minors, mentally disabled, and persons not in being
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.330. Parties; representation of minors, mentally disabled, and persons not in being (2023)
content:
All of the persons in being who have any present or contingent interest in the lands
   or estate or interest sought to be leased shall be made parties to the proceedings
   authorized inKRS 353.300to353.380, with any infant or infants being represented either by next friend or statutory
   guardian or guardian ad litem, or in the case of constructive service of summons by
   a warning order attorney appointed as in other cases.  Any person adjudged mentally disabled shall be represented by his guardian or conservator
   or by guardian ad litem, or, in the case of constructive service of summons as in
   civil actions generally, by a warning order attorney appointed as in other cases.  If the court specifically finds that the welfare or interest of any person or persons
   not in being requires special representation, the court may appoint a trustee ad litem
   to represent such unknown parties not in being or each separate class thereof, and
   such trustee ad litem shall file such pleadings or answer and take such steps as he
   deems proper, and such unknown persons will be fully bound by the proceedings hereunder.  Otherwise, and in the absence of such finding by the court, it shall not be necessary
   to make parties any persons not in being, either as “unknown defendants” or otherwise,
   but the persons in being who are parties shall stand for and represent the full title
   and whole interest in said lands or estate or interest therein, and all parties not
   in being who might have some contingent or future interest therein, and all persons,
   whether in being or not in being, having any interest, present, future or contingent,
   in the property sought to be leased, will be fully bound by the proceedings hereunder.  It shall be permissible, however, to make defendants any unknown persons who might
   have any interest in the land sought to be leased, under the style of “unknown defendants.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.220. Nature of agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.220. Nature of agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.220. Nature of agreement (2023)
content:
A consolidation agreement, within the provisions ofKRS 353.210to353.230, is an agreement which provides for the consolidation of an oil and gas lease, or
   some portion thereof, with some other oil and gas lease or leases, or portions thereof,
   so that the oil and gas leases or portions thereof embraced in such agreement shall
   be operated and developed for oil and gas purposes as one (1) unit lease, and all
   royalties which may accrue from production on such consolidated area shall be treated
   as an entirety and shall be divided among and paid to the owners (or their lawful
   representatives) of the royalties in such area upon an acreage basis, so that each
   shall receive a share of such royalties calculated upon the basis of the ratio between
   each owner's interest in royalty and the entire interest in the royalties embraced
   in the consolidated area.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.340. Alignment of parties; process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.340. Alignment of parties; process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.340. Alignment of parties; process (2023)
content:
Parties to the proceedings hereunder may be aligned either as plaintiffs or defendants,
   but there shall be one (1) or more parties plaintiff and one (1) or more parties defendant.  In the proceedings authorized hereunder any defendant who does not enter his appearance
   may be served with process as provided by law with reference to civil actions generally.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.320. Who may institute proceedings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.320. Who may institute proceedings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.320. Who may institute proceedings (2023)
content:
The proceedings provided for byKRS 353.300to353.380may be instituted upon the petition of any one (1) or more of the parties who have
   a present interest or a contingent interest in the land or estate or interest therein.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.310. Jurisdiction of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.310. Jurisdiction of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.310. Jurisdiction of court (2023)
content:
The Circuit Court of the county wherein the land sought to be leased, or some portion
   thereof, is situated shall have jurisdiction of the proceedings authorized underKRS 353.300to353.380.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.230. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.230. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.230. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon the execution of such a consolidation agreement, the trustee shall file
      with the clerk of the Circuit Court in the county in which the land covered by the
      lease to be consolidated hereunder, or the greater portion thereof, lies a petition
      for an order approving such consolidation agreement setting forth a copy of the consolidation
      agreement and a statement of facts constituting the grounds relied upon to secure
      the approval of such agreement, and shall submit with the petition the affidavits
      of not less than three (3) disinterested owners of real estate in the county wherein
      the proceedings hereunder are brought, as to whether such agreement will be advantageous
      or beneficial to the beneficiaries for whom such trustee is acting, which affidavits
      shall be filed and preserved as records of the Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.260. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.260. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.260. Petition for court approval; affidavits; guardian ad litem; order of approval (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon the execution of such a consolidation agreement, the guardian shall file
      with the clerk of the Circuit Court in the county in which the land covered by the
      lease to be consolidated hereunder, or the greater portion thereof, lies a petition
      for an order approving such consolidation agreement setting forth a copy of the consolidation
      agreement and a statement of facts constituting the grounds relied upon to secure
      the approval of such agreement, and shall submit with the petition the affidavits
      of not less than three (3) disinterested owners of real estate in the county wherein
      the proceedings hereunder are brought, as to whether such agreement will be advantageous
      or beneficial to the minor or minors for whom such guardian is acting, which affidavits
      shall be filed and preserved as records of the Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.300. Appointment of trustee to execute mineral lease where contingent future interests are involved
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.300. Appointment of trustee to execute mineral lease where contingent future interests are involved
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.300. Appointment of trustee to execute mineral lease where contingent future interests are involved (2023)
content:
Where lands, or any estate or interest therein, are subject to any contingent future
   interest, legal or equitable, by way of remainder, reversion, or possibility of reverter,
   upon the happening of a condition subsequent, or otherwise, created by deed, will,
   or otherwise, and whether a trust is involved or not, and it is made to appear that
   it will be advantageous to the present and ultimate owners of said lands or estate
   or interest therein, the court shall have the power, pending the happening of any
   contingency and the vesting of such future interest or interests, to declare a trust
   in said lands or estate or interest therein, appoint a trustee therefor, and to authorize
   such trustee to sell, execute and deliver a valid oil, gas, coal or other mineral
   lease covering said lands or estate or interest therein.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.240. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by guardian
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.240. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by guardian
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.240. Agreement consolidating oil and gas leases may be executed by guardian (2023)
content:
A guardian of a minor may enter into a consolidation agreement, as defined inKRS 353.250, subject to approval by the Circuit Judge as provided inKRS 353.260.  The detailed provisions of such agreement may be such as the court approves, consistently
   with the provisions ofKRS 353.250.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.350. Bond of trustee; terms of sale of lease
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.350. Bond of trustee; terms of sale of lease
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.350. Bond of trustee; terms of sale of lease (2023)
content:
Should the court appoint a trustee pursuant toKRS 353.300, the court shall, in its decree, require such trustee to give a bond in favor of
   the owners of the property which is to be leased and shall fix the amount of such
   bond.  The decree of the court shall further provide for all the terms and provisions of
   the lease which the trustee is authorized to make.  It shall be discretionary with the court as to whether or not the trustee's sale
   of lease shall be public or private, and the decree shall provide therefor, and if
   a public sale be authorized the court shall, in its decree, fix and determine the
   notice to be given.  Such sale shall be for cash, payable on confirmation of sale.  No appraisement shall be required.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.250. Nature of agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.250. Nature of agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.250. Nature of agreement (2023)
content:
A consolidation agreement, within the provisions ofKRS 353.240to353.260, is an agreement which provides for the consolidation of an oil and gas lease, or
   some portion thereof, with some other oil and gas lease or leases, or portions thereof,
   so that the oil and gas leases or portions thereof embraced in such agreement shall
   be operated and developed for oil and gas purposes as one (1) unit lease, and all
   royalties which may accrue from production on such consolidated area shall be treated
   as an entirety and shall be divided among and paid to the owners (or their lawful
   representatives) of the royalties in such area upon an acreage basis, so that each
   shall receive a share of such royalties calculated upon the basis of the ratio between
   each owner's interest in royalty and the entire interest in the royalties embraced
   in the consolidated area.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.360. Execution of sale of lease; report; confirmation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.360. Execution of sale of lease; report; confirmation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.360. Execution of sale of lease; report; confirmation (2023)
content:
The trustee shall proceed, conformably to the provisions of such decree, to sell the
   lease authorized thereby, and after making such sale shall make a report thereof to
   the court.  Upon filing of such report, the court may hear evidence as to whether or not the
   sale price is reasonable, and, if the court be satisfied with the sale and the amount
   received therefor, such sale shall be confirmed by the court and the lease executed
   by the trustee approved by the court on the face thereof.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.380. Disposition of proceeds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.380. Disposition of proceeds (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals›Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development›KY REV ST 353.370. Separate lease by guardian or conservator unnecessary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXVIII. Mines and Minerals › Chapter 353. Mineral Conservation and Development › KY REV ST 353.370. Separate lease by guardian or conservator unnecessary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 353.370. Separate lease by guardian or conservator unnecessary (2023)
content:
If a trustee's lease is granted hereunder, even though one (1) of the parties who
   has an interest or possible interest in the property covered by such lease is a minor
   or a person adjudged mentally disabled, no separate guardian's lease or conservator's
   lease shall be necessary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 1. General Provisions›Part 2. General Definitions and Principles of Interpretation›KY REV ST 355.1-206. Presumptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 2. General Definitions and Principles of Interpretation › KY REV ST 355.1-206. Presumptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-206. Presumptions (2023)
content:
Whenever the Uniform Commercial Code creates a “presumption” with respect to a fact,
   or provides that a fact is “presumed,” the trier of fact must find the existence of
   the fact unless and until evidence is introduced that supports a finding of its nonexistence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 1. General Provisions›Part 1. Short Title; Construction, Application, and Subject Matter of This Chapter›KY REV ST 355.1-105. Severability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 1. Short Title; Construction, Application, and Subject Matter of This Chapter › KY REV ST 355.1-105. Severability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-105. Severability (2023)
content:
If any provision or clause of the Uniform Commercial Code or its application to any
   person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions
   or applications of the Uniform Commercial Code which can be given effect without the
   invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of the Uniform Commercial
   Code are severable.

content:

   its subject matter, no part of it shall be deemed to be impliedly repealed by subsequent
   legislation if such construction can reasonably be avoided.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 1. General Provisions›Part 3. Applicability and General Rules›KY REV ST 355.1-305. Remedies to be liberally administered
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-305. Remedies to be liberally administered
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-305. Remedies to be liberally administered (2023)
content:
(1)  The remedies provided by the Uniform Commercial Code must be liberally administered
      to the end that the aggrieved party may be put in as good a position as if the other
      party had fully performed, but neither consequential or special damages nor penal
      damages may be had except as specifically provided in the Uniform Commercial Code
      or by other rule of law.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-306. Waiver or renunciation of claim or right after breach

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 1. General Provisions›Part 3. Applicability and General Rules›KY REV ST 355.1-310. Subordinated obligations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-310. Subordinated obligations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-310. Subordinated obligations (2023)
content:
An obligation may be issued as subordinated to performance of another obligation of
   the person obligated, or a creditor may subordinate its right to performance of an
   obligation by agreement with either the person obligated or another creditor of the
   person obligated.  Subordination does not create a security interest as against either the common debtor
   or a subordinated creditor.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-308. Performance or acceptance under reservation of rights

content:
(1)  A party that with explicit reservation of rights performs or promises performance
      or assents to performance in a manner demanded or offered by the other party does
      not thereby prejudice the rights reserved.  Such words as “without prejudice,” “under protest,” or the like are sufficient.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-307. Prima facie evidence by third-party documents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-307. Prima facie evidence by third-party documents (2023)
content:
A document in due form purporting to be a bill of lading, policy or certificate of
   insurance, official weigher's or inspector's certificate, consular invoice, or any
   other document authorized or required by the contract to be issued by a third party
   is prima facie evidence of its own authenticity and genuineness and of the facts stated
   in the document by the third party.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 1. General Provisions›Part 3. Applicability and General Rules›KY REV ST 355.1-309. Option to accelerate at will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 1. General Provisions › Part 3. Applicability and General Rules › KY REV ST 355.1-309. Option to accelerate at will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.1-309. Option to accelerate at will (2023)
content:
A term providing that one (1) party or that party's successor in interest may accelerate
   payment or performance or require collateral or additional collateral “at will” or when the party “deems itself insecure,” or words of similar import, means that the party has power to do so only if that
   party in good faith believes that the prospect of payment or performance is impaired.  The burden of establishing lack of good faith is on the party against which the
   power has been exercised.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency” (2023)
content:
(1)  “Merchant” means a person who deals in goods of the kind or otherwise by his occupation holds
      himself out as having knowledge or skill peculiar to the practices or goods involved
      in the transaction or to whom such knowledge or skill may be attributed by his employment
      of an agent or broker or other intermediary who by his occupation holds himself out
      as having such knowledge or skill.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from this article
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from this article
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from this article (2023)
content:
Unless the context otherwise requires, this article applies to transactions in goods;
   it does not apply to any transaction which although in the form of an unconditional
   contract to sell or present sale is intended to operate only as a security transaction
   nor does this article impair or repeal any statute regulating sales to consumers,
   farmers or other specified classes of buyers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 1. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit” (2023)
content:
(1)  “Goods” means all things (including specially manufactured goods) which are movable at the
      time of identification to the contract for sale other than the money in which the
      price is to be paid, investment securities (Article 8) and things in action. “Goods” also includes the unborn young of animals and growing crops and other identified
      things attached to realty as described in the section on goods to be severed from
      realty (KRS 355.2-107).

content:
Terms with respect to which the confirmatory memoranda of the parties agree or which
   are otherwise set forth in a writing intended by the parties as a final expression
   of their agreement with respect to such terms as are included therein may not be contradicted
   by evidence of any prior agreement or of a contemporaneous oral agreement but may
   be explained or supplemented:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this section a contract for the sale of goods
      for the price of $500 or more is not enforceable by way of action or defense unless
      there is some writing sufficient to indicate that a contract for sale has been made
      between the parties and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought or
      by his authorized agent or broker.  A writing is not insufficient because it omits or incorrectly states a term agreed
      upon but the contract is not enforceable under this paragraph beyond the quantity
      of goods shown in such writing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative (2023)
content:
The affixing of a seal to a writing evidencing a contract for sale or an offer to
   buy or sell goods does not constitute the writing a sealed instrument and the law
   with respect to sealed instruments does not apply to such a contract or offer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for the sale of minerals or the like (including oil and gas) or a
      structure or its materials to be removed from realty is a contract for the sale of
      goods within this article if they are to be severed by the seller, but until severance
      a purported present sale thereof which is not effective as a transfer of an interest
      in land is effective only as a contract to sell.

content: (1)  Unless otherwise unambiguously indicated by the language or circumstances

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers (2023)
content:
An offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed writing which by its terms
   gives assurance that it will be held open is not revocable, for lack of consideration,
   during the time stated or if no time is stated for a reasonable time, but in no event
   may such period of irrevocability exceed three (3) months;  but any such term of assurance
   on a form supplied by the offeree must be separately signed by the offeror.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for sale of goods may be made in any manner sufficient to show agreement,
      including conduct by both parties which recognizes the existence of such a contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation (2023)
content:
(1)  A definite and seasonable expression of acceptance or a written confirmation
      which is sent within a reasonable time operates as an acceptance even though it states
      terms additional to or different from those offered or agreed upon, unless acceptance
      is expressly made conditional on assent to the additional or different terms.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-106. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation” (2023)
content: (1)  In this article unless the context otherwise requires “contract” and “agreement” are limited to those relating to the present or future sale of goods. “Contract for sale” includes both a present sale of goods and a contract to sell goods at a future time.  A “sale” consists in the passing of title from the seller to the buyer for a price (KRS 355.2-401).  A “present sale” means a sale which is accomplished by the making of the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver (2023)
content:
(1)  An agreement modifying a contract within this article needs no consideration
      to be binding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights (2023)
content:
(1)  A party may perform his duty through a delegate unless otherwise agreed or unless
      the other party has a substantial interest in having his original promisor perform
      or control the acts required by the contract.  No delegation of performance relieves the party delegating of any duty to perform
      or any liability for breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties (2023)
content:
The obligation of the seller is to transfer and deliver and that of the buyer is to
   accept and pay in accordance with the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks (2023)
content:
Where this article allocates a risk or a burden as between the parties “unless otherwise
   agreed,” the agreement may not only shift the allocation but may also divide the risk
   or burden.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise (2023)
content:
(1)  The price can be made payable in money or otherwise.  If it is payable in whole or in part in goods each party is a seller of the goods
      which he is to transfer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause (2023)
content:
(1)  If the court as a matter of law finds the contract or any clause of the contract
      to have been unconscionable at the time it was made the court may refuse to enforce
      the contract, or it may enforce the remainder of the contract without the unconscionable
      clause, or it may so limit the application of any unconscionable clause as to avoid
      any unconscionable result.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination (2023)
content:
(1)  The time for shipment or delivery or any other action under a contract if not
      provided in this article or agreed upon shall be a reasonable time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings (2023)
content:
(1)  A term which measures the quantity by the output of the seller or the requirements
      of the buyer means such actual output or requirements as may occur in good faith,
      except that no quantity unreasonably disproportionate to any stated estimate or in
      the absence of a stated estimate to any normal or otherwise comparable prior output
      or requirements may be tendered or demanded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-305. Open price term

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-305. Open price term (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-307. Delivery in single lot or several lots
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-307. Delivery in single lot or several lots
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-307. Delivery in single lot or several lots (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed all goods called for by a contract for sale must be tendered
   in a single delivery and payment is due only on such tender but where the circumstances
   give either party the right to make or demand delivery in lots the price if it can
   be apportioned may be demanded for each lot.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose (2023)
content:
Where the seller at the time of contracting has reason to know any particular purpose
   for which the goods are required and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill
   or judgment to select or furnish suitable goods, there is unless excluded or modified
   underKRS 355.2-316an implied warranty that the goods shall be fit for such purpose.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-312. Warranty of title and against infringement; buyer's obligation against infringement (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-316. Exclusion or modification of warranties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-316. Exclusion or modification of warranties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-316. Exclusion or modification of warranties (2023)
content:
(1)  Words or conduct relevant to the creation of an express warranty and words or
      conduct tending to negate or limit warranty shall be construed wherever reasonable
      as consistent with each other;  but subject to the provisions of this article on parol
      or extrinsic evidence (KRS 355.2-202) negation or limitation is inoperative to the extent that such construction is unreasonable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied (2023)
content:
A seller's warranty whether express or implied extends to any natural person who is
   in the family or household of his buyer or who is a guest in his home if it is reasonable
   to expect that such person may use, consume or be affected by the goods and who is
   injured in person by breach of the warranty.  A seller may not exclude or limit the operation of this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless excluded or modified (KRS 355.2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their
      sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.  Under this section the serving for value of food or drink to be consumed either
      on the premises or elsewhere is a sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied (2023)
content:
Warranties whether express or implied shall be construed as consistent with each other
   and as cumulative, but if such construction is unreasonable the intention of the parties
   shall determine which warranty is dominant.  In ascertaining that intention the following rules apply:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms (2023)
content:
(1)  The term C.I.F. means that the price includes in a lump sum the cost of the goods
      and the insurance and freight to the named destination.  The term C. & F. or C.F. means that the price so includes cost and freight to the
      named destination.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-322. Delivery “ex-ship”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-322. Delivery “ex-ship”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-322. Delivery “ex-ship” (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless otherwise agreed a term for delivery of goods “ex-ship” (which means from
      the carrying vessel) or in equivalent language is not restricted to a particular ship
      and requires delivery from a ship which has reached a place at the named port of destination
      where goods of the kind are usually discharged.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-502. Buyer's right to goods on seller's repudiation, failure to deliver, or insolvency

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas” (2023)
content:
(1)  Where the contract contemplates overseas shipment and contains a term C.I.F.
      or C. & F. or F.O.B. vessel, the seller unless otherwise agreed must obtain a negotiable
      bill of lading stating that the goods have been loaded on board or, in the case of
      a term C.I.F. or C. & F., received for shipment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-319. F.O.B. and F.A.S. terms

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-503. Manner of seller's tender of delivery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-503. Manner of seller's tender of delivery

content:
(1)  Tender of delivery requires that the seller put and hold conforming goods at
      the buyer's disposition and give the buyer any notification reasonably necessary to

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance (2023)
content:
(1)  An agreement for sale which is otherwise sufficiently definite (subsection (3)
      ofKRS 355.2-204) to be a contract is not made invalid by the fact that it leaves particulars of performance
      to be specified by one (1) of the parties.  Any such specification must be made in good faith and within limits set by commercial
      reasonableness.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-328. Sale by auction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-328. Sale by auction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-328. Sale by auction (2023)
content:
(1)  In a sale by auction if goods are put up in lots each lot is the subject of a
      separate sale.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › KY REV ST 355.2-402. Rights of seller's creditors against sold goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-402. Rights of seller's creditors against sold goods (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsections (2) and (3), rights of unsecured creditors
      of the seller with respect to goods which have been identified to a contract for sale
      are subject to the buyer's rights to recover the goods under this article (KRS 355.2-502and355.2-716).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›KY REV ST 355.2-401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of this section
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › KY REV ST 355.2-401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of this section
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of this section (2023)
content:
Each provision of this article with regard to the rights, obligations and remedies
   of the seller, the buyer, purchasers or other third parties applies irrespective of

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-501. Insurable interest in goods; manner of identification of goods

content:
(1)  The buyer obtains a special property and an insurable interest in goods by identification
      of existing goods as goods to which the contract refers even though the goods so identified
      are nonconforming and he has an option to return or reject them.  Such identification can be made at any time and in any manner explicitly agreed
      to by the parties.  In the absence of explicit agreement identification occurs

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›KY REV ST 355.2-403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › KY REV ST 355.2-403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting” (2023)
content:
(1)  A purchaser of goods acquires all title which his transferor had or had power
      to transfer except that a purchaser of a limited interest acquires rights only to

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-507. Effect of seller's tender; delivery on condition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-507. Effect of seller's tender; delivery on condition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-507. Effect of seller's tender; delivery on condition (2023)
content:
(1)  Tender of delivery is a condition to the buyer's duty to accept the goods and,
      unless otherwise agreed, to his duty to pay for them.  Tender entitles the seller to acceptance of the goods and to payment according to

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency (2023)
content:
(1)  A financing agency by paying or purchasing for value a draft which relates to
      a shipment of goods acquires to the extent of the payment or purchase and in addition
      to its own rights under the draft and any document of title securing it any rights
      of the shipper in the goods including the right to stop delivery and the shipper's
      right to have the draft honored by the buyer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement

content:
(1)  Where any tender or delivery by the seller is rejected because nonconforming
      and the time for performance has not yet expired, the seller may seasonably notify
      the buyer of his intention to cure and may then within the contract time make a conforming
      delivery.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-510. Effect of breach on risk of loss

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-510. Effect of breach on risk of loss (2023)
content:
(1)  Where a tender or delivery of goods so fails to conform to the contract as to
      give a right of rejection the risk of their loss remains on the seller until cure
      or acceptance.

content:

      to tender and complete any delivery.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-513. Buyer's right to inspection of goods

content:
(1)  Unless otherwise agreed and subject to subsection (3), where goods are tendered
      or delivered or identified to the contract for sale, the buyer has a right before
      payment or acceptance to inspect them at any reasonable place and time and in any
      reasonable manner.  When the seller is required or authorized to send the goods to the buyer, the inspection
      may be after their arrival.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed documents against which a draft is drawn are to be delivered
   to the drawee on acceptance of the draft if it is payable more than three (3) days
   after presentment;  otherwise, only on payment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-602. Manner and effect of rightful rejection

content: (1)  Rejection of goods must be within a reasonable time after their delivery or tender.  It is ineffective unless the buyer seasonably notifies the seller.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-603. Merchant buyer's duties as to rightfully rejected goods
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-603. Merchant buyer's duties as to rightfully rejected goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-603. Merchant buyer's duties as to rightfully rejected goods (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to any security interest in the buyer (subsection (3) ofKRS 355.2-711), when the seller has no agent or place of business at the market of rejection a
      merchant buyer is under a duty after rejection of goods in his possession or control
      to follow any reasonable instructions received from the seller with respect to the
      goods and in the absence of such instructions to make reasonable efforts to sell them
      for the seller's account if they are perishable or threaten to decline in value speedily.  Instructions are not reasonable if on demand indemnity for expenses is not forthcoming.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-605. Waiver of buyer's objections by failure to particularize

content:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-604. Buyer's options as to salvage of rightfully rejected goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-604. Buyer's options as to salvage of rightfully rejected goods (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions ofKRS 355.2-603on perishables if the seller gives no instructions within a reasonable time after
   notification of rejection the buyer may store the rejected goods for the seller's
   account or reship them to him or resell them for the seller's account with reimbursement
   as provided inKRS 355.2-603.  Such action is not acceptance or conversion.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part (2023)
content:
(1)  The buyer may revoke his acceptance of a lot or commercial unit whose nonconformity
      substantially impairs its value to him if he has accepted it

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-612. “Installment contract”; breach
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-612. “Installment contract”; breach
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-612. “Installment contract”; breach (2023)
content:
(1)  An “installment contract” is one which requires or authorizes the delivery of goods in separate lots to be
      separately accepted, even though the contract contains a clause “each delivery is
      a separate contract” or its equivalent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-613. Casualty to identified goods

content:
Where the contract requires for its performance goods identified when the contract

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for sale imposes an obligation on each party that the other's expectation
      of receiving due performance will not be impaired.  When reasonable grounds for insecurity arise with respect to the performance of
      either party the other may in writing demand adequate assurance of due performance
      and until he receives such assurance may if commercially reasonable suspend any performance
      for which he has not already received the agreed return.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance (2023)
content:
(1)  Where without fault of either party the agreed berthing, loading, or unloading
      facilities fail or an agreed type of carrier becomes unavailable or the agreed manner
      of delivery otherwise becomes commercially impracticable but a commercially reasonable
      substitute is available, such substitute performance must be tendered and accepted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation (2023)
content:
(1)  Until the repudiating party's next performance is due he can retract his repudiation
      unless the aggrieved party has since the repudiation canceled or materially changed
      his position or otherwise indicated that he considers the repudiation final.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired (2023)
content:
Remedies for breach of any obligation or promise collateral or ancillary to a contract
   for sale are not impaired by the provisions of this article.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-703. Seller's remedies in general
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-703. Seller's remedies in general
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-703. Seller's remedies in general (2023)
content:
Where the buyer wrongfully rejects or revokes acceptance of goods or fails to make
   a payment due on or before delivery or repudiates with respect to a part or the whole,
   then with respect to any goods directly affected and, if the breach is of the whole
   contract (KRS 355.2-612), then also with respect to the whole undelivered balance, the aggrieved seller may

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-705. Seller's stoppage of delivery in transit or otherwise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-705. Seller's stoppage of delivery in transit or otherwise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-705. Seller's stoppage of delivery in transit or otherwise (2023)
content:
(1)  The seller may stop delivery of goods in the possession of a carrier or other
      bailee when he discovers the buyer to be insolvent (KRS 355. 2-702) and may stop delivery of carload, truckload, planeload or larger shipments
      of express or freight when the buyer repudiates or fails to make a payment due before
      delivery or if for any other reason the seller has a right to withhold or reclaim
      the goods.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-709. Action for the price
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-709. Action for the price
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-709. Action for the price (2023)
content:
(1)  When the buyer fails to pay the price as it becomes due the seller may recover,
      together with any incidental damages underKRS 355.2-710, the price

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-707. “Person in the position of a seller”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-707. “Person in the position of a seller”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-707. “Person in the position of a seller” (2023)
content:
(1)  A “person in the position of a seller” includes as against a principal an agent who has paid or become responsible for
      the price of goods on behalf of his principal or anyone who otherwise holds a security
      interest or other right in goods similar to that of a seller.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-708. Seller's damages for nonacceptance or repudiation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-708. Seller's damages for nonacceptance or repudiation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-708. Seller's damages for nonacceptance or repudiation (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to subsection (2) and to the provisions of this article with respect
      to proof of market price (KRS 355.2-723), the measure of damages for nonacceptance or repudiation by the buyer is the difference
      between the market price at the time and place for tender and the unpaid contract
      price together with any incidental damages provided in this article (KRS 355.2-710), but less expenses saved in consequence of the buyer's breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-713. Buyer's damages for nondelivery or repudiation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-713. Buyer's damages for nondelivery or repudiation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-713. Buyer's damages for nondelivery or repudiation (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to the provisions of this article with respect to proof of market price
      (KRS 355.2-723), the measure of damages for nondelivery or repudiation by the seller is the difference
      between the market price at the time when the buyer learned of the breach and the
      contract price together with any incidental and consequential damages provided in
      this article (KRS 355.2-715), but less expenses saved in consequence of the seller's breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-706. Seller's resale including contract for resale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-706. Seller's resale including contract for resale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-706. Seller's resale including contract for resale (2023)
content:
(1)  Under the conditions stated inKRS 355.2-703on seller's remedies, the seller may resell the goods concerned or the undelivered
      balance thereof.  Where the resale is made in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner the
      seller may recover the difference between the resale price and the contract price
      together with any incidental damages allowed under the provisions of this article
      (KRS 355.2-710), but less expenses saved in consequence of the buyer's breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-714. Buyer's damages for breach in regard to accepted goods
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-714. Buyer's damages for breach in regard to accepted goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-714. Buyer's damages for breach in regard to accepted goods (2023)
content:
(1)  Where the buyer has accepted goods and given notification (subsection (3) ofKRS 355.2-607) he may recover as damages for any nonconformity of tender the loss resulting in
      the ordinary course of events from the seller's breach as determined in any manner
      which is reasonable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-715. Buyer's incidental and consequential damages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-715. Buyer's incidental and consequential damages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-715. Buyer's incidental and consequential damages (2023)
content:
(1)  Incidental damages resulting from the seller's breach include expenses reasonably
      incurred in inspection, receipt, transportation and care and custody of goods rightfully
      rejected, any commercially reasonable charges, expenses or commissions in connection
      with effecting cover and any other reasonable expense incident to the delay or other
      breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from this article
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from this article
