content:
Unless the context otherwise requires, this article applies to transactions in goods;
   it does not apply to any transaction which although in the form of an unconditional
   contract to sell or present sale is intended to operate only as a security transaction
   nor does this article impair or repeal any statute regulating sales to consumers,
   farmers or other specified classes of buyers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-710. Seller's incidental damages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-710. Seller's incidental damages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-710. Seller's incidental damages (2023)
content:
Incidental damages to an aggrieved seller include any commercially reasonable charges,
   expenses or commissions incurred in stopping delivery, in the transportation, care
   and custody of goods after the buyer's breach, in connection with return or resale
   of the goods or otherwise resulting from the breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-103. Definitions and index of definitions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-103. Definitions and index of definitions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-103. Definitions and index of definitions (2023)
content: (1)  In this article unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-101. Short title
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-101. Short title
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-101. Short title (2023)
content: This article shall be known and may be cited as Uniform Commercial Code--Sales.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency” (2023)
content:
(1)  “Merchant” means a person who deals in goods of the kind or otherwise by his occupation holds
      himself out as having knowledge or skill peculiar to the practices or goods involved
      in the transaction or to whom such knowledge or skill may be attributed by his employment
      of an agent or broker or other intermediary who by his occupation holds himself out
      as having such knowledge or skill.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit” (2023)
content:
(1)  “Goods” means all things (including specially manufactured goods) which are movable at the
      time of identification to the contract for sale other than the money in which the
      price is to be paid, investment securities (Article 8) and things in action. “Goods” also includes the unborn young of animals and growing crops and other identified
      things attached to realty as described in the section on goods to be severed from
      realty (KRS 355.2-107).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-107. Goods to be severed from realty; recording (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for the sale of minerals or the like (including oil and gas) or a
      structure or its materials to be removed from realty is a contract for the sale of
      goods within this article if they are to be severed by the seller, but until severance
      a purported present sale thereof which is not effective as a transfer of an interest
      in land is effective only as a contract to sell.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-711. Buyer's remedies in general; buyer's security interest in rejected goods
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-711. Buyer's remedies in general; buyer's security interest in rejected goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-711. Buyer's remedies in general; buyer's security interest in rejected goods (2023)
content:
(1)  Where the seller fails to make delivery or repudiates or the buyer rightfully
      rejects or justifiably revokes acceptance then with respect to any goods involved,
      and with respect to the whole if the breach goes to the whole contract (KRS 355.2-612), the buyer may cancel and whether or not he has done so may in addition to recovering
      so much of the price as has been paid

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-202. Final written expression; parol or extrinsic evidence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-202. Final written expression; parol or extrinsic evidence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-202. Final written expression; parol or extrinsic evidence (2023)
content:
Terms with respect to which the confirmatory memoranda of the parties agree or which
   are otherwise set forth in a writing intended by the parties as a final expression
   of their agreement with respect to such terms as are included therein may not be contradicted
   by evidence of any prior agreement or of a contemporaneous oral agreement but may
   be explained or supplemented:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-716. Buyer's right to specific performance or replevin
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-716. Buyer's right to specific performance or replevin
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-716. Buyer's right to specific performance or replevin (2023)
content:
(1)  Specific performance may be decreed where the goods are unique or in other proper
      circumstances.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this section a contract for the sale of goods
      for the price of $500 or more is not enforceable by way of action or defense unless
      there is some writing sufficient to indicate that a contract for sale has been made
      between the parties and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought or
      by his authorized agent or broker.  A writing is not insufficient because it omits or incorrectly states a term agreed
      upon but the contract is not enforceable under this paragraph beyond the quantity
      of goods shown in such writing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-718. Liquidation or limitation of damages; deposits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-718. Liquidation or limitation of damages; deposits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-718. Liquidation or limitation of damages; deposits (2023)
content:
(1)  Damages for breach by either party may be liquidated in the agreement but only
      at an amount which is reasonable in the light of the anticipated or actual harm caused
      by the breach, the difficulties of proof of loss, and the inconvenience or nonfeasibility
      of otherwise obtaining an adequate remedy.  A term fixing unreasonably large liquidated damages is void as a penalty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-712. “Cover”; buyer's procurement of substitute goods
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-712. “Cover”; buyer's procurement of substitute goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-712. “Cover”; buyer's procurement of substitute goods (2023)
content:
(1)  After a breach withinKRS 355.2-711the buyer may “cover” by making in good faith and without unreasonable delay any
      reasonable purchase of or contract to purchase goods in substitution for those due
      from the seller.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-717. Deduction of damages from the price
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-717. Deduction of damages from the price
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-717. Deduction of damages from the price (2023)
content:
The buyer on notifying the seller of his intention to do so may deduct all or any
   part of the damages resulting from any breach of the contract from any part of the
   price still due under the same contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter›KY REV ST 355.2-106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 1. Short Title; General Construction and Subject Matter › KY REV ST 355.2-106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation” (2023)
content: (1)  In this article unless the context otherwise requires “contract” and “agreement” are limited to those relating to the present or future sale of goods. “Contract for sale” includes both a present sale of goods and a contract to sell goods at a future time.  A “sale” consists in the passing of title from the seller to the buyer for a price (KRS 355.2-401).  A “present sale” means a sale which is accomplished by the making of the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-719. Contractual modification or limitation of remedy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-719. Contractual modification or limitation of remedy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-719. Contractual modification or limitation of remedy (2023)
content: (1)  Subject to the provisions of subsections (2) and (3) of this section and ofKRS 355.2-718on liquidation and limitation of damages,

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-720. Effect of “cancellation” or “rescission” on claims for antecedent breach
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-720. Effect of “cancellation” or “rescission” on claims for antecedent breach
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-720. Effect of “cancellation” or “rescission” on claims for antecedent breach (2023)
content:
Unless the contrary intention clearly appears, expressions of “cancellation” or “rescission” of the contract or the like shall not be construed as a renunciation or discharge
   of any claim in damages for an antecedent breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-204. Formation in general (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for sale of goods may be made in any manner sufficient to show agreement,
      including conduct by both parties which recognizes the existence of such a contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-203. Seals inoperative (2023)
content:
The affixing of a seal to a writing evidencing a contract for sale or an offer to
   buy or sell goods does not constitute the writing a sealed instrument and the law
   with respect to sealed instruments does not apply to such a contract or offer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-723. Proof of market price: time and place
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-723. Proof of market price: time and place
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-723. Proof of market price: time and place (2023)
content:
(1)  If an action based on anticipatory repudiation comes to trial before the time
      for performance with respect to some or all of the goods, any damages based on market
      price (KRS 355.2-708or355.2-713) shall be determined according to the price of such goods prevailing at the time
      when the aggrieved party learned of the repudiation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-206. Offer and acceptance in formation of contract
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-206. Offer and acceptance in formation of contract
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-206. Offer and acceptance in formation of contract (2023)
content: (1)  Unless otherwise unambiguously indicated by the language or circumstances

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation (2023)
content:
(1)  A definite and seasonable expression of acceptance or a written confirmation
      which is sent within a reasonable time operates as an acceptance even though it states
      terms additional to or different from those offered or agreed upon, unless acceptance
      is expressly made conditional on assent to the additional or different terms.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-209. Modification, rescission and waiver (2023)
content:
(1)  An agreement modifying a contract within this article needs no consideration
      to be binding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-722. Who can sue third parties for injury to goods
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-722. Who can sue third parties for injury to goods
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-722. Who can sue third parties for injury to goods (2023)
content:
Where a third party so deals with goods which have been identified to a contract for
   sale as to cause actionable injury to a party to that contract

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-304. Price payable in money, goods, realty, or otherwise (2023)
content:
(1)  The price can be made payable in money or otherwise.  If it is payable in whole or in part in goods each party is a seller of the goods
      which he is to transfer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-303. Allocation or division of risks (2023)
content:
Where this article allocates a risk or a burden as between the parties “unless otherwise
   agreed,” the agreement may not only shift the allocation but may also divide the risk
   or burden.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-305. Open price term
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-305. Open price term
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-305. Open price term (2023)
content:
(1)  The parties if they so intend can conclude a contract for sale even though the
      price is not settled.  In such a case the price is a reasonable price at the time for delivery if

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-205. Firm offers (2023)
content:
An offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed writing which by its terms
   gives assurance that it will be held open is not revocable, for lack of consideration,
   during the time stated or if no time is stated for a reasonable time, but in no event
   may such period of irrevocability exceed three (3) months;  but any such term of assurance
   on a form supplied by the offeree must be separately signed by the offeror.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings (2023)
content:
(1)  A term which measures the quantity by the output of the seller or the requirements
      of the buyer means such actual output or requirements as may occur in good faith,
      except that no quantity unreasonably disproportionate to any stated estimate or in
      the absence of a stated estimate to any normal or otherwise comparable prior output
      or requirements may be tendered or demanded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-301. General obligations of parties (2023)
content:
The obligation of the seller is to transfer and deliver and that of the buyer is to
   accept and pay in accordance with the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-721. Remedies for fraud
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-721. Remedies for fraud
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-721. Remedies for fraud (2023)
content:
Remedies for material misrepresentation or fraud include all remedies available under
   this article for nonfraudulent breach.  Neither rescission or a claim for rescission of the contract for sale nor rejection
   or return of the goods shall bar or be deemed inconsistent with a claim for damages
   or other remedy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-724. Admissibility of market quotations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-724. Admissibility of market quotations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-724. Admissibility of market quotations (2023)
content:
Whenever the prevailing price or value of any goods regularly bought and sold in any
   established commodity market is in issue, reports in official publications or trade
   journals or in newspapers or periodicals of general circulation published as the reports
   of such market shall be admissible in evidence.  The circumstances of the preparation of such a report may be shown to affect its
   weight but not its admissibility.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 2. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights (2023)
content:
(1)  A party may perform his duty through a delegate unless otherwise agreed or unless
      the other party has a substantial interest in having his original promisor perform
      or control the acts required by the contract.  No delegation of performance relieves the party delegating of any duty to perform
      or any liability for breach.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-311. Options and cooperation respecting performance (2023)
content:
(1)  An agreement for sale which is otherwise sufficiently definite (subsection (3)
      ofKRS 355.2-204) to be a contract is not made invalid by the fact that it leaves particulars of performance
      to be specified by one (1) of the parties.  Any such specification must be made in good faith and within limits set by commercial
      reasonableness.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination (2023)
content:
(1)  The time for shipment or delivery or any other action under a contract if not
      provided in this article or agreed upon shall be a reasonable time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Article 2. Sales›Part 7. Remedies›KY REV ST 355.2-725. Statute of limitations in contracts for sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Article 2. Sales › Part 7. Remedies › KY REV ST 355.2-725. Statute of limitations in contracts for sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-725. Statute of limitations in contracts for sale (2023)
content:
(1)  An action for breach of any contract for sale must be commenced within four (4)
      years after the cause of action has accrued.  By the original agreement the parties may reduce the period of limitation to not
      less than one (1) year but may not extend it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-308. Absence of specified place for delivery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-308. Absence of specified place for delivery
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-308. Absence of specified place for delivery (2023)
content: Unless otherwise agreed

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-313. Express warranties by affirmation, promise, description, sample
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-313. Express warranties by affirmation, promise, description, sample
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-313. Express warranties by affirmation, promise, description, sample (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-316. Exclusion or modification of warranties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-316. Exclusion or modification of warranties

      conduct tending to negate or limit warranty shall be construed wherever reasonable
      as consistent with each other;  but subject to the provisions of this article on parol
      or extrinsic evidence (KRS 355.2-202) negation or limitation is inoperative to the extent that such construction is unreasonable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-307. Delivery in single lot or several lots

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-307. Delivery in single lot or several lots (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed all goods called for by a contract for sale must be tendered
   in a single delivery and payment is due only on such tender but where the circumstances
   give either party the right to make or demand delivery in lots the price if it can
   be apportioned may be demanded for each lot.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-302. Unconscionable contract or clause (2023)
content:
(1)  If the court as a matter of law finds the contract or any clause of the contract
      to have been unconscionable at the time it was made the court may refuse to enforce
      the contract, or it may enforce the remainder of the contract without the unconscionable
      clause, or it may so limit the application of any unconscionable clause as to avoid
      any unconscionable result.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-315. Implied warranty; fitness for particular purpose (2023)
content:
Where the seller at the time of contracting has reason to know any particular purpose
   for which the goods are required and that the buyer is relying on the seller's skill
   or judgment to select or furnish suitable goods, there is unless excluded or modified
   underKRS 355.2-316an implied warranty that the goods shall be fit for such purpose.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied

content:
Warranties whether express or implied shall be construed as consistent with each other
   and as cumulative, but if such construction is unreasonable the intention of the parties

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-321. C.I.F. or C. & F.: “net landed weights”; “payment on arrival”; warranty of condition on arrival
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-321. C.I.F. or C. & F.: “net landed weights”; “payment on arrival”; warranty of condition on arrival

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-314. Implied warranty; merchantability; usage of trade (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless excluded or modified (KRS 355.2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their
      sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.  Under this section the serving for value of food or drink to be consumed either
      on the premises or elsewhere is a sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms (2023)
content:
(1)  The term C.I.F. means that the price includes in a lump sum the cost of the goods
      and the insurance and freight to the named destination.  The term C. & F. or C.F. means that the price so includes cost and freight to the
      named destination.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied (2023)
content:
A seller's warranty whether express or implied extends to any natural person who is
   in the family or household of his buyer or who is a guest in his home if it is reasonable
   to expect that such person may use, consume or be affected by the goods and who is
   injured in person by breach of the warranty.  A seller may not exclude or limit the operation of this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 3. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›KY REV ST 355.2-322. Delivery “ex-ship”

content:
(1)  Unless otherwise agreed a term for delivery of goods “ex-ship” (which means from
      the carrying vessel) or in equivalent language is not restricted to a particular ship
      and requires delivery from a ship which has reached a place at the named port of destination
      where goods of the kind are usually discharged.

(1)  Where the contract contemplates overseas shipment and contains a term C.I.F.

Each provision of this article with regard to the rights, obligations and remedies

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 4. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›KY REV ST 355.2-402. Rights of seller's creditors against sold goods

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-507. Effect of seller's tender; delivery on condition (2023)
content:
(1)  Tender of delivery is a condition to the buyer's duty to accept the goods and,
      unless otherwise agreed, to his duty to pay for them.  Tender entitles the seller to acceptance of the goods and to payment according to
      the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-506. Rights of financing agency (2023)
content:
(1)  A financing agency by paying or purchasing for value a draft which relates to
      a shipment of goods acquires to the extent of the payment or purchase and in addition
      to its own rights under the draft and any document of title securing it any rights
      of the shipper in the goods including the right to stop delivery and the shipper's
      right to have the draft honored by the buyer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 5. Performance › KY REV ST 355.2-508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement

      the buyer of his intention to cure and may then within the contract time make a conforming
      delivery.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-513. Buyer's right to inspection of goods

content:
(1)  Unless otherwise agreed and subject to subsection (3), where goods are tendered
      or delivered or identified to the contract for sale, the buyer has a right before
      payment or acceptance to inspect them at any reasonable place and time and in any
      reasonable manner.  When the seller is required or authorized to send the goods to the buyer, the inspection
      may be after their arrival.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 5. Performance›KY REV ST 355.2-514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment

content:
Unless otherwise agreed documents against which a draft is drawn are to be delivered
   to the drawee on acceptance of the draft if it is payable more than three (3) days
   after presentment;  otherwise, only on payment.

content: (1)  Rejection of goods must be within a reasonable time after their delivery or tender.  It is ineffective unless the buyer seasonably notifies the seller.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-601. Buyer's rights on improper delivery

      goods and in the absence of such instructions to make reasonable efforts to sell them
      for the seller's account if they are perishable or threaten to decline in value speedily.  Instructions are not reasonable if on demand indemnity for expenses is not forthcoming.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-612. “Installment contract”; breach

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-612. “Installment contract”; breach (2023)
content:
(1)  An “installment contract” is one which requires or authorizes the delivery of goods in separate lots to be
      separately accepted, even though the contract contains a clause “each delivery is
      a separate contract” or its equivalent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-610. Anticipatory repudiation

Where the contract requires for its performance goods identified when the contract

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-614. Substituted performance (2023)
content:
(1)  Where without fault of either party the agreed berthing, loading, or unloading
      facilities fail or an agreed type of carrier becomes unavailable or the agreed manner
      of delivery otherwise becomes commercially impracticable but a commercially reasonable
      substitute is available, such substitute performance must be tendered and accepted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code›Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse›KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 355. Uniform Commercial Code › Part 6. Breach, Repudiation, and Excuse › KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 355.2-609. Right to adequate assurance of performance (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract for sale imposes an obligation on each party that the other's expectation
      of receiving due performance will not be impaired.  When reasonable grounds for insecurity arise with respect to the performance of
      either party the other may in writing demand adequate assurance of due performance
      and until he receives such assurance may if commercially reasonable suspend any performance
      for which he has not already received the agreed return.

(1)  Until the repudiating party's next performance is due he can retract his repudiation
      unless the aggrieved party has since the repudiation canceled or materially changed
      his position or otherwise indicated that he considers the repudiation final.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities›KY REV ST 359.220. Lien on stored property held by operator of facility; notice provisions in rental agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities › KY REV ST 359.220. Lien on stored property held by operator of facility; notice provisions in rental agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 359.220. Lien on stored property held by operator of facility; notice provisions in rental agreement (2023)
content:
(1)  The operator of a self-service storage facility or self-contained storage unit
      shall have a lien on all personal property stored within each leased space for rent,
      labor, or other charges, and for expenses reasonably incurred in its sale, as provided
      inKRS 359.200to359.250.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities›KY REV ST 359.250. Short title
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities › KY REV ST 359.250. Short title

content: KRS 359.200to359.250shall be known as the “Kentucky Self-Service Storage Act of 1988.”

content:
(1)  (a) If the occupant is in default for a period of more than forty-five (45) days,
         the operator may enforce a lien by selling the property stored in the leased space
         at a public or private sale, for cash.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities›KY REV ST 359.215. Late fees and other reasonable expense incurred in rent collection or lien enforcement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities › KY REV ST 359.215. Late fees and other reasonable expense incurred in rent collection or lien enforcement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 359.215. Late fees and other reasonable expense incurred in rent collection or lien enforcement (2023)
content:
(1)  A reasonable late fee may be imposed and collected by an owner for each service
      period that an occupant does not pay rent when due under a rental agreement, provided
      that the due date for the rental payment is not earlier than the day before the first
      day of the service period to which the rental payment applies.  No late payment fee shall be assessed unless the rental fee remains unpaid for at
      least five (5) days after the date specified within the rental agreement for the payment
      of the rental fee.

content:
(1)  Except as provided inKRS 360.040, the legal rate of interest is eight percent (8%) per annum, but any party or parties
      may agree, in writing, for the payment of interest in excess of that rate as follows:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.020. Civil penalty for charging excessive interest; partial payment applied first to interest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.020. Civil penalty for charging excessive interest; partial payment applied first to interest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.020. Civil penalty for charging excessive interest; partial payment applied first to interest (2023)
content:
(1)  The taking, receiving, reserving, or charging a rate of interest greater than
      is allowed byKRS 360.010, when knowingly done, shall be deemed a forfeiture of the entire interest which the
      note, bill, or other evidence of debt carries with it, or which has been agreed to
      be paid thereon.  In case the greater rate of interest has been paid, the person by whom it has been
      paid, or his legal representatives, may recover, in an action in the nature of an
      action of debt, twice the amount of the interest thus paid from the creditors taking
      or receiving the same:  provided, that such action is commenced within two (2) years
      from the time the usurious transaction occurred.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities›KY REV ST 359.240. Pre-existing rental agreements unaffected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities › KY REV ST 359.240. Pre-existing rental agreements unaffected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 359.240. Pre-existing rental agreements unaffected (2023)
content:
All rental agreements, entered into before July 15, 1988, which have not been extended
   or renewed after July 15, 1988, shall remain valid and may be enforced or terminated
   in accordance with their terms or as permitted by any other statute or law of this
   state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.040. Interest on judgments
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.040. Interest on judgments
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.040. Interest on judgments (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsections (2), (3), and (4) of this section, a judgment,
      including a judgment for prejudgment interest, shall bear six percent (6%) interest
      compounded annually from the date the judgment is entered.  A judgment may be for the principal and accrued interest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.027. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of limited partnership, limited liability company, or business or statutory trust
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.027. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of limited partnership, limited liability company, or business or statutory trust
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.027. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of limited partnership, limited liability company, or business or statutory trust (2023)
content:
(1)  No limited partnership, limited liability company, or business or statutory trust
      shall hereafter plead or set up the taking of more than the legal rate of interest,
      as a defense to any action brought against it to recover damages on, or enforce payment
      of, or other remedy on, any mortgage, bond, note or other obligation, executed or
      assumed by such limited partnership, limited liability, or business or statutory trust;
      provided, that this section shall not apply to any action instituted subsequent to
      June 16, 1972, upon any mortgage, bond, note or other obligation executed or assumed
      by such limited partnership or business trust prior to June 16, 1972.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.022. Other laws not affected by KRS 360.010, 360.020, or § 360.990
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.022. Other laws not affected by KRS 360.010, 360.020, or § 360.990
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.022. Other laws not affected by KRS 360.010, 360.020, or § 360.990 (2023)
content:
Nothing contained inKRS 360.010,360.020, or360.990shall be construed to amend, repeal, or abrogate any other law of this state pertaining
   to any particular types of transactions for which exemptions, pleading of defenses
   is denied, or the maximum rate of interest is specifically prescribed or provided.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.030. Premiums on insurance to secure loan not considered as interest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.030. Premiums on insurance to secure loan not considered as interest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.030. Premiums on insurance to secure loan not considered as interest (2023)
content:
Where an insurance company, as a condition for a secured loan, requires the borrower
   to insure his life or the life of another, or his property, with the company, and
   to assign the policy of insurance to the company as security for the loan and agree
   to pay the premiums thereon during the continuance of the loan, and the premiums charged
   do not exceed those charged for similar policies to persons who do not obtain loans,
   the premiums in any such case shall not be considered as interest on the loan, and
   the loan shall not be rendered usurious by reason of any such requirement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.025. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of corporation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.025. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of corporation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.025. Excess rate of interest prohibited as defense of corporation (2023)
content:
(1)  No corporation shall hereafter plead or set up the taking of more than the legal
      rate of interest, as a defense to any action brought against it to recover damages
      on, or enforce payment of, or other remedy on, any mortgage, bond, note or other obligation,
      executed or assumed by such corporation:  provided, that this section shall not apply
      to any action which is now pending or to any suit or action instituted subsequent
      to June 16, 1960, upon any mortgage, bond, note or other obligation executed or assumed
      by such corporation prior to June 16, 1960.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.060. Interest on holdbacks or reserves by persons financing loans on personal property; reports to dealers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.060. Interest on holdbacks or reserves by persons financing loans on personal property; reports to dealers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.060. Interest on holdbacks or reserves by persons financing loans on personal property; reports to dealers (2023)
content:
(1)  Each person engaged in the business of financing loans on personal property sold
      by dealers to purchasers on credit shall pay interest at the rate of two and one-half
      percent (2.5%) per annum on holdbacks, reserves or other money withheld from the dealer
      under any contract for financing such a purchase on credit.  Interest on such money withheld shall be paid to each dealer on January 1 and July
      1 of each year.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities›KY REV ST 359.210. Prohibition on using leased spaces for residential purposes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 359. Self-Service Storage Facilities › KY REV ST 359.210. Prohibition on using leased spaces for residential purposes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 359.210. Prohibition on using leased spaces for residential purposes (2023)
content:
(1)  An operator shall not knowingly permit a leased space at a self-service storage
      facility or in a self-contained storage unit to be used for residential purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.050. Presumption as to interest on foreign debt or judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.050. Presumption as to interest on foreign debt or judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.050. Presumption as to interest on foreign debt or judgment (2023)
content:
Any indebtedness incurred or judgment rendered out of this state is presumed to bear
   interest in accordance with the provisions ofKRS 360.040.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 360. Interest and Usury›KY REV ST 360.070. Rates of exchange for commercial paper, how fixed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 360. Interest and Usury › KY REV ST 360.070. Rates of exchange for commercial paper, how fixed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 360.070. Rates of exchange for commercial paper, how fixed (2023)
content:
Once in each month or oftener, each bank and each institution authorized to deal in
   bills of exchange shall fix the rates of exchange at which bills shall be purchased
   and enter them upon the proceedings of the board of directors, designating the difference
   to be made, if any, on account of the time the bill has to run.  A copy of the rates shall be posted in some conspicuous place in the public room
   of the bank or institution.  If the rates of exchange are fixed by a branch of the bank or institution, they
   shall not be entered on its records or acted upon by it until corrected, if necessary,
   and approved by the principal bank or institution.  Any alteration made in the rates of exchange shall, before it is acted upon, be
   noted on the copy posted in the public room.  All officers of any such bank or institution shall conform to its rates of exchange
   so fixed.

Each bank and each institution authorized to deal in bills of exchange shall, each
   month, transmit copies of its rates of exchange to the Governor for his information

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.165. Rules of construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.165. Rules of construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.165. Rules of construction (2023)
content:
(1)  The rule that statutes in derogation of the common law are to be strictly construed
      shall have no application toKRS 362.150to362.360.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.150. Short title
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.150. Short title

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.160. Interpretation of knowledge and notice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.160. Interpretation of knowledge and notice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.160. Interpretation of knowledge and notice (2023)
content:
(1)  A person has “knowledge” of a fact within the meaning ofKRS 362.150to362.360not only when he has actual knowledge thereof, but also when he has knowledge of
      such other facts as in the circumstances shows bad faith.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.180. Rules for determining the existence of a partnership
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.180. Rules for determining the existence of a partnership
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.180. Rules for determining the existence of a partnership (2023)
content: In determining whether a partnership exists, these rules shall apply:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.185. Partnership property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.185. Partnership property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.185. Partnership property (2023)
content:
(1)  All property originally brought into the partnership stock or subsequently acquired
      by purchase or otherwise, on account of the partnership, is partnership property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.205. Partnership charged with knowledge of or notice to partner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.205. Partnership charged with knowledge of or notice to partner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.205. Partnership charged with knowledge of or notice to partner (2023)
content:
Notice to any partner of any matter relating to partnership affairs, and the knowledge
   of the partner acting in the particular matter, acquired while a partner or then present
   to his mind, and the knowledge of any other partner who reasonably could and should
   have communicated it to the acting partner, operate as notice to or knowledge of the
   partnership, except in the case of a fraud on the partnership committed by or with
   the consent of that partner.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.170. Rules for other cases
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.170. Rules for other cases
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.170. Rules for other cases (2023)
content: In any case not provided for inKRS 362.150to362.360the rules of law and equity, including the law merchant, shall govern.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.175. Partnership defined
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.175. Partnership defined
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.175. Partnership defined (2023)
content:
(1)  A partnership is an association of two (2) or more persons to carry on as co-owners
      a business for profit and includes, for all purposes of the laws of this Commonwealth,
      a registered limited liability partnership.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.155. Definitions for KRS 362.150. to § 362.360
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.155. Definitions for KRS 362.150. to § 362.360
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.155. Definitions for KRS 362.150. to § 362.360 (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.190. Partner agent of partnership as to partnership business
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.190. Partner agent of partnership as to partnership business
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.190. Partner agent of partnership as to partnership business (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to the limitations set forth inKRS 362.220(2), every partner shall be an agent of the partnership for the purpose of its business,
      and the act of every partner, including the execution in the partnership name of any
      instrument, for apparently carrying on in the usual way the business of the partnership
      of which he is a member shall bind the partnership, unless the partner so acting has
      in fact no authority to act for the partnership in the particular matter, and the
      person with whom he is dealing has knowledge of the fact that he has no authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.195. Conveyance of real property of the partnership
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.195. Conveyance of real property of the partnership
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.195. Conveyance of real property of the partnership (2023)
content:
(1)  Where title to real property is in the partnership name, any partner may convey
      title to such property by a conveyance executed in the partnership name;  but the
      partnership may recover such property unless the partner's act binds the partnership
      under the provisions ofKRS 362.190(1)or unless such property has been conveyed by the grantee or a person claiming through
      such grantee to a holder for value without knowledge that the partner, in making the
      conveyance, has exceeded his authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.210. Partnership bound by partner's wrongful act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.210. Partnership bound by partner's wrongful act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.210. Partnership bound by partner's wrongful act (2023)
content:
When, by any wrongful act or omission of any partner acting in the ordinary course
   of the business of the partnership or with the authority of his co-partners, loss
   or injury is caused to any person, not being a partner in the partnership, or any
   penalty is incurred, the partnership is liable therefor to the same extent as the
   partner so acting or omitting to act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.215. Partnership bound by partner's breach of trust
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.215. Partnership bound by partner's breach of trust
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.215. Partnership bound by partner's breach of trust (2023)
content: The partnership is bound to make good the loss:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.225. Partner by estoppel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.225. Partner by estoppel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.225. Partner by estoppel (2023)
content:
(1)  When a person, by words spoken or written or by conduct, represents himself,
      or consents to another representing him to anyone, as a partner in an existing partnership
      or with one or more persons not actual partners, he is liable to any such person to
      whom such representation has been made, who has, on the faith of such representation
      given credit to the actual or apparent partnership, and if he has made such representation
      or consented to its being made in a public manner he is liable to such person, whether
      the representation has or has not been made or communicated to such person so giving
      credit by or with the knowledge of the apparent partner making the representation
      or consenting to its being made:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.235. Rules determining rights and duties of partners
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.235. Rules determining rights and duties of partners
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.235. Rules determining rights and duties of partners (2023)
content:
The rights and duties of the partners in relation to the partnership shall be determined,
   subject to any agreement between them, by the following rules:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.240. Partnership books
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.240. Partnership books
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.240. Partnership books (2023)
content:
The partnership books shall be kept, subject to any agreement between the partners,
   at the principal place of business of the partnership, and every partner shall at
   all times have access to and may inspect and copy any of them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.230. Liability of incoming partner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.230. Liability of incoming partner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.230. Liability of incoming partner (2023)
content:
A person admitted as a partner into an existing partnership is liable for all the
   obligations of the partnership arising before his admission as though he had been
   a partner when such obligations were incurred, except that the liability shall be
   satisfied only out of partnership property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.220. Nature of partner's liability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.220. Nature of partner's liability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.220. Nature of partner's liability (2023)
content: (1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, all partners shall be liable:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.245. Duty of partners to render information
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.245. Duty of partners to render information
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.245. Duty of partners to render information (2023)
content:
Partners shall render on demand true and full information on all things affecting
   the partnership to any partner or to the legal representative of any deceased partner
   or partner under legal disability.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.265. Extent of property rights of a partner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.265. Extent of property rights of a partner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.265. Extent of property rights of a partner (2023)
content:
The property rights of a partner are (1) his rights in specific partnership property,
   (2) his interest in the partnership, and (3) his right to participate in the management.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.255. Right to an account
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.255. Right to an account
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.255. Right to an account (2023)
content: Any partner shall have the right to a formal account as to partnership affairs:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.250. Partner accountable as a fiduciary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.250. Partner accountable as a fiduciary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.250. Partner accountable as a fiduciary (2023)
content:
(1)  Every partner must account to the partnership for any benefit, and hold as trustee
      for it any profits derived by him without the consent of the other partners from any
      transaction connected with the formation, conduct, or liquidation of the partnership
      or from any use by him of its property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.260. Continuation of partnership beyond fixed term
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.260. Continuation of partnership beyond fixed term
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.260. Continuation of partnership beyond fixed term (2023)
content:
(1)  When a partnership for a fixed term or particular undertaking is continued after
      the termination of such term or particular undertaking without any express agreement,
      the rights and duties of the partners remain the same as they were at such termination,
      so far as is consistent with a partnership at will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.270. Nature of a partner's right in specific partnership property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.270. Nature of a partner's right in specific partnership property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.270. Nature of a partner's right in specific partnership property (2023)
content:
(1)  A partner is co-owner with his partners of specific partnership property holding
      as a tenant in partnership.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.285. Partner's interest subject to charging order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.285. Partner's interest subject to charging order
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.285. Partner's interest subject to charging order (2023)
content:
(1)  This section provides the exclusive remedy by which the judgment creditor of
      a partner or the transferee of a partner may satisfy a judgment out of the judgment
      debtor's transferable interest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.280. Assignment of partner's interest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.280. Assignment of partner's interest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.280. Assignment of partner's interest (2023)
content:
(1)  A conveyance by a partner of his interest in the partnership does not of itself
      dissolve the partnership, nor, as against the other partners in the absence of agreement,
      entitle the assignee, during the continuance of the partnership, to interfere in the
      management or administration of the partnership business or affairs, or to require
      any information or account of partnership transactions, or to inspect the partnership
      books;  but it merely entitles the assignee to receive in accordance with his contract
      the profits to which the assigning partner would otherwise be entitled.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.295. Partnership not terminated by dissolution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.295. Partnership not terminated by dissolution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.295. Partnership not terminated by dissolution (2023)
content:
On dissolution the partnership is not terminated, but continues until the winding
   up of partnership affairs is completed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.275. Nature of partner's interest in the partnership
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.275. Nature of partner's interest in the partnership
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.275. Nature of partner's interest in the partnership (2023)
content:
A partner's interest in the partnership is his share of the profits and surplus, and
   the same is personal property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.290. Dissolution defined
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.290. Dissolution defined
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.290. Dissolution defined (2023)
content:
The dissolution of a partnership is the change in the relation of the partners caused
   by any partner ceasing to be associated in the carrying on as distinguished from the
   winding up of the business.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade›Chapter 362. Partnerships›Uniform Partnership Act›KY REV ST 362.305. Dissolution by decree of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.305. Dissolution by decree of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 362.305. Dissolution by decree of court (2023)
content: (1)  On application by or for a partner the court shall decree a dissolution whenever:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.300. Causes of dissolution

content: Dissolution is caused:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXIX. Commerce and Trade › Chapter 362. Partnerships › Uniform Partnership Act › KY REV ST 362.320. Power of partner to bind partnership to third persons after dissolution

content:
(1)  After dissolution a partner can bind the partnership except as provided in subsection
