content: (1)  An agreement for debt adjusting shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.090. Annual disclosure of debt adjuster’s policies and practices to be provided to debtor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.090. Annual disclosure of debt adjuster’s policies and practices to be provided to debtor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.090. Annual disclosure of debt adjuster’s policies and practices to be provided to debtor (2023)
content:
(1)  Prior to obtaining a debtor's personal information, a debt adjuster shall provide
      a clear and conspicuous disclosure to the debtor of the debt adjuster's policies and
      practices with respect to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.060. Person engaged in debt adjusting to contract with debtor; disclosure and notice to debtor; debtor’s right to cancel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.060. Person engaged in debt adjusting to contract with debtor; disclosure and notice to debtor; debtor’s right to cancel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.060. Person engaged in debt adjusting to contract with debtor; disclosure and notice to debtor; debtor’s right to cancel (2023)
content:
(1)  A person engaged in debt adjusting shall contract in writing with the debtor
      and obtain the debtor's signature on the contract which shall designate the date on
      which the debtor actually signs the contract as the date of the transaction and fully
      disclose the exact nature of the debt-adjusting services and the total amount and
      terms of compensation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.080. Debt adjuster prohibited from sale of debtor’s personal information without written authorization; confidentiality agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.080. Debt adjuster prohibited from sale of debtor’s personal information without written authorization; confidentiality agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.080. Debt adjuster prohibited from sale of debtor’s personal information without written authorization; confidentiality agreement (2023)
content:
(1)  Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a debt adjuster shall not sell or
      transfer a debtor's personal information unless the debtor provides a valid authorization
      that includes a specification that the debtor's personal information may be sold or
      transferred by the debt adjuster who received the debtor's personal information.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.110. Cause of action for loss resulting from violation of KRS Chapter 380; time limitation on prosecution of action
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.110. Cause of action for loss resulting from violation of KRS Chapter 380; time limitation on prosecution of action
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.110. Cause of action for loss resulting from violation of KRS Chapter 380; time limitation on prosecution of action (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person who enters into a debt-adjusting transaction and thereby suffers any
      ascertainable loss of money or property, real or personal, as a result of a violation
      of this chapter, may bring an action under the Rules of Civil Procedure in the Circuit
      Court in which the person resides or where the transaction in question occurred, to
      recover actual damages.  The court may, in its discretion, award actual damages and may provide such equitable
      relief as it deems necessary or proper.  Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit a person's right to seek punitive
      damages where appropriate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.990. Penalties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.990. Penalties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.990. Penalties (2023)
content:
(1)  In any action brought alleging a violation of this chapter, if the court finds
      that a person is willfully using or has willfully used a method, act, or practice
      declared unlawful by this chapter, the Attorney General, upon petition to the court,
      may recover, on behalf of the Commonwealth, a civil penalty of not more than five
      thousand dollars ($5,000) per violation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.020. Titles allodial and subject to escheat; right of eminent domain
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.020. Titles allodial and subject to escheat; right of eminent domain
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.020. Titles allodial and subject to escheat; right of eminent domain (2023)
content:
All land titles in this state are allodial, and, subject to escheat, the entire and
   absolute property in all land in this state is vested in the owners, according to
   the nature of their respective estates;  except that the Commonwealth retains the
   right of eminent domain in and to all real estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations›Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting›KY REV ST 380.130. Prohibition of limitation on right of financial institution to collect valid debts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXI. Debtor-Creditor Relations › Chapter 380. Debt Adjusting › KY REV ST 380.130. Prohibition of limitation on right of financial institution to collect valid debts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 380.130. Prohibition of limitation on right of financial institution to collect valid debts (2023)
content:
Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to limit the ability of a financial institution
   licensed by KRS Chapter 286 from collecting on debts it is owed by a debtor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.010. Commonwealth vested with ultimate property to lands
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.010. Commonwealth vested with ultimate property to lands
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.010. Commonwealth vested with ultimate property to lands (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth of Kentucky is deemed to have possessed the original, and has the
   ultimate property in and to all lands within her boundaries.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.030. Death of disseizor; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.030. Death of disseizor; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.030. Death of disseizor; effect (2023)
content:
The death of a disseizor while seized of property shall not be such descent in law
   as to take away the right of entry of any person who has such right at the death of
   the disseizor, unless the disseizor has had fifteen (15) years' peaceable possession
   after the disseizin was committed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.060. Fee simple created, when; possession vests in grantee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.060. Fee simple created, when; possession vests in grantee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.060. Fee simple created, when; possession vests in grantee (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless a different purpose appears by express words or necessary inference, every
      estate in land created by deed or will, without words of inheritance, shall be deemed
      a fee simple or such other estate as the grantor or testator had power to dispose
      of.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.070. Estates tail converted into estates in fee; limitation on
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.070. Estates tail converted into estates in fee; limitation on
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.070. Estates tail converted into estates in fee; limitation on (2023)
content:
All estates heretofore or hereafter created, which, in former times, would have been
   deemed estates entailed, shall henceforth be held to be estates in fee simple;  and
   every limitation on such an estate shall be held valid, if it would be valid when
   limited upon an estate in fee simple.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.090. Construction of “estate for life, remainder to heirs”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.090. Construction of “estate for life, remainder to heirs”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.090. Construction of “estate for life, remainder to heirs” (2023)
content:
If any estate is given by deed or will to any person for his life, and after his death
   to his heirs, or the heirs of his body, or his issue or descendants, such estate shall
   be construed to be an estate for life only in such person, and a remainder in fee
   simple in his heirs, or the heirs of his body, or his issue or descendants.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.050. Estate created by conveyance to husband and wife; will not to defeat right to the entirety by survivorship
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.050. Estate created by conveyance to husband and wife; will not to defeat right to the entirety by survivorship
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.050. Estate created by conveyance to husband and wife; will not to defeat right to the entirety by survivorship (2023)
content:
(1)  If real estate is conveyed or devised to husband and wife, unless a right by
      survivorship is expressly provided for, there shall be no mutual right to the entirety
      by survivorship between them, but they shall take as tenants in common, and the respective
      moieties shall be subject to the respective rights of the husband or wife as fixed
      in KRS Chapter 392, with all other incidents to such tenancy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.100. Contingent remainder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.100. Contingent remainder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.100. Contingent remainder (2023)
content:
A contingent remainder shall, in no case, fail for the want of a particular estate
   to support it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.130. Exceptions to KRS § 381.120
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.130. Exceptions to KRS § 381.120
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.130. Exceptions to KRS § 381.120 (2023)
content:
(1)KRS 381.120shall not apply to any estate which joint tenants hold as executors or trustees,
      nor, except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, to an estate conveyed or
      devised to persons in their own right, when it manifestly appears, from the tenor
      of the instrument, that it was intended that the part of the one dying should belong
      to the others, neither shall it affect the mode of proceeding on any joint contract
      or judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.040. Estates may commence in future
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.040. Estates may commence in future
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.040. Estates may commence in future (2023)
content:
Any estate may be made to commence in the future by deed, in like manner as by will,
   and any estate which would be good as an executory devise or bequest shall be good
   if created by deed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.110. Alienation or union of estate does not affect remainder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.110. Alienation or union of estate does not affect remainder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.110. Alienation or union of estate does not affect remainder (2023)
content:
The alienation of a particular estate on which a remainder depends, or the union of
   such estate with the inheritance by purchase or descent, shall not operate by merger
   or otherwise to defeat, impair or affect such remainder.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.080. Construction of “without heirs,” “without children” or “issue” in deed or will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.080. Construction of “without heirs,” “without children” or “issue” in deed or will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.080. Construction of “without heirs,” “without children” or “issue” in deed or will (2023)
content:
Unless a different purpose is plainly expressed in the instrument, every limitation
   in a deed or will contingent upon a person dying “without heirs,” or “without children”
   or “issue,” or other words of like import, shall be construed a limitation to take
   effect when such person dies, unless the object on which the contingency is made to
   depend is then living, or, if a child of his body, such child is born within ten (10)
   months next thereafter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.120. Joint tenants; partition; death of one
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.120. Joint tenants; partition; death of one
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.120. Joint tenants; partition; death of one (2023)
content:
Joint tenants may be compelled to make partition, and when a joint tenant dies, the
   joint tenant's part of the joint estate, real or personal, shall descend to the joint
   tenant's heirs, or pass by devise, or go to the joint tenant's personal representative,
   subject to debts, curtesy, dower, or distribution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.136. Life tenants and their descendants; partition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.136. Life tenants and their descendants; partition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.136. Life tenants and their descendants; partition (2023)
content:
(1)  Where the land is held under a deed or will vesting a life estate in two (2)
      or more persons or in trust for their benefit, with remainder as to the share of each
      to his or her children or descendants, it shall be lawful for a court of equity, on
      the petition of one (1) of such life tenants and his or her children or descendants
      who would then be entitled to such remainder, all persons having interests in such
      lands being made parties, to partition such land so as to set apart to such life tenants
      and children or descendants so much of said land to which they shall be entitled in
      severalty;  and to that alone shall attach the title or interest of after-born children
      or descendants in whom, by the terms of said deed or will, such a remainder would
      vest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.150. Conveyance of greater estate than grantor owns; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.150. Conveyance of greater estate than grantor owns; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.150. Conveyance of greater estate than grantor owns; effect (2023)
content:
A deed and warranty of land purporting to pass or assure a greater right or estate
   than the person can lawfully pass or assure, shall operate to convey on warrant so
   much of the right and estate as such person can lawfully convey.  If such conveyance is made by a tenant for life it shall not work a forfeiture of
   his estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.135. Court-appointed commissioners to determine division of land jointly held and allotment of dower or curtesy; survey requirement
