Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.135. Court-appointed commissioners to determine division of land jointly held and allotment of dower or curtesy; survey requirement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.135. Court-appointed commissioners to determine division of land jointly held and allotment of dower or curtesy; survey requirement (2023)
content: (1)  (a) As used in this subsection:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.190. Sale of realty by trustee by virtue of pledge or deed of trust
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.190. Sale of realty by trustee by virtue of pledge or deed of trust
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.190. Sale of realty by trustee by virtue of pledge or deed of trust (2023)
content:
No sale of real estate by a trustee, by virtue of a pledge or deed of trust to secure
   the payment of debts, shall be valid or pass the title of the property specified in
   the deed or pledge, unless the sale is in pursuance to a judgment of court, or is
   made by an assignee under a voluntary deed of assignment, or unless the maker of the
   deed or pledge joins in a writing evidencing the sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.140. Posthumous child may take estate in remainder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.140. Posthumous child may take estate in remainder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.140. Posthumous child may take estate in remainder (2023)
content:
When any estate is limited by deed or will in remainder to the son or daughter, or
   the use of the son or daughter to be begotten of any person, such son or daughter,
   born after the death of his or her parent, shall take the estate in the same manner
   as if he or she had been born in the lifetime of the parent although no estate was
   created to support the remainder after the death of the parent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.170. Consideration paid by other than grantee; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.170. Consideration paid by other than grantee; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.170. Consideration paid by other than grantee; effect (2023)
content:
When a deed is made to one (1) person, and the consideration is paid by another no
   use or trust results in favor of the latter unless the grantee takes a deed in his
   own name without the consent of the person paying the consideration, or unless the
   grantee in violation of a trust purchases the lands deeded with the effects of another
   person.  Such deeds are fraudulent as against the existing debts and liabilities of the person
   paying the consideration.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.231. Definitions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.231. Definitions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.231. Definitions (2023)
content:
(1)  A “trespasser” means any person who enters or goes upon the real estate of another without any
      right, lawful authority or invitation, either expressed or implied, but does not include
      persons who come within the scope of the “attractive nuisance” doctrine.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.160. Purchaser evicted by heir of grantor may recover to extent of estate inherited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.160. Purchaser evicted by heir of grantor may recover to extent of estate inherited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.160. Purchaser evicted by heir of grantor may recover to extent of estate inherited (2023)
content:
If a deed such as that mentioned inKRS 381.150, contains a general warranty of the estate it purports to convey, and there is a
   claimant of the land who has received any estate, real or personal, by gift, advancement,
   descent, devise or distribution from the vendor, such claimant shall be barred of
   recovery to the extent of the value of the estate so devised.  If, after the claimant has recovered the land from such vendee, or if, after having
   been required to answer, he has denied the reception of any estate in either of the
   modes before named, the estate shall come to him in any such manner, the vendee, his
   heirs or personal representative, may recover from such claimant upon the warranty
   the value of such estate or so much thereof as will be sufficient to satisfy his demand.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.218. Abolition of fee simple determinable and possibility of reverter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.218. Abolition of fee simple determinable and possibility of reverter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.218. Abolition of fee simple determinable and possibility of reverter (2023)
content:
The estate known at common law as the fee simple determinable and the interest known
   as the possibility of reverter are abolished.  Words which at common law would create a fee simple determinable shall be construed
   to create a fee simple subject to a right of entry for condition broken.  In any case where a person would have a possibility of reverter at common law, he
   shall have a right of entry.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.221. Termination and preservation of forfeiture restrictions created before July 1, § 1960
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.221. Termination and preservation of forfeiture restrictions created before July 1, § 1960
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.221. Termination and preservation of forfeiture restrictions created before July 1, § 1960 (2023)
content:
(1)  Every possibility of reverter and right of entry created prior to July 1, 1960,
      shall cease to be valid or enforceable at the expiration of thirty (30) years after
      the effective date of the instrument creating it, unless before July 1, 1965, a declaration
      of intention to preserve it is filed for record with the county clerk of the county
      in which the real property is located.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.210. Reversion may be sold; rights and duties of purchaser
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.210. Reversion may be sold; rights and duties of purchaser
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.210. Reversion may be sold; rights and duties of purchaser (2023)
content:
Rights of reversion may be sold and conveyed.  The purchaser thereof shall be vested with all the privileges and advantages which
   attach to the estate in the hands of the reversioner, and shall be subject to all
   the duties and responsibilities in law or equity which any tenant might assert against
   the owner of the reversion, the right to which accrued before notice of the transfer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.222. Exceptions to KRS 381.219. and § 381.221
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.222. Exceptions to KRS 381.219. and § 381.221
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.222. Exceptions to KRS 381.219. and § 381.221 (2023)
content:
KRS 381.219and381.221shall not apply to any possibility of reverter or right of entry contained in a deed,
   gift or grant from the Commonwealth or any political subdivision thereof;  nor shall
   they apply where both the fee simple determinable and the succeeding interest, or
   both the fee simple subject to a right of entry and the right of entry, are for public,
   charitable or religious purposes;  nor shall they affect any lease present or future
   or any easement, right of way, mortgage or trust, or any communication, transmission,
   or transportation lines, or any public highway, right to take minerals, or charge
   for support during the life of a person or persons, or any restrictive covenant without
   right of entry or reverter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.200. Deeds construed to include buildings and appurtenances; solar easements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.200. Deeds construed to include buildings and appurtenances; solar easements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.200. Deeds construed to include buildings and appurtenances; solar easements (2023)
content:
(1)  Every deed, unless an exception is made therein, shall be construed to include
      all buildings, privileges and appurtenances of every kind attached to the lands therein
      conveyed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.226. Applicability of KRS 381.224. and 381.225. to property interests and powers of appointment; construction of provisions requiring vesting within period provided by common law rule against perpetuities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.226. Applicability of KRS 381.224. and 381.225. to property interests and powers of appointment; construction of provisions requiring vesting within period provided by common law rule against perpetuities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.226. Applicability of KRS 381.224. and 381.225. to property interests and powers of appointment; construction of provisions requiring vesting within period provided by common law rule against perpetuities (2023)
content: (1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section,KRS 381.224and381.225shall apply to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.219. Termination after thirty years of rights of entry created after July 1, § 1960
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.219. Termination after thirty years of rights of entry created after July 1, § 1960
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.219. Termination after thirty years of rights of entry created after July 1, § 1960 (2023)
content:
A fee simple subject to a right of entry for condition broken shall become a fee simple
   absolute if the specified contingency does not occur within thirty (30) years from
   the effective date of the instrument creating such fee simple subject to a right of
   entry.  If such contingency occurs within said thirty (30) years the right of entry, which
   may be created in a person other than the person creating the interest or his heirs,
   shall become exercisable notwithstanding the rule against perpetuities.  This section shall not apply to rights of entry created prior to July 1, 1960.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.223. Application of KRS 381.218, 381.219, 381.221, 381.222, and § 381.223
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.223. Application of KRS 381.218, 381.219, 381.221, 381.222, and § 381.223
content:
To the extent they are not superseded byKRS 381.224,381.225, and381.226, and except as provided inKRS 381.218,381.219,381.221,381.222, and381.223shall apply only to inter vivos instruments and wills taking effect after July 1,
   1960, and to appointments made after July 1, 1960, including appointments by inter
   vivos instrument or will under powers created before July 1, 1960.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.225. Permissible period of power of alienation under trust; future interest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.225. Permissible period of power of alienation under trust; future interest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.225. Permissible period of power of alienation under trust; future interest (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) A future interest or trust is void if it suspends the power of alienation
         for longer than the permissible period.  The power of alienation is the power to convey to another an absolute fee in possession
         of land, or full ownership of personalty.  The permissible period is within twenty-one (21) years after the death of an individual
         or individuals then alive.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.224. Rule against perpetuities abrogated
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.224. Rule against perpetuities abrogated
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.224. Rule against perpetuities abrogated (2023)
content:
An interest created in real or personal property shall not be void by reason of any
   rule against perpetuities, whether the common law rule or otherwise.  The common law rule against perpetuities shall not be in force in this Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.232. Liability for certain injuries
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.232. Liability for certain injuries
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.232. Liability for certain injuries (2023)
content:
The owner of real estate shall not be liable to any trespasser for injuries sustained
   by the trespasser on the real estate of the owner, except for injuries which are intentionally
   inflicted by the owner or someone acting for the owner.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.240. Title to land in adverse possession not to be certified
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.240. Title to land in adverse possession not to be certified
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.240. Title to land in adverse possession not to be certified (2023)
content:
No county clerk or other county or state officer shall officially certify to any abstract
   or statement of title to lands in this state, where such lands are in the actual possession
   of another than the person or corporation shown to be the owner of the abstract or
   certificate, when such person in possession is claiming such lands under title adverse
   to that shown in such abstract or certificate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.230. Possession unnecessary in action for trespass
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.230. Possession unnecessary in action for trespass
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.230. Possession unnecessary in action for trespass (2023)
content:
The owner of land may maintain the appropriate action to recover damages for any trespass
   or injury committed thereon, or to prevent or restrain any trespass or other injury
   thereto or thereon, notwithstanding the owner may not have the actual possession of
   the land at the time of the commission of the trespass.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.250. Certification prohibited when more than one patent
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.250. Certification prohibited when more than one patent
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.250. Certification prohibited when more than one patent (2023)
content:
If two (2) or more patents have been issued for the same land, whether by this state
   or by the State of Virginia, no county clerk or other county or state officer shall
   officially certify that the records show, or that the fact is that the title is in
   any of the patentees, or in any person claiming under any of the patents.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.270. Gift to charity not defeated for want of trustee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.270. Gift to charity not defeated for want of trustee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.270. Gift to charity not defeated for want of trustee (2023)
content:
No charity shall be defeated for want of a trustee or other person in whom the title
   may vest;  but courts of equity may uphold the charity by appointing trustees, if
   there be none, or by taking control of the fund or property, and directing its management
   and settling who is the beneficiary thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.260. Grants-in-aid of charity valid
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.260. Grants-in-aid of charity valid
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.260. Grants-in-aid of charity valid (2023)
content:
(1)  Every grant, conveyance, legacy, bequest, devise, gift, appointment, assignment
      and transfer of property, whenever made and in whatever form, shall be valid (a) if
      made to any corporation, association, trust, foundation, or similar organization or
      entity, created or formed for and devoted solely to charitable, religious, scientific,
      literary, educational, humane, benevolent or like purposes or, (b) except as otherwise
      provided by statute, if it is made for any charitable or humane purpose and if it
      points out with reasonable certainty the purposes of the charity and the beneficiaries
      thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.280. Forfeiture of right to property for killing or victimizing decedent; exemptions; escheat to elder and vulnerable victims trust fund
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.280. Forfeiture of right to property for killing or victimizing decedent; exemptions; escheat to elder and vulnerable victims trust fund
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.280. Forfeiture of right to property for killing or victimizing decedent; exemptions; escheat to elder and vulnerable victims trust fund (2023)
content:
(1)  If the husband, wife, heir-at-law, beneficiary under a will, joint tenant with
      the right of survivorship or the beneficiary under any insurance policy takes the
      life of the decedent or victimizes the decedent by the commission of any felony under
      KRS Chapter 209 and in either circumstance is convicted therefor, the person so convicted
      forfeits all interest in and to the property of the decedent, including any interest
      he or she would receive as surviving joint tenant, and the property interest or insurable
      interest so forfeited descends to the decedent's other heirs-at-law, beneficiaries,
      or joint tenants, unless otherwise disposed of by the decedent.  A judge sentencing a person for a offense that triggers a forfeiture under this
      section shall inform the defendant of the provisions of this section at sentencing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.320. Alien's right as to personalty; as to realty if resident
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.320. Alien's right as to personalty; as to realty if resident
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.320. Alien's right as to personalty; as to realty if resident (2023)
content:
Any alien, not an enemy, may take and hold any personal property except chattels real.  If such alien resides within this state he may take and hold any lands for the purposes
   of residence, or of occupation by him or his servants, or for the purpose of any business,
   trade, or manufacture, for as long as he remains a resident of the state.  An alien so taking and holding shall have like rights, remedies and exemptions concerning
   such property as if he were a citizen of the United States.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.300. Realty of nonresident alien liable to escheat after eight years unless he becomes citizen
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.300. Realty of nonresident alien liable to escheat after eight years unless he becomes citizen
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.300. Realty of nonresident alien liable to escheat after eight years unless he becomes citizen (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the real estate of a nonresident
      alien may be escheated to the state at any time after the expiration of eight (8)
      years after the time he acquires title thereto.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.330. Nonresident alien; rights as to real property inherited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.330. Nonresident alien; rights as to real property inherited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.330. Nonresident alien; rights as to real property inherited (2023)
content:
If real estate passes to a nonresident alien by descent or devise, such property may
   be held and alienated by such nonresident alien for eight (8) years after the final
   settlement of the decedent's estate from which it was acquired.  If such heir or devisee is a minor, the real estate may be held for his benefit
   by a guardian or curator, and may be sold by proper proceeding had in conformity with
   the laws regulating sales of infant's real estate, if commenced within such eight
   (8) years.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.290. Rights of alien intending to be naturalized
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.290. Rights of alien intending to be naturalized
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.290. Rights of alien intending to be naturalized (2023)
content:
After declaring his intention to become a citizen of the United States, according
   to the forms required by law, any alien, not an enemy, may recover, inherit, hold,
   and pass by descent, devise or otherwise, any interest in real or personal property,
   in the same manner as if he were a citizen of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.310. Spouses and children of citizens; property rights
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.310. Spouses and children of citizens; property rights
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.310. Spouses and children of citizens; property rights (2023)
content:
Any person whose spouse is a citizen of the United States, and any person whose father
   or mother, at the time of his birth, was a citizen thereof, although born out of the
   United States, may take and hold real or personal estate by devise, purchase, descent,
   or distribution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.340. Nonresident alien; distribution of property on death of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.340. Nonresident alien; distribution of property on death of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.340. Nonresident alien; distribution of property on death of (2023)
content:
If a nonresident alien obtains possession of real estate by descent or devise, and
   dies before the expiration of the period limiting his right of enjoyment or sale,
   the right thus acquired shall pass by descent or devise.  If such heir or devisee is a nonresident alien, the property of the deceased nonresident
   alien shall be held or disposed of within the period applicable to such alien as provided
   inKRS 381.290to381.330.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.370. Action by heir for waste done in ancestor's lifetime
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.370. Action by heir for waste done in ancestor's lifetime
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.370. Action by heir for waste done in ancestor's lifetime (2023)
content:
An heir may bring and maintain an action for waste done in the lifetime of his ancestor,
   as well as in his own lifetime.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.350. Waste by tenant for life or years; forfeiture; damages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.350. Waste by tenant for life or years; forfeiture; damages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.350. Waste by tenant for life or years; forfeiture; damages (2023)
content:
If any tenant for life or years commits waste during his estate or term, of anything
   belonging to the tenement so held, without special written permission to do so, he
   shall be subject to an action of waste, shall lose the thing wasted, and pay treble
   the amount at which the waste is assessed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.360. Remainderman or reversioner may bring action for waste
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.360. Remainderman or reversioner may bring action for waste
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.360. Remainderman or reversioner may bring action for waste (2023)
content:
The action for waste may be maintained by one who has the remainder or reversion in
   fee simple after an intervening estate for life or years, and also by one who has
   a remainder or reversion for life or years only, and each of them shall recover such
   damages as he has suffered by the waste complained of.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.390. Waste by joint tenant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.390. Waste by joint tenant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.390. Waste by joint tenant (2023)
content:
If a tenant in common, joint tenant or parcener commits waste, he shall be liable
   to his cotenants jointly or severally for damages.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.380. Waste by seller before delivery of possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.380. Waste by seller before delivery of possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.380. Waste by seller before delivery of possession (2023)
content:
If a vendor or tenant of land commits any waste thereon, after he has sold his interest
   in it, but while he remains in possession, he shall be liable to the party injured
   for damages.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.450. Tenants may remove improvements from city lots, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.450. Tenants may remove improvements from city lots, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.450. Tenants may remove improvements from city lots, when (2023)
content:
Owners of particular estates of freehold in possession or in estates for years, in
   unimproved or unproductive lots in cities in which other persons are the owners of
   the reversion or remainder, may, within ninety (90) days after the interest or estate
   in such lots ceases, remove any improvements they have erected thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.410. Action against representative of tenant; revivor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.410. Action against representative of tenant; revivor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.410. Action against representative of tenant; revivor (2023)
content:
An action for waste may be brought against the representatives of a tenant, or if
   instituted in the lifetime of a tenant may be revived against his representative after
   his death.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.400. Damages when waste wantonly committed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.400. Damages when waste wantonly committed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.400. Damages when waste wantonly committed (2023)
content:
If, in any action for waste, the jury finds that the waste was wantonly committed,
   judgment shall be entered for three (3) times the amount of the damages assessed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.470. Proceedings to ascertain value of improvements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.470. Proceedings to ascertain value of improvements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.470. Proceedings to ascertain value of improvements (2023)
content:
At the request of either party, the court in which the judgment or decree of eviction
   is rendered shall impanel a jury of twelve (12) discreet and impartial freeholders,
   not kin to either party, to meet upon the premises recovered, on a day named in the
   summons.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.420. Waste committed while action pending; receiver; injunction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.420. Waste committed while action pending; receiver; injunction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.420. Waste committed while action pending; receiver; injunction (2023)
content:
If the tenant or person in possession of any land commits or is about to commit any
   waste thereon, pending an action to recover or charge such land, the court in which
   the action is pending may order a receiver to take possession of the land, or may
   stay the committing of waste by injunction or restraining order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.460. Occupant in good faith to be paid for improvements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.460. Occupant in good faith to be paid for improvements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.460. Occupant in good faith to be paid for improvements (2023)
content:
If any person, believing himself to be the owner by reason of a claim in law or equity
   founded on a public record, peacefully occupies and improves any land, and the land,
   upon judicial investigation, is held to belong to another, the value of the improvements
   shall be paid by the successful party to the occupant, or the person under whom and
   for whom he entered and holds, before the court rendering judgment or decree of eviction
   causes the possession to be delivered to the successful party.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.440. Excavations in a city of the first class and consolidated local government; protection of adjacent property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.440. Excavations in a city of the first class and consolidated local government; protection of adjacent property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.440. Excavations in a city of the first class and consolidated local government; protection of adjacent property (2023)
content:
Whenever the owner of a lot in a city of the first class or a consolidated local government
   proposes to excavate upon the lot to a depth greater than ten (10) feet below the
   top of the curbstone of the sidewalk adjoining the lot, he shall, at his own expense,
   protect any wall on adjoining land near the excavation from injury from such excavation,
   if the necessary license is afforded him to enter upon the adjoining land for that
   purpose, but not otherwise.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.430. Possession of minerals and other interests in land; effect on possession of surface
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.430. Possession of minerals and other interests in land; effect on possession of surface
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.430. Possession of minerals and other interests in land; effect on possession of surface (2023)
content:
Wherever the mineral or other interests in or rights appurtenant to land in this state
   have passed, or shall hereafter pass, in any way, from a claimant in possession of
   the surface of the land, the continuity of the possession of such mineral, interests
   and rights shall not be deemed thereby to have been broken;  but the possession of
   the surface by the original claimant thereof, from whom such mineral, interests or
   rights passed, or by those claiming through or under him, or by virtue of a judgment
   against him in an action to which the holder of the mineral, interests or rights is
   not a party, shall be deemed to be for the benefit of the person, his heirs and assigns,
   to whom the mineral, interests or rights have passed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.480. Oath of jurors
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.480. Oath of jurors
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.480. Oath of jurors (2023)
content:
The clerk of the court shall administer to the jurors, after they have been selected,
   the following oath:  “Each of you do solemnly swear, that you will impartially, and
   to the best of your skill and judgment, discharge the duties required of you in the
   present case, by the provisions of the law concerning occupying claimants.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.490. Inquest; proceedings; duty of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.490. Inquest; proceedings; duty of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.490. Inquest; proceedings; duty of court (2023)
content:
The court shall swear the witnesses, preside over the inquest and trial, decide all
   matters of law, preserve order, and may adjourn from day to day until the jury has
   completed the inquest.  In case the jury first summoned fails to attend, or, after being sworn, fails to
   agree and render their verdict, the court shall summon another jury, on a day to be
   named in his mandate in writing.  The court shall make out and return to the clerk's office from which the writ issued,
   a complete record of the proceedings before him, together with the original writ,
   the verdict, and assessment of the jury, certified by him.  Either party shall have the right of challenge to the jurors allowed in civil cases,
   and any deficiency in the jury may be supplied by summoning others.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.510. Inquest may be quashed and new writ awarded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.510. Inquest may be quashed and new writ awarded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.510. Inquest may be quashed and new writ awarded (2023)
content:
The court to whom the inquest is returned may, upon the motion of either party, for
   good cause, quash the inquest, and award a new writ as often as it is deemed necessary
   to the ends of justice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.500. Assessment of damages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.500. Assessment of damages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.500. Assessment of damages (2023)
content:
After the jury has been sworn, it shall, from an examination of the premises, and
   upon such legal evidence as either party may produce, assess:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.520. Witnesses; how summoned
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.520. Witnesses; how summoned
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.520. Witnesses; how summoned (2023)
content:
The clerk issuing the writ, or the justice summoned to preside, shall issue summons
   for the witnesses, whose attendance shall be coerced by the justice as in other cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.680. Person condemning land may enter it, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.680. Person condemning land may enter it, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.680. Person condemning land may enter it, when (2023)
content:
By virtue of the judgment of the court, the party to whom the privilege has been granted
   shall have the right to ingress and egress upon the premises to erect and repair the
   pipes necessary to conduct the water.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.550. Lien of occupant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.550. Lien of occupant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.550. Lien of occupant (2023)
content:
The occupant shall have a lien upon the land recovered from him to satisfy the judgment,
   and may enforce it by suit in equity, order of court, or other procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.530. Copies of inquest; fees of sheriff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.530. Copies of inquest; fees of sheriff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.530. Copies of inquest; fees of sheriff (2023)
content:
The clerk shall make out two (2) copies of the inquest, and deliver one (1) to each
   party on request.  The party demanding the inquest shall pay to the sheriff, for his services, four
   dollars ($4), which shall be taxed in the bill of costs against the adverse party,
   if the court gives judgment for any amount against him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.540. Trial on return of inquest; rents
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.540. Trial on return of inquest; rents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.540. Trial on return of inquest; rents (2023)
content:
The inquest, when returned, shall be docketed as other causes.  The court shall, after deducting the lesser from the greater assessments, give judgment
   for the remainder in favor of the occupant or successful claimant.  The rent, from the day of the inquest until the time fixed for issuing the writ
   of possession, shall be computed by the court at the same rate per year as that fixed
   by the jury for the previous years.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.570. Growing crop
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.570. Growing crop
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.570. Growing crop (2023)
content:
The occupant shall be entitled to the crop growing on the land at the time of judgment
   of eviction and order for possession.  If any part of the land, at the time of eviction, has no crop growing upon it, the
   court may order the possession of such part to be delivered at any time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.560. Judgment for lien satisfied if all land taken
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.560. Judgment for lien satisfied if all land taken
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.560. Judgment for lien satisfied if all land taken (2023)
content:
Satisfaction of a judgment in favor of an occupant for improvement must be sought
   by the enforcement of the lien given inKRS 381.550, and if, in the enforcement thereof, all the land recovered by the successful claimant
   is taken, the judgment shall be deemed to be satisfied.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.640. Joint owners of private passway to share costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.640. Joint owners of private passway to share costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.640. Joint owners of private passway to share costs (2023)
content:
(1)  Where two (2) or more persons in this state have acquired real estate, not exceeding
      twenty (20) feet in width, sufficient for a passway to benefit their lands along side
      of, or near the proposed passway, the owners of such passways who are benefited thereby
      shall pay all the costs expended for the passway or the opening of and fixing the
      passway for travel.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.650. Enforcement of payment of joint expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.650. Enforcement of payment of joint expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.650. Enforcement of payment of joint expenses (2023)
content:
The collection of indebtedness for liability imposed byKRS 381.640may be enforced by a proceeding in a court of equity;  and the lands benefited by
   those who own such passways will be subjected to a lien for the due portion of such
   expense that may be necessarily incurred.  Enough of the property of any delinquent owner may be sold by a proceeding in equity
   to pay his portion of such assessment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.635. Right of condemnation of underground passageway to mine
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.635. Right of condemnation of underground passageway to mine
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.635. Right of condemnation of underground passageway to mine (2023)
content:
Whenever it is necessary for the owner of land to have access over, under or through
   the land of one or more other persons, for the purpose of operating a coal mine or
   other mine, and marketing the products therefrom, and access over the surface of the
   land of such other persons, for the purpose, would be impracticable, but there exist
   shafts, slopes, passageways or entries below the surface of the land of such other
   persons, suitable for the purpose and which could be used for the purpose without
   undue or unreasonable inconvenience to the owner thereof, or there exist coal seams
   or other strata below the surface of the land of such other persons, through which
   shafts, slopes, passageways or entries may be made without unreasonable inconvenience
   to the owner thereof, the right to use, or to make and use, such shafts, slopes, passageways
   or entries may be condemned under the procedure set forth in the Eminent Domain Act
   of Kentucky, subject to the exceptions prescribed inKRS 381.636.  The right of use so condemned shall include the right to install tracks, power lines,
   lights, ventilating equipment, and other things necessary for satisfactory use.  And provided further that in any case where the rights or uses herein provided for
   are sought to be condemned through any land already devoted to mining purposes, if
   such proposed rights or uses in any wise interfere with or disrupt any approved mining
   methods, plans or practices, as established or projected as a part of a general plan
   of mining to conform to or comply with any safety provisions, rules or regulations
   under the existing mining laws of the state of Kentucky or of the United States of
   America as now in effect or hereafter enacted, such rights or uses shall be conclusively
   presumed to be undue and unreasonable inconvenience to the owner within the meaning
   of this section andKRS 381.636.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.636. Findings required by commissioners in condemnation of underground passageway; basis of compensation; immediate possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.636. Findings required by commissioners in condemnation of underground passageway; basis of compensation; immediate possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.636. Findings required by commissioners in condemnation of underground passageway; basis of compensation; immediate possession (2023)
content:
All of the provisions of the Eminent Domain Act of Kentucky shall be applicable for
   the purposes ofKRS 381.635and this section, except as follows:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.660. Condemnation for underground water pipes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.660. Condemnation for underground water pipes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.660. Condemnation for underground water pipes (2023)
content:
When the owner or lessee of a salt, or other well or spring, or stream or body of
   water, desires to convey the water therefrom to a point more convenient by means of
   pipes underground, he may, if necessary, condemn the use of so much land of another
   as is needed for the purpose.  The procedure for condemnation shall be that set forth in the Eminent Domain Act
   of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.670. Owner's consent required for certain routes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.670. Owner's consent required for certain routes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.670. Owner's consent required for certain routes (2023)
content:
No such route shall pass through the yard or garden, or between the dwelling and spring
   or other buildings of any owner or occupant of land, without the consent, in writing,
   of the owner and occupant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.710. Evidence of dedication or use of land as burying ground
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.710. Evidence of dedication or use of land as burying ground
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.710. Evidence of dedication or use of land as burying ground (2023)
content:
The fact that any tract of land has been set apart for burial purposes and that a
   part or all of the grounds has been used for burial purposes shall be evidence that
   such grounds were set aside and used for burial purposes.  The fact that graves are not visible on any part of the grounds shall not be construed
   as evidence that such grounds were not set aside and used for burial purposes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.697. Cemeteries maintained by legal owners
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.697. Cemeteries maintained by legal owners
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.697. Cemeteries maintained by legal owners (2023)
content:
(1)  Every cemetery in Kentucky except private family cemeteries shall be maintained
      by its legal owner or owners, without respect to the individual owners of burial plots
      in the cemetery, in such a manner so as to keep the burial grounds or cemetery free
      of growth of weeds, free from accumulated debris, displaced tombstones, or other signs
      and indication of vandalism or gross neglect.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.730. Notice of suit
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.730. Notice of suit
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.730. Notice of suit (2023)
content:
Upon the filing of the complaint the city or other governmental agency created by
   the city shall give notice thereof by publication pursuant to KRS Chapter 424.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.690. Protection of burial grounds by cities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.690. Protection of burial grounds by cities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.690. Protection of burial grounds by cities (2023)
content:
Whenever any burial grounds lie within the corporate limits of a city the governing
   authorities of the city shall protect the burial grounds from being used for dumping
   grounds, building sites, playgrounds, places of entertainment and amusement, public
   parks, athletic fields or parking grounds.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.740. Assertion of claim to compensation for value of interest in cemetery or lot
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.740. Assertion of claim to compensation for value of interest in cemetery or lot
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.740. Assertion of claim to compensation for value of interest in cemetery or lot (2023)
content:
Within thirty (30) days after the last advertisement, any party having a claim to
   the cemetery or any lot therein or to the mortal remains of a person interred therein,
   may file his claim in the said proceeding for damages as compensation for the value
   of his interest in the cemetery or lot to which he has claim.  Upon the filing of the aforesaid claim the circuit court shall appoint as commissioners
   three (3) impartial housekeepers who are owners of land.  They shall be sworn to faithfully and impartially discharge their duties.  The commissioners shall view the land involved and they may hear evidence or make
   any inquiry they desire touching the value thereof and award to the claimants who
   are owners thereof the value of the property taken.  They shall return a written report to the office of the clerk of the circuit court
   describing separately the property which is the subject of each claim.  Either the claimant or the complainant may file exceptions to this report and demand
   a jury trial.  The commissioners shall be allowed a reasonable fee which shall be taxed as cost.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.750. Judgment; removal of bodies and monuments
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.750. Judgment; removal of bodies and monuments
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.750. Judgment; removal of bodies and monuments (2023)
content:
If no claim is made within thirty (30) days after the last advertisement, or if claims
   have been made and compensation duly paid either to the claimants or into court, the
   court shall declare the cemetery to be abandoned and enter judgment accordingly, vesting
   fee simple title in the complainant.  Thereafter claimants shall have thirty (30) days in which to remove the mortal remains
   and monuments from lots to which they have been adjudged to have claim, the reasonable
   cost thereof to be paid by the claimant.  If, within thirty (30) days after entry of judgment said remains have not been removed
   by the claimants thereto, it shall be the duty of such complainant, through its proper
   officers, to pay for the removal of the monument and the disinterment, removal, and
   the reinterment of such body, or bodies, in such other cemetery in the county in which
   said city is located as the protesting lot owner may designate, or if no designation
   be made, to another suitable cemetery in the county.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.720. Abandoned cemetery in cities; proceedings to vest title in city
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.720. Abandoned cemetery in cities; proceedings to vest title in city
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.720. Abandoned cemetery in cities; proceedings to vest title in city (2023)
content:
Whenever in the opinion of the legislative body of a city a cemetery located within
   the boundaries of such city has been abandoned and the land comprising the said cemetery
   is needed for a public purpose, an ordinance may be enacted declaring such cemetery,
   as described by metes and bounds, to be abandoned and authorizing the city attorney
   to institute suit for the city or other governmental agency created by the city in
   the Circuit Court of the county in which the city is located against the property
   comprising the cemetery to declare the said cemetery abandoned and to vest title thereto
   in the said city, or any governmental agency created by it pursuant to or by authority
   of the Kentucky Revised Statutes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.755. Removal of grave or cemetery on application of landowner or county; procedure; expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.755. Removal of grave or cemetery on application of landowner or county; procedure; expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.755. Removal of grave or cemetery on application of landowner or county; procedure; expenses (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon application of the owner of property upon which is located an abandoned
      grave or cemetery or whenever the fiscal court of any county deems it to be in the
      best interest of the county to remove and relocate any such grave or cemetery the
      court may issue an order or resolution authorizing such removal or relocation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.715. Burial rights in cemetery lots; abandonment; resale by cemetery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.715. Burial rights in cemetery lots; abandonment; resale by cemetery
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.715. Burial rights in cemetery lots; abandonment; resale by cemetery (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “cemetery lot” is a lot containing one (1) or more grave spaces and located within a cemetery registered
      pursuant toKRS 367.946in a county containing an urban-county government or in a city.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.765. Disinterment, removal, and reinterment of graves by Commonwealth, political subdivision or electric power company; removal by licensed funeral director
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.765. Disinterment, removal, and reinterment of graves by Commonwealth, political subdivision or electric power company; removal by licensed funeral director
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.765. Disinterment, removal, and reinterment of graves by Commonwealth, political subdivision or electric power company; removal by licensed funeral director (2023)
content:
If disinterment, removal, and reinterment of graves is effected by the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky or any of its agencies, public institutions, or political subdivisions,
   the United States of America or any agency thereof, or any electric power or lighting
   company, such disinterment, removal, and reinterment shall be performed by a funeral
   director duly licensed under the provisions of KRS Chapter 316;  provided, however,
   a person holding a valid funeral director's license of another state may perform disinterment,
   removal and reinterment if the state in which such person is licensed has a reciprocal
   agreement whereby a license granted under the provisions of KRS Chapter 316 is recognized
   and accepted in that state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.780. Removal of open toilets in urban-county government, city of the first class, or city of the home rule class; lien on property for cost of removal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.780. Removal of open toilets in urban-county government, city of the first class, or city of the home rule class; lien on property for cost of removal
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.780. Removal of open toilets in urban-county government, city of the first class, or city of the home rule class; lien on property for cost of removal (2023)
content:
(1)  The maintenance of an outdoor toilet not connected to a septic tank or sewer
      system, hereinafter called an open toilet, within the boundaries of an urban-county
      government, a city of the first class, or a city of the home rule class is hereby
      declared to be a public nuisance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.760. Cost of proceeding; burden of proof
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.760. Cost of proceeding; burden of proof
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.760. Cost of proceeding; burden of proof (2023)
content:
The cost of the proceeding shall be borne by the complainant, and the burden of proof
   shall be upon the claimant to establish his interest and to establish that it has
   not been abandoned.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation›KY REV ST 381.767. Contracts exempt from KRS § 381.765
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 381. Title to Property and Restrictions on Use, Ownership, and Alienation › KY REV ST 381.767. Contracts exempt from KRS § 381.765
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.767. Contracts exempt from KRS § 381.765 (2023)
content:
The provisions ofKRS 381.765shall not affect grave removals for which contracts have been entered into prior
   to June 17, 1978.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property›Chapter 382. Conveyances and Encumbrances›KY REV ST 382.020. Deeds of release
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXII. Ownership and Conveyance of Property › Chapter 382. Conveyances and Encumbrances › KY REV ST 382.020. Deeds of release
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 382.020. Deeds of release (2023)
content:
Every deed of release shall be executed as deeds are executed and shall be as effectual
   for the purposes therein expressed, without the execution of a lease, as if a lease
   had been executed.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 381.775. Voluntary agreement with property owner for demolition or removal of dilapidated building (2023)
