path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393. Escheats›KY REV ST 393.082. Special expendable trust fund for unclaimed sums under KRS 393.080(3); administration and distribution of fund; claims procedures
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393. Escheats › KY REV ST 393.082. Special expendable trust fund for unclaimed sums under KRS 393.080(3); administration and distribution of fund; claims procedures
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393.082. Special expendable trust fund for unclaimed sums under KRS 393.080(3); administration and distribution of fund; claims procedures (2023)
content:
(1)  Unclaimed sums delivered to the Kentucky State Treasurer pursuant toKRS 393.080(3)shall be placed in a special expendable trust fund established by the Kentucky Workers'
      Compensation Funding Commission.  The Kentucky Workers' Compensation Funding Commission shall establish a separate
      trust account with respect to each final determination or order providing for a refund
      that the Attorney General determines to have a reasonable relationship to the workers'
      compensation liability of a bankrupt employer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393. Escheats›KY REV ST 393.117. Conditions governing enforceability of agreements to locate property presumed abandoned
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393. Escheats › KY REV ST 393.117. Conditions governing enforceability of agreements to locate property presumed abandoned
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393.117. Conditions governing enforceability of agreements to locate property presumed abandoned (2023)
content:
(1)  An agreement by an owner, the primary purpose of which is to locate, deliver,
      recover, or assist in the recovery of property that is presumed abandoned, is void
      and unenforceable if it was entered into during the period commencing on the date
      that the property was presumed abandoned and extending to a time that is twenty-four
      (24) months after the date that the property is paid or delivered to the department.  This subsection shall not apply to an owner's agreement with an attorney to file
      a claim as to identified property or contest the administrator's denial of a claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393. Escheats›KY REV ST 393.170. Property in federal custody; determination of whether escheat has occurred
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393. Escheats › KY REV ST 393.170. Property in federal custody; determination of whether escheat has occurred
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393.170. Property in federal custody; determination of whether escheat has occurred (2023)
content:
Whenever any property escheated under this chapter by reason of actual abandonment,
   or death or presumption of death of the owner without leaving any person entitled
   to take the legal or equitable title under the laws of this state relating to wills,
   or descent and distribution, has been deposited with, or in the custody or under the
   control of, any federal court in and for any district in this state, or in the custody
   of any depository, clerk or other officer of such court, or has been surrendered by
   such court or its officers to the United States Treasury, the Circuit Court of any
   county in which such federal court sits shall have jurisdiction to ascertain whether
   an escheat has occurred, and to enter a judgment of escheat in favor of the state.  This section does not authorize a judgment to require such courts, officers, agents
   or depositories to pay or surrender funds to this state on a presumption of abandonment
   as provided inKRS 393A.040to393A.140.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›General Provisions›KY REV ST 393A.030. Administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › General Provisions › KY REV ST 393A.030. Administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.030. Administrative regulations (2023)
content:
The administrator may promulgate administrative regulations under KRS Chapter 13A
   to implement and administer this chapter.  In promulgating the administrative regulations, the administrator shall use the
   most cost-effective methods available for the submission of reports to the administrator
   and the notice and advertisement of property transferred to the administrator.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393. Escheats›KY REV ST 393.300. Restriction on escheat of real property held by lending corporation under supervision
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393. Escheats › KY REV ST 393.300. Restriction on escheat of real property held by lending corporation under supervision
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393.300. Restriction on escheat of real property held by lending corporation under supervision (2023)
content:
No person shall institute proceedings to escheat real property the title to which
   was acquired by any lending corporation in satisfaction of debts previously contracted
   in the course of its business, or that it purchases under a judgment for any such
   debt in its favor, if such lending corporation is under the supervision of the Department
   of Financial Institutions of this state, comptroller of currency of the United States
   or any other duly constituted supervising banking authority, state or Federal, without
   first obtaining the consent of the supervising authority having supervision over that
   corporation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Rules for Taking Custody of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.200. Traveler’s check, money order, or similar instrument
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Rules for Taking Custody of Property Presumed Abandoned › KY REV ST 393A.200. Traveler’s check, money order, or similar instrument
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.200. Traveler’s check, money order, or similar instrument (2023)
content:
The administrator may take custody of sums payable on a traveler's check, money order,
   or similar instrument presumed abandoned to the extent permissible under12 U.S.C. secs. 2501to2503, as amended.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Report by Holder›KY REV ST 393A.240. When report to be filed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Report by Holder › KY REV ST 393A.240. When report to be filed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.240. When report to be filed (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in subsection (2) of this section, and subject to
      subsection (3) of this section, the report underKRS 393A.220shall be filed before November 1 of each year and cover the twelve (12) months preceding
      July 1 of that year.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Report by Holder›KY REV ST 393A.220. Report required by holder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Report by Holder › KY REV ST 393A.220. Report required by holder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.220. Report required by holder (2023)
content:
(1)  A holder of property presumed abandoned and subject to the custody of the administrator
      shall report in a record to the administrator concerning the property.  A holder shall not be required to file a report if the holder has no property that
      is presumed abandoned.  The administrator shall not require a holder to file a paper report.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Rules for Taking Custody of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.210. Burden of proof to establish administrator’s right to custody

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Report by Holder›KY REV ST 393A.250. Retention of records by holder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Report by Holder › KY REV ST 393A.250. Retention of records by holder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.250. Retention of records by holder (2023)
content:
A holder required to file a report underKRS 393A.220shall retain records for ten (10) years after the later of the date the report was
   filed or the last date a timely report was due to be filed, unless a shorter period
   shall be provided by rule of the administrator.  The holder may satisfy the requirement to retain records under this section through
   an agent.  The records shall contain:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.280. Contents of notice by holder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned › KY REV ST 393A.280. Contents of notice by holder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.280. Contents of notice by holder (2023)
content:
(1)  Notice underKRS 393A.270shall contain a heading that reads substantially as follows:  “Notice.  The Commonwealth of Kentucky requires us to notify you that your property may be
      transferred to the custody of the Kentucky State Treasurer if you do not contact us
      before (insert date that is thirty (30) days after the date of this notice).”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.290. Notice by administrator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned › KY REV ST 393A.290. Notice by administrator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.290. Notice by administrator (2023)
content:
(1)  The administrator shall give notice to an apparent owner that property presumed
      abandoned and appears to be owned by the apparent owner shall be held by the administrator
      under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.300. Cooperation among state officers and agencies to locate apparent owner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned › KY REV ST 393A.300. Cooperation among state officers and agencies to locate apparent owner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.300. Cooperation among state officers and agencies to locate apparent owner (2023)
content:
Unless prohibited by law other than this chapter, on request of the administrator,
   each officer, agency, board, commission, division, and department of this state, any
   body politic and corporate created by this state for a public purpose, and each political
   subdivision of this state shall make its books and records available to the administrator
   and cooperate with the administrator to determine the current address of an apparent
   owner of property held by the administrator under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Report by Holder›KY REV ST 393A.260. Property reportable and payable or deliverable absent owner demand
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Report by Holder › KY REV ST 393A.260. Property reportable and payable or deliverable absent owner demand
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.260. Property reportable and payable or deliverable absent owner demand (2023)
content:
Property shall be reportable and payable or deliverable under this chapter even if
   the owner fails to make demand or present an instrument or document otherwise required
   to obtain payment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.310. Definition of good faith

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.310. Definition of good faith (2023)
content: InKRS 393A.310to393A.390, payment or delivery of property shall be made in good faith if a holder:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned›KY REV ST 393A.270. Notice to apparent owner by holder
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Notice to Apparent Owner of Property Presumed Abandoned › KY REV ST 393A.270. Notice to apparent owner by holder
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.270. Notice to apparent owner by holder (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to subsection (2) of this section, the holder of property presumed abandoned
      shall send to the apparent owner notice by first-class United States mail that complies
      withKRS 393A.280in a format acceptable to the administrator not more than one hundred eighty (180)
      days nor less than sixty (60) days before filing the report underKRS 393A.220if:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.330. Payment or delivery of property to administrator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Taking Custody of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.330. Payment or delivery of property to administrator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.330. Payment or delivery of property to administrator (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this section, on filing a report underKRS 393A.220, the holder shall pay or deliver to the administrator the property described in the
      report.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.320. Dormancy charge

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.320. Dormancy charge (2023)
content:
(1)  A holder may deduct a dormancy charge from property required to be paid or delivered
      to the administrator if:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.370. Administrator’s options as to custody

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.370. Administrator’s options as to custody (2023)
content: (1)  The administrator may decline to take custody of property reported underKRS 393A.220if the administrator determines that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.340. Effect of payment or delivery of property to administrator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Taking Custody of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.340. Effect of payment or delivery of property to administrator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.340. Effect of payment or delivery of property to administrator (2023)
content:
(1)  On payment or delivery of property to the administrator under this chapter, the
      administrator as agent for the state assumes custody and responsibility for safekeeping
      the property.  A holder that pays or delivers property to the administrator in good faith and substantially
      complies withKRS 393A.270and393A.280shall be relieved of liability arising thereafter with respect to payment or delivery
      of the property to the administrator.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.350. Recovery of property by holder from administrator

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.350. Recovery of property by holder from administrator (2023)
content:
(1)  A holder that pays money to the administrator under this chapter may file a claim
      for reimbursement from the administrator of the amount paid if the holder:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.360. Property removed from safe-deposit box
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Taking Custody of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.360. Property removed from safe-deposit box
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.360. Property removed from safe-deposit box (2023)
content:
Property removed from a safe-deposit box and delivered under this chapter to the administrator
   shall be subject to the holder's right to reimbursement for the cost of opening the
   box and a lien or contract providing reimbursement to the holder for unpaid rent charges
   for the box.  The administrator shall reimburse the holder from the proceeds remaining after deducting
   the expense incurred by the administrator in selling the property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.390. Periods of limitation and repose
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Taking Custody of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.390. Periods of limitation and repose
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.390. Periods of limitation and repose (2023)
content:
(1)  Expiration, before, on, or after July 14, 2018, of a period of limitation on
      an owner's right to receive or recover property, whether specified by contract, statute,
      or court order, shall not prevent the property from being presumed abandoned or affect
      the duty of a holder under this chapter to file a report or pay or deliver property
      to the administrator.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Deposit of Funds by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.480. Administrator holds property as custodian for owner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Deposit of Funds by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.480. Administrator holds property as custodian for owner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.480. Administrator holds property as custodian for owner (2023)
content:
Property received by the administrator under this chapter shall be held in custody
   for the benefit of the owner and shall not be owned by the state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Sale of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.400. Public sale of property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Sale of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.400. Public sale of property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.400. Public sale of property (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject toKRS 393A.410, the administrator may sell the property no earlier than three (3) years after receipt
      of property presumed abandoned.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Taking Custody of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.380. Disposition of property having no substantial value; immunity from liability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Taking Custody of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.380. Disposition of property having no substantial value; immunity from liability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.380. Disposition of property having no substantial value; immunity from liability (2023)
content:
(1)  If the administrator takes custody of property delivered under this chapter and
      later determines that the property has no substantial commercial value or that the
      cost of disposing of the property will exceed the value of the property, the administrator
      may return the property to the holder or destroy or otherwise dispose of the property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Sale of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.420. Recovery of securities or value by owner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Sale of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.420. Recovery of securities or value by owner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.420. Recovery of securities or value by owner (2023)
content:
(1)  If securities are sold by the administrator before the expiration of three (3)
      years after their delivery to the administrator, a person making a claim under this
      chapter before the end of the three (3) year period shall be entitled to the proceeds
      of the sale of the securities or the market value of the securities at the time the
      claim is made, plus dividends, interest, and other increments up to the time the claim
      is made, less any deduction for expenses of the sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Sale of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.410. Disposal of securities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Sale of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.410. Disposal of securities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.410. Disposal of securities (2023)
content:
(1)  The administrator shall not sell or otherwise liquidate a security until three
      (3) years after the administrator receives the security and gives the apparent owner
      notice underKRS 393A.290that the administrator holds the security.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.550. Verified report of property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records › KY REV ST 393A.550. Verified report of property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.550. Verified report of property (2023)
content:
If a person does not file a report required byKRS 393A.220or the administrator believes that a person may have filed an inaccurate, incomplete,
   or false report, the administrator may require the person to file a verified report
   in a form prescribed by the administrator.  The verified report shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Sale of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.440. Military medal or decoration
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Sale of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.440. Military medal or decoration
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.440. Military medal or decoration (2023)
content:
(1)  The administrator shall not sell a medal or decoration awarded for military service
      in the Armed Forces of the United States.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Claim to Recover Property from Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.490. Claim of another state to recover property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.490. Claim of another state to recover property (2023)
content:
(1)  If the administrator knows that property held by the administrator under this

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Deposit of Funds by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.450. Deposit of funds by administrator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Deposit of Funds by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.450. Deposit of funds by administrator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.450. Deposit of funds by administrator (2023)
content:
The administrator shall deposit in the State Treasury all funds received under this
   chapter, including proceeds from the sale of property underKRS 393A.400to393A.440.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.610. Report to person whose records were examined

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.610. Report to person whose records were examined (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Sale of Property by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.430. Purchaser owns property after sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Sale of Property by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.430. Purchaser owns property after sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.430. Purchaser owns property after sale (2023)
content:
A purchaser of property at a sale conducted by the administrator under this chapter
   takes the property free of all claims of the owner, a previous holder, or a person
   claiming through the owner or holder.  The administrator shall execute documents necessary to complete the transfer of
   ownership to the purchaser.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.620. Complaint to administrator about conduct of person conducting examination
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records › KY REV ST 393A.620. Complaint to administrator about conduct of person conducting examination
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.620. Complaint to administrator about conduct of person conducting examination (2023)
content:
(1)  If a person subject to examination underKRS 393A.560believes the person conducting the examination has made an unreasonable or unauthorized
      request or is not proceeding expeditiously to complete the examination, the person
      in a record may ask the administrator to intervene and take appropriate remedial action,
      including countermanding the request of the person conducting the examination, imposing
      a time limit for completion of the examination, or reassigning the examination to
      another person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Claim to Recover Property from Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.500. When property subject to recovery by another state

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.500. When property subject to recovery by another state (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Claim to Recover Property from Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.540. Filing a claim under KRS 393A.510; request for administrative hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Claim to Recover Property from Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.540. Filing a claim under KRS 393A.510; request for administrative hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.540. Filing a claim under KRS 393A.510; request for administrative hearing (2023)
content:
Not later than one (1) year after filing a claim underKRS 393A.510(1), the claimant may request in writing an administrative hearing, to be conducted in
   accordance with KRS Chapter 13B.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Claim to Recover Property from Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.520. When administrator must honor claim for property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Claim to Recover Property from Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.520. When administrator must honor claim for property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.520. When administrator must honor claim for property (2023)
content:
(1)  The administrator shall pay or deliver property to a claimant underKRS 393A.510(1)if the administrator receives evidence sufficient to establish to the satisfaction
      of the administrator that the claimant is the owner of the property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.650. Determination of liability for unreported reportable property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records › KY REV ST 393A.650. Determination of liability for unreported reportable property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.650. Determination of liability for unreported reportable property (2023)
content:
If the administrator determines from an examination conducted underKRS 393A.560that a putative holder failed or refused to pay or deliver to the administrator property
   which is reportable under this chapter, the administrator shall issue a determination
   of the putative holder's liability to pay or deliver and give notice in a record to
   the putative holder of the determination.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Claim to Recover Property from Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.530. Allowance of claim for property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Claim to Recover Property from Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.530. Allowance of claim for property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.530. Allowance of claim for property (2023)
content:
(1)  Not later than thirty (30) days after a claim is allowed underKRS 393A.520(2), the administrator shall pay or deliver to the owner the property or pay to the owner
      the net proceeds of a sale of the property.  On request of the owner, the administrator may sell or liquidate a security and
      pay the net proceeds to the owner, even if the security had been held by the administrator
      for less than three (3) years or the administrator has not complied with the notice
      requirements underKRS 393A.410.

content:

      administrator may file a claim for the property on a form prescribed by the administrator.  The claimant shall verify the claim as to its completeness and accuracy.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.570. Administrative regulations for conducting examination (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.600. Failure of person examined to retain records

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.600. Failure of person examined to retain records (2023)
content:
If a person subject to examination underKRS 393A.560does not retain the records required byKRS 393A.250, the administrator may determine the value of property due using a reasonable method
   of estimation based on all information available to the administrator, including extrapolation
   and use of statistical sampling when appropriate and necessary, consistent with examination
   procedures and standards adopted underKRS 393A.570.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records›KY REV ST 393A.640. Limit on future employment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Verified Report of Property; Examination of Records › KY REV ST 393A.640. Limit on future employment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.640. Limit on future employment (2023)
content:
The administrator or an individual employed by the administrator who participates
   in, recommends, or approves the award of a contract underKRS 393A.630on or after July 14, 2018, shall not be employed by, contract with, or compensated
   in any capacity by the contractor or an affiliate of the contractor for two (2) years
   after the latest of participation in, recommendation of, or approval of the award
   or conclusion of the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Enforcement by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.730. Interest and penalty for failure to act in timely manner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Enforcement by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.730. Interest and penalty for failure to act in timely manner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.730. Interest and penalty for failure to act in timely manner (2023)
content:
(1)  A holder that fails to report, pay, or deliver property within the time prescribed
      by this chapter shall pay to the administrator interest at the tax interest rate determined
      underKRS 131.183on the property or value of the property from the date the property should have been
      reported, paid, or delivered to the administrator until the date reported, paid, or
      delivered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Enforcement by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.700. Judicial action to enforce liability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Enforcement by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.700. Judicial action to enforce liability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.700. Judicial action to enforce liability (2023)
content:
(1)  If a determination underKRS 393A.650becomes final and not subject to administrative or judicial review, the administrator
      may commence an action in the court or in an appropriate court of another state to
      enforce the determination and secure payment or delivery of past due, unpaid, or undelivered
      property.  The action shall be brought not later than one (1) year after the determination
      becomes final.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Enforcement by Administrator›KY REV ST 393A.740. Other civil penalties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Enforcement by Administrator › KY REV ST 393A.740. Other civil penalties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.740. Other civil penalties (2023)
content:
(1)  If a holder enters into a contract or other arrangement for the purpose of evading
      an obligation under this chapter or otherwise willfully fails to perform a duty imposed
      on the holder under this chapter, the administrator may require the holder to pay
      the administrator, in addition to interest as provided inKRS 393A.730, a civil penalty of one thousand dollars ($1,000) for each day the obligation is
      evaded or the duty is not performed, up to a cumulative maximum amount of twenty-five
      thousand dollars ($25,000), plus twenty-five percent (25%) of the amount or value
      of property that should have been but was not reported, paid, or delivered as a result
      of the evasion or failure to perform.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.760. Right of agent of apparent owner to recover property held by administrator (2023)

      or assist in the location, delivery, or recovery of property of the apparent owner

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.010. “Will” defined
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.010. “Will” defined
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.010. “Will” defined (2023)
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context requires otherwise, “will” means a last will or testament, codicil, appointment by will, writing in the nature
   of a will in exercise of a power, and any other testamentary disposition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act›Miscellaneous Provisions›KY REV ST 393A.840. Uniformity of application and construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 393A. Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act › Miscellaneous Provisions › KY REV ST 393A.840. Uniformity of application and construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 393A.840. Uniformity of application and construction (2023)
content:
In applying and construing this chapter, consideration shall be given to the need
   to promote uniformity of the law with respect to its subject matter among states that
   enact the Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.035. Uniform disclaimer of transfers under nontestamentary instruments
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.035. Uniform disclaimer of transfers under nontestamentary instruments
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.035. Uniform disclaimer of transfers under nontestamentary instruments (2023)
content:
(1)  A person, or the representative of an incapacitated person or protected person,
      who is a grantee, donee, surviving joint tenant, person succeeding to a disclaimed
      interest, beneficiary under a nontestamentary instrument or contract, or appointee
      under a power of appointment exercised by a nontestamentary instrument, may disclaim
      in whole or in part the right of transfer to him of any property, or interest therein
      by delivering or filing a written disclaimer under this section.  A surviving joint tenant may disclaim as a separate interest any property or interest
      therein devolving to him by right of survivorship.  A surviving joint tenant may disclaim the entire interest in any property, or interest
      therein, that is the subject of a joint tenancy devolving to him, if the joint tenancy
      was created by act of a deceased joint tenant, if the survivor did not join in creating
      the joint tenancy and he has not accepted a benefit thereunder.  The right to disclaim shall survive the death of the person having it and may be
      exercised by the personal representative of such person's estate.  The disclaimer shall describe the property or interest therein disclaimed, declare
      the disclaimer and extent thereof, and be signed by the disclaimant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.020. Persons competent to make; what may be disposed of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.020. Persons competent to make; what may be disposed of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.020. Persons competent to make; what may be disposed of (2023)
content:
Any person of sound mind and eighteen (18) years of age or over may by will dispose
   of any estate, right, or interest in real or personal estate that he may be entitled
   to at his death, which would otherwise descend to his heirs or pass to his personal
   representatives, even though he becomes so entitled after the execution of his will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.145. Application for probate of will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.145. Application for probate of will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.145. Application for probate of will (2023)
content:
When any will is offered for probate, the court shall require a verified application
   to be filed by the person offering the same.  Such application shall state the residence of the testator at the time of his death
   and such other facts as may be necessary to establish the jurisdiction of the court,
   and the names, ages and post office addresses of the testator's surviving spouse and,
   if required by the court, heirs at law, or such as are known.  An application for probate and for appointment as executor or administrator with
   the will annexed may be combined in one (1) application.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.030. Minor can make will, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.030. Minor can make will, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.030. Minor can make will, when (2023)
content:
No person under eighteen (18) years of age can make any will, except in pursuance
   of a power specially given to that effect, and except also, that a parent, though
   under eighteen (18) years of age, may by will appoint a guardian for his child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.040. Requisites of a valid will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.040. Requisites of a valid will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.040. Requisites of a valid will (2023)
content:
No will is valid unless it is in writing with the name of the testator subscribed
   thereto by himself, or by some other person in his presence and by his direction.  If the will is not wholly written by the testator, the subscription shall be made
   or the will acknowledged by him in the presence of at least two (2) credible witnesses,
   who shall subscribe the will with their names in the presence of the testator, and
   in the presence of each other.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.065. Validity of trust, devise or legacy not affected by specified provisions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.065. Validity of trust, devise or legacy not affected by specified provisions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.065. Validity of trust, devise or legacy not affected by specified provisions (2023)
content:
(1)  No writing declaring and creating a trust, including a life insurance trust,
      when otherwise valid, shall be an invalid trust or a testamentary disposition of property
      because the grantor of the trust reserves to himself:  (a) the income of the trust
      estate for his life, or any other period, or the right to receive the income of the
      trust estate or have it used for his benefit for his life, or any other period, whether
      at the grantor's direction or in the trustee's discretion;  and/or (b) the right to
      receive amounts of the trust principal or have such amounts used for his benefit whether
      at the grantor's direction or in the discretion of the trustee;  and/or (c) the right,
      at any time during his lifetime, to modify, alter, amend or revoke the trust instrument,
      in whole or in part;  and/or (d) the right, at any time during his lifetime, to make
      recommendations to or direct the trustee as to any or all investments of the trustee
      and any or all administrative or other functions of the trustee.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.076. Uniform testamentary additions to trust act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.076. Uniform testamentary additions to trust act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.076. Uniform testamentary additions to trust act (2023)
content: (1)  A will may validly transfer property to the trustee of a trust:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.092. Effect of divorce or annulment of marriage of testator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.092. Effect of divorce or annulment of marriage of testator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.092. Effect of divorce or annulment of marriage of testator (2023)
content:
If after executing a will the testator is divorced or his marriage annulled, the divorce
   or annulment revokes any disposition or appointment of property made by the will to
   the former spouse, any provision conferring a general or special power of appointment
   on the former spouse, and any nomination of the former spouse as executor, trustee,
   conservator or guardian, unless the will expressly provides otherwise.  Property prevented from passing to a former spouse because of revocation by divorce
   or annulment passes as if the former spouse failed to survive the decedent, and other
   provisions conferring some power or office on the former spouse are interpreted as
   if the spouse failed to survive the decedent.  If provisions are revoked solely by this section, they are revived by the testator's
   remarriage to the former spouse.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.100. Revoked will may be revived, how
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.100. Revoked will may be revived, how
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.100. Revoked will may be revived, how (2023)
content:
A will or codicil, or part thereof, that has been revoked shall be revived only by
   reexecution or by a codicil executed in the manner required for making a will, and
   then only to the extent to which an intention to revive is shown thereby.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.080. Revocation of will; how effected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.080. Revocation of will; how effected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.080. Revocation of will; how effected (2023)
content: No will or codicil, or any part thereof, shall be revoked, except:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.090. Nonrevocation of will by marriage of testator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.090. Nonrevocation of will by marriage of testator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.090. Nonrevocation of will by marriage of testator (2023)
content: A will shall not be revoked by the marriage of the person who made the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.160. Court may compel production of a will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.160. Court may compel production of a will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.160. Court may compel production of a will (2023)
content:
Any District Court, on being informed that a person has in his custody the will of
   a testator, may summon him, and, by proper process, compel him to produce it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.235. Proof of will where witnesses unavailable
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.235. Proof of will where witnesses unavailable
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.235. Proof of will where witnesses unavailable (2023)
content:
When it appears to the court that a will cannot be proven as otherwise provided by
   law because one (1) or more or all of the subscribing witnesses to the will, at the
   time the will is offered for probate, are serving in or present with the Armed Forces
   of the United States or as merchant seamen, or are dead or mentally or physically
   incapable of testifying or otherwise unavailable, the court may admit the will to
   probate upon the testimony in person or by deposition of at least two (2) credible
   disinterested witnesses that the signature to the will is in the handwriting of the
   person whose will it purports to be, or upon other sufficient proof of such handwriting.   The foregoing provision shall not preclude the court, in its discretion, from requiring
   in addition, proof of such other pertinent facts and circumstances as the court may
   deem necessary to admit the will to probate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.130. Will not admissible as evidence until probated; effect of probate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.130. Will not admissible as evidence until probated; effect of probate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.130. Will not admissible as evidence until probated; effect of probate (2023)
content:
No will shall be received in evidence until it has been allowed and admitted to record
   by a District Court;  and its probate before such court shall be conclusive, except
   as to the jurisdiction of the court, until superseded, reversed or annulled.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.120. Validity of nonresident's will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.120. Validity of nonresident's will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.120. Validity of nonresident's will (2023)
content:
The will of a person domiciled out of this state at the time of his death shall be
   valid as to his personal property and his real property in this state, if it is executed
   according to the law of the place where he was domiciled.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.150. Probate of nonresident's will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.150. Probate of nonresident's will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.150. Probate of nonresident's will (2023)
content:
When a will of a nonresident has been proved out of the state, an authenticated copy
   and the certificate of probate may be offered for probate in this state.  When such copy is offered the court shall presume, in the absence of evidence to
   the contrary, that the will was duly executed and admitted to probate as a will in
   the state or country of the testator's domicile, and shall admit the copy to probate
   as a will in this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.140. Will probated in district court; venue
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.140. Will probated in district court; venue
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.140. Will probated in district court; venue (2023)
content:
Wills shall be proved before, and admitted to record by, the District Court of the
   testator's residence (if such residence was on a United States Army post, military
   reservation or fort, it may be proved and admitted to record in the District Court
   of any county adjacent thereto);  if he had no known place of residence in this state,
   and land is devised, then in the county where the land or part thereof lies;  if no
   land is devised, then in the county where he died, or where his estate or part thereof
   is, or where there is a debt or demand owing to him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.170. Propounder of will may have interested parties summoned
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.170. Propounder of will may have interested parties summoned
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.170. Propounder of will may have interested parties summoned (2023)
content:
A person offering or intending to offer to a District Court a will for probate may
   obtain from the clerk of the court process directed to the proper officer of any county,
   requiring him to summon any person interested in the probate to appear and show cause
   why the will should not be admitted to record.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.190. Summons or warning order; persons under disability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.190. Summons or warning order; persons under disability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.190. Summons or warning order; persons under disability (2023)
content:
Any person interested in such probate may be summoned, or proceeded against by warning
   order, and if an infant or mentally disabled person, a guardian ad litem shall be
   appointed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.210. Attesting witness; effect of subsequent incompetency of or devise to
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.210. Attesting witness; effect of subsequent incompetency of or devise to
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.210. Attesting witness; effect of subsequent incompetency of or devise to (2023)
content:
(1)  If any person who attests the execution of a will shall, after its execution,
      become incompetent to be admitted as a witness to prove its execution, the will shall
      not, on that account, be invalid.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.180. Court may order interested parties summoned
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.180. Court may order interested parties summoned
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.180. Court may order interested parties summoned (2023)
content:
The court to which a will is offered for probate may cause all persons interested
   in the probate to be summoned to appear on a certain day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.200. Creditors and executors are competent witnesses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.200. Creditors and executors are competent witnesses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.200. Creditors and executors are competent witnesses (2023)
content:
(1)  If a will charging any estate with debts is attested by a creditor, or the wife
      or husband of a creditor, whose debt is so charged, the creditor shall be a competent
      witness for or against the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.220. Court may probate will without summoning parties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.220. Court may probate will without summoning parties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.220. Court may probate will without summoning parties (2023)
content:
A District Court may, without summoning any party, proceed to probate and admit the
   will to record or reject it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.240. Actions in Circuit Court; time in which to be brought; filing notice of proceeding
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.240. Actions in Circuit Court; time in which to be brought; filing notice of proceeding
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.240. Actions in Circuit Court; time in which to be brought; filing notice of proceeding (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person aggrieved by the action of the District Court in admitting a will
      to record or rejecting it may bring an original action in the Circuit Court of the
      same county to contest the action of the District Court.  Such action shall be brought within two (2) years after the decision of the District
      Court.  The parties may, in the same action, or in a separate action if the validity of
      the will is not in issue, seek construction, interpretation or reformation of a will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.230. Deposition of subscribing witness; when and how may be taken
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.230. Deposition of subscribing witness; when and how may be taken
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.230. Deposition of subscribing witness; when and how may be taken (2023)
content:
When any will or any authenticated copy, as provided inKRS 394.150, is offered for probate, and an attesting witness resides out of this state, or though
   in the state is in confinement in another county under legal process, or is unable
   from sickness, age or other infirmity to attend the court before which the will or
   copy is offered, or resides at a distance of more than fifty (50) miles, the court
   may cause a commission to be issued, annexed to the will or copy and directed to any
   person authorized to take depositions, to take his deposition.  The deposition of such witness shall be taken and certified as depositions are taken
   in other cases, except that no notice need be given of the time and place of taking,
   unless the probate is opposed by some person who has made himself a party.  The proof so given shall have the same effect as if it had been given in the court
   from which the commission issued.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.225. Self-proved will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.225. Self-proved will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.225. Self-proved will (2023)
content:
(1)  Any will may be simultaneously executed, attested, and made self-proved, by acknowledgment
      thereof by the testator and affidavits of the witnesses, each made before an officer
      authorized to administer oaths under the laws of this state and evidenced by the officer's
      certificate, in substantially the following form:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.260. Proceedings in Circuit Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.260. Proceedings in Circuit Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.260. Proceedings in Circuit Court (2023)
content:
When the proceeding is taken to the Circuit Court, all necessary parties shall be
   brought before the court by the plaintiff.  The final decision given shall, subject to appeal to the Court of Appeals, be a
   bar to any other proceeding calling the probate or rejection of the will in question.   This section does not preclude a court of justice from its jurisdiction to impeach
   such final decision for any reason that would give it jurisdiction over any other
   judgment at law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.250. When action in circuit court stays proceedings under will; court may stop distribution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.250. When action in circuit court stays proceedings under will; court may stop distribution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.250. When action in circuit court stays proceedings under will; court may stop distribution (2023)
content:
An action filed in the circuit court, pursuant toKRS 394.240, shall not, unless taken within twelve (12) months from the entry of the district
   court's order, prevent the appointment of an administrator or executor by the district
   court or the settlement, distribution, and division of the decedent's estate.  The circuit court in which proceedings are pending may make an order restraining
   the further distribution and division of the estate.  Should such a restraining order be made, the court may in its discretion require
   the plaintiffs to give bond as required by the Rules of Civil Procedure concerning
   injunctive relief in civil actions generally.  Such an order shall not restrain administration of the estate other than as set
   out in the order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.295. Vacation or modification of judgment upon discovery of later will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.295. Vacation or modification of judgment upon discovery of later will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.295. Vacation or modification of judgment upon discovery of later will (2023)
content:
The court in which a judgment has been rendered shall have power to vacate or modify
   it when any paper purporting to be the last will of any person has been, or may be
   hereafter admitted to probate, and a later will has been discovered.  A judgment on this ground, however, shall not be vacated or modified, unless proceedings
   to that end shall be instituted within ten (10) years after the death of the testator.  If the earlier will shall have been established by judgment of the Circuit Court,
   the proceedings to vacate shall be instituted in the Circuit Court.  The proceedings to vacate shall be by petition to which all persons interested in
   the earlier will shall be made defendants.  Otherwise, the proceedings to vacate shall be instituted in the District Court.  Provided, however, that a judgment on the ground herein named shall not be vacated
   or modified until the validity of such later will has been determined in such proceedings.  When such former judgment has been vacated or modified such later will shall be
   admitted to probate in the manner and under the laws governing the probation of wills
   before the expiration of five (5) years.  The judgment establishing such later will and vacating the judgment establishing
   the former will shall be without prejudice to the vested rights of innocent third
   parties.  The court in which relief is sought for the reasons herein set out, may enter such
   orders as may be necessary to protect the rights of the parties during the pendency
   of the proceedings.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.300. Recording of wills
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.300. Recording of wills
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.300. Recording of wills (2023)
content:
(1)  Every will or authenticated copy admitted to record by any court shall be recorded
      by the county clerk, and remain in his office, except during such time as it may be
      carried to another court under subpoena duces tecum.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.280. Nonresidents, persons not parties and infants may have retrial; time; extent of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.280. Nonresidents, persons not parties and infants may have retrial; time; extent of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.280. Nonresidents, persons not parties and infants may have retrial; time; extent of (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person interested who, at the time of the final decision in the Circuit Court,
      resided out of this state and was proceeded against by warning order only, without
      actual appearance or being personally served with process, and any other person interested
      who was not a party to the proceeding by actual appearance or being personally served
      with process, may, within three (3) years after the final decision in the Circuit
      Court, by petition in equity, impeach the decision and have a retrial of the question
      of probate;  and either party shall be entitled to a jury for the trial thereof.  An infant, not a party, shall not be barred of such proceeding in equity until twelve
      (12) months after attaining full age.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.310. Original will may be withdrawn from court, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.310. Original will may be withdrawn from court, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.310. Original will may be withdrawn from court, when (2023)
content:
The District Court before which a will has been probated may permit any person interested
   to withdraw the will temporarily upon proper terms, if it is shown that the original
   will is necessary as evidence in any proceeding pending in a foreign government, or
   in any state of the United States.  A copy of the will shall always be retained and entered upon the records of the
   court permitting the withdrawal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.330. Will speaks as of time testator dies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.330. Will speaks as of time testator dies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.330. Will speaks as of time testator dies (2023)
content:
A will shall be construed, with reference to the real and personal estate comprised
   in it, to speak and take effect as if it had been executed immediately before the
   death of the testator, unless a contrary intention appears in the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.270. Evidence given on probate may be read at trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.270. Evidence given on probate may be read at trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.270. Evidence given on probate may be read at trial (2023)
content:
The record of what is proved or deposed in court by witnesses on the motion to admit
   a will to record, and any deposition lawfully taken out of court on such motion, of
   witnesses who cannot be produced at a trial in the Circuit Court before a jury, may,
   on such trial, be admitted as evidence, to have such weight as the jury thinks they
   deserve.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.382. Share of pretermitted child
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.382. Share of pretermitted child
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.382. Share of pretermitted child (2023)
content:
(1)  If a testator fails to provide in his will for any of his children born or adopted
      after the execution of his will, the omitted child receives a share in the estate
      equal in value to that which he would have received if the testator had died intestate
      unless:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.350. Conveyance or act subsequent to will; effect as to interest owned at death
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.350. Conveyance or act subsequent to will; effect as to interest owned at death
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.350. Conveyance or act subsequent to will; effect as to interest owned at death (2023)
content:
No conveyance or other act subsequent to the execution of a will shall, unless it
   be an act by which the will is revoked, prevent its operation with respect to such
   interest in the estate comprised in the will as the testator would have power to dispose
   of by will at the time of his death.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.340. General devise of land includes all interests therein owned by testator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.340. General devise of land includes all interests therein owned by testator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.340. General devise of land includes all interests therein owned by testator (2023)
content:
A devise of the land of the testator, or of the land of the testator in any place
   or occupied by any person mentioned in his will or otherwise described in a general
   manner, and any other general devise which would describe a leasehold estate, if the
   testator had no freehold estate which could be described by it, shall be construed
   to include his leasehold estates, or any of them to which the description extends,
   as well as freehold estates, unless a contrary intention appears in the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.360. Conversion or removal of devised property not an ademption unless intended
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.360. Conversion or removal of devised property not an ademption unless intended
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.360. Conversion or removal of devised property not an ademption unless intended (2023)
content:
(1)  The conversion of money or property or the proceeds of property, devised to one
      (1) of the testator's heirs, into other property or thing, with or without the assent
      of the testator, shall not be an ademption of the legacy or devise unless the testator
      so intended;  but the devisee shall have and receive the value of such devise, unless
      a contrary intention on the part of the testator appears from the will, or by parol
      or other evidence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.370. Advancement, when deemed satisfaction of devise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.370. Advancement, when deemed satisfaction of devise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.370. Advancement, when deemed satisfaction of devise (2023)
content:
A provision for or advancement to any person shall be deemed a satisfaction in whole
