   or in part of a devise or bequest to such person contained in a previous will, if
   it would be so deemed in case the devisee or legatee were the child of the testator;
   and whether he is a child or not, it shall be so deemed in all cases in which it appears
   from parol or other evidence to have been so intended.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.400. Issue of dead devisee or legatee take parent's share
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.400. Issue of dead devisee or legatee take parent's share
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.400. Issue of dead devisee or legatee take parent's share (2023)
content:
If a devisee or legatee dies before the testator, or is dead at the making of the
   will, leaving issue who survive the testator, such issue shall take the estate devised
   or bequeathed, as the devisee or legatee would have done if he had survived the testator,
   unless a different disposition thereof is made or required by the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.410. Death of part of group of devisees before testator; children includes grandchildren
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.410. Death of part of group of devisees before testator; children includes grandchildren
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.410. Death of part of group of devisees before testator; children includes grandchildren (2023)
content:
(1)  When a devise is made to several as a class or as tenants in common, and one
      (1) or more of the devisees die before the testator, and another or others survive
      the testator, the share or shares of such as so die shall go to his or their descendants,
      if any;  if none, to the surviving devisees, unless a different disposition is made
      by the devisor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.420. Contribution, when devised estate used for payment of testator's debt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.420. Contribution, when devised estate used for payment of testator's debt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.420. Contribution, when devised estate used for payment of testator's debt (2023)
content:
(1)  When any devised estate, real or personal, is taken from the devisee for the
      payment of a debt of the testator, or one (1) of the devisees pays such debt to save
      his devise, each of the other devisees shall contribute his proportion of the debt,
      interest, and costs to the person paying the same, according to the value received
      by him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.460. Posthumous child; how share made up
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.460. Posthumous child; how share made up
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.460. Posthumous child; how share made up (2023)
content:
When a testator shall have a posthumous child, the share of such child shall be first
   taken from the estate not disposed of by the will, if any be left after paying debts
   and other charges, and the residue shall be made up ratably by the devisees.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.430. Residuary and other legatees not entitled to contribution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.430. Residuary and other legatees not entitled to contribution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.430. Residuary and other legatees not entitled to contribution (2023)
content:
A residuary legatee, or legatee after or subject to the payment of debts, or a devisee
   to whom an estate has or shall be devised to pay debts, shall not, after paying such
   debts, be entitled to contribution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.440. Specific and general devises; distinction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.440. Specific and general devises; distinction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.440. Specific and general devises; distinction (2023)
content:
As respects the payment of the testator's debts, there shall be no distinction between
   specific and general devises except as provided in this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.490. Law as to property devised subject to lien
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.490. Law as to property devised subject to lien
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.490. Law as to property devised subject to lien (2023)
content:
KRS 394.420to394.490shall not affect any statutory provision in relation to property devised which may
   be subject to a lien.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.450. Contribution when title to estate devised to heir fails
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.450. Contribution when title to estate devised to heir fails
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.450. Contribution when title to estate devised to heir fails (2023)
content:
When any real or personal estate is devised to any heir at law of the testator, and
   the title to the estate, or any part thereof, proves invalid, such devisee shall have
   contribution from the others, unless it appears from the will that such was not the
   intention of the testator.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.480. Contribution when curtesy or dower taken from devise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.480. Contribution when curtesy or dower taken from devise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.480. Contribution when curtesy or dower taken from devise (2023)
content:
(1)  When a widower's curtesy or widow's dower is taken, or the survivor's portion
      is made up, in whole or in part, from the estate devised to a devisee, such devisee
      shall have contribution on the principles ofKRS 394.420to394.490unless the will otherwise directs, or it is necessarily to be inferred therefrom
      that the testator intended the same to fall on such devisee.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.470. Posthumous child to make contribution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.470. Posthumous child to make contribution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.470. Posthumous child to make contribution (2023)
content:
A posthumous child shall be considered a devisee under the law of contribution and
   entitled to all his rights, and liable to all his responsibilities.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.500. Void or lapsed devise included in residuary devise
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.500. Void or lapsed devise included in residuary devise
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.500. Void or lapsed devise included in residuary devise (2023)
content:
Unless a contrary intention appears from the will, real or personal estate, comprised
   in a devise or bequest incapable of taking effect, shall be included in the residuary
   devise contained in the will.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.510. Obligee has lien on devise charged with obligation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.510. Obligee has lien on devise charged with obligation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.510. Obligee has lien on devise charged with obligation (2023)
content:
When any property is devised subject to or upon the payment by the devisee to another
   of a sum of money or his doing some other thing, the latter shall have a lien on the
   legacy for the sum to be paid, or for the value of the thing to be done.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.520. Specific legacy; when payable
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.520. Specific legacy; when payable
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.520. Specific legacy; when payable (2023)
content:
If no time is fixed for the payment of a specific pecuniary legacy, it shall be payable
   one (1) year after the probate of the will, and carry interest after due.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.530. Purchaser of trust estate; when required to see to application
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.530. Purchaser of trust estate; when required to see to application
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.530. Purchaser of trust estate; when required to see to application (2023)
content:
Where lands are devised to be sold on special or general trust, or are conveyed or
   devised to trustees or executors in trust to be sold generally or for any specific
   purpose, the purchaser shall not be bound to look to the application of the purchase
   money, unless so expressly required by the conveyance or devise.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.005. Who may be appointed as fiduciary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.005. Who may be appointed as fiduciary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.005. Who may be appointed as fiduciary (2023)
content: The following persons may be appointed as fiduciary:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.550. Stock legacy to include split shares, dividends, and shares issued in merger and exchange
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.550. Stock legacy to include split shares, dividends, and shares issued in merger and exchange
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.550. Stock legacy to include split shares, dividends, and shares issued in merger and exchange (2023)
content:
A legacy of stock, regardless of whether it is construed to be general or specific,
   shall include:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.001. Definition of “fiduciary”
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.001. Definition of “fiduciary”
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.001. Definition of “fiduciary” (2023)
content: The term “fiduciary” as used in this chapter:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 394. Wills›KY REV ST 394.540. Contract to make a will, not to revoke a will or to die intestate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 394. Wills › KY REV ST 394.540. Contract to make a will, not to revoke a will or to die intestate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 394.540. Contract to make a will, not to revoke a will or to die intestate (2023)
content:
(1)  A contract to make a will or devise, or not to revoke a will or devise or to
      die intestate, if executed after June 16, 1972, can be established only by:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.015. Applications for appointment of personal representative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.015. Applications for appointment of personal representative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.015. Applications for appointment of personal representative (2023)
content:
(1)  Before being appointed as executor, administrator, curator, or administrator
      with the will annexed, every person shall make and file in duplicate a written application
      under oath, which must state the names of the deceased's surviving spouse and all
      of his heirs-at-law or such as are known, their post office address if known, the
      date of death and also a statement in general terms as to what the estate consists
      of and the probable value of the personal and real estate and also a statement of
      any indebtedness owing by the applicant to the deceased.  The foregoing requirement in respect to names and addresses of heirs-at-law may
      be omitted when the application is being made by the executor named in the will unless
      requested by the court.  The application of a nonresident shall include the designation of a resident of
      the county where administration is pending as his agent for the service of process
      in any action against him as personal representative or personally, provided that
      such personal action must have accrued in the administration of the estate.  A duplicate copy of said application shall be mailed by the clerk to the secretary
      of revenue of the State of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.070. Executor of executor cannot administer estate of first testator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.070. Executor of executor cannot administer estate of first testator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.070. Executor of executor cannot administer estate of first testator (2023)
content:
The executor of an executor shall have no authority, as such, to administer the estate
   of the first testator, but on the death of the sole or surviving executor of any last
   will, administration with the will annexed of the estate of the first testator may
   be granted, if the estate has not already been administered, to such person as would
   have been entitled to administration if the testator had died intestate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.016. Notice of hearing of application
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.016. Notice of hearing of application
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.016. Notice of hearing of application (2023)
content:
When notice of hearing of an application for the appointment of an administrator,
   administrator with will annexed or guardian is required, it shall be given by mailing
   written notice of the time, place and purpose of such hearing at least five (5) days
   before said hearing.  Proof of such notice shall be by certified mail, return receipt requested or by
   applicant's affidavit that the same was mailed to each of the parties entitled thereto
   in a sealed envelope, postage prepaid, and the date when posted, which proof shall
   be filed at the time of hearing.  If all parties entitled to notice are under no disability and waive notice in writing,
   the court may hear such application as if notice had been given.  A minor over fourteen (14) years of age may waive notice if present in person at
   the time of hearing of application for appointment of his guardian;  provided, however
   in any estate where the gross amount involved is less than five thousand dollars ($5,000)
   the court in its discretion may dispense with the requirements of this section relating
   to notice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.010. Administration must be within ten years after death
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.010. Administration must be within ten years after death
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.010. Administration must be within ten years after death (2023)
content:
Original administration shall not be granted after the expiration of ten (10) years
   from the death of the testator or intestate and if made after that time, it shall
   be void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.012. Right to file demand for notice of action regarding estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.012. Right to file demand for notice of action regarding estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.012. Right to file demand for notice of action regarding estate (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person having a financial or property interest in a decedent's estate may
      file a demand for notice with the court at any time after the death of the decedent,
      stating the name of the decedent, the nature of the demandant's interest in the estate,
      and his address or that of his attorney.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.030. Jurisdiction of administration of intestate's estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.030. Jurisdiction of administration of intestate's estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.030. Jurisdiction of administration of intestate's estate (2023)
content:
When a person dies intestate, the District Court which would have had jurisdiction
   to probate his will, had he made a will, shall have jurisdiction to grant administration
   on his estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.020. Executor not to act until will probated; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.020. Executor not to act until will probated; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.020. Executor not to act until will probated; exception (2023)
content:
The person named in a will as executor shall not act as executor to any extent until
   the will or an authenticated copy of the will is admitted to record, and he has executed
   bond and taken oath in the court in which the record is made.  He may, however, provide for the burial of the testator, pay the reasonable funeral
   expenses, and take care of and preserve the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.040. Administrator; persons entitled to be appointed; discovery of will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.040. Administrator; persons entitled to be appointed; discovery of will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.040. Administrator; persons entitled to be appointed; discovery of will (2023)
content:
(1)  The court shall grant administration to the relations of the deceased who apply
      for administration, preferring the surviving husband or wife, or if the surviving
      husband or wife does not nominate a suitable administrator, then such others as are
      next entitled to distribution, or one (1) or more of them whom the court judges will
      best manage the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.080. When minor may be executor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.080. When minor may be executor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.080. When minor may be executor (2023)
content:
If all the persons nominated as executors are under the age of eighteen (18) at the
   time of probating the will, or those who are of age fail to qualify, administration
   with the will annexed may be granted during such minority.   But if a testator, by his will, so directs, then such infant executor may qualify
   and give bond as an adult.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.100. Appointment of debtor does not extinguish debt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.100. Appointment of debtor does not extinguish debt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.100. Appointment of debtor does not extinguish debt (2023)
content:
The appointment of a debtor executor does not extinguish the debt unless the will
   so directs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.105. Fiduciary must have letters of appointment; general duties; when appointment effective
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.105. Fiduciary must have letters of appointment; general duties; when appointment effective
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.105. Fiduciary must have letters of appointment; general duties; when appointment effective (2023)
content:
Every fiduciary, before entering upon the execution of the trust, shall receive letters
   of appointment from the District Court having jurisdiction as now fixed by law.  The duties of a fiduciary shall be such as are required by law, and such additional
   duties not inconsistent therewith as the court may order.  The appointment shall be effective with the signing of an order by the judge.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.120. Oaths of representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.120. Oaths of representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.120. Oaths of representatives (2023)
content:
(1)  Each executor, administrator and curator shall take an oath to faithfully perform
      the duties of his office to the best of his judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.050. Administrator with will annexed; appointment; functions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.050. Administrator with will annexed; appointment; functions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.050. Administrator with will annexed; appointment; functions (2023)
content:
(1)  If no executor is appointed by the will, or if all the executors named in the
      will die, refuse the executorship or fail to give bond the court may grant administration
      with the will annexed to the person who would have been entitled to administration
      if there had been no will, but no person shall be eligible to appointment as administrator
      with the will annexed whose interests are antagonistic to the provisions of the will.  Failure to give bond shall amount to refusal to act as executor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.140. Bond; persons not to be surety on; recording of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.140. Bond; persons not to be surety on; recording of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.140. Bond; persons not to be surety on; recording of (2023)
content:
(1)  The District Court shall not accept as surety, in any bond of a personal representative,
      any master or other commissioner whose duty is to settle the accounts of personal
      representatives or any judge or clerk of a District Court or practicing attorney of
      that court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.110. Copy of order effectual as probate or letters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.110. Copy of order effectual as probate or letters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.110. Copy of order effectual as probate or letters (2023)
content:
A copy of the order by which a certificate is granted to any personal representative
   obtaining probate or letters of administration shall be as effectual as the probate
   or letters made out in due form.  The clerk of the court making such an order shall, when required by any personal
   representative, make out such letters and probate in due form, and certify them, under
   the seal of his court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.060. Continuation of administration when powers of representatives cease
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.060. Continuation of administration when powers of representatives cease
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.060. Continuation of administration when powers of representatives cease (2023)
content:
When the powers of one personal representative cease, the remaining personal representatives
   may carry the trust into execution.  If there is no remaining personal representative, an administrator de bonis non,
   or, if there is a will, an administrator with the will annexed, shall be appointed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.130. Bond, when required; cost of corporate surety paid from estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.130. Bond, when required; cost of corporate surety paid from estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.130. Bond, when required; cost of corporate surety paid from estate (2023)
content:
(1)  Every fiduciary, except as provided inKRS 286.3-220and386B.7-020, shall provide surety on his bond unless, on the petition of any interested party,
      the court upon being satisfied that all interests are adequately protected excuses
      the requirement of a surety, or unless, by the terms of the will or trust, surety
      is not required.  Subsequent to the qualification of a fiduciary and on motion of any interested party
      the court may reduce the amount of the bond, release the surety, or permit the substitution
      of another bond with the same or different sureties.  If an executor does not give bond when required to do so, he shall not be permitted
      to qualify, and, if he has already qualified, he shall be removed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.145. Attorney for fiduciary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.145. Attorney for fiduciary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.145. Attorney for fiduciary (2023)
content:
At the time of appointment of a fiduciary, he may designate an attorney who will represent
   him in matters relating to the trust, and when so designated notices to such fiduciary
   shall also be sent by the court to such attorney.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.170. Nonresident representatives; bond; actions by
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.170. Nonresident representatives; bond; actions by
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.170. Nonresident representatives; bond; actions by (2023)
content:
(1)  By giving bond, with surety that is resident of the county in which the action
      is brought, nonresident executors or administrators of persons who were nonresidents
      at the time of their death may prosecute actions for the recovery of debts due to
      such decedents.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.150. Compensation of representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.150. Compensation of representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.150. Compensation of representatives (2023)
content:
(1)  The compensation of an executor, administrator or curator, for services as such,
      shall not exceed five percent (5%) of the value of the personal estate of the decedent,
      plus five percent (5%) of the income collected by the executor, administrator or curator
      for the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.160. Removal of representatives
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.160. Removal of representatives
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.160. Removal of representatives (2023)
content:
(1)  If a personal representative moves out of the state and fails to designate a
      process agent as required byKRS 395.015(1), becomes insane or otherwise incapable to discharge the trust, goes bankrupt or insolvent
      or is in failing circumstances, the District Court shall remove him, and the other
      personal representative, if there is another, shall discharge the trust.  If he resides in the county of his appointment or in an adjoining county, and is
      not insane, he shall have ten (10) days' notice before the order of removal is made.  If he is insane, the notice shall be given to his committee, if he has one, and
      if there is no committee, the court may appoint one.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.195. Transactions authorized for personal representative; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.195. Transactions authorized for personal representative; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.195. Transactions authorized for personal representative; exceptions (2023)
content:
Except as restricted or otherwise provided by the will, or byKRS 395.200, a personal representative, acting reasonably for the benefit of the interested persons,
   may properly:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.155. Computation of personal representative's commission
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.155. Computation of personal representative's commission
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.155. Computation of personal representative's commission (2023)
content:
For the purpose of computing commissions whenever any portion of the dividends, interests,
   rents or other amounts payable to an executor, administrator, trustee, guardian, conservator,
   curator or other personal representative or fiduciary is required by any law of the
   United States or other governmental unit to be withheld for income tax purposes by
   the person, corporation, organization or governmental unit paying the same, the amount
   so withheld shall be deemed to have been collected.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.190. Time for distribution of estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.190. Time for distribution of estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.190. Time for distribution of estate (2023)
content:
A personal representative may distribute the estate of a decedent six (6) months after
   qualification.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.200. Sale of personal property by fiduciary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.200. Sale of personal property by fiduciary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.200. Sale of personal property by fiduciary (2023)
content:
At any time after the appointment of a fiduciary, the fiduciary, when satisfied that
   it would be for the best interests of the estate, may sell, at public or private sale,
   at the best price obtainable, and for cash or on such terms as the fiduciary may determine,
   any part or all of the personal property belonging to the estate, including dividend-paying
   and interest-bearing securities, except:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.255. Notice to compel filing of inventory or account; removal for delinquency; disallowance of compensation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.255. Notice to compel filing of inventory or account; removal for delinquency; disallowance of compensation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.255. Notice to compel filing of inventory or account; removal for delinquency; disallowance of compensation (2023)
content:
If a fiduciary neglects or refuses to file an inventory or account when due according
   to law, or when ordered by the court, the court shall notify the fiduciary of his
   delinquency and fix a date when such inventory or account must be filed.  Unless there is pending in the circuit court a suit to settle the estate such neglect
   or refusal shall be grounds for removal by the court.  If the fiduciary fails to file such account within thirty days after the date fixed
   in said notice, no allowance shall be made for his services unless the court enters
   upon its minutes an order that such delay was justified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.196. Powers in KRS 395.195. not exclusive
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.196. Powers in KRS 395.195. not exclusive
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.196. Powers in KRS 395.195. not exclusive (2023)
content:
The powers set forth inKRS 395.195are not intended to be exclusive but rather in addition to any powers which the personal
   representative has at the time of enactment of the provisions ofKRS 395.195.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.330. Acts prior to revocation of powers valid
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.330. Acts prior to revocation of powers valid
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.330. Acts prior to revocation of powers valid (2023)
content:
Where an order of administration is set aside or letters of administration revoked,
   or where any executor or administrator is removed, or the will under which he acted
   is declared invalid, all previous sales of personal estate made lawfully by the executor
   or administrator and with good faith on the part of the purchaser and all other lawful
   acts done by the executor or administrator, shall remain valid and effectual.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.197. Applicability of powers in KRS 395.195. and § 395.196
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.197. Applicability of powers in KRS 395.195. and § 395.196
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.197. Applicability of powers in KRS 395.195. and § 395.196 (2023)
content:
The powers set forth inKRS 395.195and395.196shall not be effective as to wills executed or personal representatives appointed
   and qualifying prior to June 19, 1976.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.250. Inventory; when to be returned; copies are evidence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.250. Inventory; when to be returned; copies are evidence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.250. Inventory; when to be returned; copies are evidence (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of a personal representative of a decedent to return an inventory
   in duplicate within two (2) months from the time of qualifying as such, to the clerk's
   office of the court in which he qualified, the original of which shall be recorded
   by the clerk and the duplicate shall be mailed by the clerk to the secretary of revenue.  Copies from the record of the inventory or appraisement shall be prima facie evidence
   for or against such representative.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.220. Sale of land when authorized by will
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.220. Sale of land when authorized by will
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.220. Sale of land when authorized by will (2023)
content:
(1)  The executors, or such of them as undertake the execution of the will, or, if
      all or more than one (1) undertake the execution of the will and part die or vacate
      the office, the residue or survivor, may sell and convey the land which the will directs
      or devises to the executor or to another person to be sold, or gives a discretionary
      power to sell, if no other person is appointed for that purpose, or if the person
      appointed refuses to perform the trust or dies before he has completed it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.240. Sale of choses in action; compromise of claims
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.240. Sale of choses in action; compromise of claims
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.240. Sale of choses in action; compromise of claims (2023)
content:
In actions for the settlement of decedents' estates, the court may direct the sale
   of choses in action, including judgments, and may authorize the personal representative
   to compromise claims growing out of contract or tort due the estate, as well as claims
   on contract or tort against the estate.  A personal representative may compromise and settle any claim or demand for damages
   growing out of injury to or the death of the decedent.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.370. Tombstone allowed as funeral expense
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.370. Tombstone allowed as funeral expense
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.370. Tombstone allowed as funeral expense (2023)
content:
The personal representative or heirs may cause to be erected over the grave of the
   deceased an appropriate memorial tablet, the cost of which shall be allowed as funeral
   expenses on the settlement of the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.260. Personal estate of nonresident; administration of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.260. Personal estate of nonresident; administration of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.260. Personal estate of nonresident; administration of (2023)
content:
When administration is taken in this state on the estate of a nonresident decedent,
   the residue of his personal estate, after payment of his debts to citizens of this
   state, may either be distributed and disposed of according to the law of the decedent's
   domicile, and if he has a will it shall be governed by the law of his domicile, or,
   if the court thinks best and so orders, such residue may be transmitted to the personal
   representatives, if there are any, in the state of the decedent's domicile, to be
   disposed of there according to the law of that state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.280. Successor of representative may be substituted in actions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.280. Successor of representative may be substituted in actions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.280. Successor of representative may be substituted in actions (2023)
content:
When any personal representative commences an action or is sued, and then dies, is
   removed or is superseded by another before the termination of the action, his successor
   may, by order of court, be substituted for the original plaintiff or defendant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.278. When party may revive action and limitation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.278. When party may revive action and limitation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.278. When party may revive action and limitation (2023)
content:
An application to revive an action in the name of the representative or successor
   of a plaintiff, or against the representative or successor of a defendant, shall be
   made within one (1) year after the death of a deceased party.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.380. Public administrator and guardian
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.380. Public administrator and guardian
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.380. Public administrator and guardian (2023)
content:
(1)  The District Court of each county shall appoint a discreet, fit person to act
      as administrator of decedents' estates of which there is no personal representative,
      and as guardian of orphans who have no guardian.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.290. Extent of liability of representative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.290. Extent of liability of representative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.290. Extent of liability of representative (2023)
content:
No failure to plead or make defense and no plea or answer made by a personal representative
   shall render him liable for more than the amount of assets that come to his hands
   to be administered, but the judgment of the court shall render him liable only for
   the amount of assets in his hands unadministered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.270. When action against representative may be commenced
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.270. When action against representative may be commenced
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.270. When action against representative may be commenced (2023)
content:
Two (2) months must run after the date of the qualification of the first personal
   representative of a decedent's estate before an action shall be commenced against
   any executor or administrator thereof, except against an executor de son tort.  Any action brought in violation of this section shall be dismissed with costs, except
   that an alleged creditor whose claim has been denied in writing by the fiduciary may
   commence action immediately after receipt of such denial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.310. Interest charged representative on assets
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.310. Interest charged representative on assets
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.310. Interest charged representative on assets (2023)
content:
A personal representative, after the expiration of two (2) years from the time he
   qualifies, shall be charged with interest on the surplus assets in his hands from
   that period, and before the expiration of two (2) years shall be charged with all
   interest realized on assets.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.300. Successor may sue former representative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.300. Successor may sue former representative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.300. Successor may sue former representative (2023)
content:
An administrator de bonis non or any other successor appointed in the place of a personal
   representative who has resigned or has been removed or whose letters have been revoked,
   or who has ceased to act or has died, may maintain an action against the former personal
   representative and the sureties on the administration bond and against the predecessor's
   real and personal representatives, for all damages or debts arising from the maladministration
   or omission of the predecessor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.325. Fiduciary resignation or disability; settlement of accounts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.325. Fiduciary resignation or disability; settlement of accounts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.325. Fiduciary resignation or disability; settlement of accounts (2023)
content:
(1)  If any fiduciary resigns or is removed, he shall upon the appointment of his
      successor settle his accounts.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.340. Estate for life of another considered personal estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.340. Estate for life of another considered personal estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.340. Estate for life of another considered personal estate (2023)
content:
Estates held by a deceased person for life of another shall go to the personal representative
   of the deceased as assets in his hands, and, shall be applied and distributed as the
   personal estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.350. Emblements; when personalty and when real estate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.350. Emblements; when personalty and when real estate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.350. Emblements; when personalty and when real estate (2023)
content:
(1)  All the emblements of the lands of a person dying after March 1 which are severed
      before the following December 31 shall be assets in the hands of his personal representative.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.490. Procedure when administration already granted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.490. Procedure when administration already granted
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.490. Procedure when administration already granted (2023)
content:
If administration or letters testamentary have been granted before application for
   an order dispensing with administration, the court shall not make such an order except
   upon notice to the personal representative and opportunity for him to be heard, nor
   until the costs of the administration have been paid and the accounts of the personal
   representative settled.  If the order is then entered, the administration or letters testamentary shall be
   ipso facto revoked.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.480. Consent of persons under disability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.480. Consent of persons under disability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.480. Consent of persons under disability (2023)
content:
If any person beneficially interested in an estate is not sui juris, consent for that
   person to the written agreement provided by subsection (1) ofKRS 395.470may be given by his guardian, curator or conservator.  In the case of a prisoner otherwise sui juris, consent may be given by him personally
   instead of by his curator if it is acknowledged before the superintendent or keeper
   of the prison and the superintendent or keeper certifies that, in his opinion, the
   prisoner gave his consent freely.  If any person not sui juris is beneficially interested, a trustee appointed under
   subsection (2) ofKRS 395.470to collect claims and demands shall not act until he has given bond to account for
   the share of that person and the bond has been approved by the District Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.360. Apportionment of rents
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.360. Apportionment of rents
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.360. Apportionment of rents (2023)
content:
When a person who has a freehold or an uncertain interest in land rents out the land
   and dies before the rent becomes due, the rent of the land shall be apportioned between
   the personal representatives of the deceased and the person who succeeds to the land
   as heir, personal representative, devisee or person in reversion or remainder, unless,
   in the case of a devisee, the will otherwise directs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.400. Functions of public administrator and sheriff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.400. Functions of public administrator and sheriff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.400. Functions of public administrator and sheriff (2023)
content:
The public administrator and guardian or sheriff shall, by virtue of his office and
   the order of court, be the administrator or administrator de bonis non, or if there
   is a will, administrator with the will annexed, and shall have all the rights and
   powers and be subjected to the same liabilities and be governed by the same laws prescribed
   for administrators and guardians.  If the sheriff is acting, his powers, rights, duties and liabilities shall not expire
   with his office of sheriff.  The court may, however, at any time, set aside the order entrusting the estate to
   the public administrator and guardian or sheriff and allow an executor or administrator
   to qualify.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.515. Contents of petition, adjudication of rights of interested persons; realty sold, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.515. Contents of petition, adjudication of rights of interested persons; realty sold, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.515. Contents of petition, adjudication of rights of interested persons; realty sold, when (2023)
content:
In such an action the petition must state the amount of the debts and the nature and
   value of the property, real and personal, of the decedent, so far as known to the
   plaintiff;  if it appears that there is a genuine issue concerning the right of any
   creditor, beneficiary or heir-at-law to receive payment or distribution, or if it
   appears that there is a genuine issue as to what constitutes a correct and lawful
   settlement of the estate, or a correct and lawful distribution of the assets, such
   issues may be adjudicated by the court;  and, if it shall appear that the personal
   estate is insufficient for the payment of all debts, the court may order the real
   property descended or devised to the heirs or devisees who may be parties to the action,
   or so much thereof as shall be necessary, to be sold for the payment of the residue
   of such debts.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.390. Public administrator and guardian to act, when
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.390. Public administrator and guardian to act, when
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.390. Public administrator and guardian to act, when (2023)
content:
(1)  The District Court of a county which has a public administrator and guardian
      shall, after the expiration of sixty (60) days from the death of the decedent, order
      the public administrator and guardian to administer the estate of the decedent where
      the surviving spouse and heirs waive their right to be appointed, or if the surviving
      spouse does not nominate a suitable administrator, or in the event any of the persons
      designated inKRS 395.040are unable, or found to be incapable of handling or managing the estate, or if from
      any other cause there is no personal representative.  If there is no public administrator and guardian, the court shall order the sheriff
      to administer the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.410. Curator; grounds for appointment; bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.410. Curator; grounds for appointment; bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.410. Curator; grounds for appointment; bond (2023)
content:
(1)  During the contest about the probate of a will, or when the court for any valid
      cause is delayed in granting letters testamentary or administration, it may appoint
      a curator to collect and preserve the estate of the decedent until probate of the
      will is granted, or until the cause for which the order was made is removed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.430. Application for curator for absent person; notice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.430. Application for curator for absent person; notice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.430. Application for curator for absent person; notice (2023)
content:
(1)  Before any curator is appointed for an absent person under subsection (2) ofKRS 395.410, a written application requesting the appointment shall be filed with the District
      Court Clerk.  The application shall be verified and shall recite the fact of absence, the last
      known address of the absent person and the presence of property within this state
      or other ground requiring the appointment of a curator for the protection of the property
      or rights of the absent person.  The application may be made by any relative, creditor or debtor of the absent person,
      or by any person in possession of or interested in any property or rights of the absent
      person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.440. Appeal from order appointing curator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.440. Appeal from order appointing curator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.440. Appeal from order appointing curator (2023)
content:
(1)  An appeal from an order appointing a curator to collect and preserve the estate
      of an absent person may be taken as in the case of an administrator.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.420. Functions of curator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.420. Functions of curator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.420. Functions of curator (2023)
content:
(1)  A curator appointed under subsection (1) ofKRS 395.410shall collect and safely keep the estate of the decedent, and make and return to
      court, within sixty (60) days, a full and complete inventory of the estate and deliver
      up the estate, when required, to the executor or administrator.  He may pay debts, sue and be sued and sell perishable and other goods.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.455. Transfer of assets without administration
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.455. Transfer of assets without administration
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.455. Transfer of assets without administration (2023)
content:
(1)  Where the exemption of the surviving spouse alone, or together with preferred
      claims paid by a widow or by the widower where the wife's estate is legally liable
      for payment, equals or exceeds the amount of probatable assets, the court may order
      that administration of the estate be dispensed with and such assets be transferred
      to the surviving spouse or to a person designated by such surviving spouse to receive
      all or part of such assets.  The court may so order in both testate and intestate estates and without requiring
      the renunciation of a will or the giving of bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.500. Order may be set aside
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.500. Order may be set aside
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.500. Order may be set aside (2023)
content:
An order dispensing with administration pursuant toKRS 395.470may be set aside at any time within one (1) year from the order dispensing with administration
   underKRS 395.470upon motion of any person who satisfies the court by prima facie proof that he has
   a just and unsatisfied claim or demand against the estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.450. Jurisdiction to dispense with administration
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.450. Jurisdiction to dispense with administration
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.450. Jurisdiction to dispense with administration (2023)
content:
The District Court that has jurisdiction to grant administration of the estate of
   a person dying intestate shall have jurisdiction of proceedings to dispense with administration.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.470. Dispensing with administration by agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.470. Dispensing with administration by agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.470. Dispensing with administration by agreement (2023)
content:
(1)  Administration of the estate of a person dying intestate may be dispensed with
      by agreement if there are no debts owing by the estate;  all persons beneficially
      entitled to the personal estate have agreed in writing that there shall be no administration;
      and either there are no claims or demands due the estate, or the written agreement
      to dispense with administration designates a trustee with power to collect claims
      and demands.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.520. Claims to be proved before commissioner; notice to creditors
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.520. Claims to be proved before commissioner; notice to creditors
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.520. Claims to be proved before commissioner; notice to creditors (2023)
content:
In all actions the court shall make an order for the creditors of the decedent to
   appear before a commissioner, to be appointed by the court, and prove their claims
   before a certain day to be named in the order, notice of which shall be given by publication
   pursuant to KRS Ch. 424;  and, by such other publication as the court directs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.530. Effect of creditor presenting claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.530. Effect of creditor presenting claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.530. Effect of creditor presenting claim (2023)
content:
A creditor appearing before the commissioner and presenting his claim becomes thereby
   a party to the action, and is concluded by the final judgment of the court allowing
   or rejecting his claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.510. Persons who may bring actions for settlement of estates; parties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.510. Persons who may bring actions for settlement of estates; parties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.510. Persons who may bring actions for settlement of estates; parties (2023)
content:
(1)  A representative, legatee, distributee or creditor of a deceased person may bring
      an action in circuit court for the settlement of his estate provided that no such
      suit shall be brought by any of the parties named except the personal representative
      until the expiration of six months after the qualification of such representative.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.550. Creditors actions may be enjoined while action for settlement pending
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.550. Creditors actions may be enjoined while action for settlement pending
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.550. Creditors actions may be enjoined while action for settlement pending (2023)
content:
Upon the institution of the action mentioned inKRS 395.510, an order may be made enjoining the prosecution of actions against the representatives
   of a decedent, by creditors, for their demands.  But such enjoining shall not be made, unless the action for the settlement of the
   estate be commenced within three (3) years after the qualification of the personal
   representative.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.010. Short title (2023)
content: KRS 395A.010to395A.180may be cited as the Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015).

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.140. Disclosure of digital assets to conservator of protected person
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.140. Disclosure of digital assets to conservator of protected person
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.140. Disclosure of digital assets to conservator of protected person (2023)
content:
(1)  After an opportunity for a hearing under KRS Chapter 387, the court may grant
      a conservator access to the digital assets of a protected person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.040. User direction for disclosure of digital assets
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.040. User direction for disclosure of digital assets
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.040. User direction for disclosure of digital assets (2023)
content:
(1)  A user may use an online tool to direct the custodian to disclose to a designated
      recipient or not to disclose some or all of the user's digital assets, including the
      content of electronic communications.  If the online tool allows the user to modify or delete a direction at all times,
      a direction regarding disclosure using an online tool overrides a contrary direction
      by the user in a will, trust, power of attorney, or other record.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.050. Terms-of-service agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.050. Terms-of-service agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.050. Terms-of-service agreement (2023)
content:
(1)  This chapter does not change or impair a right of a custodian or a user under
      a terms-of-service agreement to access and use digital assets of the user.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395. Personal Representatives›KY REV ST 395.535. Effect of creditor failing to present claim; liability of distributees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395. Personal Representatives › KY REV ST 395.535. Effect of creditor failing to present claim; liability of distributees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395.535. Effect of creditor failing to present claim; liability of distributees (2023)
content:
Creditors failing to appear and prove their claims, pursuant to such order, shall
   have no claim against the executor or administrator who has actually paid out the
   estate in expenses of administration, and to creditors, legatees or distributees,
   and shall have no claim against the legatees or distributees.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.080. Disclosure of other digital assets of deceased user

Unless the user prohibited disclosure of digital assets or the court directs otherwise,
   a custodian shall disclose to the personal representative of the estate of a deceased
   user a catalogue of electronic communications sent or received by the user and digital
   assets, other than the content of electronic communications, of the user, if the representative
   gives the custodian:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.100. Disclosure of other digital assets of principal
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.100. Disclosure of other digital assets of principal

   gives the custodian:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.120. Disclosure of contents of electronic communications held in trust when trustee is not original user
