path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.160. Custodian compliance and authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.160. Custodian compliance and authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.160. Custodian compliance and authority (2023)
content:
(1)  Not later than sixty (60) days after receipt of the information required underKRS 395A.070to395A.150, a custodian shall comply with a request under this chapter from a fiduciary or designated
      recipient to disclose digital assets or terminate an account.  If the custodian fails to comply, the fiduciary or designated recipient may apply
      to the court for an order directing compliance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.055. Allowance or disallowance of claims; notice; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.055. Allowance or disallowance of claims; notice; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.055. Allowance or disallowance of claims; notice; effect (2023)
content:
(1)  As to claims presented in the manner described inKRS 396.015within the time limit prescribed inKRS 396.011, the personal representative may mail a notice to any claimant stating that the claim
      has been allowed or disallowed.  If, after allowing or disallowing a claim, the personal representative changes his
      decision concerning the claim, he shall notify the claimant.  The personal representative may not change a disallowance of a claim after the time
      for the claimant to commence an action on the claim has run and the claim has been
      barred.  Every claim which is disallowed in whole or in part by the personal representative
      is barred so far as not allowed unless the claimant commences an action against the
      personal representative not later than sixty (60) days after the mailing of the notice
      of disallowance or partial allowance if the notice warns the claimant of the impending
      bar.  Failure of the personal representative to mail notice to a claimant of action on
      his claim for sixty (60) days after the time for original presentation of the claim
      has expired has the effect of a notice of allowance, except that upon petition of
      the personal representative and upon notice to the claimant, the court at any time
      before payment of such claim may for cause shown permit the personal representative
      to disallow such claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.110. Disclosure of digital assets held in trust when trustee is original user
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.110. Disclosure of digital assets held in trust when trustee is original user
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.110. Disclosure of digital assets held in trust when trustee is original user (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise ordered by the court or provided in a trust, a custodian shall disclose
   to a trustee that is an original user of an account any digital asset of the account
   held in trust, including a catalogue of electronic communications of the trustee and
   the content of electronic communications.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.150. Fiduciary duty and authority

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.170. Uniformity of application and construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.170. Uniformity of application and construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.170. Uniformity of application and construction (2023)
content:

   to promote uniformity of the law with respect to its subject matter among states that
   enact it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.011. Presentation of claims against estate; time limitations; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.011. Presentation of claims against estate; time limitations; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.011. Presentation of claims against estate; time limitations; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  All claims against a decedent's estate which arose before the death of the decedent,
      excluding claims of the United States, the State of Kentucky and any subdivision thereof,
      whether due or to become due, absolute or contingent, liquidated or unliquidated,
      founded on contract, tort, or other legal basis, if not barred earlier by other statute
      of limitations, are barred against the estate, the personal representative, and the
      heirs and devisees, unless presented within six (6) months after the appointment of
      the personal representative, or where no personal representative has been appointed,
      within two (2) years after the decedent's death.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.026. Affidavit of claimant (2023)
content:
Upon any claim being presented in the manner described in subsection (1) ofKRS 396.015, the personal representative may require by written request mailed to the claimant,
   the affidavit of the claimant or other satisfactory evidence that such claim is justly
   due, that no payments have been made thereon, and that there are no offsets against
   same to the knowledge of the claimant;  or if any payments have been made, or any
   offsets exist, that their nature and amount be shown by the evidence or stated in
   the affidavit.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.075. Payment of claims
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.075. Payment of claims
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.075. Payment of claims (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon the expiration of six (6) months from the date of his appointment, the personal
      representative may proceed to pay the claims allowed against the estate in the order
      of priority prescribed, after making appropriate provision for exemptions and allowances
      provided by law, for claims already presented which have not yet been allowed and
      for unbarred claims which may yet be presented, including costs and expenses of administration.  By petition to the court in a proceeding for the purpose, a claimant whose claim
      has been allowed but not paid as provided herein may secure an order directing the
      personal representative to pay the claim to the extent that funds of the estate are
      available for the payment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.045. Claims not barred by statute of limitations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.045. Claims not barred by statute of limitations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.045. Claims not barred by statute of limitations (2023)
content:
(1)  No claim shall be barred by a statute of limitations which would expire during
      the period commencing with the decedent's death and ending six (6) months thereafter
      if such claim is presented within six (6) months after the decedent's death.  This subsection shall not apply with respect to any statute of limitations imposed
      by KRS Chapter 396.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.035. Limitation on commencement of action on claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.035. Limitation on commencement of action on claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.035. Limitation on commencement of action on claim (2023)
content:
No action shall be brought against a personal representative on a claim against decedent's
   estate unless the claimant shall have first presented his claim in the manner described
   inKRS 396.015.  The foregoing limitation shall be in addition to that limitation on the commencement
   of an action against a personal representative set forth inKRS 395.270.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.175. Proportionate payment of claims
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.175. Proportionate payment of claims
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.175. Proportionate payment of claims (2023)
content:
(1)  All assets of estates being administered in this state are subject to all claims,
      allowances and charges existing or established against the personal representative
      wherever appointed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.065. Waiver of defense of limitations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.065. Waiver of defense of limitations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.065. Waiver of defense of limitations (2023)
content:
If an estate is solvent the personal representative, with the consent of all successors
   of the decedent whose interests would be affected, may waive any defense of limitations
   available to the estate.  If the defense is not waived, no claim which was barred by any statute of limitations
   at the time of the decedent's death shall be allowed or paid.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015)›KY REV ST 395A.180. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 395A. Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act (2015) › KY REV ST 395A.180. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 395A.180. Relation to Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (2023)
content:
This chapter modifies, limits, or supersedes the Electronic Signatures in Global and
   National Commerce Act,15 U.S.C. secs. 7001 et seq.,but does not modify, limit, or supersede Section 101(c) of that act, codified as15 U.S.C. sec. 7001(c), or authorize electronic delivery of any of the notices described in Section 103(b)
   of that act, codified as15 U.S.C. sec. 7003(b).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.085. Interest on allowed claims
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.085. Interest on allowed claims
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.085. Interest on allowed claims (2023)
content: Unless otherwise provided in any judgment against the personal representative:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.115. Payment of contingent, unliquidated or future claims
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.115. Payment of contingent, unliquidated or future claims
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.115. Payment of contingent, unliquidated or future claims (2023)
content:
(1)  If a claim which will mature at a future time, or a contingent or unliquidated
      claim, matures or becomes certain before the distribution of the estate, and if the
      claim has been allowed, it shall be paid in the same manner as matured and absolute
      claims of the same class.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.125. Deduction of counterclaim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.125. Deduction of counterclaim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.125. Deduction of counterclaim (2023)
content:
In allowing a claim the personal representative may deduct any counterclaim which
   the estate has against the claimant.  In determining a claim against an estate a court shall reduce the amount allowed
   by the amount of any counterclaims and, if the counterclaims exceed the claim, render
   a judgment against the claimant in the amount of the excess.  A counterclaim, liquidated or unliquidated, may arise from a transaction other than
   that upon which the claim is based.  A counterclaim may give rise to relief exceeding in amount or different in kind
   from that sought in the claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.105. Payment of secured claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.105. Payment of secured claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.105. Payment of secured claim (2023)
content:
Payment of a secured claim shall be upon the basis of the amount allowed if the creditor
   surrenders his security;  otherwise payment shall be upon the basis of one (1) of
   the following:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.155. Payment of encumbrances
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.155. Payment of encumbrances
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.155. Payment of encumbrances (2023)
content:
If any assets of the estate are encumbered by mortgage, pledge, lien, or secured interest,
   the personal representative may pay the encumbrance or any part thereof, renew or
   extend any obligation secured by the encumbrance or convey or transfer the assets
   to the creditor in satisfaction of his lien, in whole or in part, whether or not the
   holder of the encumbrance has presented a claim, if it appears to be for the best
   interest of the estate.  Payment of an encumbrance does not increase the share of the distributee entitled
   to the encumbered assets unless the distributee is entitled to exoneration.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.165. Recovery of overpayment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.165. Recovery of overpayment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.165. Recovery of overpayment (2023)
content:
If a personal representative pays to a creditor an undue portion of his demand or
   to a distributee or devisee a part or all of his share of the estate, under a mistake
   as to the solvency of the estate or otherwise, he may recover from the creditor, distributee
   or devisee the amount of the overpayment with interest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.145. Compromise of claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.145. Compromise of claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.145. Compromise of claim (2023)
content:
When a claim against the estate has been presented in any manner, the personal representative
   may, if it appears for the best interest of the estate, compromise the claim, whether
   matured or unmatured, absolute or contingent, liquidated or unliquidated.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.135. Execution against estate property prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.135. Execution against estate property prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.135. Execution against estate property prohibited (2023)
content:
No execution may issue upon nor may any levy be made against any property of the estate
   under any judgment against a decedent or a personal representative, but this section
   shall not be construed to prevent the enforcement of mortgages, pledges or liens upon
   real or personal property in an appropriate proceeding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.205. Limitation on actions not otherwise barred
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.205. Limitation on actions not otherwise barred
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.205. Limitation on actions not otherwise barred (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other statute to the contrary, no cause of action on any claim
   not otherwise barred by the provisions ofKRS 396.011andKRS 396.055(1), or any other applicable statute of limitations, shall be brought against the personal
   representative or against any distributee after the expiration of two (2) years from
   the date of the order of discharge of the personal representative.  The foregoing limitation shall not preclude an action by any claimant against the
   personal representative or any distributee for fraud.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.185. Liability of personal representative
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.185. Liability of personal representative
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.185. Liability of personal representative (2023)
content:
(1)  Unless otherwise provided in the contract, a personal representative is not individually
      liable on a contract properly entered into in his fiduciary capacity in the course
      of administration of the estate unless he fails to reveal his representative capacity
      and identify the estate in the contract.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1003. Presumptions of survivorship when donative provisions of a governing instrument are affected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1003. Presumptions of survivorship when donative provisions of a governing instrument are affected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1003. Presumptions of survivorship when donative provisions of a governing instrument are affected (2023)
content:
Except as provided inKRS 397.1006, for purposes of a donative provision of a governing instrument, an individual who
   is not established by clear and convincing evidence to have survived an event, including
   the death of another individual, by one hundred twenty (120) hours is deemed to have
   predeceased the event.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates›KY REV ST 396.195. Undischarged claim; proceeding against distributees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 396. Claims Against Decedents' Estates › KY REV ST 396.195. Undischarged claim; proceeding against distributees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 396.195. Undischarged claim; proceeding against distributees (2023)
content:
After assets of an estate have been distributed and subject toKRS 396.205, an undischarged claim not barred may be prosecuted in a proceeding against one (1)
   or more distributees.  No distributee shall be liable to claimants for amounts received as exempt property
   or allowances, or for amounts in excess of the value of his distribution as of the
   time of distribution.  As between distributees, each shall bear the cost of satisfaction of unbarred claims
   as if the claim had been satisfied in the course of administration.  Any distributee who shall have failed to notify other distributees of the demand
   made upon him by the claimant in sufficient time to permit them to join in any proceeding
   in which the claim was asserted against him loses his right of contribution against
   other distributees who have not been notified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1004. Co-owner with right of survivorship; requirement of survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1004. Co-owner with right of survivorship; requirement of survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours (2023)

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1001. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1001. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: As used in this chapter, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1002. Requirement of survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1002. Requirement of survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1002. Requirement of survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours (2023)
content:
Except as provided inKRS 397.1006, if the title to property, the devolution of property, the right to elect an interest
   in property, or the right to exempt property, homestead, or family allowance depends
   upon an individual's survivorship of the death of another individual, an individual
   who is not established by clear and convincing evidence to have survived the other
   individual by one hundred twenty (120) hours is deemed to have predeceased the other
   individual.  This section shall not apply if its application would result in a taking of intestate
   estate by the state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1007. Protection of payors, bona fide purchases, and other third parties; personal liability of recipient
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1007. Protection of payors, bona fide purchases, and other third parties; personal liability of recipient
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1007. Protection of payors, bona fide purchases, and other third parties; personal liability of recipient (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) A payor or other third party shall not be liable for having made a payment
         or transferred an item of property or any other benefit to a beneficiary designated
         in a governing instrument who, under this chapter, is not entitled to the payment
         or item of property, or for having taken any other action in good faith reliance on
         the beneficiary's apparent entitlement under the terms of the governing instrument,
         before the payor or other third party received written notice of a claimed lack of
         entitlement under this chapter.  A payor or other third party shall be liable for a payment made or other action
         taken after the payor or other third party received written notice of a claimed lack
         of entitlement under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1005. Evidence of death or status
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1005. Evidence of death or status
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1005. Evidence of death or status (2023)
content:
In addition to the rules of evidence in courts of general jurisdiction, for the purposes
   ofKRS 397.1001to397.1007only, the following rules relating to a determination of death and status shall apply:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1008. Uniformity of application and construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1008. Uniformity of application and construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1008. Uniformity of application and construction (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be applied and construed to effectuate its general purpose to make
   uniform the law with respect to the subject of this chapter among states enacting
   it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1006. Exceptions in which specified survival requirement does not apply

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1006. Exceptions in which specified survival requirement does not apply (2023)
content: Survival by one hundred twenty (120) hours is not required if:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 401. Change of Name›KY REV ST 401.040. Certification of order for name change; index kept by county clerk
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 401. Change of Name › KY REV ST 401.040. Certification of order for name change; index kept by county clerk
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 401.040. Certification of order for name change; index kept by county clerk (2023)
content:
(1)  If the District Court, Family Court, or Circuit Court, as authorized byKRS 401.020, orders any person's name to be changed under this chapter, a copy of the order shall
      be certified by the clerk of that court to the county clerk, for record.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates›Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act›KY REV ST 397.1009. Short title for chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIV. Descent, Wills, and Administration of Decedents' Estates › Chapter 397. Uniform Simultaneous Death Act › KY REV ST 397.1009. Short title for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 397.1009. Short title for chapter (2023)
content: This chapter may be cited as the Uniform Simultaneous Death Act (1991).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 402. Marriage›KY REV ST 402.005. Definition of marriage
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 402. Marriage › KY REV ST 402.005. Definition of marriage
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 402.005. Definition of marriage (2023)
content:
As used and recognized in the law of the Commonwealth, “marriage” refers only to the
   civil status, condition, or relation of one (1) man and one (1) woman united in law
   for life, for the discharge to each other and the community of the duties legally
   incumbent upon those whose association is founded on the distinction of sex.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 401. Change of Name›KY REV ST 401.030. Information to be entered on order book of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 401. Change of Name › KY REV ST 401.030. Information to be entered on order book of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 401.030. Information to be entered on order book of court (2023)
content:
The original name, age, and place of birth, the name to which the change is made,
   and the names of the infant's father and mother, if known, and of the person on whose
   motion the change is made shall be entered on the order book of the District Court,
   Family Court, or Circuit Court in which the action was brought and is authorized to
   do so pursuant toKRS 401.020.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 401. Change of Name›KY REV ST 401.010. Adult may have name changed by District Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 401. Change of Name › KY REV ST 401.010. Adult may have name changed by District Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 401.010. Adult may have name changed by District Court (2023)
content:
Any person at least eighteen (18) years of age may have his or her name changed by
   the District Court of the county in which he or she resides.  If he or she resides on a United States Army post, military reservation, or fort,
   his or her name may be changed by the District Court of any county adjacent thereto.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.042. Judgment of divorce from bed and board may be annulled
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.042. Judgment of divorce from bed and board may be annulled
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.042. Judgment of divorce from bed and board may be annulled (2023)
content:
A judgment of divorce from bed and board may be annulled by the court which rendered
   it, at the instance of either party showing just cause therefor in an equitable action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 401. Change of Name›KY REV ST 401.020. Parents or guardian may have child's name changed in District, Family, or Circuit Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 401. Change of Name › KY REV ST 401.020. Parents or guardian may have child's name changed in District, Family, or Circuit Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 401.020. Parents or guardian may have child's name changed in District, Family, or Circuit Court (2023)
content:
Both parents, provided both are living, or one (1) parent if one (1) is deceased,
   or if no parent is living, the guardian, may have the name of a child under the age
   of eighteen (18) changed by the District Court, or if the Family Court or Circuit
   Court has a case before it involving the family, the Family Court of a county with
   a Family Court, or the Circuit Court of a county without a Family Court of the county
   in which the child resides.  However, if one (1) parent refuses or is unavailable to execute the petition, proper
   notice of filing the petition shall be served in accordance with the Rules of Civil
   Procedure.  If the child resides on a United States Army post, military reservation, or fort,
   his or her name may be changed by the District Court, or the Family Court of a county
   with a Family Court, or the Circuit Court of a county without a Family Court of any
   county adjacent thereto.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.010. Court may grant divorce; remarriage
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.010. Court may grant divorce; remarriage
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.010. Court may grant divorce; remarriage (2023)
content:
A jury shall not be impaneled in any action for divorce, alimony or maintenance, but
   courts having general jurisdiction may grant a divorce for the cause set out in this
   chapter.  A decree of dissolution of marriage authorizes either party to marry again.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.033. Advisory committee appointment; functions; recommendations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.033. Advisory committee appointment; functions; recommendations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.033. Advisory committee appointment; functions; recommendations (2023)
content:
The judge of any Circuit Court may appoint an advisory committee to counsel with litigants
   in divorce actions.  The committee shall serve without salary or expenses.  The court may request the parties involved in these proceedings to appear before
   the said committee at a designated time and place.  The committee may make recommendation to the court as to their conclusions from
   said counseling.  These recommendations are not binding on the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.036. Mediation not to be ordered unless conditions are met
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.036. Mediation not to be ordered unless conditions are met
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.036. Mediation not to be ordered unless conditions are met (2023)
content:
In any court proceeding conducted pursuant toKRS 403.010to403.350, if there is a finding of domestic violence and abuse, as defined inKRS 403.720, the court shall not order mediation unless requested by the victim of the alleged
   domestic violence and abuse, and the court finds that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.044. Testimony in certain cases not taken for sixty days after complaint filed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.044. Testimony in certain cases not taken for sixty days after complaint filed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.044. Testimony in certain cases not taken for sixty days after complaint filed (2023)
content:
In divorce actions in which there are minor children who are the issue of the marriage
   no testimony other than on temporary motions shall be taken or heard before sixty
   (60) days have elapsed from the date of service of summons, the appointment of a warning
   order attorney or the filing of an entry of appearance or a responsive pleading by
   the defendant, whichever occurs first.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.050. Divorce from bed and board; grounds and legal effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.050. Divorce from bed and board; grounds and legal effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.050. Divorce from bed and board; grounds and legal effect (2023)
content:
Divorce from bed and board may be rendered for any cause that allows divorce, or for
   any other cause that the court in its discretion considers sufficient.  A divorce from bed and board shall operate as to property thereafter acquired, and
   upon the personal rights and legal capacities of the parties, as a divorce from the
   bond of matrimony, except that neither shall marry again during the life of the other,
   and except that it shall not bar curtesy, dower or distributive right.  The judgment may be revised or set aside at any time by the court rendering it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.040. Annulment of divorce decree; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.040. Annulment of divorce decree; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.040. Annulment of divorce decree; effect (2023)
content:
The court rendering a judgment for divorce may, at any time, annul it on the joint
   application of the parties, and restore the parties to the condition of husband and
   wife.  The annulment voids the divorce decree and any separation agreement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.090. Friend of the court; appointment; tenure; duties; wage withholding collections; compensation (Effective until July 1, 2025)
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.090. Friend of the court; appointment; tenure; duties; wage withholding collections; compensation (Effective until July 1, 2025)
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.090. Friend of the court; appointment; tenure; duties; wage withholding collections; compensation (Effective until July 1, 2025) (2023)
content:
(1)  The fiscal court of any county may, by resolution, authorize the appointment
      of a “friend of the court.”  If the Circuit Court of the county has but one (1) judge, the appointment shall be
      made by the judge.  If the court has two (2) or more judges, the appointment shall be made by joint
      action of the judges, at the general term.  The person appointed to the office of friend of the court shall serve at the pleasure
      of, and subject to removal by, the appointing authority.  The person appointed shall be a licensed practicing attorney.  The appointed person shall take the constitutional oath of office and shall give
      bond in such sum as may be fixed by the appointing judge or judges.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.100. Compensation of guardian ad litem when petitioner is victim of KRS Chapter 507, 508, 509, or 510. offense committed by respondent
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.100. Compensation of guardian ad litem when petitioner is victim of KRS Chapter 507, 508, 509, or 510. offense committed by respondent
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.100. Compensation of guardian ad litem when petitioner is victim of KRS Chapter 507, 508, 509, or 510. offense committed by respondent (2023)
content:
In any court proceeding conducted pursuant toKRS 403.010to403.350, if the respondent is incarcerated for a conviction pursuant to KRS Chapter 507,
   508, 509, or 510, where the petitioner is the victim, the guardian ad litem shall
   be paid by the Finance and Administration Cabinet.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.041. Judgment of divorce may be annulled
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.041. Judgment of divorce may be annulled
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.041. Judgment of divorce may be annulled (2023)
content:
A judgment of divorce from the bond of matrimony may be annulled by the court which
   rendered it, upon a petition verified by the parties in person so requesting.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›General Provisions›KY REV ST 403.025. Proof in action for dissolution of marriage; credible witnesses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › General Provisions › KY REV ST 403.025. Proof in action for dissolution of marriage; credible witnesses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.025. Proof in action for dissolution of marriage; credible witnesses (2023)
content:
(1)  The statements of a petition for dissolution of marriage concerning the residence
      of the parties and irretrievable breakdown of the marriage shall not be taken as true
      because of the respondent's failure to deny the statements, and the facts as to residence
      of the parties must be proved by one (1) or more credible witnesses.

(1)  When a release of medical records, including mental health records of either

      just proportions considering all relevant factors including:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.160. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.160. Temporary orders; maintenance, child support, injunction; disclosure of information on domestic violence or child abuse (2023)
content:
(1)  In a proceeding for dissolution of marriage or for legal separation, or in a
      proceeding for disposition of property or for maintenance or support following dissolution
      of the marriage by a court which lacked personal jurisdiction over the absent spouse,
      either party may move for temporary maintenance.  The motion shall be accompanied by an affidavit setting forth the factual basis
      for the motion and the amounts requested.

      filed with the court, the party making the filing shall provide the personal identifier
      in accordance with the Kentucky Rules of Civil Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.170. Marriage; irretrievable breakdown
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.170. Marriage; irretrievable breakdown
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.170. Marriage; irretrievable breakdown (2023)
content:
(1)  If both of the parties by petition or otherwise have stated under oath or affirmation
      that the marriage is irretrievably broken, or one of the parties has so stated and
      the other has not denied it, the court, after hearing, shall make a finding whether
      the marriage is irretrievably broken.  No decree shall be entered until the parties have lived apart for 60 days.  Living apart shall include living under the same roof without sexual cohabitation.  The court may order a conciliation conference as a part of the hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.210. Recognition of “Family Support Act of 1988” mandate
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.210. Recognition of “Family Support Act of 1988” mandate
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.210. Recognition of “Family Support Act of 1988” mandate (2023)
content: The General Assembly recognizes that under the federal “Family Support Act of 1988,”P.L. 100-4851, the Commonwealth of Kentucky is required to implement child support guidelines.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.213. Criteria for modification of orders for child support and for health care; effects of emancipation and death of obligated parent; commission to review guidelines
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.213. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.213. Criteria for modification of orders for child support and for health care; effects of emancipation and death of obligated parent; commission to review guidelines (2023)
content:
(1)  The Kentucky child support guidelines may be used by the parent, custodian, or
      agency substantially contributing to the support of the child as the basis for periodic
      updates of child support obligations and for modification of child support orders
      for health care.  The provisions of any decree respecting child support may be modified only as to
      installments accruing subsequent to the filing of the motion for modification and
      only upon a showing of a material change in circumstances that is substantial and
      continuing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.180. Separation agreement; court may find unconscionable
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.180. Separation agreement; court may find unconscionable
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.180. Separation agreement; court may find unconscionable (2023)
content:
(1)  To promote amicable settlement of disputes between parties to a marriage attendant
      upon their separation or the dissolution of their marriage, the parties may enter
      into a written separation agreement containing provisions for maintenance of either
      of them, disposition of any property owned by either of them, and custody, support
      and visitation of their children.

content:
(1)  An action to establish or enforce child support may be initiated by the parent,
      custodian, or agency substantially contributing to the support of the child.  The action may be brought in the county in which the child resides or where the
      defendant resides.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.200. Maintenance; court may grant order for either spouse
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.200. Maintenance; court may grant order for either spouse

content:
(1)  In a proceeding for dissolution of marriage or legal separation, or a proceeding
      for maintenance following dissolution of a marriage by a court which lacked personal
      jurisdiction over the absent spouse, the court may grant a maintenance order for either
      spouse only if it finds that the spouse seeking maintenance:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.215. Assignment of wages for child support obligations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.215. Assignment of wages for child support obligations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.215. Assignment of wages for child support obligations (2023)
content:
After July 15, 1990, any new or modified order or decree which contains provisions
   for the support of a minor child or minor children, shall provide for a wage assignment
   which shall begin immediately except for good cause shown, and which shall be paid
   based upon the payment schedule of wages of the employer to whom the wage assignment
   is directed, and at a minimum, on a monthly basis.  If good cause is shown, the wage assignment shall take effect when an arrearage
   accrues that is equal to the amount of support payable for one (1) month, pursuant
   toKRS 405.465.  Notice of all orders providing for wage assignment issued in Kentucky on or after
   January 1, 1994, shall be sent to the employer using the federally approved Income
   Withholding for Support (IWO) form that contains the accompanying OMB number.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.220. Costs of action and attorney's fees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.220. Costs of action and attorney's fees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.220. Costs of action and attorney's fees (2023)
content:
The court from time to time after considering the financial resources of both parties
   may order a party to pay a reasonable amount for the cost to the other party of maintaining
   or defending any proceeding under this chapter and for attorney's fees, including
   sums for legal services rendered and costs incurred prior to the commencement of the
   proceeding or after entry of judgment.  The court may order that the amount be paid directly to the attorney, who may enforce
   the order in his name.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.230. Legal separation; court may convert, to a decree of dissolution; restoration of former name
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.230. Legal separation; court may convert, to a decree of dissolution; restoration of former name
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.230. Legal separation; court may convert, to a decree of dissolution; restoration of former name (2023)
content:
(1)  No earlier than one year after entry of a decree of legal separation, the court
      on motion of either party shall convert the decree to a decree of dissolution of marriage.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.240. Decree or temporary order; failure to comply with; good-cause defense; attorney's fees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.240. Decree or temporary order; failure to comply with; good-cause defense; attorney's fees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.240. Decree or temporary order; failure to comply with; good-cause defense; attorney's fees (2023)
content:
(1)  If a party fails to comply with a provision of a decree or temporary order or
      injunction, the obligation of the other party to make payments for support or maintenance
      or to permit visitation is not suspended;  but he may move the court to grant an appropriate
      order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.270. Custodial issues; best interests of child shall determine; rebuttable presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in child’s best interests; de facto custodian
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.270. Custodial issues; best interests of child shall determine; rebuttable presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in child’s best interests; de facto custodian
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.270. Custodial issues; best interests of child shall determine; rebuttable presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in child’s best interests; de facto custodian (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) As used in this chapter andKRS 405.020, unless the context requires otherwise, “de facto custodian” means a person who has been shown by clear and convincing evidence to have been
         the primary caregiver for, and financial supporter of, a child who within the last
         two (2) years has resided with the person for an aggregate period of six (6) months
         or more if the child is under three (3) years of age and for an aggregate period of
         one (1) year or more if the child is three (3) years of age or older or has been placed
         by the Department for Community Based Services.  Any period of time after a legal proceeding has been commenced by a parent seeking
         to regain custody of the child shall not be included in determining whether the child
         has resided with the person for the required minimum period.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.290. Child; court may interview, court may seek advice of professional personnel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.290. Child; court may interview, court may seek advice of professional personnel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.290. Child; court may interview, court may seek advice of professional personnel (2023)
content:
(1)  The court may interview the child in chambers to ascertain the child's wishes
      as to his custodian and as to visitation.  The court may permit counsel to be present at the interview.  The court shall cause a record of the interview to be made and to be part of the
      record in the case.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.310. Hearings; custody proceedings shall receive priority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.310. Hearings; custody proceedings shall receive priority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.310. Hearings; custody proceedings shall receive priority (2023)
content: (1)  Custody proceedings shall receive priority in being set for hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Dissolution; Legal Separation›KY REV ST 403.250. Modification or termination of provisions for maintenance and property disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Dissolution; Legal Separation › KY REV ST 403.250. Modification or termination of provisions for maintenance and property disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.250. Modification or termination of provisions for maintenance and property disposition (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in subsection (6) ofKRS 403.180, the provisions of any decree respecting maintenance may be modified only upon a
      showing of changed circumstances so substantial and continuing as to make the terms
      unconscionable.  The provisions as to property disposition may not be revoked or modified, unless
      the court finds the existence of conditions that justify the reopening of a judgment
      under the laws of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.315. Presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in best interest of child inapplicable if domestic violence order entered against a party
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.315. Presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in best interest of child inapplicable if domestic violence order entered against a party
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.315. Presumption that joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in best interest of child inapplicable if domestic violence order entered against a party (2023)
content:
When determining or modifying a custody order pursuant toKRS 403.270,403.280,403.340,403.740, the court shall consider the safety and well-being of the parties and of the children.  If a domestic violence order is being or has been entered against a party by another
   party or on behalf of a child at issue in the custody hearing, the presumption that
   joint custody and equally shared parenting time is in the best interest of the child
   shall not apply as to the party against whom the domestic violence order is being
   or has been entered.  The court shall weigh all factors set out inKRS 403.270in determining the best interest of the child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.300. Investigation; court may order in custody proceedings; attorney to receive copy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.300. Investigation; court may order in custody proceedings; attorney to receive copy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.300. Investigation; court may order in custody proceedings; attorney to receive copy (2023)
content:
(1)  In contested custody proceedings, and in other custody proceedings if a parent
      or the child's custodian so requests, the court may order an investigation and report
      concerning custodial arrangements for the child.  The investigation and report may be made by the friend of the court or such other
      agency as the court may select.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.280. Temporary custody orders
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.280. Temporary custody orders
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.280. Temporary custody orders (2023)
content:
(1)  A party to a custody proceeding may move for a temporary custody order.  The motion must be supported by an affidavit as provided inKRS 403.350.  The court may award temporary custody under the standards ofKRS 403.270after a hearing, or, if there is no objection, solely on the basis of the affidavits.  If the parents or a de facto custodian joined under subsection (9) of this section
      present a temporary custody agreement and mutually agreed plan for parenting time,
      and the court confirms that the agreement adequately provides for the welfare of the
      child, the agreement shall become the temporary custody order of the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.325. Visitation denied parent convicted of homicide of other parent; exception; hearing required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.325. Visitation denied parent convicted of homicide of other parent; exception; hearing required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.325. Visitation denied parent convicted of homicide of other parent; exception; hearing required (2023)
content:
(1)  Notwithstanding the provisions ofKRS 403.320, if a parent of a child is convicted of murder or manslaughter in the first degree
      of the other parent, a court shall not grant the convicted parent visitation rights
      with respect to that child unless the court, through a hearing, determines that visitation
      is in the child's best interest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.350. Affidavit required with motion for temporary custody order or for modification of custody decree
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.350. Affidavit required with motion for temporary custody order or for modification of custody decree
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.350. Affidavit required with motion for temporary custody order or for modification of custody decree (2023)
content:
A party seeking a temporary custody order or modification of a custody decree shall
   submit together with his moving papers an affidavit setting forth facts supporting
   the requested order or modification and shall give notice, together with a copy of
   his affidavit, to other parties to the proceeding, who may file opposing affidavits.  If a court determines that a child is in the custody of a de facto custodian, the
   court shall make the de facto custodian a party to the proceeding.  The court shall deny the motion unless it finds that adequate cause for hearing
   the motion is established by the affidavits, in which case it shall set a date for
   hearing on an order to show cause why the requested order or modification should not
   be granted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.320. Visitation of minor child; visitation rights of custodial relatives following termination of parental rights of others
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.320. Visitation of minor child; visitation rights of custodial relatives following termination of parental rights of others
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.320. Visitation of minor child; visitation rights of custodial relatives following termination of parental rights of others (2023)
content:
(1)  A parent not granted custody of the child and not awarded shared parenting time
      under the presumption specified inKRS 403.270(2),403.280(2), or403.340(5)is entitled to reasonable visitation rights unless the court finds, after a hearing,
      that visitation would endanger seriously the child's physical, mental, moral, or emotional
      health.  Upon request of either party, the court shall issue orders which are specific as
      to the frequency, timing, duration, conditions, and method of scheduling visitation
      and which reflect the development age of the child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.330. Judicial supervision of custody decree or agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.330. Judicial supervision of custody decree or agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.330. Judicial supervision of custody decree or agreement (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise agreed by the parties in writing at the time of the custody
      decree, the custodian may determine the child's upbringing, including his education,
      health care, and religious training, unless the court after hearing, finds, upon motion
      by the noncustodial parent, that in the absence of a specific limitation of the custodian's
      authority, the child's physical health would be endangered or his emotional development
      significantly impaired.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.353. Form of power of attorney authorized by this section, KRS 403.352, and KRS Chapter 403A
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.353. Form of power of attorney authorized by this section, KRS 403.352, and KRS Chapter 403A
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.353. Form of power of attorney authorized by this section, KRS 403.352, and KRS Chapter 403A (2023)
content:
(1)  A power of attorney established pursuant to this section,KRS 403.352, and KRS Chapter 403A shall be substantially in the following form, and may include
      other specific directions which are in accordance with accepted legal practice and
      not specifically prohibited by any other statute.  If any other specific directions are held by a court of appropriate jurisdiction
      to be invalid, that invalidity shall not affect the power of attorney or other provisions
      established in this section,KRS 403.352, and KRS Chapter 403A.

content:

      for a period not to exceed one (1) year any of the traditional parental rights and
      responsibilities regarding care and custody of the child except the following authorities:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.340. Modification of custody decree
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.340. Modification of custody decree
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.340. Modification of custody decree (2023)
content: (1)  As used in this section, “custody” means sole or joint custody, whether ordered by a court or agreed to by the parties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.322. Custody, visitation, and inheritance rights denied parent convicted of felony sexual offense from which victim delivered a child; waiver; child support obligation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.322. Custody, visitation, and inheritance rights denied parent convicted of felony sexual offense from which victim delivered a child; waiver; child support obligation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.322. Custody, visitation, and inheritance rights denied parent convicted of felony sexual offense from which victim delivered a child; waiver; child support obligation (2023)
content:
(1)  The Commonwealth recognizes that certain victims of sexual assault may conceive
      a child as a result of the sexual assault and may choose to bear and raise the child.  The Commonwealth also recognizes that victims of a sexual assault who have elected
      to raise a child born as a result of the sexual assault, as well as that child, may
      suffer serious emotional or physical trauma if the perpetrator of the assault is granted
      parental rights with the child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Custody›KY REV ST 403.355. Definition of “safe child drop-off location”; child custody exchanges in these locations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Custody › KY REV ST 403.355. Definition of “safe child drop-off location”; child custody exchanges in these locations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.355. Definition of “safe child drop-off location”; child custody exchanges in these locations (2023)
content:
(1)  As used in this section, “safe child drop-off location” means any public building owned, leased, or occupied by the Commonwealth, or by
      any city or county within the Commonwealth, to which access is limited and security
      measures, including metal detectors, are in place.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.730. Immediate review of petition; summons to evidentiary hearing; ex parte emergency protective order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.730. Immediate review of petition; summons to evidentiary hearing; ex parte emergency protective order
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.730. Immediate review of petition; summons to evidentiary hearing; ex parte emergency protective order (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) The court shall review a petition for an order of protection immediately
         upon its filing.  If the review indicates that domestic violence and abuse exists, the court shall
         summons the parties to an evidentiary hearing not more than fourteen (14) days in
         the future.  If the review indicates that such a basis does not exist, the court may consider
         an amended petition or dismiss the petition without prejudice.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.7527. Filing of foreign protective order and affidavit; certification by issuing court official; entry into Law Information Network of Kentucky (2023)
content:
(1)  A copy of a foreign protective order may be filed in the office of the clerk
      of any court of competent jurisdiction of this state.  A foreign protective order so filed shall have the same effect and shall be enforced
      in the same manner as an order of protection issued by a court of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.763. Violation of order of protection constitutes contempt of court and criminal offense
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.763. Violation of order of protection constitutes contempt of court and criminal offense
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.763. Violation of order of protection constitutes contempt of court and criminal offense (2023)
content:
(1)  Violation of the terms or conditions of an order of protection after the person
      has been served or given notice of the order shall constitute contempt of court and
      a criminal offense under this section.  Once a criminal or contempt proceeding has been initiated, the other shall not be
      undertaken regardless of the outcome of the original proceeding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.785. Duties of law enforcement officers and agencies

content:
(1)  A court issuing an order of protection shall direct the appropriate law enforcement
      agency to assist the petitioner in having the provisions of the order complied with.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.7505. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.7505. Certification standards for mental health professionals providing court-mandated treatment; list of certified providers to Administrative Office of the Courts; collection of data (2023)

(1)  The Cabinet for Health and Family Services shall, by administrative regulations

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.7521. Foreign protective orders; rebuttable presumption of validity; enforcement; civil and criminal proceedings mutually exclusive
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.7521. Foreign protective orders; rebuttable presumption of validity; enforcement; civil and criminal proceedings mutually exclusive
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.7521. Foreign protective orders; rebuttable presumption of validity; enforcement; civil and criminal proceedings mutually exclusive (2023)
content:
(1)  All foreign protective orders shall have the rebuttable presumption of validity.  The validity of a foreign protective order shall only be determined by a court of
      competent jurisdiction.  Until a foreign protective order is declared to be invalid by a court of competent
      jurisdiction, it shall be given full faith and credit by all peace officers and courts
      in the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.750. Order of protection for family member or member of unmarried couple upon filing of petition or action under KRS Chapter § 403
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.750. Order of protection for family member or member of unmarried couple upon filing of petition or action under KRS Chapter § 403
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.750. Order of protection for family member or member of unmarried couple upon filing of petition or action under KRS Chapter § 403 (2023)
content:
(1)  Any family member or any member of an unmarried couple may file for and receive
      protection under this chapter from domestic violence and abuse, notwithstanding the
      existence of or intent to file an action under this chapter by either party.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.745. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.745. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.745. Duration of emergency protective order and domestic violence order; prohibited costs and conditions; mutual orders of protection; amendment; expungement (2023)
content:
(1)  An emergency protective order and a domestic violence order shall become effective
      and binding on the respondent when the respondent is given notice of the existence
      and terms of the order by a peace officer or the court or upon personal service of
      the order, whichever is earlier.  A peace officer or court giving notice of an unserved order shall make all reasonable
      efforts to arrange for the order's personal service upon the respondent.  Once effective, a peace officer or the court may enforce the order's terms and act
      immediately upon their violation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXV. Domestic Relations›Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody›Domestic Violence and Abuse›KY REV ST 403.7529. Authentication of foreign protective order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.7529. Authentication of foreign protective order

      pursuant toKRS 403.7527, and after determining the order is entitled to full faith and credit in this Commonwealth
      pursuant to18 U.S.C. sec. 2265, the court shall declare the order to be authenticated and record the finding on
      the affidavit.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXV. Domestic Relations › Chapter 403. Dissolution of Marriage; Child Custody › Domestic Violence and Abuse › KY REV ST 403.754. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 403.754. Petitioner for protective order may apply for temporary permit to carry concealed deadly weapon; criteria; denial of application final; conversion to concealed carry license; automated listing of temporary permit holders (2023)
