path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXVIII. Witnesses, Evidence, Notaries, Commissioners of Foreign Deeds, and Legal Notices›Chapter 424. Legal Notices›Matters Required to Be Published›KY REV ST 424.250. School district budget
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXVIII. Witnesses, Evidence, Notaries, Commissioners of Foreign Deeds, and Legal Notices › Chapter 424. Legal Notices › Matters Required to Be Published › KY REV ST 424.250. School district budget
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 424.250. School district budget (2023)
content:
At the same time that copies of the budget of a school district are filed with the
   clerk of the tax levying authority for the district, as provided inKRS 160.470, the board of education of the district shall cause the budget to be advertised for
   the district by publishing a copy of the budget in a newspaper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.031. Conduct of hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.031. Conduct of hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.031. Conduct of hearing (2023)
content:
Upon request of a defendant or intervening party, the judicial officer shall conduct
   a hearing at which each party shall be provided the opportunity to present witnesses
   on his behalf and to cross-examine adverse witnesses.  The parties shall have the right to compel the attendance of witnesses by subpoena
   and to be represented at the hearing by counsel.  The judicial officer shall make his determination upon the evidence adduced at the
   hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.076. Issuance of ex parte writ of possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.076. Issuance of ex parte writ of possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.076. Issuance of ex parte writ of possession (2023)
content:
(1)  A judicial officer, except as otherwise provided by statute, shall not issue
      an ex parte writ of possession unless it appears from facts shown by affidavit that
      great or irreparable injury would result to the plaintiff if issuance of the writ
      were delayed until the matter could be heard on notice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.011. Motion for writ of possession; required allegations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.011. Motion for writ of possession; required allegations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.011. Motion for writ of possession; required allegations (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon filing of the complaint or at any time prior to judgment, in an action to
      recover the possession of specific personal property, the plaintiff may apply pursuant
      to this chapter for a writ of possession by filing a written motion for the writ with
      the court in which the action is brought.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.081. Motion to quash writ
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.081. Motion to quash writ
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.081. Motion to quash writ (2023)
content:
(1)  Any defendant whose property has been taken pursuant to a writ of possession
      issued under this chapter may apply for an order that the writ be quashed and any
      property levied on pursuant to the writ be released.  Such application shall be made by noticed motion and the provisions ofKRS 425.031.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.066. Temporary restraining order; preliminary injunction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.066. Temporary restraining order; preliminary injunction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.066. Temporary restraining order; preliminary injunction (2023)
content:
(1)  At or after the time he files his motion for writ of possession, the plaintiff
      may apply for a temporary restraining order by setting forth in the motion a statement
      of grounds justifying the issuance of such order.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.046. Requirements of writ of possession (2023)
content: (1)  The writ of possession shall meet all of the following requirements:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.061. Effect of determinations of judicial officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.061. Effect of determinations of judicial officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.061. Effect of determinations of judicial officer (2023)
content:
The determinations of the judicial officer under this chapter shall have no effect
   on the determination of any issues in the action other than the issues relevant to
   proceedings under this chapter, nor shall they affect the rights of any party in any
   other action arising out of the same claim.  The determinations of the judicial officer under this chapter shall not be given
   in evidence nor referred to in the trial of any such action.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › General Provisions › KY REV ST 425.006. Definitions

content: As used in this chapter:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.051. Ex parte motion; endorsement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.051. Ex parte motion; endorsement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.051. Ex parte motion; endorsement (2023)
content:
(1)  The plaintiff may apply ex parte in writing to the court in which the action
      was brought for an endorsement on the writ directing the sheriff to seize the property
      at a private place not specified in the writ.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.036. Issuance of writ of possession (2023)
content:
(1)  At the hearing, the judicial officer shall issue a writ of possession if he finds

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.012. Writ of possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.012. Writ of possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.012. Writ of possession (2023)
content:
(1)  Before a writ of possession shall be issued by the clerk, the person seeking
      the writ must first make a demand in writing at or after the time the suit is filed,
      by delivering such demand and a copy of the complaint, motion and summons to the defendant
      or by sending them to him by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested,
      to the last known place of residence, at least seven (7) and not more than sixty (60)
      days before such order is sought.  The demand shall contain a statement in substance that the defendant has seven (7)
      days in which to petition the court for a hearing or in which to pay the amount claimed
      in the complaint in full, and that unless a hearing is set or the amount paid, a writ
      of possession will issue.  The statement shall identify the court in which the suit has been filed, the grounds
      therefor, the date of the demand, the amount claimed, and the name and address of
      the plaintiff and his attorney.  An affidavit of the plaintiff or his attorney evidencing compliance with this subsection
      shall be filed before a writ shall be issued.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.086. Issuance of temporary restraining order in lieu of writ of possession; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.086. Issuance of temporary restraining order in lieu of writ of possession; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.086. Issuance of temporary restraining order in lieu of writ of possession; effect (2023)
content:
(1)  In any case where the plaintiff has made a motion for a writ of possession underKRS 425.076the court may in its discretion deny the motion for the writ and issue instead a
      temporary restraining order under this chapter if it determines that the requirements
      of subsection (3) ofKRS 425.076are satisfied but that the issuance of the temporary restraining order instead of
      the writ of possession would be in the interest of justice and equity to the parties,
      taking into account the effect on the defendant of issuing a writ of possession ex
      parte, the effect on the plaintiff of issuing the temporary restraining order instead
      of the writ and other factors that bear on equity and justice under the circumstances
      of the particular case.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.071. Prohibitions by temporary restraining order

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.056. Effect of failure of defendant to oppose writ or rebut evidence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.056. Effect of failure of defendant to oppose writ or rebut evidence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.056. Effect of failure of defendant to oppose writ or rebut evidence (2023)
content:
Neither the failure of the defendant to oppose the issuance of a writ of possession
   under this chapter nor his failure to rebut any evidence produced by the plaintiff
   in connection with proceedings under this chapter shall constitute a waiver of any
   defense to plaintiff's claim in the action or any other action or have any effect
   on the right of the defendant to produce or exclude evidence at the trial of any such
   action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.041. Order transferring possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.041. Order transferring possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.041. Order transferring possession (2023)
content:
If a writ of possession is issued, the judicial officer may also issue an order directing
   the defendant to transfer possession of the property to the plaintiff.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.106. Return of writ; procedure when claimed property has been disposed of or concealed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.106. Return of writ; procedure when claimed property has been disposed of or concealed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.106. Return of writ; procedure when claimed property has been disposed of or concealed (2023)
content:
(1)  The levying officer shall return the writ of possession with his proceedings
      thereon, to the court in which the action is pending within 30 days after levy but
      in no event more than 60 days after the writ is issued.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›General Provisions›KY REV ST 425.001. Exemption of surety on specified bonds
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › General Provisions › KY REV ST 425.001. Exemption of surety on specified bonds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.001. Exemption of surety on specified bonds (2023)
content:
No surety shall be required on any bond made for the purpose of the issuance of a
   temporary restraining order, writ of possession, or order of attachment pursuant to
   this chapter by any domestic bank, savings and loan institution, or institution which
   is a member of the Farm Credit System, as defined by12 U.S.C. Section 2002.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.091. Levy on property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.091. Levy on property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.091. Levy on property (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as otherwise provided in this section, upon receipt of the writ of possession
      the levying officer shall search for and take custody of the specified property, if
      it be in the possession of the defendant or his agent, either by removing the property
      to a place of safe keeping or upon order of the judicial officer by installing a keeper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.101. Delivery of property; redelivery; levy upon perishable property; control of property

content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.301. Grounds for attachment in action for recovery of money

Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.126. Execution on transferable securities, security entitlements, or an option or right to acquire a security; requirements of the order; duty of corporate officials
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.126. Execution on transferable securities, security entitlements, or an option or right to acquire a security; requirements of the order; duty of corporate officials (2023)
content:
(1)  If any claim be made by attachment, garnishment, or other judicial order to a
      security or security entitlement, as defined inKRS 355.8-102(1), such order shall not be valid as against any securities intermediary, as defined
      inKRS 355.8-102(1), or any issuer, as defined inKRS 355.8-201, or nominee or agent of either having any interest in, custody of, or control over
      such security or security entitlement, unless such order specifies the following:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.111. Plaintiff's bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.111. Plaintiff's bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.111. Plaintiff's bond (2023)
content:
(1)  The judicial officer shall not issue a temporary restraining order or a writ
      of possession until the plaintiff has filed with the court a written bond that, if
      the plaintiff fails to recover judgment in the action, the plaintiff shall return
      the property to the defendant, if return thereof be ordered, and shall pay all costs
      that may be awarded to the defendant and all damages referred to in subsection (2),
      not exceeding the amount of the bond.  The bond shall be executed by one (1) or more sufficient sureties in an amount not
      less than twice the value of the property as determined by the judicial officer.  This subsection may be satisfied by the posting of a cash bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.096. Service of writ and bond by levying officer; attachment of property removed from the county
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.096. Service of writ and bond by levying officer; attachment of property removed from the county
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.096. Service of writ and bond by levying officer; attachment of property removed from the county (2023)
content:
(1)  At the time of the levy, the levying officer shall deliver to the person in possession
      of the property a copy of the writ of possession with a copy of the plaintiff's bond
      attached.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.116. Defendant's bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.116. Defendant's bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.116. Defendant's bond (2023)
content:
(1)  The defendant or any other person claiming interest in the property, may prevent
      the plaintiff from taking possession of property pursuant to a writ of possession
      or regain possession of property so taken by filing with the court in which the action
      was brought, a written bond executed by one (1) or more sufficient sureties in an
      amount equal to either the amount of the plaintiff's bond required byKRS 425.111or if there has been no judicial determination, the value of the property stated
      in the plaintiff's application for a writ of possession.  The bond shall state that, if the plaintiff recovers judgment on the action, the
      defendant shall pay all costs awarded to the plaintiff and all damages that the plaintiff
      may sustain by reason of the loss of possession of the property, not exceeding the
      amount of the bond.  The damages recoverable by the plaintiff pursuant to this section shall include
      all damages proximately caused by the plaintiff's failure to gain or retain possession.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Writ of Possession›KY REV ST 425.121. Exception to sureties; effect of failure to justify
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Writ of Possession › KY REV ST 425.121. Exception to sureties; effect of failure to justify
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.121. Exception to sureties; effect of failure to justify (2023)
content:
(1)  The defendant may except to the plaintiff's sureties not later than 10 days after
      levy of the writ of possession by filing with the court in which the action was brought
      a notice of exception to sureties and mailing a copy of the notice to the levying
      officer and to the plaintiff.  The notice of exception filed with the court shall contain a certification that
      copies have been mailed to the levying officer and to the plaintiff.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.302. Application for release of attachment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.302. Application for release of attachment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.302. Application for release of attachment (2023)
content:
Any defendant whose property is attached pursuant to an attachment issued underKRS 425.301,425.306, or425.308, may apply for an order that the attachment be quashed and any property taken, or
   attached, be released from the attachment.  Such application shall be made by noticed motion.  A defendant making a motion to quash pursuant to this section shall be entitled
   to an immediate hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.306. Grounds of attachment for debt or liability upon a contract
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.306. Grounds of attachment for debt or liability upon a contract
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.306. Grounds of attachment for debt or liability upon a contract (2023)
content:
(1)  Before a debt or liability upon a contract becomes due or matures, an equitable
      action for indemnity may be brought by a creditor against his debtor;  by a surety
      against his principal;  or by one who is jointly liable with another for such debt
      or liability, against the latter:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.316. Examination
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.316. Examination
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.316. Examination (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person owing debts to the defendant, or having in his possession or under
      his control any personal property belonging to the defendant, may be required to appear
      before the court and be examined on oath regarding such property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.307. Motion for order of attachment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.307. Motion for order of attachment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.307. Motion for order of attachment (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon filing of the complaint or at any time prior to judgment, the plaintiff
      may apply pursuant to this chapter for an order of attachment by filing a written
      motion for the order with the court in which the action is brought.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.309. Posting of bond by plaintiff; posting of bond by defendant; exceptions to sureties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.309. Posting of bond by plaintiff; posting of bond by defendant; exceptions to sureties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.309. Posting of bond by plaintiff; posting of bond by defendant; exceptions to sureties (2023)
content:
(1)  An order of attachment shall not be issued until a bond has been executed by
      one (1) or more sufficient sureties of the plaintiff in an amount not less than double
      the amount of the plaintiff's claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Attachment›KY REV ST 425.308. Ex parte order of attachment, issuance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Attachment › KY REV ST 425.308. Ex parte order of attachment, issuance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.308. Ex parte order of attachment, issuance (2023)
content:
(1)  A judicial officer, except as otherwise provided by statute, may issue an ex
      parte order of attachment if it appears from facts shown by affidavit that great or
      irreparable injury would result to the plaintiff if issuance of the order were delayed
      until the matter could be heard on notice.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.506. Attachment or garnishment of earnings; priority; order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.506. Attachment or garnishment of earnings; priority; order
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.506. Attachment or garnishment of earnings; priority; order (2023)
content:
(1)  An order of garnishment of earnings, as defined inKRS 427.005, shall create a lien on all nonexempt earnings earned during the pay period in which
      the order is served on the employer and during those succeeding pay periods which
      may be designated by the order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.516. Payment by garnishee; costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.516. Payment by garnishee; costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.516. Payment by garnishee; costs (2023)
content:
The garnishee may pay the money owing to the defendant by him, not exceeding the plaintiff's
   claim and costs, to the sheriff having in his hands the order of attachment, or into
   the court or to such person as the court may direct in accordance with the Rules of
   Civil Procedure;  and to that extent he shall be discharged from liability to the
   defendant.  He shall not be subjected to costs beyond those caused by his resistance of the
   claim against him;  and, if he discloses the property of the defendant in his hands,
   or the true sum owing by him, and delivers or pays the same to the sheriff, or according
   to the order of the court, he shall be allowed his costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.511. Appearance of garnishee; failure to appear
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.511. Appearance of garnishee; failure to appear
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.511. Appearance of garnishee; failure to appear (2023)
content:
(1)  Each garnishee summoned shall appear.  The appearance may be in person;  or by the affidavit of the garnishee, served and
      filed in the manner and at the time required for an answer by the Rules of Civil Procedure,
      disclosing truly the sum owing by him to the defendant, whether due or not, and the
      property of the defendant in the possession or under the control of the garnishee;
      and, in the case of a corporation, any shares of stocks therein held by or for the
      benefit of the defendant, at or after the service of the order of attachment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.501. Proceedings for obtaining order of garnishment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.501. Proceedings for obtaining order of garnishment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.501. Proceedings for obtaining order of garnishment (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person in whose favor a final judgment in personam has been entered in any
      court of record of this state may, upon the filing of an affidavit by him or his agent
      or attorney in the office of the clerk of the court in which the judgment was entered,
      and in the same cause in which said judgment was obtained showing the date of the
      judgment and the amount due thereon, and that one (1) or more named persons hold property
      belonging to, or are indebted to, the judgment debtor, obtain an order of garnishment
      to be served in accordance with the Rules of Civil Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Receivership›KY REV ST 425.600. Appointment of receiver; appeal from order appointing or refusing to appoint; powers of receiver
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Receivership › KY REV ST 425.600. Appointment of receiver; appeal from order appointing or refusing to appoint; powers of receiver
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.600. Appointment of receiver; appeal from order appointing or refusing to appoint; powers of receiver (2023)
content:
(1)  On the motion of any party to an action who shows that he has, or probably has,
      a right to, a lien upon, or an interest in, any property or fund, the right to which
      is involved in the action, and that the property or fund is in danger of being lost,
      removed or materially injured, the court may appoint a receiver, or order the master
      commissioner to take charge of the property or fund during the pendency of the action,
      and may order and coerce the delivery of it to him.  The order of a court appointing or refusing to appoint a receiver, shall be deemed
      a final order for the purpose of an appeal;  Provided, that such order shall not be
      superseded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.005. Personal judgment in action to enforce mortgage or lien; when mortgage may be enforced
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.005. Personal judgment in action to enforce mortgage or lien; when mortgage may be enforced
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.005. Personal judgment in action to enforce mortgage or lien; when mortgage may be enforced (2023)
content:
(1)  In an action to enforce a mortgage or lien, judgment may be rendered for the
      sale of the property and for the recovery of the debt against the defendant personally.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.521. Procedure if garnishee indebted to defendant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.521. Procedure if garnishee indebted to defendant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.521. Procedure if garnishee indebted to defendant (2023)
content:
If a garnishee, or officer of a corporation summoned as a garnishee, appear in person,
   he may be examined on oath;  and, if it be discovered on such examination that, at
   the service of the order of attachment upon him, he or the corporation was possessed
   of any property of the defendant, or was indebted to him, the court may order the
   delivery of such property, and the payment, or security for the payment, of the sum
   owing by the garnishee, into court, or to such person as it may direct--who shall
   give bond, with security, for the same;  or the court may permit the garnishee to
   retain the property or the sum owing upon the execution of a bond with one (1) or
   more sufficient sureties, to the effect that the sum shall be paid, or the property
   be forthcoming, as the court may direct.  Performance of such bonds, for the forthcoming of property, may be enforced, as
   in cases of contempt;  upon such bonds for payment of money, execution may be issued
   as upon replevin bonds.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.040. Return of execution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.040. Return of execution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.040. Return of execution (2023)
content:
(1)  An execution against property by the levying officer shall be returnable to the
      court in which the action is pending within 30 days after levy but in no event more
      than 60 days after the execution is issued.  Each court shall by an order of record appoint a monthly return day of executions.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.010. Execution against property may issue on personal judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.010. Execution against property may issue on personal judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.010. Execution against property may issue on personal judgment (2023)
content:
If a final judgment in personam is rendered in any court of record in this state for
   an ascertained sum of money, with interest and cost, or for either, an execution against
   property may issue thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.006. Other liens to be stated in action to enforce lien; cross claim
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.006. Other liens to be stated in action to enforce lien; cross claim
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.006. Other liens to be stated in action to enforce lien; cross claim (2023)
content:
The plaintiff in an action for enforcing a lien on property shall state in his petition
   the liens held thereon by others, making them defendants;  and may ask for and obtain
   a judgment for a sale of the property to satisfy all of said liens which are shown
   to exist, though the defendants fail to assert their claims.  Such defendants shall not, however, be allowed to withdraw or receive any of the
   proceeds of such sale, until they have shown their right thereto by answer and cross
   claim, which shall be asserted as provided in the Rules of Civil Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.020. Form of execution against property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.020. Form of execution against property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.020. Form of execution against property (2023)
content:
The form of an execution against property, varied to suit the particular case, may
   be in substance as follows:  “The Commonwealth of Kentucky, to the sheriff of __________ County, greeting:  We command you that of the estate of A B, you cause to be made
   the sum of $ _____ which C D late in our __________ court hath recovered against him for debt, with interest thereon from the _____ day of __________ until paid;  also the sum of $ _____ which to the said C D in the same court was adjudged for his costs in that suit expended,
   whereof he is convicted as appears to us of record, and that you have the said sums
   of money before our court on the _____ day of __________, to render to the said C D his debt, interest and costs aforesaid and have then there
   this writ.  Witness.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.030. Execution not to issue for ten days; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.030. Execution not to issue for ten days; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.030. Execution not to issue for ten days; exception (2023)
content:
No execution shall issue on any judgment, unless ordered by the court, until after
   the expiration of ten days from the rendition thereof.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies›Garnishment›KY REV ST 425.526. Action by plaintiff against garnishee; attachment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 425. Provisional Remedies › Garnishment › KY REV ST 425.526. Action by plaintiff against garnishee; attachment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 425.526. Action by plaintiff against garnishee; attachment (2023)
content:
If a garnishee fails to make a disclosure satisfactory to the plaintiff, the latter
   may bring an action against him, by petition or amended petition, in the same manner,
   and the proceedings therein shall be the same as in other actions;  and the plaintiff
   may procure an order of attachment in the same manner, and the proceedings thereupon
   shall be the same, as is hereinbefore and hereinafter authorized concerning attachments--except
   that the plaintiff's affidavit shall state, in addition to the facts required to be
   stated inKRS 425.301(3), the sum which the defendant owes to the plaintiff's debtor;  and the plaintiff shall
   not be entitled to attach for or recover more than that sum and costs nor more than
   the amount of the plaintiff's claim against his debtor and costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.035. Execution may issue until barred by limitation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.035. Execution may issue until barred by limitation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.035. Execution may issue until barred by limitation (2023)
content:
An execution may be issued upon a judgment at any time until the collection of it
   is barred by the statute of limitation, although no execution may have been previously
   issued within a year and a day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.080. Counties to which executions may issue; liability for wrongful issuance
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.080. Counties to which executions may issue; liability for wrongful issuance
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.080. Counties to which executions may issue; liability for wrongful issuance (2023)
content:
(1)  No execution against property shall issue to any other county than that in which
      the judgment was rendered, or that in which the defendant resides, until execution
      has issued to one of the counties named and has been returned endorsed by the proper
      officer that no property was found, as to all or part thereof.  However, if the plaintiff or his agent or attorney makes and files with the clerk
      of the court in which the judgment was rendered an affidavit stating that the defendant
      in the judgment has not sufficient property subject to execution in the county in
      which the judgment was rendered, or in the county in which he resides, to satisfy
      the judgment, execution shall issue to any or as many counties as the plaintiff directs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.060. Order of property sold when joint execution issued against personal representative, heir and devisee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.060. Order of property sold when joint execution issued against personal representative, heir and devisee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.060. Order of property sold when joint execution issued against personal representative, heir and devisee (2023)
content:
When an execution is issued jointly against a personal representative, an heir and
   a devisee, or any two of them, the officer in whose hands it is placed for collection
   shall sell, first, the estate in the hands of the personal representative;  second,
   the estate descended to the heir;  and third, the estate devised.  The defendants may, in writing, direct the sale to take place in any order they
   desire.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.050. Issuance of second or joint executions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.050. Issuance of second or joint executions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.050. Issuance of second or joint executions (2023)
content:
If an execution against property is issued and the plaintiff desires to take out another
   at his own cost, the clerk may issue it although the previous execution has not been
   returned.  If the execution is returned in whole or in part not satisfied, a new one may issue.  On a joint judgment against several persons the execution must be joint.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.180. Railroads; property subject to execution; receiver to enforce judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.180. Railroads; property subject to execution; receiver to enforce judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.180. Railroads; property subject to execution; receiver to enforce judgment (2023)
content:
(1)  The rolling stock and other movable property belonging to any railroad company
      in this state shall be considered personal property, and liable to execution and sale
      in the same manner as the property of individuals.  The earnings, money and choses in action of any railroad company in the hands of
      any officer, agent or employee may be subjected to the payment of debts in the same
      manner as similar property of individuals.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.100. Plaintiff may designate agent to receive money
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.100. Plaintiff may designate agent to receive money
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.100. Plaintiff may designate agent to receive money (2023)
content:
When an execution is placed in the hands of an officer for collection, in a county
   in which the plaintiff does not reside, the plaintiff may, by endorsement on the execution,
   name an agent in the county to which the execution is directed, who may receive and
   receipt for the money collected.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.090. Sheriff not required to leave county to return
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.090. Sheriff not required to leave county to return
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.090. Sheriff not required to leave county to return (2023)
content:
A sheriff shall not be required to go out of his county to return an execution in
   a civil case.  He shall, if the plaintiff has no known agent or attorney in the county, keep a
   copy and mail the execution, with the return thereon, to the clerk of the court which
   issued it.  When so sent in proper time and manner, the officer shall not be liable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.120. Defendant's estate bound by execution from receipt by officer; time received to be noted; priority; apportionment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.120. Defendant's estate bound by execution from receipt by officer; time received to be noted; priority; apportionment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.120. Defendant's estate bound by execution from receipt by officer; time received to be noted; priority; apportionment (2023)
content:
(1)  An execution against property shall bind the estate of the defendant only from
      the time of its delivery to the proper officer to execute.  The officer to whom the execution is delivered shall, on receipt of it, endorse
      thereon the day, month, year and time of day of its receipt by him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.110. Execution from another county levied on land; duty of sheriff and clerk
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.110. Execution from another county levied on land; duty of sheriff and clerk
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.110. Execution from another county levied on land; duty of sheriff and clerk (2023)
content:
Where an execution issued in one county is sent to another county where land is levied
   upon, the sheriff levying the execution shall deliver it to the clerk of the circuit
   court in his county, who shall record the same as executions are now required to be
   recorded.  After recording it, the clerk shall deliver the execution to the sheriff, who shall
   return it to the office of the court where it was issued.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.130. Order in which property shall be levied on and sold
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.130. Order in which property shall be levied on and sold
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.130. Order in which property shall be levied on and sold (2023)
content:
Property shall be liable to levy and sale under execution in the following order:
   First, personalty;  second, land.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.140. Personalty insufficient, land may be sold
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.140. Personalty insufficient, land may be sold
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.140. Personalty insufficient, land may be sold (2023)
content:
If there is not enough personal property, the officer may levy on land at the same
   time and sell a sufficiency thereof to satisfy the execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.150. Defendant may select property to be sold; may surrender property not levied on
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.150. Defendant may select property to be sold; may surrender property not levied on
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.150. Defendant may select property to be sold; may surrender property not levied on (2023)
content:
The defendant may, on the day of the sale, in writing, direct the property levied
   on to be sold in any succession he desires.  He may produce other property or the title to land in the county not levied on and,
   by writing, direct the same to be sold first, and in that case the residue of the
   execution and costs, if any, shall be made out of the property levied on.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.160. Personal property; time and place of sale; advertisement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.160. Personal property; time and place of sale; advertisement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.160. Personal property; time and place of sale; advertisement (2023)
content:
Personal property may be sold at or in the vicinity of the place of levy in ten days
   after the levy.  The time and place of sale and a description of the property shall be advertised,
   by posting written or printed notices ten days preceding the sale at three of the
   most public places in the vicinity of the place of sale, and by newspaper notice if
   required byKRS 426.560.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.170. Growing crop; when may be sold; passes with sale of land
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.170. Growing crop; when may be sold; passes with sale of land
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.170. Growing crop; when may be sold; passes with sale of land (2023)
content:
No crop shall be levied on or sold under execution, attachment or any other legal
   or equitable proceeding, except an attachment for rent or to secure a mortgage or
   statutory lien, unless it has been severed from the ground, until after October 1
   in each year.  But, if the estate of the defendant in the land is liable to be sold, and is levied
   on and sold, the title to the growing crop may pass by the sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.200. Sale of land; place of; advertisement; appraisement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.200. Sale of land; place of; advertisement; appraisement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.200. Sale of land; place of; advertisement; appraisement (2023)
content:
(1)  Land shall be sold under execution to the highest bidder at the courthouse door
      of the county in which it lies.  Only so much land shall be sold as will satisfy the execution under which the sale
      is made.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.210. Defendant may designate tract or part of tract to be sold; duty of officer; title papers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.210. Defendant may designate tract or part of tract to be sold; duty of officer; title papers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.210. Defendant may designate tract or part of tract to be sold; duty of officer; title papers (2023)
content:
(1)  If the defendant in execution has an interest as provided inKRS 426.190in several tracts of land in the same county, he or his agent or attorney may, by
      writing, direct an officer having an execution against him to make the amount of the
      execution first out of such of the tracts as he may designate.  This direction shall not preclude the officer from levying on and selling other
      property at the same time to supply any deficiency.  Proper title papers shall be delivered to the officer with the directions.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.190. Land liable to execution; what interest defendant must have therein
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.190. Land liable to execution; what interest defendant must have therein
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.190. Land liable to execution; what interest defendant must have therein (2023)
content:
Land to which the defendant has a legal or equitable title in fee, for life or for
   a term, whether in possession, reversion or remainder, or in which the defendant has
   a contingent interest or a contingent remainder or a defeasible fee, may be taken
   and sold under execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.250. Conveyance to purchaser by sheriff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.250. Conveyance to purchaser by sheriff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.250. Conveyance to purchaser by sheriff (2023)
content:
The sheriff who sells land under execution or his deputy or successor shall, on demand,
   convey the title sold to the purchaser or his assignee, heirs or devisees, if the
   land is not redeemed and the redemption period has expired.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.205. Sale of vacant and abandoned real property to enforce mortgage or lien; proof of vacancy and abandonment; confirmation of sale and conveyance of property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.205. Sale of vacant and abandoned real property to enforce mortgage or lien; proof of vacancy and abandonment; confirmation of sale and conveyance of property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.205. Sale of vacant and abandoned real property to enforce mortgage or lien; proof of vacancy and abandonment; confirmation of sale and conveyance of property (2023)
content:
(1)  In an action otherwise properly brought to enforce a mortgage or lien against
      real property, including a lien pursuant toKRS 65.8801to65.8839orKRS 65.8840, which has been determined by the court to be vacant and abandoned, a sale of the
      property shall be ordered expeditiously.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.260. Motion for possession by purchaser; notice; judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.260. Motion for possession by purchaser; notice; judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.260. Motion for possession by purchaser; notice; judgment (2023)
content:
(1)  The purchaser of land sold under execution and not redeemed, after obtaining
      a conveyance therefor may, upon ten (10) days' notice in writing to the defendant
      in the execution, whose lands have been sold, enter a motion on the docket in the
      circuit court of the county where the land is situated for a judgment for the possession
      of the land.  If, upon the hearing of the motion, the court is of the opinion that the purchaser
      is entitled to the possession, it shall render a judgment accordingly and award possession,
      with costs.  The proceedings on the motion shall be as provided inKRS 418.005to418.015, andRule 6.03 of the Rules of Civil Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.280. Proceedings for possession if title of defendant equitable or encumbered
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.280. Proceedings for possession if title of defendant equitable or encumbered
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.280. Proceedings for possession if title of defendant equitable or encumbered (2023)
content:
If it appears in the proceedings provided for inKRS 426.260, that the title of the defendant to the land sold was only equitable, or the land
   was encumbered by mortgage or lien, the court shall, if the purchaser requires it,
   subject the land to the payment of the debt of the execution creditor in the same
   manner as if there was a return of no property found.  The court may cause such pleadings to be filed and parties brought before the court
   as may be necessary to a final equitable judgment in respect to the rights of all
   parties interested.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.220. Redemption; right of; payment of money; possession of defendant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.220. Redemption; right of; payment of money; possession of defendant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.220. Redemption; right of; payment of money; possession of defendant (2023)
content:
(1)  If land sold under execution does not bring two-thirds of its appraised value,
      the defendant and his representatives may redeem it within six (6) months from the
      day of sale, by paying the purchaser or his representative the original purchase money
      and ten percent per annum interest thereon.  The defendant redeeming his land shall take a receipt from the purchaser and lodge
      it with the clerk of the court, which receipt shall be filed and recorded with the
      execution under which the sale was made.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.270. Proceedings for possession if defendant had no title; damages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.270. Proceedings for possession if defendant had no title; damages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.270. Proceedings for possession if defendant had no title; damages (2023)
content:
If, upon the trial of the motion provided for inKRS 426.260, it appears that the defendant had no title to the land sold under execution, the
   court may set the sale aside, quash the return of the officer, and award execution
   for the debt as if no sale had been made.  If the land sold had been given up by the defendant to the officer for levy and
   sale and the sale is set aside, the court shall render judgment against the defendant
   for ten percent damages upon the amount of the execution, including interest and cost.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.290. Sale of encumbered property under execution; rights of purchaser, creditor; redemption; bond of purchaser of personalty; control of courts
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.290. Sale of encumbered property under execution; rights of purchaser, creditor; redemption; bond of purchaser of personalty; control of courts
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.290. Sale of encumbered property under execution; rights of purchaser, creditor; redemption; bond of purchaser of personalty; control of courts (2023)
content:
(1)  If the defendant in an execution owns the legal title to any real or personal
      property on which a bona fide encumbrance created prior to the execution lien exists,
      the interest of the defendant in the property may be levied on and sold, subject to
      the encumbrance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.230. Conveyance of land subject to redemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.230. Conveyance of land subject to redemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.230. Conveyance of land subject to redemption (2023)
content:
Land sold under execution which is subject to redemption shall not be conveyed by
   the officer making the sale until the expiration of six (6) months from the sale,
   nor shall he convey after that period if the land has been redeemed or an affidavit
   made and the money deposited with the clerk as provided inKRS 426.220, unless by court order or with the written assent of the defendant in the execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.295. Form of judgment in action for possession of specific personal property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.295. Form of judgment in action for possession of specific personal property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.295. Form of judgment in action for possession of specific personal property (2023)
content:
In an action for the possession of specific personal property, the plaintiff may have
   judgment for its delivery, if it can be had;  and, if not, for its value and for damages
   for its detention.  If the property have been delivered to the plaintiff, and the defendant claim a
   return thereof, judgment for the defendant may be for the return of the property,
   or its value if a return can not be had, and damages for the taking and withholding
   of the property.  There shall be no pre-judgment attachment of specific personal property except under
   the provisions of KRS Chapter 425.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.240. Redemption right may be sold; rights of defendant and purchaser
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.240. Redemption right may be sold; rights of defendant and purchaser
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.240. Redemption right may be sold; rights of defendant and purchaser (2023)
content:
The right of redemption may be sold under execution.  The land shall still be subject to redemption by the defendant, from both purchasers,
   for six (6) months from the first sale.  The purchaser of the right of redemption may, before the end of six (6) months from
   the first sale, pay the prior purchaser his money and interest as provided inKRS 426.220, and be entitled to the land, subject to the rights of possession and redemption
   held by the defendant in the execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.300. Specific property; execution on judgment for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.300. Specific property; execution on judgment for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.300. Specific property; execution on judgment for (2023)
content:
(1)  If a judgment is recovered for a specific thing, the plaintiff may have an execution
      issued thereon, commanding the proper officer to seize the property, and deliver it
      to the plaintiff.  The plaintiff may, if he so elect, take an execution for the assessed value of the
      property recovered.  In either case, the execution shall embrace the damages assessed for the detention
      and costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.350. Liability of officer for failing to make return in time; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.350. Liability of officer for failing to make return in time; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.350. Liability of officer for failing to make return in time; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  Any sheriff or like officer, in whose hands a writ of execution is placed, who
      fails, without reasonable excuse, to return the writ to the office where it was issued
      within thirty days after the return day, shall, with his sureties or the personal
      representatives, heirs or devisees of either, be liable jointly and severally to the
      plaintiff in the execution for the amount of the execution, with thirty percent damages
      thereon and the costs of recovery.  The remedy shall be the same as provided inKRS 426.360.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.370. Payment on execution after return day; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.370. Payment on execution after return day; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.370. Payment on execution after return day; effect (2023)
content:
Any payment made to a sheriff or other officer, or his deputy, on an execution after
   the return day and while the execution remains in his hands shall be a satisfaction
   to that extent.  The officer and his sureties on his official bond shall be responsible therefor,
   in the same manner as if the payment were made before the return day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.320. Sales invalid if made by fraud or collusion; proceedings to set aside; when lien not affected
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.320. Sales invalid if made by fraud or collusion; proceedings to set aside; when lien not affected
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.320. Sales invalid if made by fraud or collusion; proceedings to set aside; when lien not affected (2023)
content:
(1)  Sales made under execution by fraud or collusion may be set aside, in the court
      where the execution issued, on the motion of any person aggrieved or by petition in
      equity.  If by motion, the proceeding must be commenced within one year from the sale.  The parties affected by the motion shall have ten days' notice in writing, setting
      forth the grounds relied on for invalidating the sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.330. Purchase by officer at sale made by him void
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.330. Purchase by officer at sale made by him void
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.330. Purchase by officer at sale made by him void (2023)
content:
No officer shall, directly or indirectly, bid for or buy any property sold under an
   execution by him or his deputy, principal or codeputy.  The right of property so sold and purchased by any such officer, or by another for
   his use, shall not thereby be changed.  Any deed or bill of sale made for property so sold shall be void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.310. Livestock; execution on; quashed or stayed; duty and cost of caring for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.310. Livestock; execution on; quashed or stayed; duty and cost of caring for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.310. Livestock; execution on; quashed or stayed; duty and cost of caring for (2023)
content:
(1)  If an execution is levied on livestock and no forthcoming or replevin bond is
      immediately given, the officer shall provide sufficient sustenance for the livestock
      levied on until it is legally disposed of.  The officer shall make a fair estimate of his expenses and collect them, subject
      to correction by the court.  Upon the return of the execution, if either party desires, the court shall fix what
      the officer shall be allowed for his expenses, which shall be considered a part of
      the taxed costs in the case and collected accordingly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.340. Duty of officer in advertising sale under execution; returning equitable writ; defense
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.340. Duty of officer in advertising sale under execution; returning equitable writ; defense
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.340. Duty of officer in advertising sale under execution; returning equitable writ; defense (2023)
content:
(1)  No officer shall delay advertising property for sale, taken by him under execution,
      for more than twenty days after the levy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.360. Money collected by officer on execution; liability for failure to pay over; duty on stay of proceedings; remedies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.360. Money collected by officer on execution; liability for failure to pay over; duty on stay of proceedings; remedies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.360. Money collected by officer on execution; liability for failure to pay over; duty on stay of proceedings; remedies (2023)
content:
(1)  If a sheriff or other like officer receives money on any writ of execution or
      other process, and fails on proper demand to immediately pay the money to the party
      entitled thereto or to his agent or attorney, the officer and his sureties or any
      one of them, or his personal representatives, heirs or devisees, shall be liable to
      such party for the amount collected and fifteen percent per annum interest thereon
      from the demand until paid, together with the costs of recovery, legal and extraordinary.  The remedy shall be by motion or action in the court where the execution issued.  Ten days' notice of the motion, specifying the grounds thereof, shall be given.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.383. Creation of lien on defendant's property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.383. Creation of lien on defendant's property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.383. Creation of lien on defendant's property (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.380. Officer paying execution; assignment; substitution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.380. Officer paying execution; assignment; substitution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.380. Officer paying execution; assignment; substitution (2023)
content:
If a sheriff or other officer is compelled to pay an execution or any part of it,
   by reason of some default of his concerning the same, he shall be entitled to an assignment
   of the judgment, and a substitution in the place of the plaintiff in the same manner
   as is provided in favor of a surety paying a judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.381. Proceedings for discovery and satisfaction of judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.381. Proceedings for discovery and satisfaction of judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.381. Proceedings for discovery and satisfaction of judgment (2023)
content:
(1)  After an execution of fieri facias, directed to the county in which the judgment
      was rendered, or to the county of the defendant's residence, is returned by the proper
      officer, either as to the whole or part thereof, in substance, no property found to
      satisfy the same, the plaintiff in the execution may by an amended and supplemental
      petition filed in the action have the same redocketed and join with the execution
      defendant or defendants any person believed to be indebted to him or them, or to hold
      money or other property in which he or they have an interest, or to hold evidences
      or securities for the same.  Upon the filing of such amended petition the case shall be transferred to the equity
      docket and summons issued thereon.  In such supplemental proceeding or in a separate suit in equity against such parties
      (at his option) the plaintiff may have discovery and disclosure from the judgment
      creditor and his debtor or bailee, and may have any property discovered, or a sufficiency
      thereof, subjected to the satisfaction of the judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.382. Answer to be verified; court may enforce discoveries
