title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.382. Answer to be verified; court may enforce discoveries
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.382. Answer to be verified; court may enforce discoveries (2023)
content:
The answer of each defendant shall be verified by his oath, and not by that of an
   agent or attorney, and the court shall, if necessary, enforce full and explicit discoveries
   in such answers by process of contempt.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.440. Property levied on but unsold; writ authorizing and commanding sale; form of; proceedings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.440. Property levied on but unsold; writ authorizing and commanding sale; form of; proceedings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.440. Property levied on but unsold; writ authorizing and commanding sale; form of; proceedings (2023)
content:
(1)  When the sheriff or other officer makes a return on an execution that the estate
      levied on, or any part thereof, remains in his hands unsold, a writ authorizing and
      commanding the sheriff to sell the property may issue.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.384. Court may compel surrender of property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.384. Court may compel surrender of property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.384. Court may compel surrender of property (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.430. Judgments in equity; how enforced; issuance and return of execution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.430. Judgments in equity; how enforced; issuance and return of execution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.430. Judgments in equity; how enforced; issuance and return of execution (2023)
content:
A final order or judgment in equity for money, land or other specific thing may be
   enforced by any appropriate writ of execution, allowable on a judgment at law, or
   by the ancient practice of courts of chancery.  The writ shall issue and be returnable as other writs of execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.420. Choses in action; petition for discovery; sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.420. Choses in action; petition for discovery; sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.420. Choses in action; petition for discovery; sale (2023)
content:
Where choses in action are brought into court by virtue of a petition for discovery
   of assets instituted against an insolvent debtor, the court may order their sale upon
   the same terms as are prescribed for the sale of other personal property.  The court shall make all needful orders for the transfer of title to the purchaser.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.450. Replevy of judgment allowed before execution issues; form of bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.450. Replevy of judgment allowed before execution issues; form of bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.450. Replevy of judgment allowed before execution issues; form of bond (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person against whom a judgment for money is rendered, except as provided
      inKRS 426.470, may, if an execution thereon has not been placed in the hands of a collecting officer,
      replevy the judgment for three months before the circuit court clerk by giving bond
      with good surety to be approved by the officer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.480. Agreement to waive right to replevy
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.480. Agreement to waive right to replevy
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.480. Agreement to waive right to replevy (2023)
content:
An agreement to waive the right to replevy, or any other legal agreement in relation
   to any judgment, if entered on the record among the orders of court, shall be specifically
   enforced.  The proper endorsement shall be made on the execution by the clerk or judge.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.510. Motions authorized by KRS 426.010. to 426.500. or 426.990; limitation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.510. Motions authorized by KRS 426.010. to 426.500. or 426.990; limitation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.510. Motions authorized by KRS 426.010. to 426.500. or 426.990; limitation (2023)
content: Any motion authorized byKRS 426.010to426.500or426.990shall be commenced within two (2) years after the cause of the motion accrues.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.470. Judgments and executions that may not be replevied
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.470. Judgments and executions that may not be replevied
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.470. Judgments and executions that may not be replevied (2023)
content:
A judgment to enforce a lien, or against any collecting officer, attorney at law or
   agent for a delinquency or default in executing or fulfilling his duties, or of a
   surety against his principal, or upon a debt due by obligation having the force of
   a judgment, or for specific property or for the property or its value, shall not be
   replevied.  An execution on a sale, replevin or forthcoming bond shall not be replevied.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.490. Sale bond; where no replevin and sale made on three months' time; form
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.490. Sale bond; where no replevin and sale made on three months' time; form
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.490. Sale bond; where no replevin and sale made on three months' time; form (2023)
content:
(1)  If the right to replevy exists and is not exercised, sales under execution shall
      be on a credit of three (3) months, upon the purchaser giving bond with good surety
      to the plaintiff in execution for the payment of the sale money, bearing interest
      from date.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.460. Executions that may be replevied; form of bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.460. Executions that may be replevied; form of bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.460. Executions that may be replevied; form of bond (2023)
content:
(1)  Any execution on a judgment, which could be replevied before the execution issued,
      may be replevied for three (3) months at any time before a sale of property under
      the same, by the defendant giving to the officer a bond with good surety payable to
      the plaintiff, for the amount thereof including interest, costs, and half commission
      up to that time.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.500. Surplus proceeds of sale; disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.500. Surplus proceeds of sale; disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.500. Surplus proceeds of sale; disposition (2023)
content:
(1)  If the property sold on credit sells for more than necessary to satisfy the execution,
      costs and commission, the officer making the sale shall take a bond payable to the
      defendant, the owner of the property, but otherwise similar to and having like force
      and effect as that provided for inKRS 426.490, for the excess.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.520. Appraisal of real property before judicial sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.520. Appraisal of real property before judicial sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.520. Appraisal of real property before judicial sale (2023)
content:
(1)  Before any real property is to be sold under an order or judgment of a court,
      other than an execution, the commissioner or other officer selling the property shall
      have it appraised, under oath, by two (2) disinterested, intelligent housekeepers
      of the county, who may be sworn by the officer.  If they disagree, the officer shall act as umpire.  If only a part of a tract of land is sold, the part sold shall, after the sale,
      be revalued in like manner.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.522. Public, judicial sale of real or personal property; when conducted by licensed auctioneer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.522. Public, judicial sale of real or personal property; when conducted by licensed auctioneer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.522. Public, judicial sale of real or personal property; when conducted by licensed auctioneer (2023)
content:
(1)  If real or personal property is sold at public sale under any order or decree
      of any court in this state, then the court under whose jurisdiction the sale is to
      be made may secure the services of an auctioneer licensed in this state to conduct
      the public sale, fix the auctioneer's fee, and order the fee to be paid out of the
      proceeds of the sale.  The fee:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.530. Right of redemption; manner of redeeming; purchaser to receive writ of possession and deed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.530. Right of redemption; manner of redeeming; purchaser to receive writ of possession and deed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.530. Right of redemption; manner of redeeming; purchaser to receive writ of possession and deed (2023)
content:
(1)  If real property sold in pursuance of a judgment or order of a court, other than
      an execution, does not bring two-thirds (2/3) of its appraised value, the defendant and his or her representatives may redeem
      it within six (6) months from the day of sale, by paying the original purchase money
      and ten percent (10%) per annum interest thereon, and any reasonable costs incurred
      by the purchaser after the sale for maintenance or repair of the property, including
      but not limited to utility expenses, insurance, association fees, taxes, and the costs
      to conform the property to the minimum standards of local nuisance code provisions
      and other local ordinances as authorized inKRS 65.8801to65.8839.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.570. Conveyances to be made by commissioner; deed of partition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.570. Conveyances to be made by commissioner; deed of partition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.570. Conveyances to be made by commissioner; deed of partition (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise specially ordered by the court, the master commissioner of a Circuit
   Court shall make all conveyances of real property that are authorized by law to be
   made by a commissioner of the Circuit Court.  In the partition of land, there shall be but one (1) deed, unless otherwise ordered
   by the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.525. Mortgage foreclosure forbidden; rights of mortgagee after default
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.525. Mortgage foreclosure forbidden; rights of mortgagee after default
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.525. Mortgage foreclosure forbidden; rights of mortgagee after default (2023)
content:
Foreclosure of a mortgage is forbidden;  provided, however, that this section shall
   not preclude a mortgagee after default from taking possession of property subject
   to the mortgage which has been abandoned by the mortgagor, for the purpose of preserving
   and maintaining the same, harvesting crops, or letting the same, all to the account
   of the mortgagor;  and any reasonable expenses incident thereto including taxes and
   insurance shall be added to the principal of the mortgage, and secured by it.  For the purpose of this section, property shall be deemed to have been abandoned
   when the mortgagor has moved from the property and when by the nature of the property
   in question when further neglect or failure to attend will decrease its value.  Any right a mortgagee acquires in a tenant's interest in crops raised on shares
   is inferior to any prior existing lien of the landlord on the tenant's interest.  Nothing in this section shall be construed as conflicting with the provisions ofKRS 383.110or426.205.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.551. Issual of execution after death of plaintiff; who treated as plaintiff
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.551. Issual of execution after death of plaintiff; who treated as plaintiff
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.551. Issual of execution after death of plaintiff; who treated as plaintiff (2023)
content:
(1)  The death of a party, after recovering a judgment, shall not prevent the issuing
      of an execution afterward;  but

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.550. Death of party after sale under court order; revivor not necessary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.550. Death of party after sale under court order; revivor not necessary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.550. Death of party after sale under court order; revivor not necessary (2023)
content:
If, by the judgment of any court of this state, real property is sold and any party
   to the action dies after the sale is confirmed, or, if the court orders any conveyance
   of real property by a commissioner and a party to the proceedings dies before the
   conveyance is perfected, it shall not be necessary on that account to revive the action,
   but the sale or conveyance when perfected shall pass title to the same extent as if
   all the parties were living.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.540. Redemption right may be sold; rights of purchaser and debtor; report of sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.540. Redemption right may be sold; rights of purchaser and debtor; report of sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.540. Redemption right may be sold; rights of purchaser and debtor; report of sale (2023)
content:
If the proceeds of sale fail to satisfy the judgment, the right of redemption provided
   for inKRS 426.530may be sold to satisfy the residue of the judgment.  The right of redemption shall also be liable to sale under execution.  The land shall be subject to redemption from both purchasers for one (1) year from
   the first sale.  The purchaser of the right of redemption may, before the end of a year from the
   first sale, pay the prior purchaser his purchase money and interest as provided inKRS 426.530, and shall then be entitled to the land, subject to the rights of possession and
   redemption held by the defendant in the execution.  A sale made in pursuance of any such judgment or order shall be reported to the
   court by the commissioner or officer who made the sale, and the report shall state
   at what sum the property sold was appraised.  If the report is not excepted to, the sale may be confirmed, but if the land is
   redeemed the confirmation shall thereafter be null and void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.552. Affidavit and other documents required before issuance of execution; when bond required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.552. Affidavit and other documents required before issuance of execution; when bond required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.552. Affidavit and other documents required before issuance of execution; when bond required (2023)
content:
The clerk, before making the indorsements required by paragraph (d) of subsection
   (1) ofKRS 426.551, shall require the person claiming right thereto to file an affidavit showing his
   right.  If the affiant state that he is a personal representative or successor of a decedent,
   the clerk shall also require him to file a copy, properly certified, of his appointment
   as such by a competent tribunal in the United States;  and, unless the appointment
   was made in Kentucky, the clerk shall also require of him a covenant, with good surety,
   that he will dispose, according to law, of any property which he may receive upon
   the execution.  If the affiant state that he is a devisee of a decedent, the clerk shall require
   him to file a copy of the will, certified by a county clerk in this state in which
   the will or a copy is recorded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.554. Court may quash execution improperly issued
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.554. Court may quash execution improperly issued
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.554. Court may quash execution improperly issued (2023)
content:
The court may, after reasonable notice, quash an execution on the ground that the
   representative or successor of a deceased plaintiff is not properly stated in the
   indorsement on the execution.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.553. Execution against surviving defendant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.553. Execution against surviving defendant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.553. Execution against surviving defendant (2023)
content:
The death of a defendant shall not prevent the issuing of an execution against a surviving
   defendant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.555. Procedure in case of death of execution defendant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.555. Procedure in case of death of execution defendant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.555. Procedure in case of death of execution defendant (2023)
content:
(1)  The death of a defendant after a sale of his property under execution shall not
      prevent a conveyance of the property.  It shall be conveyed in the same manner and with the same effect as if he were living.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.560. Newspaper advertisement required in execution and judicial sales
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.560. Newspaper advertisement required in execution and judicial sales
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.560. Newspaper advertisement required in execution and judicial sales (2023)
content:
In addition to the notices now required by statute to be posted, all public sales
   of any kind of property sold under execution, judgment or decree, shall, unless otherwise
   agreed upon by the parties, be advertised by publication pursuant to KRS Chapter 424.  The advertisement shall state the time, place and terms of sale and describe the
   property to be sold.  The newspaper advertisement shall not be necessary where the appraised value of
   the property to be sold is less than one hundred dollars ($100).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.571. When commissioner may convey real property; death of party after sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.571. When commissioner may convey real property; death of party after sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.571. When commissioner may convey real property; death of party after sale (2023)
content: (1)  Real property may be conveyed by a commissioner appointed by the court:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.572. Requisites of commissioner's deed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.572. Requisites of commissioner's deed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.572. Requisites of commissioner's deed (2023)
content:
The deed of the commissioner shall refer to the judgment, orders and proceedings,
   authorizing the conveyance, so that the same may be readily found.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.574. Title passed by deed made pursuant to order of sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.574. Title passed by deed made pursuant to order of sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.574. Title passed by deed made pursuant to order of sale (2023)
content:
A conveyance made in pursuance of a sale ordered by the court shall pass to the grantee
   the title of all the parties to the action or proceeding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.575. Court to examine and approve deed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.575. Court to examine and approve deed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.575. Court to examine and approve deed (2023)
content:
A conveyance by a commissioner shall not pass any right, until it has been examined
   and approved by the court;  which approval shall be indorsed on the conveyance, and
   recorded with it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.576. Commissioner to sign; names of parties to be stated
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.576. Commissioner to sign; names of parties to be stated
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.576. Commissioner to sign; names of parties to be stated (2023)
content:
It shall be necessary for the conveyance to be signed by the commissioner only, without
   affixing the names of the parties whose title is conveyed;  but the names of such
   parties shall be recited in the conveyance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.590. Failure to deliver property on forthcoming bond; return of officer; liability of surety; execution for balance due
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.590. Failure to deliver property on forthcoming bond; return of officer; liability of surety; execution for balance due
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.590. Failure to deliver property on forthcoming bond; return of officer; liability of surety; execution for balance due (2023)
content:
(1)  If the defendant in execution fails to pay or replevy the amount of the execution,
      and fails to deliver the property specified in the forthcoming bond or other property
      in its place sufficient to satisfy the execution and all costs and commissions, the
      officer shall return the execution and bond to the office where it was issued and
      endorse on the execution the levy, the giving of the bond, the particular property
      which is not forthcoming and all other facts.  The surety on the forthcoming bond shall be liable only for the value of the property
      specified in the bond which is not forthcoming, with interest thereon from the date
      of the bond and the accruing costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.600. Liability of officer for failure to return forthcoming bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.600. Liability of officer for failure to return forthcoming bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.600. Liability of officer for failure to return forthcoming bond (2023)
content:
Any officer taking a forthcoming bond who fails to return it to the proper office
   for twenty (20) days after the failure to comply on the part of the defendant in execution
   shall, with his sureties, be liable to the plaintiff for the amount of the execution,
   costs and commission, and for an additional twenty percent (20%) thereon, to be recovered
   by action or motion against any one (1) or more of them or their representatives.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.580. Forthcoming bond for personalty levied on; form; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.580. Forthcoming bond for personalty levied on; form; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.580. Forthcoming bond for personalty levied on; form; effect (2023)
content:
(1)  The owner of personal property taken in execution may give to the levying officer
      a bond, with good surety, to have the property forthcoming at the time and place of
      sale, which shall specify each article of property and its value.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.577. Where deed to be recorded
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.577. Where deed to be recorded
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.577. Where deed to be recorded (2023)
content:
The conveyance shall be recorded where, by law it should have been recorded, had it
   been made by the parties whose title is conveyed by it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.573. Title passed by deed made pursuant to judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.573. Title passed by deed made pursuant to judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.573. Title passed by deed made pursuant to judgment (2023)
content:
A conveyance made in pursuance of a judgment shall pass to the grantee the title of
   the parties ordered to convey the land.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.610. Bonds having the effect of a judgment; general provisions for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.610. Bonds having the effect of a judgment; general provisions for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.610. Bonds having the effect of a judgment; general provisions for (2023)
content:
(1)  Every bond taken on the sale of property under an order of judgment in chancery
      or on the sale of property under execution, and every replevin and forthcoming bond,
      shall be signed by the principal and surety, and attested by the person taking the
      bond, or by someone in his presence.  A bond so taken shall be returned to the proper office, with a report of the acts
      of the person taking it, and, if taken under an execution, the execution shall be
      returned with the bond.  Every such bond shall have the force and effect of a judgment, and if not paid at
      maturity an execution may issue, which shall be endorsed that no surety of any kind
      is to be taken.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.640. Bond required for suspension of sale of personal property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.640. Bond required for suspension of sale of personal property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.640. Bond required for suspension of sale of personal property (2023)
content:
The sale of personal property upon which an execution is levied shall be suspended
   at the instance of any person, other than the defendant in the execution, claiming
   the property, who shall execute, with one (1) or more sureties sufficient for double
   its value, a bond to the plaintiff in the execution, to the effect that, if it shall
   be adjudged that the property or any part of it is subject to the execution, he will
   pay to the plaintiff the value of the property so subject, and ten percent (10%) thereon,
   not exceeding the amount due on the execution, and ten percent (10%) thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.615. Execution plaintiff may substitute for officer in action for recovery of property taken under execution or rent attachment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.615. Execution plaintiff may substitute for officer in action for recovery of property taken under execution or rent attachment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.615. Execution plaintiff may substitute for officer in action for recovery of property taken under execution or rent attachment (2023)
content:
In an action against a sheriff or other officer for the recovery of property taken
   under an execution or rent attachment the court may, upon the application of the defendant
   and of the party in whose favor the execution or rent attachment is issued, permit
   the latter to be substituted as the defendant, security for the costs being given.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.680. Procedure for levy of execution on jointly owned property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.680. Procedure for levy of execution on jointly owned property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.680. Procedure for levy of execution on jointly owned property (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.690. Procedure in action to enforce lien where other liens exist against real property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.690. Procedure in action to enforce lien where other liens exist against real property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.690. Procedure in action to enforce lien where other liens exist against real property (2023)
content:
The plaintiff in an action to enforce a lien on real property shall state in his petition
   the liens, if any, which are held thereon by others, and make the holders defendants;
   and no sale of the property shall be ordered by the court prejudicial to the rights
   of the holders of any of the liens, and when it appears from the petition or otherwise,
   that several debts are secured by one (1) lien, or by liens of equal rank, and they
   are all due at the commencement of the action, or become so before judgment, the court
   shall order the sale for the pro rata satisfaction of all of them, but if, in such
   case, the debts be owned by different persons and be not all due, the court shall
   not order a sale of the property until they all mature.   If all such liens be held by the same party, the court may order a sale of enough
   of the property to pay the debts then due, unless it appear that it is not susceptible
   of advantageous division, or that, for some other reason, the sale would cause a sacrifice
   thereof, or seriously prejudice the interests of the defendants, but the holder of
   a prior lien may enforce the same when the debt thereby secured is due, notwithstanding
   the existence of inferior liens, whether the debts secured thereby are due or not;
   and the holder of an inferior lien, when the debt thereby secured is due, may enforce
   the same by a sale of land subject to a prior lien or liens thereon, where the debt
   or debts secured thereby are not yet due.  Provided, that the provisions of this section shall not apply to any liens now of
   record.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.655. Trial of motion for judgment on bond; judgment; execution
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.655. Trial of motion for judgment on bond; judgment; execution
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.655. Trial of motion for judgment on bond; judgment; execution (2023)
content:
The party to whom the bond is executed may move the court to which it is returned
   for a judgment thereon against all or any of the obligors or their representatives,
   having given to them ten days' notice of the motion.  The court shall direct a jury to be impaneled, and may cause such issues to be tried
   as it may prescribe, and direct which party shall be considered plaintiff in the issues.  If the property, or any part of it, be found subject to the execution, judgment
   shall be rendered in favor of the plaintiff therein for the value of the property
   so subject and ten percent thereon, not exceeding the amount due on the execution
   and ten percent thereon.  An execution may be issued upon the judgment forthwith, on which the same indorsement
   shall be made as on the execution in virtue of which the property had been seized.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.645. Property to be appraised for purpose of taking bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.645. Property to be appraised for purpose of taking bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.645. Property to be appraised for purpose of taking bond (2023)
content:
For the purpose of taking the bond mentioned inKRS 426.640, the officer shall select three (3) disinterested housekeepers, and administer to
   them an oath to make a fair appraisement of each article of the property;  whose appraisement,
   in writing, shall be recited in the bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.665. Bond not to discharge levy; motion to discharge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.665. Bond not to discharge levy; motion to discharge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.665. Bond not to discharge levy; motion to discharge (2023)
content:
The giving of the bond mentioned inKRS 426.640shall not discharge the levy of the execution upon the property claimed.  But the officer may leave it, subject to the lien of the levy, with the person in
   whose possession it was found, pending the proceeding on the bond;  and may, in the
   meantime, proceed with the execution against any other property of the defendant.  The obligor in such bond may, however, on ten (10) days' notice to the plaintiff
   in the execution, move the court to which the bond is returned to discharge the same
   and release the levy under the execution.  The provisions ofKRS 426.655and426.660shall, so far as applicable, govern the proceedings upon such motion.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.660. Trial of objection to appraisement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.660. Trial of objection to appraisement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.660. Trial of objection to appraisement (2023)
content:
Upon the trial of the motion, either party may object that the property was not fairly
   appraised;  and, thereupon, the jury trying the facts shall hear evidence respecting,
   and find, the value of the property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.695. Sale of indivisible personal property; payment of excess; proceeds
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.695. Sale of indivisible personal property; payment of excess; proceeds
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.695. Sale of indivisible personal property; payment of excess; proceeds (2023)
content:
If it be necessary to sell, for payment of debt, one or more parcels of personal property
   which, in the opinion of the officer making the sale, can not be divided without materially
   impairing the value thereof, he shall sell the whole property, though it bring more
   than the sum to be raised;  but he shall have no commission on the excess.  The excess shall be paid to the defendant, or the bond therefor shall be payable
   to him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.675. Certain jury trials of right of property abolished
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.675. Certain jury trials of right of property abolished
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.675. Certain jury trials of right of property abolished (2023)
content:
Trials by juries summoned by sheriffs or other officers, of the right of property
   taken by them under execution or rent attachment, are abolished.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.685. Provisions governing sales by court order of indivisible real property
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.685. Provisions governing sales by court order of indivisible real property
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.685. Provisions governing sales by court order of indivisible real property (2023)
content:
(1)  Before ordering a sale of real property for the payment of debt, the court must
      be satisfied by the pleadings, by an agreement of the parties, by affidavits filed,
      or by a report of a commissioner or commissioners, whether or not the property can
      be divided without materially impairing its value, and may cause it to be divided,
      with suitable avenues, streets, lanes or alleys, or without any of them.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.705. Bond required of purchaser
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.705. Bond required of purchaser
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.705. Bond required of purchaser (2023)
content:
(1)  The purchaser of property sold under an order of court shall give bond for the
      price, with good surety, approved by the officer making the sale, payable to him or
      to the person entitled to receive the money, as the court may direct;  or, if the
      court make no order on the subject, they shall be made payable to the officer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.700. Time, place and terms of sale; notice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.700. Time, place and terms of sale; notice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.700. Time, place and terms of sale; notice (2023)
content:
Every sale made under an order of court must be public, either for cash or upon reasonable
   credits to be fixed by the court;  and shall be made after such notice of the time,
   place and terms of sale as the order may direct;  and, unless the order direct otherwise,
   shall be made at the door of the courthouse of the county in which the property, or
   the greater part thereof, may be situated;  and the notice of sale must state for
   what sum of money it is to be made.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.720. Final judgment to act as lien on realty; judgment creditor's notice requirements; methods of service; expiration of judgment lien
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.720. Final judgment to act as lien on realty; judgment creditor's notice requirements; methods of service; expiration of judgment lien

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.005. Definitions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.005. Definitions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.005. Definitions (2023)
content: As used in this chapter:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.715. Lien on realty as security for purchase money; release
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.715. Lien on realty as security for purchase money; release
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.715. Lien on realty as security for purchase money; release (2023)
content:
A lien shall exist on real property sold under an order of court, as security for
   the purchase money;  and, upon payment thereof the clerk shall release the lien on
   the margin of the record of the deed in the office of the county clerk, or at the
   option of the county clerk, in a marginal entry record kept for the same purpose.  Each entry in the marginal entry record shall be linked to its respective referenced
   instrument in the indexing system for the referenced instrument.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.010. Exempt personal property, health savings funds, and disposable earnings of individual debtors
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.010. Exempt personal property, health savings funds, and disposable earnings of individual debtors
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.010. Exempt personal property, health savings funds, and disposable earnings of individual debtors (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.020. Appraisement of defendant's property; selection by defendant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.020. Appraisement of defendant's property; selection by defendant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.020. Appraisement of defendant's property; selection by defendant (2023)
content:
The officer making the levy shall, prior to selling the defendant's property, ascertain
   the value of the property by an appraisal made by two (2) discreet, disinterested
   persons, one (1) appointed by the officer and one appointed by the defendant.  The defendant may select which items of his property he chooses to retain so long
   as the total value of the property retained does not exceed the value of the exemptions
   set out in this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments›KY REV ST 426.710. Purchaser of personal property entitled to it
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 426. Enforcement of Judgments › KY REV ST 426.710. Purchaser of personal property entitled to it
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 426.710. Purchaser of personal property entitled to it (2023)
content:
The purchaser of personal property sold under an order of court shall be entitled
   to it, upon complying with the terms of sale.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.030. Debtor's tools exempt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.030. Debtor's tools exempt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.030. Debtor's tools exempt (2023)
content:
The tools, not exceeding three hundred dollars ($300) in value, of any individual
   debtor necessary in his trade are exempt from levy under execution, attachment, distress
   for rent or fee-bill.  One (1) motor vehicle not exceeding two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) in
   value and its necessary accessories, including one (1) spare tire, of a mechanic or
   other skilled artisan primarily engaged in the replacement, repair, or emergency servicing
   of essential mechanical, electrical or other equipment in general use, is exempt from
   execution, attachment, garnishment, distress warrant or fee-bill.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.080. Valuation and allotment of homestead exemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.080. Valuation and allotment of homestead exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.080. Valuation and allotment of homestead exemption (2023)
content:
(1)  No sale under execution, attachment or judgment of property occupied as a homestead
      shall be had until the officer executing the writ or judgment has the part thereof
      selected by the defendant as his homestead exemption, not to exceed five thousand
      dollars ($5,000) in value, valued under oath and set apart to him by two (2) disinterested
      housekeepers of the county.  These appraisers shall be selected by the court or officer, and if they disagree
      the officer making the sale shall act as umpire.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.070. Right of spouse and children to homestead
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.070. Right of spouse and children to homestead
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.070. Right of spouse and children to homestead (2023)
content:
(1)  The homestead shall be for the use of the widow as long as she occupies it, and
      the unmarried infant children of the husband are entitled to a joint occupancy with
      her until the youngest unmarried child arrives at full age.  The termination of the widow's occupancy shall not affect the rights of the children.  The land may be sold, subject to the right of the widow and children, if a sale
      is necessary to pay the debts of the husband.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.045. Exemptions not applicable to claims for child support
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.045. Exemptions not applicable to claims for child support
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.045. Exemptions not applicable to claims for child support (2023)
content:
The exemptions provided inKRS 342.180andKRS 427.010to427.040shall not apply for executions, attachments, or garnishments, issued for the collection
   of maintenance of minor children.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.040. Professional libraries and vehicle exempt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.040. Professional libraries and vehicle exempt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.040. Professional libraries and vehicle exempt (2023)
content:
The professional library, office equipment, instruments and furnishings of a minister,
   attorney, physician, surgeon, chiropractor, veterinarian, or dentist, necessary in
   the practice of such profession, and not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000) in
   value shall be exempt from execution, attachment, garnishment, distress warrant or
   fee-bill.  In addition to the above exemption one (1) motor vehicle not exceeding two thousand
   five hundred dollars ($2,500) in value with necessary accessories, including one (1)
   spare tire shall be exempted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.050. Out-of-state law applicable when wages earned and payable out-of-state; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.050. Out-of-state law applicable when wages earned and payable out-of-state; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.050. Out-of-state law applicable when wages earned and payable out-of-state; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  The law of the state wherein wages are earned and payable relating to exemptions
      shall apply to all garnishments served in the State of Kentucky, except that Kentucky
      law shall exclusively apply:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.060. Homestead and burial plot exemptions; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.060. Homestead and burial plot exemptions; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.060. Homestead and burial plot exemptions; exceptions (2023)
content:
In addition to any exemption of personal property, an individual debtor's aggregate
   interest, not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000) in value, in real or personal
   property that such debtor or a dependent of such debtor uses as a permanent residence
   in this state, or in a burial plot for such debtor or a dependent of such debtor is
   exempt from sale under execution, attachment or judgment, except to foreclose a mortgage
   given by the owner of a homestead or for purchase money due thereon.  This exemption shall not apply if the debt or liability existed prior to the purchase
   of the property or the erection of the improvements thereon.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.100. Waiver of homestead exemption; continuance after death
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.100. Waiver of homestead exemption; continuance after death
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.100. Waiver of homestead exemption; continuance after death (2023)
content:
No mortgage, release or waiver of an exemption granted byKRS 427.060shall be valid unless it is in writing, subscribed by the defendant and his spouse,
   and acknowledged and recorded in the same manner as conveyances of real estate.  The exemption in favor of an execution debtor or one against whom judgment has been
   rendered shall continue after the debtor's death for the benefit of his surviving
   spouse and children, but shall be estimated in allotting dower or curtesy.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.090. Payment of money in lieu of homestead exemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.090. Payment of money in lieu of homestead exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.090. Payment of money in lieu of homestead exemption (2023)
content:
If the defendant in the execution, attachment or other action owns property levied
   on or sought to be subjected to the payment of any debt or liability, which, in the
   opinion of the appraisers, is of greater value than five thousand dollars ($5,000)
   and not divisible without great diminution in value, the property shall be sold and
   five thousand dollars ($5,000) of the money arising from the sale paid to the defendant
   to enable him to purchase another homestead.  The property shall not be sold for less than five thousand dollars ($5,000).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.125. Police and firefighters' pension fund in cities of fourth class; exempt from process in some cases
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.125. Police and firefighters' pension fund in cities of fourth class; exempt from process in some cases
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.125. Police and firefighters' pension fund in cities of fourth class; exempt from process in some cases (2023)
content:
No portion of a pension fund created underKRS 95.761to95.784shall, before or after its order for distribution by the board of trustees to the
   persons entitled thereto, be held, seized, taken, subjected to or detained or levied
   upon by virtue of any attachments, execution, injunction, writ, interlocutory, or
   other order, or decree, or any process or proceeding whatever issued out of or by
   any court of this state for the payment or satisfaction, in whole or in part, of any
   debt, damage, claim, demand, or judgment against the beneficiary of said fund, except
   for court or administratively ordered child support, or owed or to-be-owed child support,
   but said fund shall be held and distributed for the purpose ofKRS 95.761to95.784, and for no other purpose whatever.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.150. Property totally or partially exempt
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.150. Property totally or partially exempt
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.150. Property totally or partially exempt (2023)
content:
(1)  To the extent reasonably necessary for the support of an individual and his dependents
      in addition to property totally exempt under subsection (2) of this section, that
      individual shall be entitled to exemption of money or property received and rights
      to receive money or property for alimony, support, or separate maintenance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.140. Employee may not be discharged for garnishment for one (1) indebtedness
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.140. Employee may not be discharged for garnishment for one (1) indebtedness
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.140. Employee may not be discharged for garnishment for one (1) indebtedness (2023)
content:
No employer may discharge any employee by reason of the fact that his earnings have
   been subjected to garnishment for any one (1) indebtedness.

content:
(1)  Any money or other benefit to be paid or rendered by any assessment or cooperative
      life or casualty insurance company is exempt from execution or other process to subject
      such money or other benefit to the payment of any debt or liability of a policyholder.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.130. Salaries of public officials and employees and sums due from governmental agencies are subject to attachment or garnishment; service of process (2023)
content:
(1)  Salaries or sums due state, county, city and school board officers and employees
      shall be subject to attachment or garnishment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.180. Grain storage receipt or scale ticket as prima facie claim of right to possession
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.180. Grain storage receipt or scale ticket as prima facie claim of right to possession
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.180. Grain storage receipt or scale ticket as prima facie claim of right to possession (2023)
content:
A claimant's production to a bankruptcy court of a grain storage receipt or scale
   ticket as evidence of ownership of a quantity of grain held by the trustee shall be
   sufficient to establish a prima facie claim of right to possession in such claimant
   of the quantity, quality, and type of grain specified in such document.  In any case where a claimant has placed the original of such document on deposit
   with any party as collateral for a loan, an affidavit from such party verifying ownership
   of such receipt or scale ticket by the claimant shall be sufficient to establish a
   prima facie claim of right to possession in such claimant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.170. Federal bankruptcy code exemptions applicable in Kentucky
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.170. Federal bankruptcy code exemptions applicable in Kentucky
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.170. Federal bankruptcy code exemptions applicable in Kentucky (2023)
content:
Solely for the purpose of applying the provisions of11 U.S.C. sec.  522(b)(2)in a federal bankruptcy proceeding and only to the extent otherwise allowed by applicable
   federal law, an individual debtor domiciled in this state is authorized to exempt
   from property of said debtor's bankruptcy estate the property specified under11 U.S.C.  sec. 522(d).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.160. Additional general exemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions › Chapter 427. Exemptions › KY REV ST 427.160. Additional general exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.160. Additional general exemption (2023)
content:
Solely for the purpose of applying the provisions of11 U.S.C. sec.  522(b)(3)(A)in a federal bankruptcy proceeding, in addition to other exemptions provided in this
   chapter and only to the extent otherwise allowed by applicable federal law, every
   debtor shall have a general exemption not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000)
   in value to be applied toward any property, real or personal, tangible or intangible
   in his estate when he or she has filed for bankruptcy under the provisions of TheBankruptcy Code of 1978, 92Stat. 2549 (1978),Public Law 95-598, as amended.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XXXIX. Provisional Remedies, Enforcement of Judgments, and Exemptions›Chapter 427. Exemptions›KY REV ST 427.990. Penalty

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 427.990. Penalty (2023)
content:
Whoever willfully violatesKRS 427.140shall be fined not more than $1,000, or imprisoned not more than one (1) year, or
   both.

content:

   and operating costs, shall be paid by the defendant.  As used in this section, “alcohol monitoring device” means an electronic device that:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.007. Arrest powers of peace officers assisting in another county; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.007. Arrest powers of peace officers assisting in another county; exception (2023)
content:
(1)  A peace officer certified pursuant toKRS 15.380to15.404, who is directly employed as a police officer by a Kentucky city, county, or urban-county
      government and whose department meets the requirements ofKRS 15.440and a sheriff, or deputy sheriff who has been certified pursuant toKRS 15.380to15.404, who is officially requested by a law enforcement agency in another county in Kentucky
      to assist in any matter within the jurisdiction of the requesting agency shall possess,
      while responding to and for the duration of the matter for which the request was made,
      the same powers of arrest in the requesting county as he possesses in the county in
      which he is a police officer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.067. Participation in global positioning monitoring system program as condition of pretrial release
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.067. Participation in global positioning monitoring system program as condition of pretrial release
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.067. Participation in global positioning monitoring system program as condition of pretrial release (2023)
content:
When considering the pretrial release of a person whose pretrial risk assessment indicates

   may order as a condition of pretrial release that the person participate in a global
   positioning monitoring system program under the same terms and conditions provided
   inKRS 431.517during all or part of the person's period of pretrial release.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.045. Pursuit in effecting arrest (2023)
content:
A peace officer in actual pursuit may continue such pursuit across corporate or county
   lines for the purpose of making an arrest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.055. Pursuit to recapture escapee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.055. Pursuit to recapture escapee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.055. Pursuit to recapture escapee (2023)
content:
If a person lawfully arrested escapes or is rescued, the person from whose custody
   he escaped or was rescued may immediately pursue and retake him in any part of the
   Commonwealth and may be joined in the pursuit and recapture by peace officers in the
   immediate area or vicinity.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.063. Human trafficking victim not to be incarcerated pending trial; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.063. Human trafficking victim not to be incarcerated pending trial; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.063. Human trafficking victim not to be incarcerated pending trial; exceptions (2023)
content:
A victim of human trafficking shall not be held in a detention center, jail, or other
   secure facility pending trial for an offense arising from the human trafficking situation,
   except where the incarceration is found to be the least restrictive alternative to
   securing the appearance of that person before the court or the release of the person
   under any other reasonable condition would be a clear threat to public safety.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.008. Insurance coverage for assistance rendered under KRS § 431.007
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.008. Insurance coverage for assistance rendered under KRS § 431.007
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.008. Insurance coverage for assistance rendered under KRS § 431.007 (2023)
content:
When a peace officer specified inKRS 431.007is lawfully conducting an assistance operation underKRS 431.007, any insurance relative to the performance of his duties, including, but not limited
   to, workers' compensation, health, liability, and motor vehicle insurance, maintained
   by the peace officer or the peace officer's employer, shall remain in force.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.017. Appearance bond of prosecuting witness
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.017. Appearance bond of prosecuting witness
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.017. Appearance bond of prosecuting witness (2023)
content:
A judge, trial commissioner, or other officer issuing an arrest warrant based upon
   the testimony or allegations of a prosecuting witness may require the witness to post
   a bond in favor of the Commonwealth to secure the attendance of that witness in court
   in all matters relating to that particular arrest warrant.  The amount of the bond shall be twenty-five dollars ($25).  In the event that the prosecuting witness fails to appear and does not present valid
   reason therefor, the trial court shall order the forfeiture of the bond.  This section shall not apply to any appeal or postconviction proceeding.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.021. Guaranteed arrest bond certificate of surety company to be accepted in lieu of cash bail in traffic cases

      same forfeiture and enforcement provisions as a bail bond or cash bail, but is not
      subject toRules 4.30and4.34 of the Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure.  However:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.105. State to receive fines and forfeitures for certain height, width, length, and weight violations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.105. State to receive fines and forfeitures for certain height, width, length, and weight violations (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any other statutory provisions to the contrary, all fines and forfeitures
   recovered in any court as a result of a conviction for the violation of any of the
   provisions ofKRS 189.221,189.222(1), or189.270, which violation occurred on a state-maintained highway and arrest was made by any
   peace officer other than a member of the Department of Kentucky State Police, Department
   of Highways, or Department of Vehicle Regulation, shall inure to the benefit of the
   state, shall be paid to the State Treasurer for the use and benefit of the Department
   of Highways, and no part shall be returned to the local governmental units from which
   they were sent.  These fines and forfeitures shall be paid into the State Treasury by the court collecting
   same and within thirty (30) days after imposition and collection.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.076. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.076. content:
(1)  (a) On or after July 15, 2020, if a court enters an order of acquittal of criminal
         charges against a person, or enters an order dismissing with prejudice all criminal
         charges in a case against a person and not in exchange for a guilty plea to another
         charge, the court shall order the record expunged upon the expiration of thirty (30)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.079. title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments › KY REV ST 431.079. Petition or application seeking expungement to include certification of eligibility for expungement from Department of Kentucky State Police and Administrative Office of the Courts; administrative regulations; construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 431.079. Petition or application seeking expungement to include certification of eligibility for expungement from Department of Kentucky State Police and Administrative Office of the Courts; administrative regulations; construction (2023)
content:
(1)  Every petition or application filed seeking expungement of a conviction shall
      include a certification of eligibility for expungement.  The Department of Kentucky State Police and the Administrative Office of the Courts
      shall certify that the agencies have conducted a criminal background check on the
      petitioner and whether or not the petitioner is eligible to have the requested record
      expunged.  The Department of Kentucky State Police shall promulgate administrative regulations
      to implement this section, in consultation with the Administrative Office of the Courts.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 431. General Provisions Concerning Crimes and Punishments›KY REV ST 431.082. Civil action by victim against defendant; damages; construction

content:
(1)  In the event of the conviction of a defendant for the violation of any offense
      proscribed by KRS Chapter 510 or 531 or any human trafficking offense proscribed by
      KRS Chapter 529, the person who was the victim of the offense may bring an action
      in damages against the defendant in the criminal case.
