path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.026. Sale or transfer of viable aborted child for use in experimentation prohibited
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.026. Sale or transfer of viable aborted child for use in experimentation prohibited
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.026. Sale or transfer of viable aborted child for use in experimentation prohibited (2023)
content:
Any person who shall sell, transfer, distribute, or give away any live or viable aborted
   child or permits such child to be used for any form of experimentation shall be guilty
   of a Class B felony.  Nothing contained in this section shall be construed as prohibiting adoption or
   foster care proceedings pursuant to the provisions of the laws of the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.165. Retail sales and activities on Sunday subject to control of legislative body of city or county; restrictions; public vote
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.165. Retail sales and activities on Sunday subject to control of legislative body of city or county; restrictions; public vote
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.165. Retail sales and activities on Sunday subject to control of legislative body of city or county; restrictions; public vote (2023)
content: In addition to the provisions ofKRS 436.160:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.185. Exhibition of walking horse where the horse's front legs or hoofs show evidence of burns, drugs, lacerations or any pain inflicting device
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.185. Exhibition of walking horse where the horse's front legs or hoofs show evidence of burns, drugs, lacerations or any pain inflicting device
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.185. Exhibition of walking horse where the horse's front legs or hoofs show evidence of burns, drugs, lacerations or any pain inflicting device (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) The term “walking horse” as used in this section shall be construed to include only that breed of horses
         known as walking horses.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.480. Pari-mutuel wagering or sports wagering exempt from KRS Chapter § 528
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.480. Pari-mutuel wagering or sports wagering exempt from KRS Chapter § 528
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.480. Pari-mutuel wagering or sports wagering exempt from KRS Chapter § 528 (2023)
content:
KRS Chapter 528 shall not apply to pari-mutuel or sports wagering authorized under
   the provisions of KRS Chapter 230.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.600. Dyeing or selling dyed baby fowl or rabbits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.600. Dyeing or selling dyed baby fowl or rabbits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.600. Dyeing or selling dyed baby fowl or rabbits (2023)
content:
No person shall sell, exchange, offer to sell or exchange, display, or possess living
   baby chicks, ducklings, or other fowl or rabbits which have been dyed or colored;
   nor dye or color any baby chicks, ducklings, or other fowl or rabbits;  nor sell,
   exchange, offer to sell or exchange or to give away baby chicks, ducklings, or other
   fowl or rabbits, under two (2) months of age in any quantity less than six (6), except
   that any rabbit weighing three (3) pounds or more may be sold at an age of six (6)
   weeks.  Any person who violates this section shall be fined not less than $100 nor more
   than $500.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.320. Minor to furnish identification to play billiards or pool; owner of table to supply blank cards
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.320. Minor to furnish identification to play billiards or pool; owner of table to supply blank cards
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.320. Minor to furnish identification to play billiards or pool; owner of table to supply blank cards (2023)
content:
No person owning or controlling a billiard or pool table shall permit, for compensation
   or reward, any minor under eighteen (18) years of age to play any game on the table,
   unless such minor shall have first displayed an identification card containing his
   name, age, photograph, and the signature of his parents or guardian.  The minor shall keep such identification card on his person, and it shall be subject
   to inspection at any time by any peace officer.  The person owning or controlling such billiard or pool table shall keep and maintain
   a registration book in which each minor shall sign.  The person owning or controlling such billiard or pool table shall supply a blank
   identification card to each parent or guardian who makes request for same.  Any person who violates this section shall be fined not less than ten ($10) nor
   more than one hundred dollars ($100) for each offense.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.510. Witnesses in investigation or prosecution for gambling
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.510. Witnesses in investigation or prosecution for gambling
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.510. Witnesses in investigation or prosecution for gambling (2023)
content:
(1)  In any prosecution or any investigation by an examining court or grand jury of
      gambling violations, it shall be no exemption for a witness that his testimony may
      incriminate himself.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.575. Motion picture rating required to be included in any motion picture advertising placed or accepted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.575. Motion picture rating required to be included in any motion picture advertising placed or accepted
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.575. Motion picture rating required to be included in any motion picture advertising placed or accepted (2023)
content:
(1)  No person shall advertise any motion picture in any media, including but not
      limited to newspapers, magazines, radio, television, or billboards, without including
      the rating assigned to that picture by the Motion Picture Coding Association of America
      or its successor, if a rating has been assigned to the said motion picture.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.605. Animal control officers and humane agents have powers of peace officers except power of arrest; search warrants; execution of search warrants; arrest by peace officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.605. Animal control officers and humane agents have powers of peace officers except power of arrest; search warrants; execution of search warrants; arrest by peace officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.605. Animal control officers and humane agents have powers of peace officers except power of arrest; search warrants; execution of search warrants; arrest by peace officer (2023)
content:
(1)  Animal control officers and officers and agents of humane societies who are employed
      by, appointed by, or have contracted with a city, county, urban-county, charter county,
      or consolidated local government to provide animal sheltering or animal control services
      shall have the powers of peace officers, except for the power of arrest, for the purpose
      of enforcing the provisions of the Kentucky Revised Statutes relating to cruelty,
      mistreatment, sexual crimes against, or torture of animals, provided they possess
      the qualifications required underKRS 61.300.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies›KY REV ST 437.030. Challenge to duel; accepting and delivering challenge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies › KY REV ST 437.030. Challenge to duel; accepting and delivering challenge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 437.030. Challenge to duel; accepting and delivering challenge (2023)
content:
Any person who, in this state, challenges another to fight with any deadly weapon,
   in or out of this state, and any person who accepts the challenge, shall be fined
   five hundred dollars ($500) and imprisoned for not less than six (6) nor more than
   twelve (12) months.  Any person who knowingly carries or delivers such a challenge in this state, or
   consents in this state to be a second to either party shall be fined one hundred dollars
   ($100) and imprisoned for thirty (30) days.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies›KY REV ST 437.140. Witness in prosecution of criminal conspirators not to claim exemption
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies › KY REV ST 437.140. Witness in prosecution of criminal conspirators not to claim exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 437.140. Witness in prosecution of criminal conspirators not to claim exemption (2023)
content:
In any prosecution for criminal conspiracy it shall be no exemption for a witness
   that his testimony may incriminate himself.  No testimony given by the witness shall be used against him in any prosecution except
   for perjury, and he shall be discharged from all liability for a violation of any
   criminal conspiracy law necessarily disclosed in his testimony.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies›KY REV ST 437.060. Use of reptiles in religious services
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 437. Offenses Against Public Peace; Conspiracies › KY REV ST 437.060. Use of reptiles in religious services
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 437.060. Use of reptiles in religious services (2023)
content:
Any person who displays, handles or uses any kind of reptile in connection with any
   religious service or gathering shall be fined not less than fifty dollars ($50) nor
   more than one hundred dollars ($100).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality›KY REV ST 436.610. Confiscation of animals on premises where violations of KRS 525.125. and 525.130. occur
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 436. Offenses Against Morality › KY REV ST 436.610. Confiscation of animals on premises where violations of KRS 525.125. and 525.130. occur
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 436.610. Confiscation of animals on premises where violations of KRS 525.125. and 525.130. occur (2023)
content:
All animals of the same species, which are on the property when an animal is caused
   to fight for pleasure or profit, in violation of the provisions ofKRS 525.125and525.130, shall be confiscated and turned over to the county animal control officer employed,
   appointed, or contracted with as provided byKRS 258.195, if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the animals were on the property
   for the purpose of fighting.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.047. Prohibition against certain billboard advertising of tobacco products within five hundred feet of school; fine
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.047. Prohibition against certain billboard advertising of tobacco products within five hundred feet of school; fine
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.047. Prohibition against certain billboard advertising of tobacco products within five hundred feet of school; fine (2023)
content:
(1)  No cigarette or tobacco products advertising shall be posted on a billboard with
      display space larger than fifty (50) square feet located within five hundred (500)
      feet of any elementary or secondary school building or adjacent school-owned property.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.050. Use of alternative nicotine products, tobacco products, and vapor products on school premises; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.050. Use of alternative nicotine products, tobacco products, and vapor products on school premises; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.050. Use of alternative nicotine products, tobacco products, and vapor products on school premises; exception (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person, except adult employees of the school system who smoke in a room on
      the school premises designated by the superintendent or principal for the purpose,
      who uses alternative nicotine products, tobacco products, or vapor products in any
      school building or any part of any building used for school purposes, or upon school
      grounds, while children are assembled there for lawful purposes, except in areas in
      secondary schools designated and supervised by the superintendent or principal for
      the purpose, shall be fined not less than one dollar ($1) nor more than five dollars
      ($5).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.060. Contaminating watercourse
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.060. Contaminating watercourse
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.060. Contaminating watercourse (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section any person who places or
      causes to be placed in any stream, dam, pool or pond any substance that renders the
      water unfit for use or produces a stench shall be fined not less than ten dollars
      ($10) nor more than one hundred dollars ($100) and imprisoned for not less than thirty
      (30) days nor more than six (6) months.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.065. Advertising or soliciting by practitioner of healing arts; exceptions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.065. Advertising or soliciting by practitioner of healing arts; exceptions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.065. Advertising or soliciting by practitioner of healing arts; exceptions (2023)
content:
(1)  No person licensed to practice medicine, dentistry, osteopathy, podiatry, optometry,
      or chiropractic, or any other healing art in this state shall solicit persons to become
      patients, or advertise by mail, card, newspaper, pamphlet, radio, television, or any
      other medium, or permit his services to be advertised;  provided, however, that such
      person may publish a brief announcement of the opening of an office or of any change
      of office location or change of office hours, and may cause to be listed in the telephone
      directory and classified advertising sections thereof his name, address, type of practice
      and office hours.  Modest signs on the doors, windows, and walls of the licensee's office or on the
      building in which he maintains an office setting out his name, professional title
      in accordance withKRS 311.375, office hours and address shall not be considered as violations of this subsection.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.160. Definitions for KRS 438.170, 438.180. and § 438.190
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.160. Definitions for KRS 438.170, 438.180. and § 438.190
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.160. Definitions for KRS 438.170, 438.180. and § 438.190 (2023)
content:
(1)  “Party line” means a subscriber's line telephone circuit, consisting of two (2) or more main
      telephone stations connected therewith, each station with a distinctive ring or telephone
      number.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.220. Transmission of false or fraudulent communications over telegraph or telephone lines; delay of messages
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.220. Transmission of false or fraudulent communications over telegraph or telephone lines; delay of messages
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.220. Transmission of false or fraudulent communications over telegraph or telephone lines; delay of messages (2023)
content:
Any person who knowingly transmits on or through any telegraph or telephone line in
   the state, any false communication or intelligence with intention to injure any other
   person or to speculate on any article of merchandise, commerce or trade, or with intent
   that another may do so;  or any agent, officer or manager of a telegraph or telephone
   line who, from corrupt or improper motives or willful negligence, withholds the transmission
   or delivery of messages or intelligence, for which the customary charges have been
   paid or tendered, shall be fined not less than ten dollars ($10) nor more than five
   hundred dollars ($500).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.170. Emergency party line use
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.170. Emergency party line use
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.170. Emergency party line use (2023)
content:
Any person who willfully refuses to yield or surrender the use of a party line to
   another person for the purpose of permitting such other person to report a fire or
   summon police, medical or other aid in case of emergency, shall be fined not less
   than twenty dollars ($20) nor more than five hundred dollars ($500) or imprisoned
   in the county jail for a period not exceeding ninety (90) days, or both.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.180. False representation of emergency
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.180. False representation of emergency
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.180. False representation of emergency (2023)
content:
Any person who asks for or requests the use of a party line on the pretext that an
   emergency exists, knowing that no emergency in fact exists, shall be fined not less
   than twenty-five ($25) nor more than one hundred dollars ($100) or imprisoned in the
   county jail for a period not exceeding ten (10) days or both so fined and imprisoned.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.250. Mandatory testing for HIV, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis, and other diseases for criminal defendants, inmates, and state patients under specified conditions; effect of refusal to be tested; costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.250. Mandatory testing for HIV, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis, and other diseases for criminal defendants, inmates, and state patients under specified conditions; effect of refusal to be tested; costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.250. Mandatory testing for HIV, hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis, and other diseases for criminal defendants, inmates, and state patients under specified conditions; effect of refusal to be tested; costs (2023)
content:
(1)  When a public servant, as defined inKRS 521.010, a health care professional who is licensed or certified under the laws of the Commonwealth,
      an employee of the health care professional, an employee of a health care facility
      that is licensed under the laws of the Commonwealth, or victim of a crime is bitten
      by, suffers a puncture wound caused by, or is exposed to the blood or body fluids
      of a criminal defendant, inmate, parolee, probationer, or patient or resident of any
      health facility owned or operated by the Commonwealth, or the blood or body fluids
      of a criminal defendant, inmate, parolee, or probationer have come into contact with
      the skin or unprotected clothing of a public servant during any incident in which
      the public servant and the criminal defendant, inmate, parolee, or probationer are
      involved, the criminal defendant, inmate, parolee, or probationer shall be ordered
      to submit to testing for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B and C viruses,
      and any other disease, if testing for that disease is recommended by the most current
      guidelines of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and if testing for any
      of these conditions is recommended, then testing will be conducted as recommended
      by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.230. Use of obscene language or proposals on telephone; notice of law on telephone books
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.230. Use of obscene language or proposals on telephone; notice of law on telephone books
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.230. Use of obscene language or proposals on telephone; notice of law on telephone books (2023)
content:
Every telephone directory published for distribution to members of the general public
   shall contain a notice which explains that it is unlawful for any person to make use
   of telephone facilities or equipment for the purpose of communicating language, suggestions
   or proposals which are obscene, profane, lewd, lascivious or indecent in a manner
   reasonably to be expected to annoy, abuse, harass, torment or embarrass another, such
   notice to be printed in type which is no smaller than the smallest type on the same
   page, and to be preceded by the word “WARNING.” The provisions of this section shall not apply to directories solely for business
   advertising purposes, commonly known as classified directories.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.240. Abandonment or discard of refrigerator, freezer, icebox or ice chest with door or lid attached; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.240. Abandonment or discard of refrigerator, freezer, icebox or ice chest with door or lid attached; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.240. Abandonment or discard of refrigerator, freezer, icebox or ice chest with door or lid attached; exception (2023)
content:
(1)  Whoever abandons or discards in any place accessible to children any refrigerator,
      freezer, icebox or ice chest, of a capacity of one and one-half (1-1/2) cubic feet
      or more, which has an attached lid or door which may be opened or shut, or who, being
      the owner, occupant, lessee, or manager of the place, knowingly permits an abandoned
      or discarded refrigerator, freezer, icebox or ice chest to remain there in such condition,
      is guilty of a Class B misdemeanor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.190. Warning publication
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.190. Warning publication
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.190. Warning publication (2023)
content:
After the ninetieth day following June 14, 1962, every telephone directory thereafter
   published for distribution to the members of the general public shall contain a notice
   which explains this law, such notice to be printed in type which is no smaller than
   any other type on the same page and to be preceded by the word “WARNING.” The provisions of this section shall not apply to directories distributed solely for
   business advertising purposes, commonly known as classified directories.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.179. Release of misdemeanants; purposes for which permitted; earnings of prisoner, records, and disposition; authority of District Judge, and jailer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.179. Release of misdemeanants; purposes for which permitted; earnings of prisoner, records, and disposition; authority of District Judge, and jailer

content:
(1)  Any person sentenced to a jail for a misdemeanor, nonpayment of a fine or forfeiture,
      or contempt of court, may be granted the privilege of leaving the jail during necessary
      and reasonable hours for any of the following purposes:

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.250. Definitions for KRS 439.250. to § 439.560
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.250. Definitions for KRS 439.250. to § 439.560 (2023)
content: As used inKRS 439.250to439.560, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.177. Parole privileges for certain misdemeanants; duties of sentencing judge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.177. Parole privileges for certain misdemeanants; duties of sentencing judge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.177. Parole privileges for certain misdemeanants; duties of sentencing judge (2023)
content: (1)  Any misdemeanant may petition the sentencing court for parole privileges.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety›KY REV ST 438.210. Interfering with communications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 438. Offenses Against Public Health and Safety › KY REV ST 438.210. Interfering with communications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 438.210. Interfering with communications (2023)
content:
Any person who willfully and maliciously prevents, obstructs or delays the sending,
   transmission, conveyance or delivery in this state of any message, communication or
   report through any telegraph or telephone line, wire or cable shall be fined not less
   than fifty dollars ($50) nor more than five hundred dollars ($500), or imprisoned
   for not more than one (1) year, or both.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.267. Shock probation in misdemeanor convictions; procedure; exercise of authority; availability for sexual offenders
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.267. Shock probation in misdemeanor convictions; procedure; exercise of authority; availability for sexual offenders
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.267. Shock probation in misdemeanor convictions; procedure; exercise of authority; availability for sexual offenders (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to the provisions of KRS Chapter 439 and Chapters 500 to 534, any District
      Court, or any Circuit Court with respect to a defendant convicted in Circuit Court
      of a misdemeanor, may, upon motion of the defendant made not earlier than thirty (30)
      days after the defendant has been delivered to the keeper of the institution to which
      he has been sentenced, suspend the further execution of the sentence and place the
      defendant on probation upon terms as the court determines.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.268. Probation program credits
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.268. Probation program credits
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.268. Probation program credits (2023)
content:
(1)  Any supervised individual on probation, probation with an alternative sentence,
      or conditional discharge shall receive credit on his or her sentence for:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.310. Administration of probation and parole laws
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.310. Administration of probation and parole laws
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.310. Administration of probation and parole laws (2023)
content:
The commissioner, with the approval of the secretary and the Governor, shall appoint
   a person charged with the administration of probation and parole laws, who, with the
   approval of the commissioner, shall appoint a number of probation and parole officers
   and other employees sufficient to administer the provisions ofKRS 439.250to439.560;  but no employee shall be appointed except in the manner hereinafter provided.  The person charged with the administration of probation and parole laws shall have
   attained at least a bachelor's degree from an accredited college, and, in addition,
   shall be a person with training and experience in probation, parole or other related
   form of welfare work.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.265. Shock probation in felony conviction; procedure; exclusions; comprehensive sex offender presentence evaluation; exercise of authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.265. Shock probation in felony conviction; procedure; exclusions; comprehensive sex offender presentence evaluation; exercise of authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.265. Shock probation in felony conviction; procedure; exclusions; comprehensive sex offender presentence evaluation; exercise of authority (2023)
content:
(1)  Subject to the provisions of KRS Chapter 439 and Chapters 500 to 534, any Circuit
      Court may, upon motion of the defendant made not earlier than thirty (30) days nor
      later than one hundred eighty (180) days after the defendant has been incarcerated
      in a county jail following his conviction and sentencing pending delivery to the institution
      to which he has been sentenced, or delivered to the keeper of the institution to which
      he has been sentenced, suspend the further execution of the sentence and place the
      defendant on probation upon terms the court determines.  Time spent on any form of release following conviction shall not count toward time
      required under this section.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3104. Duties of department concerning risk and needs assessment instrument
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3104. Duties of department concerning risk and needs assessment instrument (2023)
content: The department shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3101. Administrative regulations requiring supervision and treatment in accordance with evidence-based practices
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3101. Administrative regulations requiring supervision and treatment in accordance with evidence-based practices
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3101. Administrative regulations requiring supervision and treatment in accordance with evidence-based practices (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall promulgate administrative regulations that require the supervision
      and treatment of supervised individuals in accordance with evidence-based practices.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3105. Administrative caseload supervision program for supervised offenders; administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3105. Administrative caseload supervision program for supervised offenders; administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3105. Administrative caseload supervision program for supervised offenders; administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall promulgate administrative regulations in accordance with
      the provisions of this section to establish an administrative caseload supervision
      program for supervised individuals whose results from a risk and needs assessment
      indicate that they are low-risk offenders.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.340. Parole of prisoners confined in adult penal or correctional institutions, halfway houses, and reentry centers; notice of prisoner’s parole to be given to certain law enforcement officers, and to victims or their next of kin
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.340. Parole of prisoners confined in adult penal or correctional institutions, halfway houses, and reentry centers; notice of prisoner’s parole to be given to certain law enforcement officers, and to victims or their next of kin
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.340. Parole of prisoners confined in adult penal or correctional institutions, halfway houses, and reentry centers; notice of prisoner’s parole to be given to certain law enforcement officers, and to victims or their next of kin (2023)
content:
(1)  The board may release on parole persons confined in any adult state penal or
      correctional institution of Kentucky or sentenced felons incarcerated in county jails
      eligible for parole.  All paroles shall issue upon order of the board duly adopted.  As soon as practicable after his or her admission to an adult state penal or correctional
      institution or county jail if he or she is a sentenced felon, and at such intervals
      thereafter as it may determine, the Department of Corrections shall obtain all pertinent
      information regarding each prisoner, except those not eligible for parole.  The information shall include the results of his or her most recent risk and needs
      assessment, his or her criminal record, his or her conduct, employment, and the reports
      of physical and mental examinations that have been made.  The Department of Corrections shall furnish the circumstances of his or her offense,
      the results of his or her most recent risk and needs assessment, and his or her previous
      social history to the board.  The Department of Corrections shall prepare a report on any information it obtains.  It shall be the duty of the Department of Corrections to supplement this report
      with any material the board may request and submit the report to the board.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3106. Sanctions to which supervised individuals are subject

content: (1)  Supervised individuals shall be subject to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3107. System of graduated sanctions for violations of conditions of community supervision; administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3107. System of graduated sanctions for violations of conditions of community supervision; administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3107. System of graduated sanctions for violations of conditions of community supervision; administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall, by January 1, 2012, adopt a system of graduated sanctions
      for violations of conditions of community supervision.  Notwithstanding KRS Chapter 533, the system shall set forth a menu of presumptive
      sanctions for the most common types of supervision violations, including but not limited
      to:  failure to report;  failure to pay fines, fees, and victim restitution;  failure
      to participate in a required program or service;  failure to complete community service;
      violation of a protective or no contact order;  and failure to refrain from the use
      of alcohol or controlled substances.  The system of sanctions shall take into account factors such as the severity of
      the current violation, the supervised individual's previous criminal record, the number
      and severity of any previous supervision violations, the supervised individual's assessed
      risk level, and the extent to which graduated sanctions were imposed for previous
      violations.  The system also shall define positive reinforcements that supervised individuals
      may receive for compliance with conditions of supervision.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3103. Annual report on efforts to implement evidence-based practices to reduce recidivism
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3103. Annual report on efforts to implement evidence-based practices to reduce recidivism
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3103. Annual report on efforts to implement evidence-based practices to reduce recidivism (2023)
content:
(1)  By December 1 of each year, beginning in 2012, the department shall submit to
      the Governor, the General Assembly, and the Chief Justice a comprehensive report on
      its efforts to implement evidence-based practices to reduce recidivism.  The report shall include at a minimum:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3109. Quarterly review of recommended confinement sanctions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3109. Quarterly review of recommended confinement sanctions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3109. Quarterly review of recommended confinement sanctions (2023)
content:
The probation and parole district supervisor shall review confinement sanctions recommended
   by probation and parole officers on a quarterly basis to assess any disparities that
   may exist among officers, evaluate the effectiveness of the sanction as measured by
   the supervised individuals' subsequent conduct, and monitor the impact on the department's
   number and type of revocations for violations of the conditions of supervision.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3102. Training and professional development for department personnel concerning implementation of evidence-based practices
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3102. Training and professional development for department personnel concerning implementation of evidence-based practices
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3102. Training and professional development for department personnel concerning implementation of evidence-based practices (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall provide its employees with intensive initial and on-going
      training and professional development services to support the implementation of evidence-based
      practices.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3401. Parole for violent offenders; applicability of section to victim of domestic violence or abuse; time of offense; prohibition against award of credit

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.320. Parole board; members' qualifications, terms, compensation; chairperson; administrative regulations; quorum
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.320. Parole board; members' qualifications, terms, compensation; chairperson; administrative regulations; quorum
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.320. Parole board; members' qualifications, terms, compensation; chairperson; administrative regulations; quorum (2023)
content:
(1)  The Governor shall appoint a Parole Board consisting of nine (9) full-time members
      to be confirmed by the Senate in accordance withKRS 11.160.  The Governor shall make each appointment from a list of three (3) names given to
      him or her by the Kentucky State Corrections Commission.  Each member appointed to the board shall have had at least five (5) years of actual
      experience in the field of penology, correction work, law enforcement, sociology,
      law, education, social work, medicine, or a combination thereof, or have served at
      least five (5) years previously on the Parole Board.  No more than six (6) board members shall be of the same political party.  The board shall be attached to the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet for administrative
      purposes only.  The Department of Corrections shall provide any clerical, stenographic, administrative,
      and expert staff assistance the board deems necessary to carry out its duties.

      shall use the results from an inmate's validated risk and needs assessment and any

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3402. Exemption from KRS 439.3401. for victims of domestic violence and abuse; procedures; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3402. Exemption from KRS 439.3401. for victims of domestic violence and abuse; procedures; effect (2023)
content:
(1)  Any violent offender as defined inKRS 439.3401who was convicted prior to July 14, 1992, who claims to come within the definitions
      ofKRS 503.050and533.060and the purview of this section as the victim of domestic violence and abuse may
      be exempt fromKRS 439.3401under the conditions set forth in this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3403. Reconsideration of parole of inmate given deferment or serve-out longer than sixty months; exceptions; hearings
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3403. Reconsideration of parole of inmate given deferment or serve-out longer than sixty months; exceptions; hearings
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3403. Reconsideration of parole of inmate given deferment or serve-out longer than sixty months; exceptions; hearings (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, the board shall reconsider
      the parole of any prisoner as of June 8, 2011, who was given a deferment or serve-out
      of longer than sixty (60) months at the prisoner's most recent parole hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3405. Parole of prisoners with documented terminal medical conditions; hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3405. Parole of prisoners with documented terminal medical conditions; hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3405. Parole of prisoners with documented terminal medical conditions; hearing (2023)
content:
(1)  Notwithstanding any statute eliminating parole or establishing minimum time for
      parole eligibility for a certain class or status of offender, includingKRS 439.340(11),439.3401,532.080(7), and533.060, the board, with the written consent of a majority of the full board, may review
      the case of any prisoner and release that prisoner on parole despite any elimination
      of or minimum time for parole eligibility, when the prisoner has a documented terminal
      medical condition likely to result in death within one (1) year or severe chronic
      lung disease, end-stage heart disease, severe neuro-muscular disease such as multiple
      sclerosis;  or has severely limited mobility as a result of stroke, disease, or trauma;
      or is dependent on external life support systems and would not pose a threat to society
      if paroled.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3406. Mandatory reentry supervision six months prior to projected completion date of inmate's sentence for inmate not granted discretionary parole; exceptions; terms of supervision; no credit for time absconding; report
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3406. Mandatory reentry supervision six months prior to projected completion date of inmate's sentence for inmate not granted discretionary parole; exceptions; terms of supervision; no credit for time absconding; report (2023)
content:
(1)  The board shall order mandatory reentry supervision six (6) months prior to the
      projected completion date of an inmate's sentence for an inmate who has not been granted
      discretionary parole.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.342. Retention of prisoner on parole
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.342. Retention of prisoner on parole
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.342. Retention of prisoner on parole (2023)
content: The board may retain any prisoner on parole for a period of at least one (1) year.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3407. Conditional parole of state inmates to be served in local correctional facility, jail, or reentry center; administrative regulations; work release
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3407. Conditional parole of state inmates to be served in local correctional facility, jail, or reentry center; administrative regulations; work release
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3407. Conditional parole of state inmates to be served in local correctional facility, jail, or reentry center; administrative regulations; work release (2023)
content:
(1)  The department may promulgate administrative regulations to implement conditional
      parole of state inmates incarcerated in state corrections institutions or local correctional
      facilities or county jails to place those individuals closer to their communities
      prior to release.  A parolee placed on conditional parole shall serve that term in a local correctional
      facility or county jail or reentry center in a county in which the fiscal court has
      agreed to house parolees if beds are available in the local correctional facility
      or county jail or reentry center.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.3408. Department to approve any acceptable housing for parolees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.3408. Department to approve any acceptable housing for parolees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.3408. Department to approve any acceptable housing for parolees (2023)
content:
When considering appropriate housing options for a person considered for parole or
   a person who is being paroled, the department shall approve any form of acceptable
   housing, including but not limited to apartments, shelters for homeless or other persons,
   county jails or restricted custody facilities that a county approves for parolees,
   educational institutions with dormitories if the parolee is enrolled or accepted for
   enrollment at an educational institution, halfway houses, reentry centers, residential
   treatment or other programs in which the parolee is enrolled or accepted for enrollment,
   and other forms of transitional housing meeting the requirements of applicable statutes.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.344. Effect of parole time on sentence; exceptions

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.352. Recommitment of supervised individual on parole or post-release supervision; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.352. Recommitment of supervised individual on parole or post-release supervision; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.352. Recommitment of supervised individual on parole or post-release supervision; effect (2023)
content:
Recommitment of a supervised individual on parole or post-release supervision to prison
   or jail on a new sentence received for commission of a crime while on parole or other
   post-release supervision shall automatically terminate his or her parole or other
   post-release supervision status on any sentence on which he or she has not received
   a final discharge, or a restoration of civil rights, prior to the date of recommitment.  The prisoner shall, at the time of the recommitment on the new sentence, begin to
   accrue additional time credit toward conditional release or expiration of sentence
   on the sentence on which he or she had previously been on community supervision unless
   he or she has been finally discharged from community supervision on the sentence or
   has been restored to civil rights prior to the date of the recommitment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.341. Probable cause revocation hearings of probation, parole, and postincarceration supervision violators
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.341. Probable cause revocation hearings of probation, parole, and postincarceration supervision violators
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.341. Probable cause revocation hearings of probation, parole, and postincarceration supervision violators (2023)
content:
Probable cause revocation hearings of probation, parole, and postincarceration supervision
   violators shall be conducted by hearing officers.  These hearing officers shall be attorneys, appointed by the board and admitted to
   practice in Kentucky, who shall perform the aforementioned duties and any others assigned
   by the board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.346. Prisoner paroled or under postincarceration supervision subject to orders of board
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.346. Prisoner paroled or under postincarceration supervision subject to orders of board
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.346. Prisoner paroled or under postincarceration supervision subject to orders of board (2023)
content:
During the period of his or her parole or postincarceration supervision, the prisoner
   shall be amenable to the orders of the board and the department.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.358. Final discharge provisions; application
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.358. Final discharge provisions; application
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.358. Final discharge provisions; application (2023)
content:
The provisions of granting final discharges from parole, and the release from being
   again confined on the same sentence in the penitentiary following the granting of
   such discharge or following the restoration of the parolee's civil rights, as set
   out inKRS 439.342to439.358, shall be followed in all cases of those persons confined or paroled before, on,
   or committed after June 14, 1962.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.354. Final discharge of paroled prisoner; conditions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.354. Final discharge of paroled prisoner; conditions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.354. Final discharge of paroled prisoner; conditions (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, when any paroled prisoner
      has performed the obligations of his or her parole during his or her period of active
      parole supervision the board may, at the termination of such period to be determined
      by the board, issue a final discharge from parole to the prisoner.  Unless ordered earlier by the board, a final discharge shall be issued when the
      prisoner has been out of prison on parole a sufficient period of time to have been
      eligible for discharge from prison by minimum expiration of sentence had he or she
      not been paroled, provided before this date he or she had not absconded from parole
      supervision or that a warrant for parole violation had not been issued by the board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.370. Commonwealth's attorney to cause to be transmitted to the institution a concise statement of facts adduced at trial or hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.370. Commonwealth's attorney to cause to be transmitted to the institution a concise statement of facts adduced at trial or hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.370. Commonwealth's attorney to cause to be transmitted to the institution a concise statement of facts adduced at trial or hearing (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the Commonwealth's attorney after the imposition of prison
   sentence, unless the defendant is granted probation, to cause to be forthwith transmitted
   to the institution with the commitment papers, a concise statement of the facts adduced
   at the trial or at the hearing of a plea of guilty, together with such notes of testimony
   as the board may request.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.356. Final discharge; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.356. Final discharge; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.356. Final discharge; effect (2023)
content:
After final discharge has been ordered and a certificate issued by the board, or after
   the parolee's civil rights have been restored by an act of the Governor, the parolee
   may not be held again for a violation of that parole.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.390. Board may issue subpoenas; penalty for false testimony or failure to comply with subpoena; Circuit Court may compel the attendance of witnesses, production of documents and giving of testimony before board
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.390. Board may issue subpoenas; penalty for false testimony or failure to comply with subpoena; Circuit Court may compel the attendance of witnesses, production of documents and giving of testimony before board
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.390. Board may issue subpoenas; penalty for false testimony or failure to comply with subpoena; Circuit Court may compel the attendance of witnesses, production of documents and giving of testimony before board (2023)
content:
The board shall have the power to issue subpoenas requiring the attendance of such
   witnesses and the production of such records, books, papers, and documents as it may
   deem necessary for investigation of the case of any person before it.  Subpoenas may be signed and oaths administered by any member of the board.  Subpoenas so issued shall be served by any sheriff, constable, police, parole or
   probation officer, or other peace officer and a return made to the board in the same
   manner as similar process in the Circuit Court.  Any person who testifies falsely or fails to appear when subpoenaed, or fails or
   refuses to produce documents, records, or other such material when subpoenaed, upon
   citation by the Circuit Courts where the board meets and after hearing by that court,
   shall be subject to the same order and penalties to which persons before that court
   are subject.  Any Circuit Court, upon application of the board, may compel the attendance of witnesses,
   the production of documents, records or other such material, and the giving of testimony
   before the board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.420. Person out on parole not to be required to wear regulation dress of penitentiary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.420. Person out on parole not to be required to wear regulation dress of penitentiary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.420. Person out on parole not to be required to wear regulation dress of penitentiary (2023)
content:
No person shall be required to wear the regulation dress of the penitentiary or other
   thing indicating he is under conviction for a crime while out on parole.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.450. Board to make investigation and report to Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.450. Board to make investigation and report to Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.450. Board to make investigation and report to Governor (2023)
content:
On request of the Governor the board shall investigate and report to him with respect
   to any case of pardon, commutation of sentence, reprieve or remission of fine or forfeiture.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.410. Board's order to be sufficient authority to officer in charge of state penal institution to release from custody paroled or conditionally released prisoner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.410. Board's order to be sufficient authority to officer in charge of state penal institution to release from custody paroled or conditionally released prisoner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.410. Board's order to be sufficient authority to officer in charge of state penal institution to release from custody paroled or conditionally released prisoner (2023)
content:
An order of the board shall be sufficient warrant and authority to the officer in
   charge of any state penal institution to release from custody any paroled prisoner
   or conditionally released prisoner.

content: Probation and parole officers shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.430. Parole officer may arrest parolee or person subject to postincarceration supervision, when; detention; report to commissioner; return of prisoner to prison; prisoner for whose return a warrant has been issued to be deemed a fugitive from justice; effect of violation of parole
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.430. Parole officer may arrest parolee or person subject to postincarceration supervision, when; detention; report to commissioner; return of prisoner to prison; prisoner for whose return a warrant has been issued to be deemed a fugitive from justice; effect of violation of parole
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.430. Parole officer may arrest parolee or person subject to postincarceration supervision, when; detention; report to commissioner; return of prisoner to prison; prisoner for whose return a warrant has been issued to be deemed a fugitive from justice; effect of violation of parole (2023)
content:
(1)  Any parole officer having reason to believe that a parolee or a person on postincarceration
      supervision pursuant toKRS 532.043or532.400has violated the terms of his or her release may arrest the parolee or offender on
      postincarceration supervision without a warrant or may deputize any other peace officer
      to do so by giving him or her a written statement setting forth that the parolee or
      offender on postincarceration supervision, in the judgment of the parole officer,
      has violated the conditions of his or her release.  The written statement delivered with the parolee or offender on postincarceration
      supervision by the arresting officer to the official in charge of the station house,
      jail, workhouse, or other place of detention, shall be sufficient warrant for the
      detention of the parolee or offender on postincarceration supervision.  The parole officer who arrests or causes the arrest of the prisoner shall notify
      the commissioner or his or her designee at once of the arrest and detention of the
      parolee or offender on postincarceration supervision, and shall submit in writing
      a report showing in what manner there has been a violation of the conditions of release.  Thereupon, if the commissioner or his or her designee believes the parolee or offender
      on postincarceration supervision should be returned to prison, the commissioner or
      his or her designee at once shall submit his or her recommendations to the board,
      and, if the board approves, it shall issue a warrant upon which the releasee shall
      be returned to prison;  otherwise the prisoner shall be released upon the order of
      the commissioner or his or her designee.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.470. Powers and duties of commissioner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.470. Powers and duties of commissioner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.470. Powers and duties of commissioner (2023)
content:
(1)  The commissioner shall promulgate administrative regulations for the conduct
      of persons placed on probation or parole, except that the commissioner shall not promulgate
      any administrative regulation which conflicts with the conditions of probation imposed
      by the court or conditions of release imposed by the board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.440. Prisoner returned to state custody for violation of release to be heard by board; time
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.440. Prisoner returned to state custody for violation of release to be heard by board; time
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.440. Prisoner returned to state custody for violation of release to be heard by board; time (2023)
content:
Any prisoner returned to state custody for violation of his or her release shall be
   heard by the board within sixty (60) days on the propriety of his or her rerelease.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.483. Training of probation and parole officers regarding sexual offender registration laws; necessary documents

(1)  Each probation and parole officer shall be trained in the requirements of the
      sexual offender registration laws and shall be able to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.550. Probation by District Court; supervision by Department of Corrections, or by adult misdemeanant probation and work release agency of urban-county government
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.550. Probation by District Court; supervision by Department of Corrections, or by adult misdemeanant probation and work release agency of urban-county government
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.550. Probation by District Court; supervision by Department of Corrections, or by adult misdemeanant probation and work release agency of urban-county government (2023)
content:
(1)  If any District Court places a person on probation following a conviction of
      crime, either upon verdict or plea, the court may request that the defendant be under
      the supervision of the Department of Corrections.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.510. Information obtained by probation or parole officer to be privileged; exception
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.510. Information obtained by probation or parole officer to be privileged; exception
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.510. Information obtained by probation or parole officer to be privileged; exception (2023)
content:
All information obtained in the discharge of official duty by any probation or parole
   officer shall be privileged and shall not be received as evidence in any court.  Such information shall not be disclosed directly or indirectly to any person other
   than the court, board, cabinet, or others entitled underKRS 439.250to439.560to receive such information, unless otherwise ordered by such court, board or cabinet.  Information shall be made available to sex offender treatment programs operated
   or approved by the Department of Corrections or the Department for Behavioral Health,
   Developmental and Intellectual Disabilities who request the information in the course
   of conducting an evaluation or treatment pursuant toKRS 439.265(6),532.045(3), or532.050(4).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.485. Probation and parole officer's position considered hazardous duty for retirement purposes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.485. Probation and parole officer's position considered hazardous duty for retirement purposes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.485. Probation and parole officer's position considered hazardous duty for retirement purposes (2023)
content:
The position of probation and parole officer shall be considered as a hazardous duty
   position within the meaning ofKRS 61.592and the department shall make the employer contributions required for participation
   in the Hazardous Duty Retirement Program.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.540. Powers of department
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.540. Powers of department
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.540. Powers of department (2023)
content: The department, with the written approval of the secretary and the Governor, may:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.500. Prohibited activities of probation and parole officers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.500. Prohibited activities of probation and parole officers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.500. Prohibited activities of probation and parole officers (2023)
content: (1)  No probation or parole officer of the department shall:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.552. Early termination of probation; administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.552. Early termination of probation; administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.552. Early termination of probation; administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall promulgate administrative regulations in consultation with
      the Supreme Court to establish procedures to:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.553. Judicial determination of conditions of community supervision
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.553. Judicial determination of conditions of community supervision
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.553. Judicial determination of conditions of community supervision (2023)
content:
For supervised individuals on probation, the court having jurisdiction of the case
   shall determine the conditions of community supervision and may impose as a condition
   of community supervision that the department supervising the individual shall, in
   accordance withKRS 439.3108, impose graduated sanctions adopted by the department for violations of the conditions
   of community supervision.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.551. Graduated sanctions for probation violations; administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.551. Graduated sanctions for probation violations; administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.551. Graduated sanctions for probation violations; administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The department shall promulgate administrative regulations to develop a system
      of graduated sanctions for responding to technical violations of probation.  The department shall consult with the Supreme Court when promulgating these administrative
      regulations.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 439. Probation and Parole›KY REV ST 439.555. Conditional release of certain prisoners
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 439. Probation and Parole › KY REV ST 439.555. Conditional release of certain prisoners
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 439.555. Conditional release of certain prisoners (2023)
content:
Any prisoner having served the term for which he has been sentenced for a crime he
   committed after June 16, 1972, less good time deduction, if any has been accumulated,
   shall be released by minimum expiration of sentence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Escapes›KY REV ST 440.020. Confinement of captured convict
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Escapes › KY REV ST 440.020. Confinement of captured convict
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.020. Confinement of captured convict (2023)
content:
An escaped convict, after he is reconfined, shall remain in the penitentiary until
   the time of his trial for the escape without an examining trial or bail.  His acquittal for the offense of escape shall not affect the original sentence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Escapes›KY REV ST 440.050. Liability for aiding escape of prisoner
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Escapes › KY REV ST 440.050. Liability for aiding escape of prisoner
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.050. Liability for aiding escape of prisoner (2023)
content:
Any person who aids a prisoner to escape, or knowingly conceals him after he escapes,
   or in any way hinders or prevents his capture shall be liable to the party aggrieved
   for any damages sustained.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Escapes›KY REV ST 440.030. Escape of person from custody; warrant for capture
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Escapes › KY REV ST 440.030. Escape of person from custody; warrant for capture
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.030. Escape of person from custody; warrant for capture (2023)
content:
If any person in custody under an execution, on mesne or final process, by any order
   of a judge or on a charge of crime escapes, any judge, upon complaint and affidavit
   made of the fact, shall issue as many warrants for his capture directed to all peace
   officers as he deems necessary.  The cause of the person's original commitment shall be mentioned in the warrant,
   and it shall command all peace officers to capture the prisoner and forthwith to convey
   and commit him to the prison of the county from which he escaped, to be safely kept
   there, without bail, until discharged by due course of law.  The warrant, with the proper endorsement thereon, shall be returned by the proper
   officer to the clerk of the court having jurisdiction of the cause for which the prisoner
   was in custody.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Escapes›KY REV ST 440.010. Warrant for escaped or inadvertently-released convict; reward
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Escapes › KY REV ST 440.010. Warrant for escaped or inadvertently-released convict; reward
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.010. Warrant for escaped or inadvertently-released convict; reward (2023)
content:
(1)  If a convict escapes from a penitentiary, or is inadvertently released prior
      to the expiration of the sentence, the warden of that penitentiary shall issue a warrant
      directed to all peace officers and other persons authorizing and requiring them to
      capture and convey the convict to the penitentiary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.090. Return to this state of fugitive from justice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.090. Return to this state of fugitive from justice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.090. Return to this state of fugitive from justice (2023)
content:
When the Governor of this state makes requisition upon the Governor of another state
   for a fugitive from justice, the person named in the requisition as the agent of this
   state shall, unless a different condition is contained in his commission, be allowed
   as compensation from the State Treasury for his services a mileage allowance at the
   same rate fixed by regulations adopted by the secretary of the Finance and Administration
   Cabinet pursuant toKRS 44.060, plus an additional sum calculated at the rate of five cents ($0.05) per mile for
   the distance he travels to and from the jail of the county designated in the proclamation
   to the place where the fugitive is arrested, and any other necessary expenses he pays
