   in reclaiming and returning the fugitive.  If, in attempting to reclaim the fugitive, the agent is acting within the course
   and scope of his employment, the amount due shall be paid over to the agent's employer
   instead of the agent.  When a fugitive is to be returned to this state from a location out of state which
   is in excess of five hundred (500) miles from the jail to which he is to be returned,
   commercial air transportation may be utilized in lieu of ground transportation, unless
   the agent undertaking the transportation decides to utilize ground transportation.  Payment for air transportation shall be in lieu of the mileage payment for ground
   transportation only for that portion of the journey for which air transportation is
   used.  Ground transportation and other expenses shall be paid as authorized herein.  If the agent is not given possession of the fugitive for reasons beyond the agent's
   control, he, or his employer, shall nevertheless be allowed the compensation prescribed
   by this section.  Upon the return of the fugitive to the county in which the jail named in the proclamation
   is located, the person having him in charge shall go before a judge, who shall issue
   a mittimus to the jailer to receive the prisoner and keep him until he is discharged.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.060. Capture and return of fugitive from house of reform
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.060. Capture and return of fugitive from house of reform
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.060. Capture and return of fugitive from house of reform (2023)
content:
(1)  The officer of a house of reform and any peace officer or citizen may arrest,
      without warrant, and return to the institution, any child who escapes from a house
      of reform or home in which an inmate has been placed on parole.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Escapes›KY REV ST 440.040. Liability of officer for permitting escape of prisoner in custody
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Escapes › KY REV ST 440.040. Liability of officer for permitting escape of prisoner in custody
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.040. Liability of officer for permitting escape of prisoner in custody (2023)
content:
Any officer and his sureties shall be liable, in an action upon his official bond,
   for the use of the parties aggrieved, in any damages resulting from his voluntarily
   or negligently permitting the escape of a prisoner in custody.  No judgment in such action shall be given unless the jury, by its verdict, finds
   “that the escape was with the consent of the officer, or by his negligence, or that
   the prisoner might have been retaken if the officer had, in good faith, made proper
   efforts to do so.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.100. Reward for apprehension of fugitive from justice
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.100. Reward for apprehension of fugitive from justice
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.100. Reward for apprehension of fugitive from justice (2023)
content:
In aggravated cases of murder and other felonies against the person when the accused
   flees from justice, the Governor, on petition of the Circuit or District Judge of
   the county, may issue a proclamation offering a reward of not more than five hundred
   dollars ($500) for the apprehension of the accused.  This reward shall be paid upon production of a receipt from the officer named in
   the Governor's proclamation, showing delivery of the fugitive to him, approved and
   certified by the Circuit Court of the county of that officer's residence.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.160. Definitions for KRS 440.150. to § 440.420
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.160. Definitions for KRS 440.150. to § 440.420
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.160. Definitions for KRS 440.150. to § 440.420 (2023)
content:
Where appearing inKRS 440.150to440.420, the term “Governor” includes any person performing the functions of Governor by authority of the law
   of this state.  The term “executive authority” includes the Governor, and any person performing the functions of Governor in a
   state other than this state, and the term “state,” referring to a state other than this state, includes any other state or territory,
   organized or unorganized, of the United States of America.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.120. Reward is payment in full
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.120. Reward is payment in full
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.120. Reward is payment in full (2023)
content:
Anyone claiming a reward for the apprehension of a fugitive from justice shall be
   paid the amount of the reward as full compensation for all services and expenses in
   arresting and returning the fugitive.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.170. Duty of Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.170. Duty of Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.170. Duty of Governor (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions ofKRS 440.150to440.420, the provisions of the Constitution of the United States controlling, and any and
   all Acts of Congress enacted in pursuance thereof, it is the duty of the Governor
   of this state to have arrested and delivered up to the executive authority of any
   other state of the United States any person charged in that state with treason, felony,
   or other crime, who has fled from justice and is found in this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.150. Citation of KRS 440.150. to § 440.420
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.150. Citation of KRS 440.150. to § 440.420
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.150. Citation of KRS 440.150. to § 440.420 (2023)
content: KRS 440.150to440.420may be cited as the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.110. Proclamation offering reward; publication
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.110. Proclamation offering reward; publication
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.110. Proclamation offering reward; publication (2023)
content:
(1)  Whenever the Governor issues a proclamation offering a reward for a fugitive
      from justice or anyone charged with crime, he shall designate in his proclamation
      the jail to which the prisoner shall be delivered.  It need not be the jail of the county where the offense was committed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.180. Conditions of demand for extradition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.180. Conditions of demand for extradition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.180. Conditions of demand for extradition (2023)
content:
No demand for the extradition of a person charged with crime in another state shall
   be recognized by the Governor unless in writing alleging, except in cases arising
   underKRS 440.210, that the accused was present in the demanding state at the time of the commission
   of the alleged crime, and that thereafter he fled from the state, and accompanied
   by a copy of an indictment found or by information supported by affidavit in the state
   having jurisdiction of the crime, or by a copy of an affidavit made before a magistrate
   there, together with a copy of any warrant which was issued thereupon;  or by a copy
   of a judgment of conviction or of a sentence imposed in execution thereof, together
   with a statement by the executive authority of the demanding state that the person
   claimed has escaped from confinement or has broken the terms of his bail, probation
   or parole.  The indictment, information, or affidavit made before the magistrate must substantially
   charge the person demanded with having committed a crime under the law of that state;
   and the copy of indictment, information, affidavit, judgment of conviction, or sentence
   must be authenticated by the executive authority making the demand.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Fugitives›KY REV ST 440.130. Deputizing of agency head of another state for return of escapee or probation or parole violator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Fugitives › KY REV ST 440.130. Deputizing of agency head of another state for return of escapee or probation or parole violator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.130. Deputizing of agency head of another state for return of escapee or probation or parole violator (2023)
content:
(1)  The secretary of corrections may deputize the head of an agency of another state
      which is charged by that state with enforcement of penal laws to act as an agent of
      this state in effecting the return to this state of any person who has violated the
      conditions of his probation or parole or who has escaped from a penal institution
      of this state.  In all matters relating to the return of such person to this state, such agent shall
      have the powers afforded a police officer of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.230. Execution of warrant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.230. Execution of warrant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.230. Execution of warrant (2023)
content:
Such warrant shall authorize the peace officer or other person to whom directed to
   arrest the accused at any time and any place where he may be found within the state
   and to command the aid of all peace officers or other persons in the execution of
   the warrant, and to deliver the accused, subject to the provisions ofKRS 440.150to440.420, to the duly authorized agent of the demanding state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.200. Demand by this state; agreement with other state; demand on involuntary departure
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.200. Demand by this state; agreement with other state; demand on involuntary departure
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.200. Demand by this state; agreement with other state; demand on involuntary departure (2023)
content:
(1)  When it is desired to have returned to this state a person charged in this state
      with a crime, and such person is imprisoned or is held under criminal proceedings
      then pending against him in another state, the Governor of this state may agree with
      the executive authority of such other state for the extradition of such person before
      the conclusion of such proceedings or his term of sentence in such other state, upon
      condition that such person be returned to such other state at the expense of this
      state as soon as the prosecution in this state is terminated.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.220. Warrant of arrest by Governor
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.220. Warrant of arrest by Governor
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.220. Warrant of arrest by Governor (2023)
content:
If the Governor decides that the demand should be complied with, he shall sign a warrant
   of arrest, which shall be sealed with the state seal, and be directed to any peace
   officer or other person whom he may think fit to entrust with the execution thereof.  The warrant must substantially recite the facts necessary to the validity of its
   issuance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.190. Investigation by Attorney General
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.190. Investigation by Attorney General
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.190. Investigation by Attorney General (2023)
content:
When a demand shall be made upon the Governor of this state by the executive authority
   of another state for the surrender of a person so charged with crime, the Governor
   may call upon the Attorney General or any other officer of this state to investigate
   or assist in investigating the demand, and to report to him the situation and circumstances
   of the person so demanded, and whether he ought to be surrendered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.260. Confinement of prisoner en route; duty of jailer; evidence of extradition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.260. Confinement of prisoner en route; duty of jailer; evidence of extradition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.260. Confinement of prisoner en route; duty of jailer; evidence of extradition (2023)
content:
(1)  The officer or persons executing the Governor's warrant of arrest, or the agent
      of the demanding state to whom the prisoner may have been delivered may, when necessary,
      confine the prisoner in the jail of any county or city through which he may pass;
      and the keeper of such jail must receive and safely keep the prisoner until the officer
      or person having charge of him is ready to proceed on his route, such officer or person
      being chargeable with the expense of keeping.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.240. Assistance in making arrest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.240. Assistance in making arrest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.240. Assistance in making arrest (2023)
content:
Every such peace officer or other person empowered to make the arrest, shall have
   the same authority, in arresting the accused, to command assistance therein, as peace
   officers have by law in the execution of any criminal process directed to them, with
   like penalties against those who refuse their assistance.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.250. Procedure upon arrest
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.250. Procedure upon arrest
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.250. Procedure upon arrest (2023)
content:
No person arrested upon such warrant shall be delivered over to the agent whom the
   executive authority demanding him shall have appointed to receive him unless he shall
   first be taken forthwith before a judge of a Circuit Court or District Court in this
   state, who shall inform him of the demand made for his surrender and of the crime
   with which he is charged, and that he has the right to demand and procure legal counsel;
   and if the prisoner or his counsel shall state that he or they desire to test the
   legality of his arrest, the judge of such court shall fix a reasonable time to be
   allowed him within which to apply for a writ of habeas corpus.  When such writ is applied for, notice thereof, and of the time and place of hearing
   thereon, shall be given to the prosecuting attorney of the county in which the arrest
   is made and in which the accused is in custody, and to the said agent of the demanding
   state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.210. Demand when act in this state results in crime in other state
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.210. Demand when act in this state results in crime in other state
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.210. Demand when act in this state results in crime in other state (2023)
content:
The Governor of this state may also surrender, on demand of the executive authority
   of any other state, any person in this state charged in such other state in the manner
   provided inKRS 440.180with committing an act in this state, or in a third state, intentionally resulting
   in a crime in the state whose executive authority is making the demand, and the provisions
   ofKRS 440.150to440.420not otherwise inconsistent, shall apply to such cases, even though the accused was
   not in that state at the time of the commission of the crime, and has not fled therefrom.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.280. Arrest may be made without warrant; conditions; procedure
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.280. Arrest may be made without warrant; conditions; procedure
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.280. Arrest may be made without warrant; conditions; procedure (2023)
content:
The arrest of a person may be lawfully made also by any peace officer or a private
   person, without a warrant upon reasonable information that the accused stands charged
   in the courts of a state with a crime punishable by death or imprisonment for a term
   exceeding one (1) year, but when so arrested the accused must be taken before a judge
   with all practicable speed and complaint must be made against him under oath setting
   forth the ground for the arrest as in the preceding section;  and thereafter his answer
   shall be heard as if he had been arrested on a warrant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.320. Forfeiture of bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.320. Forfeiture of bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.320. Forfeiture of bond (2023)
content:
If the prisoner is admitted to bail, and fails to appear and surrender himself according
   to the conditions of his bond, the judge, by proper order, shall declare the bond
   forfeited and order his immediate arrest without warrant if he be within this state.  Recovery may be had on such bond in the name of the state as in the case of other
   bonds given by the accused in criminal proceedings within this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.350. Control of warrant
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.350. Control of warrant
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.350. Control of warrant (2023)
content:
The Governor may recall his warrant of arrest or may issue another warrant whenever
   he deems proper.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.270. Person charged with crime in other state may be arrested in this state; procedure; warrant required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.270. Person charged with crime in other state may be arrested in this state; procedure; warrant required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.270. Person charged with crime in other state may be arrested in this state; procedure; warrant required (2023)
content:
(1)  Whenever any person within this state shall be charged on the oath of any credible
      person before any judge of this state with the commission of any crime in any other
      state and, except in cases arising underKRS 440.210, with having fled from justice, or with having been convicted of a crime in that
      state and having escaped from confinement, or having broken the terms of his bail,
      probation or parole, or whenever complaint shall have been made before any judge in
      this state setting forth on the affidavit of any credible person in another state
      that a crime has been committed in such other state and that the accused has been
      charged in such state with the commission of the crime, and, except in cases arising
      underKRS 440.210, has fled from justice, or with having been convicted of a crime in that state and
      having escaped from confinement, or having broken the terms of his bail, probation
      or parole and is believed to be in this state, the judge shall issue a warrant directed
      to any peace officer commanding him to apprehend the person named therein, wherever
      he may be found in this state, and to bring him before the Circuit or District Judge
      of the county in which he was arrested who may be available in or convenient of access
      to the place where the arrest may be made, to answer the charge or complaint and affidavit,
      and a certified copy of the sworn charge or complaint and affidavit upon which the
      warrant is issued shall be attached to the warrant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.375. Extradition of persons charged with custodial interference
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.375. Extradition of persons charged with custodial interference
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.375. Extradition of persons charged with custodial interference (2023)
content:
(1)  The county attorney shall present to the Governor a written application prepared
      in accordance withKRS 440.370for the return from any other state of any person charged with a violation ofKRS 509.070.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.310. Failure to arrest under warrant of Governor; discharge; recommitment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.310. Failure to arrest under warrant of Governor; discharge; recommitment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.310. Failure to arrest under warrant of Governor; discharge; recommitment (2023)
content:
If the accused is not arrested under warrant of the Governor by the expiration of
   the time specified in the warrant or bond, the judge may discharge him or may recommit
   him for a further period not to exceed sixty (60) days, or may again take bail for
   his appearance and surrender, as provided inKRS 440.300, but within a period not to exceed sixty (60) days after the date of such new bond.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.290. Commitment in jail pending Governor's warrant issued on requisition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.290. Commitment in jail pending Governor's warrant issued on requisition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.290. Commitment in jail pending Governor's warrant issued on requisition (2023)
content:
If from the examination before the judge it appears that the person held is the person
   charged with having committed the crime alleged and, except in cases arising underKRS 440.210, that he has fled from justice, the judge must, by a warrant reciting the accusation,
   commit him to the county jail for such a time not exceeding thirty (30) days and specified
   in the warrant, as will enable the arrest of the accused to be made under a warrant
   of the Governor on a requisition of the executive authority of the state having jurisdiction
   of the offense, unless the accused give bail as provided inKRS 440.300, or until he shall be legally discharged.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.300. Bail permitted; conditions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.300. Bail permitted; conditions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.300. Bail permitted; conditions (2023)
content:
Unless the offense with which the prisoner is charged is shown to be an offense punishable
   by death or life imprisonment under the laws of the state in which it was committed,
   a judge in this state may admit the person arrested to bail by bond, with sufficient
   sureties, and in such sum as he deems proper, conditioned for his appearance before
   him at a time specified in such bond, and for his surrender, to be arrested upon the
   warrant of the Governor of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.370. Application for return of person charged with crime; person convicted; requisites and procedures
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.370. Application for return of person charged with crime; person convicted; requisites and procedures
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.370. Application for return of person charged with crime; person convicted; requisites and procedures (2023)
content:
(1)  When the return to this state of a person charged with crime in this state is
      required, the Commonwealth's attorney or county attorney shall present to the Governor
      his written application for a requisition for the return of the person charged, in
      which application shall be stated the name of the person so charged, the crime charged
      against him, the approximate time, place and circumstances of its commission, the
      state in which he is believed to be, including the location of the accused therein
      at the time the application is made and certifying that, in the opinion of the said
      prosecuting attorney the ends of justice require the arrest and return of the accused
      to this state for trial and that the proceeding is not instituted to enforce a private
      claim.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.340. Inquiry as to guilt prohibited after demand for extradition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.340. Inquiry as to guilt prohibited after demand for extradition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.340. Inquiry as to guilt prohibited after demand for extradition (2023)
content:
The guilt or innocence of the accused as to the crime of which he is charged may not
   be inquired into by the Governor or in any proceeding after the demand for extradition
   accompanied by a charge of crime in legal form as above provided shall have been presented
   to the Governor, except as it may be involved in identifying the person held as the
   person charged with the crime.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.330. Extradition may be granted person accused or convicted in this state; conditions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.330. Extradition may be granted person accused or convicted in this state; conditions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.330. Extradition may be granted person accused or convicted in this state; conditions (2023)
content:
The Governor may in his discretion surrender upon demand of the executive authority
   of another state, any person found in this state, notwithstanding the fact that a
   criminal prosecution or charges under the laws of this state are pending against such
   person, or that such person has been convicted in this state and is serving a sentence
   in any penal institution of this state.  The Governor may condition the release of such prisoner to the demanding state upon
   such terms as he may stipulate, including the condition that the prisoner be returned
   to this state immediately after trial and before commencing the service of sentence,
   if any, in the demanding state;  provided, however, in no case shall surrender of
   such prisoner be construed as a complete relinquishment of jurisdiction by this state,
   but such prisoner shall forthwith be returned to the custody of this state at expense
   of the demanding state, immediately after trial in the demanding state, or the completion
   of sentence therein, as the case may be.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.360. Warrant of Governor to receiving officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.360. Warrant of Governor to receiving officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.360. Warrant of Governor to receiving officer (2023)
content:
Whenever the Governor of this state shall demand a person charged with crime or with
   escaping from confinement or breaking the terms of his bail, probation or parole in
   this state, from the executive authority of any other state, or from the Chief Justice
   or an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia authorized
   to receive such demand under the laws of the United States, he shall issue a warrant
   under the seal of this state, to some agent, commanding him to receive the person
   so charged if delivered to him and convey him to the proper officer of the county
   in this state in which the offense was committed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.410. Construction against waiver of any of this state's rights
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.410. Construction against waiver of any of this state's rights
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.410. Construction against waiver of any of this state's rights (2023)
content:
Nothing contained inKRS 440.150to440.420shall be deemed to constitute a waiver by this state of its right, power, or privilege
   to try such demanded person for crime committed within this state, or of its right,
   power, or privilege to regain custody of such person by extradition proceedings or
   otherwise for the purpose of trial, sentence, or punishment for any crime committed
   within this state, nor shall any proceedings had underKRS 440.150to440.420which result in, or fail to result in, extradition be deemed a waiver by this state
   of any of its rights, privileges, or jurisdiction in any way whatsoever.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.390. Immunity from civil process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.390. Immunity from civil process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.390. Immunity from civil process (2023)
content:
A person brought into this state by, or after waiver of, extradition based on a criminal
   charge shall not be subject to service of personal process in civil actions arising
   out of the same facts as the criminal proceeding to answer which he is being or has
   been returned, until he has been convicted in the criminal proceeding, or, if acquitted,
   until he has had reasonable opportunity to return to the state from which he was extradited.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.380. Waiver of extradition; procedure; expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.380. Waiver of extradition; procedure; expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.380. Waiver of extradition; procedure; expenses (2023)
content:
(1)  When a person charged with commission of a felony in this state or with having
      been convicted of a felony here and having escaped from confinement or broken the
      terms of his bail, probation or parole is arrested in another state and waives extradition
      proceedings, the county judge/executive of the county in which the felony was committed,
      or from which the escape was made, may, upon filing of a verified application by the
      Commonwealth's attorney or county attorney setting forth the fact of waiver and making
      all statements required by subsection (1) or subsection (2) ofKRS 440.370, enter an order designating an officer to return the fugitive to this state without
      benefit of any procedure incidental to extradition proceedings.  Upon entry of such order the officer so designated shall be authorized to go after
      and return the fugitive as the agent of this state and shall receive from the State
      Treasury the same payment for his expenses as is provided byKRS 440.090for agents acting under requisition of the Governor.  If, in attempting to reclaim the fugitive, the agent is acting within the course
      and scope of his employment, the amount due shall be paid over to the agent's employer
      instead of the agent.  Claims for reimbursement of expenses under this subsection shall be accompanied
      by certified copies of the verified application for appointment of the agent and the
      order of appointment, together with a copy of any process showing delivery of the
      fugitive to the jailer upon return to this state.  If the agent is not given possession of the fugitive for reasons beyond the agent's
      control, he, or his employer, shall nevertheless be reimbursed as provided herein,
      if it is shown that prior to his appointment as agent and before departure from the
      state the fugitive had executed in the presence of any officer authorized to administer
      an oath a written waiver stating that he consents to return to this state without
      extradition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.400. Waiver of extradition by person arrested in this state; procedure; effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.400. Waiver of extradition by person arrested in this state; procedure; effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.400. Waiver of extradition by person arrested in this state; procedure; effect (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person arrested in this state charged with having committed any crime in
      another state or alleged to have escaped from confinement, or broken the terms of
      his bail, probation or parole may waive the issuance and service of the warrant provided
      for inKRS 440.220and440.230and all other procedure incidental to extradition proceedings, by executing or subscribing
      in the presence of a judge of any District or Circuit Court within this state a writing
      which states that he consents to return to the demanding state;  provided, however,
      that before such waiver shall be executed or subscribed by such person it shall be
      the duty of such judge to inform such person of his rights to the issuance and service
      of a warrant of extradition and to obtain a writ of habeas corpus as provided for
      inKRS 440.250.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Uniform Criminal Extradition Act›KY REV ST 440.420. Returned person subject to prosecution for other crimes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Uniform Criminal Extradition Act › KY REV ST 440.420. Returned person subject to prosecution for other crimes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.420. Returned person subject to prosecution for other crimes (2023)
content:
After a person has been brought back to this state by or after waiver of extradition
   proceedings, he may be tried in this state for other crimes which he may be charged
   with having committed here as well as that specified in the requisition for his extradition.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.470. Enforcement; cooperation of courts, agencies, etc.
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.470. Enforcement; cooperation of courts, agencies, etc.
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.470. Enforcement; cooperation of courts, agencies, etc. (2023)
content:
All courts, departments, agencies, officers and employees of this state and its political
   subdivisions are hereby directed to enforce the agreement on detainers and to cooperate
   with one another and with other party states in enforcing the agreement and effectuating
   its purpose.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.480. Construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.480. Construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.480. Construction (2023)
content:
Nothing inKRS 440.450to440.510or in the agreement on detainers shall be construed to require the application ofKRS 532.080to any person on account of any conviction had in a proceeding brought to final disposition
   by reason of the use of said agreement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Penalties›KY REV ST 440.990. Penalty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Penalties › KY REV ST 440.990. Penalty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.990. Penalty (2023)
content:
Any officer who shall deliver to the agent for extradition of the demanding state
   a person in his custody under the Governor's warrant, in willful disobedience toKRS 440.250, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, on conviction, shall be fined not less than
   one hundred ($100) nor more than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or imprisoned in the
   county jail not less than ten (10) nor more than thirty (30) days, or both.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.460. “Appropriate court” defined
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.460. “Appropriate court” defined
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.460. “Appropriate court” defined (2023)
content:
The phrase “appropriate court” as used in the agreement on detainers shall, with reference to the courts of this
   state, mean the Circuit Court of competent jurisdiction.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 441. Jails and County Prisoners›KY REV ST 441.005. Definitions for chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 441. Jails and County Prisoners › KY REV ST 441.005. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 441.005. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.450. Interstate agreement on detainers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.450. Interstate agreement on detainers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.450. Interstate agreement on detainers (2023)
content:
The agreement on detainers is hereby enacted into law and entered into by the Commonwealth
   of Kentucky with all other jurisdictions legally joining therein in the form substantially
   as follows:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.490. Escape; punishment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.490. Escape; punishment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.490. Escape; punishment (2023)
content:
An escape from custody in another state while in custody in another state pursuant
   to the agreement on detainers shall be deemed, for all purposes, as an escape from
   confinement in this state and may be punished as provided byKRS 520.020to520.040and506.010, or other provision of law, as applicable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.500. Warden's duties under agreement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.500. Warden's duties under agreement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.500. Warden's duties under agreement (2023)
content:
It shall be lawful and mandatory upon the warden or other official in charge of a
   penal or correctional institution in this state to give over the person of any inmate
   thereof whenever so required by the operation of the agreement on detainers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.012. Inclusion of osteopaths within references to physicians in statutes; inclusion of Bureau of Osteopathic Specialties within references to American Board of Medical Specialties in statutes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.012. Inclusion of osteopaths within references to physicians in statutes; inclusion of Bureau of Osteopathic Specialties within references to American Board of Medical Specialties in statutes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.012. Inclusion of osteopaths within references to physicians in statutes; inclusion of Bureau of Osteopathic Specialties within references to American Board of Medical Specialties in statutes (2023)
content:
(1)  Any reference in the Kentucky Revised Statutes to “medical doctor,” “M.D.,” or “physician” shall be deemed to include a doctor of osteopathy or D.O., unless any of those terms
      is specifically excluded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XL. Crimes and Punishments›Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition›Interstate Agreement on Detainers›KY REV ST 440.510. Administrator
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XL. Crimes and Punishments › Chapter 440. Escapes, Fugitives from Justice, and Extradition › Interstate Agreement on Detainers › KY REV ST 440.510. Administrator
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 440.510. Administrator (2023)
content:
The Governor shall name a state officer or employee to serve as central administrator
   of and information agent for the agreement on detainers.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.010. Definitions for statutes generally
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.010. Definitions for statutes generally
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.010. Definitions for statutes generally (2023)
content: As used in the statute laws of this state, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.015. Statutes to be written in nontechnical language
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.015. Statutes to be written in nontechnical language
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.015. Statutes to be written in nontechnical language (2023)
content:
All bills introduced in the General Assembly after June 17, 1978, shall be written
   in nontechnical language and in a clear and coherent manner using words with common
   and everyday meanings.  Enactment of a bill by the General Assembly shall be a conclusive presumption that
   such bill conforms to this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.013. Terms “mental retardation” and “mentally retarded” not to be used in statutes; acceptable replacement terms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.013. Terms “mental retardation” and “mentally retarded” not to be used in statutes; acceptable replacement terms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.013. Terms “mental retardation” and “mentally retarded” not to be used in statutes; acceptable replacement terms (2023)
content:
(1)  Except as provided in this section, the Kentucky Revised Statutes shall no longer
      utilize the terms “mental retardation” or “mentally retarded” or abbreviations that use the letters “MR” to signify mental retardation or mentally retarded.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.050. Majority may act for all
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.050. Majority may act for all
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.050. Majority may act for all (2023)
content:
Words giving authority to three (3) or more public officers or other persons shall
   be construed as giving such authority to a majority of such officers or other persons.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.017. Conditions under which portion of bill may be void
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.017. Conditions under which portion of bill may be void
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.017. Conditions under which portion of bill may be void (2023)
content:
When a bill enrolled, either approved by the Governor or which became law without
   the Governor's signature under the provisions ofConstitution Section 88, and which has been filed with the Secretary of State, contains language which is
   not identical to that contained in the bill passed by the legislature, and when the
   variance is material, that language not conforming to the bill as passed shall be
   severed and shall be void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.030. Computation of time
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.030. Computation of time
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.030. Computation of time (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed by order of court,
         or by any applicable statute or regulation, the day of the act, event or default after
         which the designated period of time begins to run is not to be included.  The last day of the period so computed is to be included, unless it is a Saturday,
         a Sunday, a legal holiday, or a day on which the public office in which a document
         is required to be filed is actually and legally closed, in which event the period
         runs until the end of the next day which is not one (1) of the days just mentioned.  When the period of time prescribed or allowed is less than seven (7) days, intermediate
         Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.070. Penalty no bar to civil recovery
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.070. Penalty no bar to civil recovery
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.070. Penalty no bar to civil recovery (2023)
content:
A person injured by the violation of any statute may recover from the offender such
   damages as he sustained by reason of the violation, although a penalty or forfeiture
   is imposed for such violation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.060. Writings; signature must be at end; to be in English
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.060. Writings; signature must be at end; to be in English
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.060. Writings; signature must be at end; to be in English (2023)
content:
(1)  When the law requires any writing to be signed by a party thereto, it shall not
      be deemed to be signed unless the signature is subscribed at the end or close of the
      writing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.020. Singular includes plural; masculine includes feminine
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.020. Singular includes plural; masculine includes feminine
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.020. Singular includes plural; masculine includes feminine (2023)
content:
(1)  A word importing the singular number only may extend and be applied to several
      persons or things, as well as to one (1) person or thing, and a word importing the
      plural number only may extend and be applied to one (1) person or thing as well as
      to several persons or things.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.040. Adjournment of proceedings over weekend
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.040. Adjournment of proceedings over weekend
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.040. Adjournment of proceedings over weekend (2023)
content:
If the law authorizes a court, or the proceedings of any tribunal or officer, to be
   adjourned from day to day, an adjournment from Saturday until Monday shall be legal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.080. Liberal construction; statutes not retroactive; common usage; technical terms
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.080. Liberal construction; statutes not retroactive; common usage; technical terms
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.080. Liberal construction; statutes not retroactive; common usage; technical terms (2023)
content:
(1)  All statutes of this state shall be liberally construed with a view to promote
      their objects and carry out the intent of the legislature, and the rule that statutes
      in derogation of the common law are to be strictly construed shall not apply to the
      statutes of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.190. Rules of Civil Procedure to govern taking of appeals; statutes govern time of taking certain appeals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.190. Rules of Civil Procedure to govern taking of appeals; statutes govern time of taking certain appeals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.190. Rules of Civil Procedure to govern taking of appeals; statutes govern time of taking certain appeals (2023)
content:
Where a statute grants a right of appeal to the Court of Appeals in special civil
   cases, the Rules of Civil Procedure shall govern the taking of the appeal, unless
   in conflict with a specific provision of the statute, except that any notice of appeal
   required by the Rules shall be given within the time specified in the Rules.  In all cases where the statute limits the taking of the appeal to a specific time
   the appeal shall be docketed in the Court of Appeals within the time so specified.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.120. References to sections, subsections, and paragraphs; citation of Acts of General Assembly
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.120. References to sections, subsections, and paragraphs; citation of Acts of General Assembly
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.120. References to sections, subsections, and paragraphs; citation of Acts of General Assembly (2023)
content: (1)  “KRS” may be used as an abbreviation of “Kentucky Revised Statutes.”

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.145. Manner of indicating amended, created, repealed, and repealed and reenacted sections and sections not intended to be codified
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.145. Manner of indicating amended, created, repealed, and repealed and reenacted sections and sections not intended to be codified
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.145. Manner of indicating amended, created, repealed, and repealed and reenacted sections and sections not intended to be codified (2023)
content:
(1)  Bills amending an existing section of the statutes shall indicate the material
      proposed to be deleted by brackets and by striking through the material.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.082. Published statement or restatement of law does not constitute law or policy of Commonwealth; common law adopted in absence of constitutional or statutory treatment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.082. Published statement or restatement of law does not constitute law or policy of Commonwealth; common law adopted in absence of constitutional or statutory treatment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.082. Published statement or restatement of law does not constitute law or policy of Commonwealth; common law adopted in absence of constitutional or statutory treatment (2023)
content:
(1)  A statement or restatement of the law in any legal treatise, scholarly publication,
      textbook, or other explanatory text shall not constitute the law or public policy
      of the Commonwealth of Kentucky.  No Kentucky court shall treat any such publication or text as controlling authority.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.110. Offenses committed and rights accruing prior to repeal of law
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.110. Offenses committed and rights accruing prior to repeal of law
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.110. Offenses committed and rights accruing prior to repeal of law (2023)
content:
No new law shall be construed to repeal a former law as to any offense committed against
   a former law, nor as to any act done, or penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred,
   or any right accrued or claim arising under the former law, or in any way whatever
   to affect any such offense or act so committed or done, or any penalty, forfeiture
   or punishment so incurred, or any right accrued or claim arising before the new law
   takes effect, except that the proceedings thereafter had shall conform, so far as
   practicable, to the laws in force at the time of such proceedings.  If any penalty, forfeiture or punishment is mitigated by any provision of the new
   law, such provision may, by the consent of the party affected, be applied to any judgment
   pronounced after the new law takes effect.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.090. Severability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.090. Severability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.090. Severability (2023)
content:
It shall be considered that it is the intent of the General Assembly, in enacting
   any statute, that if any part of the statute be held unconstitutional the remaining
   parts shall remain in force, unless the statute provides otherwise, or unless the
   remaining parts are so essentially and inseparably connected with and dependent upon
   the unconstitutional part that it is apparent that the General Assembly would not
   have enacted the remaining parts without the unconstitutional part, or unless the
   remaining parts, standing alone, are incomplete and incapable of being executed in
   accordance with the intent of the General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.140. Titles, headings, and notes
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.140. Titles, headings, and notes
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.140. Titles, headings, and notes (2023)
content:
Title heads, chapter heads, section and subsection heads or titles, and explanatory
   notes and cross references, in the Kentucky Revised Statutes, do not constitute any
   part of the law, except as provided inKRS 355.1-107.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.100. Effect of repeal of prior repealer or amendment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.100. Effect of repeal of prior repealer or amendment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.100. Effect of repeal of prior repealer or amendment (2023)
content:
(1)  A repealed section without a delayed effective date is revived when the section
      or act that repealed it is repealed by another statute enacted at the same session
      of the General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.150. Kentucky Revised Statutes substituted for former laws
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.150. Kentucky Revised Statutes substituted for former laws
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.150. Kentucky Revised Statutes substituted for former laws (2023)
content:
The provisions of the Kentucky Revised Statutes of 1942 shall be considered as substituted
   in a continuing way for the provisions of the prior statute laws repealed by the act
   enacting the Kentucky Revised Statutes.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.130. Kentucky Revised Statutes speak for themselves; conflicts; ambiguities
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.130. Kentucky Revised Statutes speak for themselves; conflicts; ambiguities
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.130. Kentucky Revised Statutes speak for themselves; conflicts; ambiguities (2023)
content:
The Kentucky Revised Statutes of 1942 are intended to speak for themselves, and all
   sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes of 1942 shall be considered to speak as
   of the same date, except that in cases of conflict between two (2) or more sections
   or of a latent or patent ambiguity in a section, reference may be had to the Acts
   of the General Assembly from which the sections are indicated to have been derived,
   for the purpose of applying the rules of construction relating to repeal by implication
   or for the purpose of resolving the ambiguity.  Like reference may be had to any special acts or charters granted by the General
   Assembly prior to the adoption of the present Constitution, for the like purpose.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.170. Effect of 1942. act amending or repealing section of Carroll's Statutes or of former legislative act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.170. Effect of 1942. act amending or repealing section of Carroll's Statutes or of former legislative act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.170. Effect of 1942. act amending or repealing section of Carroll's Statutes or of former legislative act (2023)
content:
Any act passed at the 1942 Regular Session of the General Assembly amending or repealing
   any provision of the statute laws by reference to a section number of the Session
   Acts or of Carroll's Statutes shall be considered as amending or repealing, as the
   case may be, so much of the Kentucky Revised Statutes as is indicated in the Kentucky
   Revised Statutes as having been derived from the section of the Session Acts or of
   Carroll's Statutes so amended or repealed, and shall not be considered as reviving
   any part of Carroll's Statutes or of any Session Acts so amended other than the part
   set forth at length in the amending act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.160. Unconstitutionality of part of Kentucky Revised Statutes, effect
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.160. Unconstitutionality of part of Kentucky Revised Statutes, effect
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.160. Unconstitutionality of part of Kentucky Revised Statutes, effect (2023)
content:
If any provision of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, derived from an act that amended
   or repealed a pre-existing statute, is held unconstitutional, the general repeal of
   all former statutes by the act enacting the Kentucky Revised Statutes shall not prevent
   the pre-existing statute from being law if that appears to have been the intent of
   the General Assembly.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules›KY REV ST 447.030. Acts and compilations of former laws, evidence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules › KY REV ST 447.030. Acts and compilations of former laws, evidence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 447.030. Acts and compilations of former laws, evidence (2023)
content:
The Session Acts and Resolutions of the General Assembly heretofore or hereafter published,
   the editions of the Statutes of Kentucky by Daniel Bradford, by William Littell, by
   Littell and Swigert, by Morehead and Brown, and in part by Preston S. Loughborough,
   the edition of the Virginia Statutes by William Waller Henning, Richard H. Stanton's
   new edition of the Revised Statutes of Kentucky, the supplement to the Revised Statutes
   by Harvey Myers, the General Statutes, the Codes of Practice, the various editions
   of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes and supplements thereto published prior to 1940, and
   the various editions of Carroll's Kentucky Codes and the supplements thereto, shall
   be received, in the courts and tribunals of this state, as evidence of the statute
   laws in force in this state at the time of their publication.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules›KY REV ST 447.040. Decisions of English courts; when authority
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules › KY REV ST 447.040. Decisions of English courts; when authority
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 447.040. Decisions of English courts; when authority (2023)
content:
The decisions of the courts of Great Britain rendered since July 4, 1776, shall not
   be of binding authority in the courts of Kentucky.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes›KY REV ST 446.200. Demurrer, motion to quash, construction
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 446. Construction of Statutes › KY REV ST 446.200. Demurrer, motion to quash, construction
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 446.200. Demurrer, motion to quash, construction (2023)
content:
As used in any statute that relates to criminal procedure, the terms “demurrer,” “motion to quash” or similar terms shall be construed to mean the motion raising a defense or objection
   as provided in the Rules of Criminal Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules›KY REV ST 447.025. Repeal of statutes enacted prior to § 1942
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules › KY REV ST 447.025. Repeal of statutes enacted prior to § 1942
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 447.025. Repeal of statutes enacted prior to § 1942 (2023)
content:
All statute laws of the Commonwealth of a general and public nature enacted prior
   to the 1942 Regular Session of the General Assembly, except the Codes of Practice
   and such statute laws as are continued in force by express provision in the body of
   sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, are hereby repealed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts›KY REV ST 451.170. Terms of judicial sales
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts › KY REV ST 451.170. Terms of judicial sales
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 451.170. Terms of judicial sales (2023)
content:
(1)  Judicial sales of property shall be for cash, or on reasonable credit or partly
      for cash and partly on reasonable credit, as the court directs;  but a sale of personal
      property shall not be on a longer credit than four (4) months.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts›KY REV ST 451.190. Taxes on property sold at judicial sale
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts › KY REV ST 451.190. Taxes on property sold at judicial sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 451.190. Taxes on property sold at judicial sale (2023)
content:
The court may, in actions for sale of real property, determine summarily, with or
   without written pleadings, the amount of any state, city or district taxes or assessments
   upon the property to be sold, and shall provide for their payment in the judgment.  If the judgment does not so provide, the purchaser shall be entitled, at any time
   before the payment of the purchase price, to a credit for the amount of the taxes
   and assessments.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.040. Responsibility for payment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.040. Responsibility for payment (2023)
content: (1)  Except as provided by subsection (2):

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts›KY REV ST 451.200. Liability of receiver or depository of court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts › KY REV ST 451.200. Liability of receiver or depository of court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 451.200. Liability of receiver or depository of court (2023)
content:
A liability incurred by any person as receiver or depository of money or property
   committed to his charge by order of the court shall rank with debts due to the state
   and shall have priority over other debts owed by the receiver or depository and precedence
   over any mortgage or lien upon the property of the receiver or depository made after
   his appointment or designation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts›KY REV ST 451.180. Bond of purchaser at judicial sale, to whom made payable; enforcement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 451. Practice in Circuit Courts › KY REV ST 451.180. Bond of purchaser at judicial sale, to whom made payable; enforcement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 451.180. Bond of purchaser at judicial sale, to whom made payable; enforcement (2023)
content:
The bond given by a purchaser of property at a judicial sale shall be made payable
   to the circuit clerk.  Proceedings on the bond may be had in the name of the clerk to whom it is made payable
   on the relation of the person interested, and the person interested shall be responsible
   for the costs.  The performance of the bond may be summarily enforced by orders of court, and by
   proceedings for contempt.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.020. Criminal prosecution, costs; collection
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.020. Criminal prosecution, costs; collection
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.020. Criminal prosecution, costs; collection (2023)
content:
(1)  The defendant in a criminal action shall be adjudged to pay the cost of all continuances
      in his behalf.  The cost of such continuances shall be collected by process as in civil cases.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLI. Laws›Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules›KY REV ST 447.154. Laws not to limit right of Court of Justice to promulgate rules
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLI. Laws › Chapter 447. Public Laws in Force; Court Rules › KY REV ST 447.154. Laws not to limit right of Court of Justice to promulgate rules
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 447.154. Laws not to limit right of Court of Justice to promulgate rules (2023)
content:
No act creating, repealing, or modifying any statute shall be construed directly,
   or by implication, to limit the right of the Court of Justice to promulgate rules
   from time to time or to supersede, modify, or amend any rule so promulgated.  Nor shall any statute be construed to limit in any manner the power of the Court
   of Justice to make rules governing practice and procedure in the courts.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.050. Cost bill of successful party; attorney's fee
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.050. Cost bill of successful party; attorney's fee
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.050. Cost bill of successful party; attorney's fee (2023)
content:
Clerks shall tax one (1) attorney's fee only in the bill of costs of the successful
   party at the termination of the action, but no attorney's fee shall be taxed in any
   court if the amount in controversy, exclusive of interest and costs, does not exceed
   fifty dollars ($50), and no garnishee shall be allowed an attorney's fee.  The bill of costs of the successful party shall include, in addition to other costs
   taxed, the tax on law process and official seals, all fees of officers with which
   the party is chargeable in the case, postage on depositions, the cost of copy of any
   pleading or exhibit obtained, the cost of any copies made exhibits and the allowance
   to witnesses, which the court may by order confine to not more than two (2) witnesses
   to any one (1) point.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.060. Attorney's fees allowed (2023)
content:
(1)  If the successful party is represented by a licensed attorney, the following
      attorney's fees shall be allowed:
