content:
(1)  Except as provided inKRS 5.005and286.12-135, and notwithstanding any other statute to the contrary, the venue for any civil action
      that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.010. Commonwealth not liable for costs; exception in civil actions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.010. Commonwealth not liable for costs; exception in civil actions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.010. Commonwealth not liable for costs; exception in civil actions (2023)
content:
No judgment for costs shall be rendered against the Commonwealth in any action prosecuted
   by or against the Commonwealth in its own right, unless specifically provided by statute;
   provided, however, that in any civil action filed in any court of competent jurisdiction
   by or against the Commonwealth of Kentucky, the costs may be paid by the Commonwealth
   when such costs are approved and allowed by the judge of the court in which the case
   was filed.  Costs shall not exceed the fees allowed for similar services in other civil actions.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.100. New trial on payment of costs; effect of nonpayment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.100. New trial on payment of costs; effect of nonpayment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.100. New trial on payment of costs; effect of nonpayment (2023)
content:
The party to whom a new trial is granted upon payment of costs shall, within forty
   (40) days thereafter, pay the costs of the former trial.  If he fails to pay the costs within that time, the court may, upon motion made by
   the adverse party within ten (10) days after the expiration of the forty (40) day
   period, set aside the order granting a new trial and enter judgment on the verdict
   already rendered.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.110. Injunction, costs on dissolution of
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.110. Injunction, costs on dissolution of
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.110. Injunction, costs on dissolution of (2023)
content:
If an injunction is dissolved, the plaintiff shall pay the costs occasioned by it,
   unless the court otherwise orders.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.070. Cost of continuance in civil action; dismissal; amendment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.070. Cost of continuance in civil action; dismissal; amendment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.070. Cost of continuance in civil action; dismissal; amendment (2023)
content:
(1)  If a party to a civil action obtains a continuance, or files an amendment that
      causes a continuance, he shall pay the costs occasioned thereby.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.090. Removal of action; tribunal giving final judgment to award costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.090. Removal of action; tribunal giving final judgment to award costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.090. Removal of action; tribunal giving final judgment to award costs (2023)
content:
When, by any procedure, an action is taken from one tribunal to another, and the latter
   gives final judgment, and proceeds to execute it without remanding the cause to the
   inferior tribunal, the tribunal rendering the final decision shall adjudge costs according
   to the provisions of this chapter, and issue execution therefor.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.080. Motion or rule; no attorney's fee allowed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.080. Motion or rule; no attorney's fee allowed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.080. Motion or rule; no attorney's fee allowed (2023)
content:
A motion or rule of court shall be considered an action, but when it is made in a
   pending suit or action, no attorney's fee shall be recovered as part of the costs
   of the motion or rule.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.140. Fiduciaries, liability for costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.140. Fiduciaries, liability for costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.140. Fiduciaries, liability for costs (2023)
content:
A personal representative, guardian, assignee, curator, conservator or trustee in
   an action shall, if unsuccessful, be adjudged to pay costs as other litigants, but
   the judgment for costs in such cases shall only be against the assets that have, or
   may, come into the hands of the fiduciary.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.150. Next friend or relator, when to pay or recover costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.150. Next friend or relator, when to pay or recover costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.150. Next friend or relator, when to pay or recover costs (2023)
content:
A next friend or relator on a bond shall, upon failure in the action, be adjudged
   to pay the defendant his costs.  If the plaintiff succeeds, the next friend or relator shall be adjudged his costs
   against the defendant.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.130. Suit to remove officer
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.130. Suit to remove officer
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.130. Suit to remove officer (2023)
content:
Any person who takes steps in any court to remove any officer from office, and fails
   in so doing, shall pay the officer his costs expended in the defense of the procedure.  If the officer is removed, the person instituting and carrying on the procedure
   shall be adjudged his costs against the officer.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.190. “Poor person” defined; when allowed to sue without paying costs; application required; treatment of inmates
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.190. “Poor person” defined; when allowed to sue without paying costs; application required; treatment of inmates
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.190. “Poor person” defined; when allowed to sue without paying costs; application required; treatment of inmates (2023)
content:
(1)  A court shall allow a poor person residing in this state to file or defend any
      action or appeal therein without paying costs, whereupon he shall have any counsel
      that the court assigns him and shall have from all officers all needful services and
      process, including the preparation of necessary transcripts for appeal, without any
      fees, except such as are included in the costs recovered from the adverse party, and
      shall not be required to post any bond except in an amount and manner reasonable under
      the circumstances of his poverty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.200. Recovery of costs by insolvent party; endorsement of costs to protect claims of officers and witnesses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.200. Recovery of costs by insolvent party; endorsement of costs to protect claims of officers and witnesses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.200. Recovery of costs by insolvent party; endorsement of costs to protect claims of officers and witnesses (2023)
content:
Whenever a party who recovers a judgment for the costs of the action or of a continuance,
   is insolvent or in doubtful circumstances, the court, on motion of any person interested,
   shall endorse the costs so recovered, or as much thereof as necessary, for the benefit
   of the officers and witnesses who have rendered services in the action, in so far
   as they are embraced in the judgment then rendered, and they shall be entitled to
   so much of the costs as will satisfy their fees.  The endorsement shall secure the officers and witnesses a preference to all transfers,
   set-offs and attorney's liens.  The endorsement shall be copied on the execution that issues for the costs, and
   shall show what part each officer and witness is entitled to, and authorize each to
   receive the amount so endorsed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.160. Tender of amount in controversy before appeal, effect on costs
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.160. Tender of amount in controversy before appeal, effect on costs
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.160. Tender of amount in controversy before appeal, effect on costs (2023)
content:
If a party, before an appeal is taken, tenders to the adverse party the amount he
   is willing to pay and the tender is refused and, upon appeal by the party to whom
   the tender was made the amount recovered does not exceed the amount tendered, the
   appellant shall pay the costs in the court trying the appeal;  but if the amount recovered
   upon the appeal is for more than the amount tendered, the appellant shall recover
   his costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.170. Court of Appeals or Supreme Court; costs on reversal of judgment by
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.170. Court of Appeals or Supreme Court; costs on reversal of judgment by
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.170. Court of Appeals or Supreme Court; costs on reversal of judgment by (2023)
content:
On a reversal of a judgment in the Court of Appeals or Supreme Court, the appellant
   shall recover of the appellee such costs as the Court of Appeals or Supreme Court,
   in its discretion, awards.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.255. Definitions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.255. Definitions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.255. Definitions (2023)
content: As used inKRS 453.260and453.265, unless the context otherwise requires:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.011. Declaration of public policy on encouragement of dispute resolution through negotiation and settlement
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.011. Declaration of public policy on encouragement of dispute resolution through negotiation and settlement
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.011. Declaration of public policy on encouragement of dispute resolution through negotiation and settlement (2023)
content:
It is the policy of this Commonwealth to encourage the peaceable resolution of disputes
   and the early, voluntary settlement of litigation through negotiation and mediation.  To the extent it is consistent with other laws, the courts and state governmental
   agencies are authorized and encouraged to refer disputing parties to mediation before
   trial or hearing.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.260. Additional costs in certain civil actions; causes for denial of additional costs; award of attorney fees and other expenses; computation of fees of attorneys and expert witnesses; exceptions to application of provisions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.260. Additional costs in certain civil actions; causes for denial of additional costs; award of attorney fees and other expenses; computation of fees of attorneys and expert witnesses; exceptions to application of provisions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.260. Additional costs in certain civil actions; causes for denial of additional costs; award of attorney fees and other expenses; computation of fees of attorneys and expert witnesses; exceptions to application of provisions (2023)
content:
(1)  In addition to any costs which are awarded as prescribed by statute, a court
      shall award costs to any party which prevails by a final adjudication on the merits
      in any of the following:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.265. Application of KRS § 453.260
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.265. Application of KRS § 453.260
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.265. Application of KRS § 453.260 (2023)
content:
(1)  The provisions ofKRS 453.260shall apply only to civil actions initiated after July 15, 1982, except in the case
      of a court proceeding to review an administrative review board decision, in which
      case the provisions ofKRS 453.260shall apply only when the administrative review process was initiated after July
      15, 1982.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.050. Infants, when to be excluded from courtroom
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.050. Infants, when to be excluded from courtroom
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.050. Infants, when to be excluded from courtroom (2023)
content:
In any civil action for slander, seduction or breach of promise of marriage, the judge
   shall exclude from the courtroom, and from the hearing of the testimony and arguments,
   all infants under the age of sixteen (16) years, except those who are witnesses in
   the case or kin to one (1) of the parties.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.020. Voter, when exempt from arrest on civil process; effect of violation
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.020. Voter, when exempt from arrest on civil process; effect of violation
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.020. Voter, when exempt from arrest on civil process; effect of violation (2023)
content:
No sheriff shall execute any civil process of arrest upon any voter attending an election
   at which he has the right to vote, or in going to or returning from such an election.  Execution by a sheriff of any such process contrary to this section is void.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.040. Trespass, joint or several damages for
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.040. Trespass, joint or several damages for
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.040. Trespass, joint or several damages for (2023)
content:
In actions of trespass the jury may assess joint or several damages against the defendants.  When the jury finds several damages, the judgment shall be in favor of the plaintiff
   against each defendant for the several damages, without regard to the amount of damages
   claimed in the petition, and shall include a joint judgment for the costs.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 453. Costs›KY REV ST 453.210. Insolvent estates, claims against
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 453. Costs › KY REV ST 453.210. Insolvent estates, claims against
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 453.210. Insolvent estates, claims against (2023)
content:
If, in the settlement of insolvent estates, a party presents a claim against the estate
   and it is not allowed, he shall pay the cost occasioned thereby, except the attorney's
   fee.  No attorney's fee shall be allowed any claimant in any case against an insolvent
   estate.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.030. Forcible entry or detainer, how notice served
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.030. Forcible entry or detainer, how notice served
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.030. Forcible entry or detainer, how notice served (2023)
content:
If the officer directed to serve notice on the defendant in forcible entry or detainer
   proceedings cannot find the defendant on the premises mentioned in the writ, he may
   explain and leave a copy of the notice with any member of the defendant's family thereon
   over sixteen (16) years of age, and if no such person is found he may serve the notice
   by posting a copy thereof in a conspicuous place on the premises and by mailing a
   copy of the notice to the mailing address of the premises mentioned in the writ by
   regular mail through the United States Postal Service, postage prepaid.  The notice shall state the time and place of meeting of the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.060. Provisions concerning bond required before injunction granted
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.060. Provisions concerning bond required before injunction granted
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.060. Provisions concerning bond required before injunction granted (2023)
content:
(1)  If an injunction be granted to stay proceedings upon a levy made under an execution,
      and the party applying for the injunction desire to discharge the levy, he shall execute
      a bond to the effect that he will satisfy the execution to the extent to which the
      injunction may be dissolved, not exceeding the value of the property released;  and
      upon the execution of such bond, and the issuing of the injunction, the levy shall
      be discharged.  If he does not desire to release the levy, he may execute a bond to the effect that,
      upon a dissolution of the injunction, in whole or in part, he will have the property,
      or its value, forthcoming and subject to the order of the court;  and, upon the execution
      of such bond, and the issuing of the injunction, the property levied on shall be delivered
      to him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.065. Order of injunction not to issue until bond executed
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.065. Order of injunction not to issue until bond executed
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.065. Order of injunction not to issue until bond executed (2023)
content:
The order of injunction shall not be issued by the clerk until a bond, as is required
   byKRS 454.060, with good surety of the party obtaining the injunction, shall have been executed
   in his office.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.095. Cause of action to be stated in judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.095. Cause of action to be stated in judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.095. Cause of action to be stated in judgment (2023)
content:
The cause of action shall be briefly stated in the judgment, or in a writing to be
   filed as pleadings in an action.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.070. Acceptance of sureties by clerk
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.070. Acceptance of sureties by clerk
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.070. Acceptance of sureties by clerk (2023)
content:
Sureties in injunction bonds shall be accepted by the clerk under the same responsibilities
   as in other cases of sureties accepted by him.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.085. Damages if injunction dissolved
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.085. Damages if injunction dissolved
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.085. Damages if injunction dissolved (2023)
content:
Upon the dissolution, in whole or in part, of an injunction to stay proceedings upon
   a judgment, the damages shall be assessed by the court;  which may hear the evidence
   and decide in a summary way, or may, at its discretion, cause a jury to be impaneled
   to find the damages.  If the collection, payment or use of money be enjoined, the damages may be any rate
   percent on the sum released by the dissolution, which, in the discretion of the court,
   may be proper, not exceeding ten percent.  And, if the delivery of property have been delayed by the injunction, the value
   of the use, hire or rent thereof shall be assessed;  judgment shall be rendered against
   the party who obtained the injunction for the damages assessed;  and the assessment
   shall be conclusive against the surety of such party.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.080. Judgment to be enjoined in court rendering; affidavit
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.080. Judgment to be enjoined in court rendering; affidavit
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.080. Judgment to be enjoined in court rendering; affidavit (2023)
content:
An injunction to stay proceedings on a judgment shall not be granted, in an action
   brought by the party seeking the injunction, in any other court than that in which
   the judgment was rendered.  Nor shall such injunction be granted, unless the party applying therefor make affidavit
   that no injunction has been previously granted to stay the proceedings on such judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.100. Effect of judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.100. Effect of judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.100. Effect of judgment (2023)
content:
Such judgment shall authorize the same proceedings as judgments rendered in actions,
   and the confession shall operate as a release of errors.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.110. When infant may vacate judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.110. When infant may vacate judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.110. When infant may vacate judgment (2023)
content:
An infant may, within twelve (12) months after attaining the age of eighteen (18)
   years, show cause against a judgment, unless it be for a tort done by, or for necessaries
   furnished to, the infant;  or unless it be rendered upon a set-off or counterclaim
   stated in an answer;  but the vacation of such judgment shall not affect the title
   of a bona fide purchaser under it.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.090. Procedure for confession of judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.090. Procedure for confession of judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.090. Procedure for confession of judgment (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.135. When defendant exempt from service of process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.135. When defendant exempt from service of process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.135. When defendant exempt from service of process (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions ofKRS 421.180, the defendant shall have no privilege of exemption from the service of the process
   on a holiday or Sunday, except from an arrest, by reason of his attendance at any
   muster, election, or order of survey, or as a witness at any court or other place.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.150. Procedure for restoration of money received by the Commonwealth where judgment rendered upon constructive service is modified or set aside
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.150. Procedure for restoration of money received by the Commonwealth where judgment rendered upon constructive service is modified or set aside
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.150. Procedure for restoration of money received by the Commonwealth where judgment rendered upon constructive service is modified or set aside (2023)
content:
When the Commonwealth shall have received money under a judgment rendered upon constructive
   service, and the defendant did not appear, and such judgment is thereafter modified
   or set aside under the provisions of the Rules of Civil Procedure, upon a retrial,
   the court in making an order for the restoration of such money, shall direct the proper
   financial officer of the Commonwealth to draw his warrant upon the Treasurer for the
   proper amount in favor of the party in whose favor the order of restoration may be
   made, and it shall thereupon become the duty of such officer to draw his warrant in
   obedience to such order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.125. Process may issue and bonds may be taken on holidays
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.125. Process may issue and bonds may be taken on holidays
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.125. Process may issue and bonds may be taken on holidays (2023)
content:
It shall be no objection to any process, writ, summons, affidavit or order for a provisional
   remedy that it was issued, made or dated on a holiday;  nor shall it be an objection
   to any bond given by or for any party to an action, or taken by an officer in the
   course of the same, that it was made or dated on any such day.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.145. Court may appoint person to serve particular process
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.145. Court may appoint person to serve particular process
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.145. Court may appoint person to serve particular process (2023)
content:
The court, for good cause, may appoint a person to serve a particular process or order,
   and he shall have the same power to execute it which a sheriff has.  His return must be verified by his affidavit.  He shall be entitled to the fees allowed to sheriffs for similar services.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.140. Officers to whom process to be directed; provisional remedies
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.140. Officers to whom process to be directed; provisional remedies
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.140. Officers to whom process to be directed; provisional remedies (2023)
content:
(1)  Every process in an action or proceeding shall be directed to the sheriff of
      the county;  or, if he be a party, or be interested, to the coroner;  or, if he be
      interested, to the jailer;  or, if all these officers be interested, to any constable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.160. Lien created only by attachment or judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.160. Lien created only by attachment or judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.160. Lien created only by attachment or judgment (2023)
content:
No lien on the property of a defendant constructively summoned shall be created otherwise
   than by an attachment, as is provided inKRS 425.301to425.316, or by judgment;  nor shall any person be restrained from paying or delivering any
   money or property in his hands belonging or due to such defendant, by notice indorsed
   on the summons, or otherwise than by attachment or judgment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.155. Effect of new trial on title to property sold under attachment or judgment
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.155. Effect of new trial on title to property sold under attachment or judgment
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.155. Effect of new trial on title to property sold under attachment or judgment (2023)
content:
The title of purchasers in good faith to any property sold under an attachment or
   judgment shall not be affected by a new trial allowed a defendant constructively summoned,
   except the title of property obtained by the plaintiff and not bought of him in good
   faith by others.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.180. Officer may require affidavit of surety's qualifications
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.180. Officer may require affidavit of surety's qualifications
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.180. Officer may require affidavit of surety's qualifications (2023)
content:
An officer whose duty it is to take a surety in any bond provided for by any statute
   derived from the former Civil Code, or by the Rules of Civil Procedure may require
   the person offered as surety to make affidavit of his qualifications, which affidavit
   may be made before such officer.  The taking of such an affidavit shall not exempt the officer from any liability
   to which he might otherwise be subject for taking insufficient security.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.170. Substitution of affirmation for oath
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.170. Substitution of affirmation for oath
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.170. Substitution of affirmation for oath (2023)
content:
An oath required by any statute derived from the former Civil Code, or by the Rules
   of Civil Procedure may be substituted by the affirmation of a person who is conscientiously
   opposed to taking an oath.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.165. Personal judgment against defendant constructively summoned forbidden
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.165. Personal judgment against defendant constructively summoned forbidden
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.165. Personal judgment against defendant constructively summoned forbidden (2023)
content:
No personal judgment shall be rendered against a defendant constructively summoned,
   and who has not appeared in the action, except as provided inKRS 454.210.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.190. Commonwealth may prosecute remedy without bond
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.190. Commonwealth may prosecute remedy without bond
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.190. Commonwealth may prosecute remedy without bond (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise expressly provided by law, no bond, obligation or security shall
   be required of the Commonwealth or any of its agencies or officers acting for or in
   behalf of the Commonwealth in order to prosecute any remedy in the courts of this
   state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.185. Qualifications of sureties
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.185. Qualifications of sureties
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.185. Qualifications of sureties (2023)
content:
The surety in every bond provided for by any statute derived from the former Civil
   Code, or by the Rules of Civil Procedure must be a resident of this state, and be
   worth double the sum to be secured beyond the amount of his debts, and have property
   liable to execution in this state equal to the sum to be secured.  If there be two (2) or more sureties in the same bond they must, in the aggregate,
   have the qualifications prescribed in this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.220. Personal jurisdiction of courts over nonresidents in certain domestic relations matters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.220. Personal jurisdiction of courts over nonresidents in certain domestic relations matters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.220. Personal jurisdiction of courts over nonresidents in certain domestic relations matters (2023)
content:
A court in any matrimonial action or family court proceeding involving a demand for
   support, alimony, maintenance, distributive awards, or special relief in matrimonial
   actions may exercise personal jurisdiction over the respondent or defendant notwithstanding
   the fact that he or she no longer is a resident or domiciliary of this state, or over
   his or her executor or administrator, if the party seeking support is a resident of
   or domiciled in this state at the time the demand is made, if this state was the matrimonial
   domicile of the parties before their separation;  the defendant abandoned the plaintiff
   in this state;  or the claim for support, alimony, maintenance, distributive awards,
   or special relief in matrimonial actions accrued under the laws of this state.  The action shall be filed within one (1) year of the date the respondent or defendant
   became a nonresident of, or moved his domicile from, this state.  Service of process may be made by personal service if the defendant or respondent
   is found within the state or by service through the use ofKRS 454.210(3).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 454.270. Appointment of Secretary of State as agent for service of process; service of process; return; applicability
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.270. Appointment of Secretary of State as agent for service of process; service of process; return; applicability
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.270. Appointment of Secretary of State as agent for service of process; service of process; return; applicability (2023)
content:
(1)  Any nonresident operator or owner of any watercraft who accepts the privilege
      extended by the laws of this state to nonresidents to operate watercraft or have them
      operated within state shall, by such acceptance and by the operation of such watercraft
      within this state, make the Secretary of State the agent of himself or his personal
      representative for the service of process in any civil action instituted in the courts
      of this state against the operator or owner, or the personal representative of the
      operator or owner, arising out of or by reason of any accident or collision or damage
      occurring within this state in which the watercraft is involved.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 455.140. Procedure for bringing federal prisoner to trial in state court on felony charge; reimbursement of expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 455.140. Procedure for bringing federal prisoner to trial in state court on felony charge; reimbursement of expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 455.140. Procedure for bringing federal prisoner to trial in state court on felony charge; reimbursement of expenses (2023)
content:
The Commonwealth's attorney may enter into an agreement with representatives of the
   federal government for conveyance of a federal prisoner to a Circuit Court of this
   state to stand trial therein on a felony charge, upon condition that such prisoner
   shall remain in the custody of an agent of the United States and be returned to the
   federal penitentiary for completion of the term of confinement there following conclusion
   of the trial in the Circuit Court, and thereafter to be returned to this state to
   serve any sentence imposed here.  It may also be agreed that the state will bear the expense of such conveyance.  The Commonwealth's attorney shall then file in the Circuit Court his verified petition
   for writ of habeas corpus ad prosequendum stating facts as to the situation of the
   prisoner, the charge against him and date set for trial, the necessity of securing
   the prisoner for trial prior to his release in due course by federal authorities and
   the terms of the agreement which has been reached with such authorities.  If the court deems the petition sufficient, it shall issue the writ and if the state
   is required to pay the expense the writ shall designate the officer to transport and
   guard the prisoner and such officer shall be reimbursed from the State Treasury for
   expenses incurred in the amount and manner provided inKRS 64.070(1);  provided, however, that if a United States marshal or other federal official is
   designated by the court to transport and guard the prisoner such marshal or officer
   shall be reimbursed at the rate authorized by federal law or regulations.  The Circuit Court shall enter an order of allowance of expenses for the officer
   upon conclusion of the trial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection›KY REV ST 456.040. Review of petition for interpersonal protective order; temporary interpersonal protective order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.040. Review of petition for interpersonal protective order; temporary interpersonal protective order
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 456.040. Review of petition for interpersonal protective order; temporary interpersonal protective order (2023)
content:
(1)  (a) The court shall review a petition for an interpersonal protective order immediately
         upon its filing.  If the review indicates that dating violence and abuse, stalking, or sexual assault
         exists, the court shall summons the parties to an evidentiary hearing not more than
         fourteen (14) days in the future.  If the review indicates that such a basis does not exist, the court may consider
         an amended petition or dismiss the petition without prejudice.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 454. Miscellaneous Civil Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 454.275. Personal service on person whose marital domicile is in Kentucky

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 454.350. Time within which judge, commissioner or hearing officer must issue judgment or report; certification of reason when delay occurs (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 455.150. Procedure for bringing material witness in state felony trial from federal prison; reimbursement of expenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 455.150. Procedure for bringing material witness in state felony trial from federal prison; reimbursement of expenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 455.150. Procedure for bringing material witness in state felony trial from federal prison; reimbursement of expenses (2023)
content:
When a material witness for the Commonwealth in a felony prosecution pending in a
   court of this state is confined under judgment of conviction in any federal penal
   institution, the Commonwealth's attorney may enter into an agreement with the appropriate
   federal authorities for conveyance of the witness at the expense of this state to
   the Circuit Court in which the trial is pending, and after trial, for return to the
   federal penitentiary.   The Commonwealth's attorney shall move the Circuit Court for an order for the attendance
   of the witness and shall state the situation of the prisoner, the date set for trial
   of the case, the importance of his testimony to the Commonwealth, and the agreement
   of the federal authorities to produce the prisoner in court.  The Circuit Court shall designate the officer to transport and guard the prisoner
   and such person shall be reimbursed from the State Treasury for his expenses in the
   amount and manner provided inKRS 64.070(1);  provided, however, that if a United States marshal or other federal official is
   designated by the court to transport and guard the prisoner such marshal or officer
   shall be reimbursed at the rate authorized by federal law or regulations.  The Circuit Court shall enter an order of allowance of expenses for the officer
   upon conclusion of the trial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions›KY REV ST 455.160. Issuance of summons for violation of KRS § 514.040
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 455. Miscellaneous Criminal Practice Provisions › KY REV ST 455.160. Issuance of summons for violation of KRS § 514.040
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 455.160. Issuance of summons for violation of KRS § 514.040 (2023)
content:
In the event of a charge for a violation ofKRS 514.040with an amount of one hundred dollars ($100) or less, a summons shall be issued prior
   to an arrest warrant.  An arrest warrant shall not be issued until the person charged fails to respond
   to the summons, unless the issuing judge determines that, based upon previous offenses
   or charges, an arrest of the person is necessary in order to reasonably assure his
   or her appearance in court.

   ofSection 10 of the Kentucky Constitution, requires the production of a paper copy of the warrant at the time it is served,
   and otherwise complies with any other requirements for search warrants generally,
   including those pertaining to their filing, execution, and return.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.070. citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 456.070. When protective order becomes effective and binding on respondent; mutual protective orders; petition hearing testimony later admissible only for impeachment purposes; interpersonal protective order intake center (2023)
content:
(1)  A temporary or ordinary interpersonal protective order shall become effective
      and binding on the respondent when the respondent is given notice of the existence
      and terms of the order by a peace officer or the court or upon personal service of
      the order, whichever is earlier.  A peace officer or court giving notice of an unserved order shall make all reasonable
      efforts to arrange for the order's personal service upon the respondent.  Once effective, a peace officer or the court may enforce the order's terms and act
      immediately upon their violation.

content:

   action under KRS Chapter 403, the party initiating the action shall make known to
   the court the existence and status of any interpersonal protective orders, which shall
   remain effective and enforceable until superseded by order of the court in which the
   KRS Chapter 403 case is filed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection›KY REV ST 456.140. Filing copy of foreign protective order; effect; required affidavit; certification by issuing court; uncertified order
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.140. Filing copy of foreign protective order; effect; required affidavit; certification by issuing court; uncertified order

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection›KY REV ST 456.110. Entry of forms, affidavits, and orders of protection into Law Information Network of Kentucky
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.110. Entry of forms, affidavits, and orders of protection into Law Information Network of Kentucky
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 456.110. Entry of forms, affidavits, and orders of protection into Law Information Network of Kentucky (2023)
content:
(1)  All forms, affidavits, and orders of protection issued or filed pursuant to this
      chapter which require entry into the Law Information Network of Kentucky shall be
      entered on forms prescribed by the Administrative Office of the Courts after consultation
      with the Justice and Public Safety Cabinet.  If the provisions of an interpersonal protective order are contained in an order
      which is narrative in nature, the prescribed form shall be used in addition to the
      narrative order.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection›KY REV ST 456.120. Foreign protective orders
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.120. Foreign protective orders
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 456.120. Foreign protective orders (2023)
content:
(1)  All foreign protective orders shall have the rebuttable presumption of validity.  The validity of a foreign protective order shall only be determined by a court of
      competent jurisdiction.  Until a foreign protective order is declared to be invalid by a court of competent
      jurisdiction, it shall be given full faith and credit by all peace officers and courts
      in the Commonwealth.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection›KY REV ST 456.180. Violation of order of protection
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 456. Civil Orders of Protection › KY REV ST 456.180. Violation of order of protection
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 456.180. Violation of order of protection (2023)
content:

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 457.040. Power of attorney is durable (2023)
content:
A power of attorney created under this chapter is durable unless it expressly provides
   that it is terminated by the incapacity of the principal.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 457.060. Validity of power of attorney (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 457. Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006)›KY REV ST 457.080. Nomination of conservator or guardian; relation of agent to court-appointed fiduciary
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 457. Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006) › KY REV ST 457.080. Nomination of conservator or guardian; relation of agent to court-appointed fiduciary
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 457.080. Nomination of conservator or guardian; relation of agent to court-appointed fiduciary (2023)
content:
(1)  In a power of attorney, a principal may nominate a limited conservator, conservator,
      limited guardian, or guardian of the principal's estate or a limited guardian or guardian
      of the principal's person for consideration by the court if protective proceedings
      for the principal's estate or person are begun after the principal executes the power
      of attorney.  As outlined inKRS 387.600, the nomination shall be treated as an indication of the principal's preference as
      to the person or entity to be appointed as his or her limited conservator, conservator,
      limited guardian, or guardian, and the court shall give the preference due consideration.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 457. Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006)›KY REV ST 457.090. When power of attorney effective
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions › Chapter 457. Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006) › KY REV ST 457.090. When power of attorney effective
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 457.090. When power of attorney effective (2023)
content:
(1)  A power of attorney is effective when executed unless the principal provides
      in the power of attorney that it becomes effective at a future date or upon the occurrence
      of a future event or contingency.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title XLII. Miscellaneous Practice Provisions›Chapter 457. Uniform Power of Attorney Act (2006)›KY REV ST 457.070. Meaning and effect of power of attorney

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 457.070. Meaning and effect of power of attorney (2023)
content:
The meaning and effect of a power of attorney is determined by the law of the jurisdiction
   indicated in the power of attorney and, in the absence of an indication of jurisdiction,
   by the law of the jurisdiction in which the power of attorney was executed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.095. Alternative sentence of community work
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 500. General Provisions › KY REV ST 500.095. Alternative sentence of community work
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.095. Alternative sentence of community work (2023)
content:
(1)  In every case in which a person pleads guilty to or is convicted of a crime punishable
      by imprisonment, the judge shall consider whether the person should be sentenced to
      a term of community service as an alternative to the prison term.  The term of community service shall not be shorter than the length of the prison
      term nor longer than twice the length of the prison term.  Failure to complete the prescribed term of community service shall be deemed a probation
      violation and shall subject the defendant to serve the prison service originally fixed
      by the court or jury.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 500. General Provisions › KY REV ST 500.093. Prohibition against court or law enforcement agency retaining firearms or ammunition to prevent their transfer or sale
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.093. Prohibition against court or law enforcement agency retaining firearms or ammunition to prevent their transfer or sale (2023)
content:
No court or law enforcement agency shall retain a firearm or ammunition for official
   use for the purpose of avoiding transfer of the firearm or ammunition to the Department
   of Kentucky State Police underKRS 237.090or500.090, or other statute to avoid its being sold pursuant toKRS 16.220.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.040. Restrictions on applicability

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.040. Restrictions on applicability (2023)
content:
(1)  The provisions of this code shall not apply to any offense committed prior to
      January 1, 1975, notwithstanding the provisions ofKRS 446.110.  Such an offense must be construed and punished according to the provisions of law
      existing at the time of the commission thereof in the same manner as if this code
      had not been enacted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.070. Burden of proof; defenses
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 500. General Provisions › KY REV ST 500.070. Burden of proof; defenses
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.070. Burden of proof; defenses (2023)
content:
(1)  The Commonwealth has the burden of proving every element of the case beyond a
      reasonable doubt, except as provided in subsection (3).  This provision, however, does not require disproof of any element that is entitled
      a “defense,” as that term is used in this code, unless the evidence tending to support
      the defense is of such probative force that in the absence of countervailing evidence
      the defendant would be entitled to a directed verdict of acquittal.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.130. Operation of unmanned aircraft system; Citizen’s Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 500. General Provisions › KY REV ST 500.130. Operation of unmanned aircraft system; Citizen’s Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.130. Operation of unmanned aircraft system; Citizen’s Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act (2023)

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.020. Offenses defined by statute; common law abolished

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.020. Offenses defined by statute; common law abolished (2023)
content:

      offense unless designated a crime or violation under this code or another statute
      of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 500. General Provisions›KY REV ST 500.110. Trial of prisoner on untried indictment within 180. days after prisoner's request for final disposition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 500. General Provisions › KY REV ST 500.110. Trial of prisoner on untried indictment within 180. days after prisoner's request for final disposition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 500.110. Trial of prisoner on untried indictment within 180. days after prisoner's request for final disposition (2023)
content:
Whenever a person has entered upon a term of imprisonment in a penal or correctional
   institution of this state, and whenever during the continuance of the term of imprisonment
   there is pending in any jurisdiction of this state any untried indictment, information
   or complaint on the basis of which a detainer has been lodged against the prisoner,
   he shall be brought to trial within one hundred and eighty (180) days after he shall
   have caused to be delivered to the prosecuting officer and the appropriate court of
   the prosecuting officer's jurisdiction written notice of the place of his imprisonment
   and his request for a final disposition to be made of the indictment, information
   or complaint;  provided that for good cause shown in open court, the prisoner or his
   counsel being present, the court having jurisdiction of the matter may grant any necessary
   or reasonable continuance.

   of their terms, to promote justice, and to effect the objects of the law.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 501.110. Offense committed with the aid of an unmanned aircraft system (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of an offense committed with the aid of an unmanned aircraft system
   if the unmanned aircraft system is under his or her control and the conduct would
   have given rise to criminal liability for the offense if performed directly by the
   person, unless the conduct consists solely of flying the unmanned aircraft system
   through navigable airspace in the normal course of operation of a legally registered
   unmanned aircraft system.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 504.085. Facility's standing to petition for clarification or modification and to appeal (2023)
content:

   inKRS 202A.011shall have standing to petition the court for any necessary clarification or modification
   of orders or judgments entered in proceedings under this chapter and to appeal from
   final orders or judgments entered in proceedings which have not complied with the
   provisions of this chapter.  A copy shall be sent to the mentally ill person or individual with an intellectual
   disability who has been charged with or convicted of a felony and to the person's
   attorney of record, if any, of whatever pleadings are filed by the forensic psychiatric
   facility or psychiatric facility.

      probability the defendant will attain competency in the foreseeable future, it shall
      commit the defendant to a treatment facility or a forensic psychiatric facility and
      order the defendant to submit to treatment for sixty (60) days or until the psychologist
      or psychiatrist treating him or her finds the defendant competent to stand trial,

      shall indict the defendant and the case shall be tried in the Circuit Court as a felony
      case.  The jury, or judge if the trial is without a jury, may decline to assess a felony

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 509. Kidnapping and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 509.050. Exemption
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 509.050. Exemption (2023)
content:
A person may not be convicted of unlawful imprisonment in the first degree, unlawful
   imprisonment in the second degree, or kidnapping when his criminal purpose is the
   commission of an offense defined outside this chapter and his interference with the
   victim's liberty occurs immediately with and incidental to the commission of that
   offense, unless the interference exceeds that which is ordinarily incident to commission
   of the offense which is the objective of his criminal purpose.  The exemption provided by this section is not applicable to a charge of kidnapping
   that arises from an interference with another's liberty that occurs incidental to
   the commission of a criminal escape.

   of this chapter to the contrary, a person who commits a third or subsequent misdemeanor
   offense under this chapter, except for violations ofKRS 510.150, may be convicted of a Class D felony.  If the Commonwealth desires to utilize the provisions of this section, the Commonwealth

   case.  The jury, or judge if the trial is without a jury, may decline to assess a felony

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 520. Escape and Other Offenses Relating to Custody›KY REV ST 520.070. Bail jumping in the first degree
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 520. Escape and Other Offenses Relating to Custody › KY REV ST 520.070. Bail jumping in the first degree
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 520.070. Bail jumping in the first degree (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of bail jumping in the first degree when, having been released
      from custody by court order, with or without bail, upon condition that he will subsequently
      appear at a specified time and place in connection with a charge of having committed
      a felony, he intentionally fails to appear at that time and place.

      appear at a specified time and place in connection with a charge of having committed
      a misdemeanor, he intentionally fails to appear at that time and place.

content:
(1)  A person is guilty of hindering prosecution or apprehension in the first degree
      when, with the intent to hinder the apprehension, prosecution, conviction or punishment
      of another whom he knows is being sought in connection with the commission of a capital

content:
(1)  A public servant is guilty of soliciting unlawful compensation when he requests
      a pecuniary benefit for the performance of an official action knowing that he was
      required to perform that action without compensation or at a level of compensation
      lower than that requested.

      of another who is being sought in connection with the commission of a criminal offense,
      he renders assistance to such person.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 523.050. Inconsistent statements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 523.050. Inconsistent statements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 523.050. Inconsistent statements (2023)
content:
(1)  When a person has made inconsistent statements under oath, both having been made
      within the period of the statute of limitations, the prosecution may proceed by setting
      forth the inconsistent statements in a single charge alleging in the alternative that
      one (1) or the other was false and not believed by the defendant.  In such case it shall not be necessary for the prosecution to prove which statement
      was false but only that one (1) or the other was false and not believed by the defendant
      to be true.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 523.060. Corroboration
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 523.060. Corroboration
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 523.060. Corroboration (2023)
content:
In any prosecution for perjury or false swearing, except prosecution based upon inconsistent
   statements pursuant toKRS 523.050, falsity of a statement may not be established solely through contradiction by the
   testimony of a single witness.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 523.070. Previous trial
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 523.070. Previous trial
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 523.070. Previous trial (2023)
content:
No prosecution shall be brought under this chapter when the substance of the defendant's
   false statement is his denial of guilt in a previous criminal trial.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 523.110. Giving peace officer false identifying information
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 523. Perjury and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 523.110. Giving peace officer false identifying information
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 523.110. Giving peace officer false identifying information (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of giving a peace officer false identifying information when
      he or she gives a false name, address, or date of birth to a peace officer who has
      asked for the same in the lawful discharge of his or her official duties with the
      intent to mislead the officer as to his or her identity.  The provisions of this section shall not apply unless the peace officer has first
      warned the person whose identification he or she is seeking that giving a peace officer
      false identifying information is a criminal offense.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 523.090. Retraction (2023)

   in the course of the proceeding in which it was made before such false statement substantially
   affected the proceeding and before it became manifest that its falsity was or would
   be exposed.

title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 524. Interference with Judicial Administration › KY REV ST 524.130. Unauthorized practice of law
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 524.130. Unauthorized practice of law (2023)
content:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 524. Interference with Judicial Administration›KY REV ST 524.070. Bribe receiving by a juror
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 524. Interference with Judicial Administration › KY REV ST 524.070. Bribe receiving by a juror
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 524.070. Bribe receiving by a juror (2023)

      agrees to accept any pecuniary benefit upon an agreement or understanding that his
      vote, opinion, decision or other action as a juror will thereby be influenced.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 524. Interference with Judicial Administration›KY REV ST 524.090. Jury tampering
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 524. Interference with Judicial Administration › KY REV ST 524.090. Jury tampering
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 524.090. Jury tampering (2023)
content:

      vote, opinion, decision or other action in a case, he communicates or attempts to
      communicate, directly or indirectly, with a juror other than as a part of the proceedings
      in the trial of the case.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.015. Obstructing an emergency responder

content:
(1)  As used in this section, “emergency responder” means state or local law enforcement personnel, fire department personnel, corrections
      officers, and emergency medical personnel and those contracted for official use by
      emergency responders.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.030. Riot in the second degree

content:

      be delivered to another a request for the payment of money on behalf of a creditor
      knowing that in form and substance it simulates any legal process issued by any court
      of this state.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.100. Public intoxication
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 525.100. Public intoxication
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.100. Public intoxication (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of public intoxication when he appears in a public place manifestly
      under the influence of a controlled substance, or other intoxicating substance, excluding
      alcohol (unless the alcohol is present in combination with any of the above), not
      therapeutically administered, to the degree that he may endanger himself or other
      persons or property, or unreasonably annoy persons in his vicinity.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.120. Abuse of a corpse

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.120. Abuse of a corpse (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of abuse of a corpse when except as authorized by law he intentionally
      treats a corpse in a way that would outrage ordinary family sensibilities.  A person shall also be guilty of abuse of a corpse if that person enters into a
      contract and accepts remuneration for the preparation of a corpse for burial or the
      burial or cremation of a corpse and then deliberately fails to prepare, bury, or cremate
      that corpse in accordance with that contract.

content:
(1)  A person is guilty of obstructing a highway or other public passage when having
      no legal privilege to do so he, alone or with other persons, intentionally or wantonly
      renders any highway or public passage impassable without unreasonable inconvenience
      or hazard.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.150. Disrupting meetings and processions in the second degree
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 525.150. Disrupting meetings and processions in the second degree
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.150. Disrupting meetings and processions in the second degree (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of disrupting meetings and processions in the second degree
      when, with intent to prevent or disrupt a lawful meeting, procession, or gathering,
      he or she does any act tending to obstruct or interfere with it physically or makes
      any utterance, gesture, or display designed to outrage the sensibilities of the group.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.145. Disrupting meetings and processions in the first degree
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 525.145. Disrupting meetings and processions in the first degree
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.145. Disrupting meetings and processions in the first degree (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of disrupting meetings and processions in the first degree
      when, with intent to prevent or disrupt a funeral or burial, funeral home viewing
      of a deceased person, funeral procession, or funeral or memorial service for a deceased
      person, he or she does any act tending to obstruct or interfere with it physically
      or makes any utterance, gesture, or display designed to outrage the sensibilities
      of the group attending the occasion.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 525.155. Interference with a funeral
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 525. Riot, Disorderly Conduct, and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 525.155. Interference with a funeral
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.155. Interference with a funeral (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of interference with a funeral when, at any point in time
      between one (1) hour prior to the commencement of an event specified in this subsection
      and one (1) hour following its conclusion, he or she blocks, impedes, inhibits, or
      in any other manner obstructs or interferes with access into or from any building
      or parking lot of a building in which a funeral, wake, memorial service, or burial
      is being conducted, or any burial plot or the parking lot of the cemetery in which
      a funeral, wake, memorial service, or burial is being conducted.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 527. Offenses Relating to Firearms and Weapons›KY REV ST 527.020. Carrying concealed deadly weapon

content:
(1)  A person is guilty of carrying a concealed weapon when he or she carries concealed
      a firearm or other deadly weapon on or about his or her person in violation of this
      section.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 525.160. Failure to disperse (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of failure to disperse if he participates with two (2) or
      more persons in a course of disorderly conduct likely to cause substantial harm or
      serious inconvenience, annoyance or alarm, and intentionally refuses to disperse when
      ordered to do so by a peace officer or other public servant engaged in executing or
      enforcing the law.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 526. Eavesdropping and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 526.020. Eavesdropping

content:
(1)  A person is guilty of eavesdropping when he intentionally uses any device to
      eavesdrop, whether or not he is present at the time.

citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 526.040. Possession of eavesdropping device (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of possession of an eavesdropping device when he possesses
      any electronic, mechanical or other device designed or commonly used for eavesdropping
      with intent to use that device to eavesdrop or knowing that another intends to use
      that device to eavesdrop.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 526. Eavesdropping and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 526.030. Installing eavesdropping device

content:
(1)  A person is guilty of installing an eavesdropping device when he intentionally
      installs or places such a device in any place with the knowledge that it is to be
      used for eavesdropping.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 526. Eavesdropping and Related Offenses›KY REV ST 526.060. Divulging illegally obtained information
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title L. Kentucky Penal Code › Chapter 526. Eavesdropping and Related Offenses › KY REV ST 526.060. Divulging illegally obtained information
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 526.060. Divulging illegally obtained information (2023)
content:
(1)  A person is guilty of divulging illegally obtained information when he knowingly
      uses or divulges information obtained through eavesdropping or tampering with private
      communications or learned in the course of employment with a communications common
      carrier engaged in transmitting the message.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title L. Kentucky Penal Code›Chapter 527. Offenses Relating to Firearms and Weapons›KY REV ST 527.030. Defacing a firearm
