      or if the county attorney elects not to proceed under KRS Chapter 640, the court may:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.070. Discharge from commitment or guardianship
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.070. Discharge from commitment or guardianship
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.070. Discharge from commitment or guardianship (2023)
content:
The Department of Juvenile Justice may discharge the child from commitment after providing
   fourteen (14) days' prior written notice to the committing court, to the legal representative
   of the child, and to the county attorney of the county in which the committing court
   presides, which may object to the discharge by holding a court review underKRS 610.120.  During the period of commitment or placement, the court may review a dispositional
   order and may continue or terminate such order as the court deems essential to the
   best interests of the child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.060. Duty of Commonwealth's attorney
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.060. Duty of Commonwealth's attorney
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.060. Duty of Commonwealth's attorney (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the Commonwealth's attorney after the imposition of youthful
   offender sentence, unless the defendant is granted probation, to cause to be forthwith
   transmitted to the facility or program with the commitment papers, a concise statement
   of the facts adduced at the trial or at the hearing of a plea of guilty.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.050. Supervision during probation or conditional discharge
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.050. Supervision during probation or conditional discharge
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.050. Supervision during probation or conditional discharge (2023)
content:
(1)  Any period of probation or conditional discharge required by the sentencing court
      to be served shall be supervised by:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.080. Jurisdiction of Parole Board; incarceration of youthful parole violators
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.080. Jurisdiction of Parole Board; incarceration of youthful parole violators
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.080. Jurisdiction of Parole Board; incarceration of youthful parole violators (2023)
content:
(1)  Youthful offenders shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Kentucky Parole
      Board and may be placed on parole to the Department of Corrections.  The Parole Board may, with regard to a youthful offender, exercise any of the powers
      which it possesses pursuant to KRS Chapter 439, except as provided in KRS Chapters
      600 to 645.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.083. Court's continuing jurisdiction over juvenile repeat offenders
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.083. Court's continuing jurisdiction over juvenile repeat offenders
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.083. Court's continuing jurisdiction over juvenile repeat offenders (2023)
content:
(1)  A juvenile convicted of or adjudged delinquent of three (3) or more offenses,
      other than violations or status offenses, by the juvenile session of District Court,
      shall be retained under the jurisdiction and supervision of the court with regard
      to the commission of that offense until the child reaches the age of eighteen (18),
      except that if the child is convicted of or adjudged delinquent of a third or subsequent
      misdemeanor offense after the child reaches the age of seventeen (17) years and six
      (6) months, the court's jurisdiction and supervision shall continue for a period not
      to exceed one (1) year.  This jurisdiction shall continue even after the service of incarceration or other
      court-ordered punishment in the form of conditional discharge.  Violation of the terms and conditions of conditional discharge shall be punished
      as contempt of court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.095. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.095. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.095. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations (2023)
content:
The Department of Juvenile Justice may promulgate administrative regulations to implement
   provisions of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.100. Graduated sanctions protocol for violation of supervised placement terms or conditions; effect of escape, absence without leave, or violation of conditions of placement; administrative hearings and regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.100. Graduated sanctions protocol for violation of supervised placement terms or conditions; effect of escape, absence without leave, or violation of conditions of placement; administrative hearings and regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.100. Graduated sanctions protocol for violation of supervised placement terms or conditions; effect of escape, absence without leave, or violation of conditions of placement; administrative hearings and regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Juvenile Justice shall develop and implement a graduated sanctions
      protocol of swift, certain, proportionate, and graduated sanctions that the department
      shall apply in response to a committed child's violations of the terms or conditions
      of supervised placement.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.120. Release of records of juvenile tried as an adult
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.120. Release of records of juvenile tried as an adult
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.120. Release of records of juvenile tried as an adult (2023)
content:
(1)  Records, limited to the records of the present case in which the child has been
      charged, of juveniles tried as adults in the Circuit Court shall be open to the public
      after the child has been indicted and arraigned on the offense for trial of the child
      as an adult.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 635. Public Offenders›KY REV ST 635.110. Human immunodeficiency virus testing for juveniles accused of certain sexual offenses; results; counseling when test positive
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 635. Public Offenders › KY REV ST 635.110. Human immunodeficiency virus testing for juveniles accused of certain sexual offenses; results; counseling when test positive
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 635.110. Human immunodeficiency virus testing for juveniles accused of certain sexual offenses; results; counseling when test positive (2023)
content: (1)  A juvenile session of a District Court shall comply with the provisions ofKRS 510.320when a child is accused of commission of a public offense as described therein.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.010. Preliminary hearing; proof required to try child as youthful offender in Circuit Court
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.010. Preliminary hearing; proof required to try child as youthful offender in Circuit Court
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.010. Preliminary hearing; proof required to try child as youthful offender in Circuit Court (2023)
content:
(1)  For children who are alleged to be youthful offenders by falling in the purview
      ofKRS 635.020(2)to(8), the court shall at arraignment ensure that the child's rights as specified inKRS 610.060have been explained and followed.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.020. Detention of youthful offender if unable to meet conditions of release or bail
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.020. Detention of youthful offender if unable to meet conditions of release or bail
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.020. Detention of youthful offender if unable to meet conditions of release or bail (2023)
content:
(1)  Any person proceeded against as a youthful offender under the provisions of this
      chapter who is under eighteen (18) years of age shall be detained in a secure juvenile
      detention facility if he is unable to meet the conditions of release or bail established
      pursuant to KRS Chapter 431 and the Kentucky Rules of Criminal Procedure.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.040. Capital punishment and other prohibited dispositions
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.040. Capital punishment and other prohibited dispositions
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.040. Capital punishment and other prohibited dispositions (2023)
content:
(1)  No youthful offender who has been convicted of a capital offense who was under
      the age of sixteen (16) years at the time of the commission of the offense shall be
      sentenced to capital punishment.  A youthful offender may be sentenced to capital punishment if he was sixteen (16)
      years of age or older at the time of the commission of the offense.  A youthful offender convicted of a capital offense regardless of age may be sentenced
      to a term of imprisonment appropriate for one who has committed a Class A felony and
      may be sentenced to life imprisonment without benefit of parole for twenty-five (25)
      years.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.030. Sentencing after conviction or plea of guilty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.030. Sentencing after conviction or plea of guilty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.030. Sentencing after conviction or plea of guilty (2023)
content:
A youthful offender, who is convicted of, or pleads guilty to, a felony offense in
   Circuit Court, shall be subject to the same type of sentencing procedures and duration
   of sentence, including probation and conditional discharge, as an adult convicted
   of a felony offense, except that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.070. Committing youthful offender to Department of Corrections
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.070. Committing youthful offender to Department of Corrections
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.070. Committing youthful offender to Department of Corrections (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon motion of the Department of Juvenile Justice, the sentencing Circuit Court
      may, after notice and hearing, order a youthful offender committed to an adult facility
      operated by the Department of Corrections if it is established by a preponderance
      of the evidence that the youthful offender has:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.075. Youthful offender transferred to Department of Corrections may remain in custody of Department of Juvenile Justice; transfer; petition for reconsideration of probation and for early parole
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.075. Youthful offender transferred to Department of Corrections may remain in custody of Department of Juvenile Justice; transfer; petition for reconsideration of probation and for early parole
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.075. Youthful offender transferred to Department of Corrections may remain in custody of Department of Juvenile Justice; transfer; petition for reconsideration of probation and for early parole (2023)
content:
(1)  Any other provision of KRS Chapter 640 to the contrary notwithstanding, any youthful
      offender ordered transferred to the Department of Corrections underKRS 640.030(2)(c)may, at the discretion of the Department of Juvenile Justice, after consultation
      with the Department of Corrections, remain in the custody of the Department of Juvenile
      Justice and in a Department of Juvenile Justice facility or program, until expiration
      of sentence or until the youthful offender is released on parole, but in no event
      past the age of twenty-one (21).

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.090. Right of Parole Board and Department of Corrections to records
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.090. Right of Parole Board and Department of Corrections to records
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.090. Right of Parole Board and Department of Corrections to records (2023)
content:
Upon the determination that a person is a youthful offender, the Cabinet for Health
   and Family Services, the Department of Juvenile Justice, and all other public agencies
   possessing records relating to the youthful offender shall, upon request, provide
   copies of the records to the Kentucky Parole Board and to the Department of Corrections.  No record relating to the child, except records maintained by the youthful offender's
   defense attorney or the Department of Public Advocacy, if he was defended by that
   department, shall be deemed privileged from disclosure to the Parole Board.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.100. Access of Parole Board to youthful offender and reports
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.100. Access of Parole Board to youthful offender and reports
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.100. Access of Parole Board to youthful offender and reports (2023)
content:
All officials of the Department of Juvenile Justice and the Department of Corrections
   shall furnish members of the Parole Board or its properly accredited representatives:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.030. Voluntary admission to hospital; transport from originating hospital to receiving hospital or psychiatric facility
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.030. Voluntary admission to hospital; transport from originating hospital to receiving hospital or psychiatric facility
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.030. Voluntary admission to hospital; transport from originating hospital to receiving hospital or psychiatric facility (2023)
content:
(1)  An authorized staff physician may admit for observation, diagnosis, and treatment
      at a hospital any child who is mentally ill or has symptoms of mental illness:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.120. Administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.120. Administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.120. Administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The Department of Juvenile Justice may promulgate administrative regulations
      to implement the provisions of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.050. Contents of certification petition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.050. Contents of certification petition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.050. Contents of certification petition (2023)
content:
The petition for certification and all subsequent court documents shall be entitled
   “In the interest of ..., a child.”  The petition for certification shall state:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.010. Title of chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.010. Title of chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.010. Title of chapter (2023)
content: This chapter may be cited as the Mental Health Act of The Unified Juvenile Code.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders›KY REV ST 640.110. Duty of Department of Juvenile Justice to transfer records to Department of Corrections
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 640. Youthful Offenders › KY REV ST 640.110. Duty of Department of Juvenile Justice to transfer records to Department of Corrections
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 640.110. Duty of Department of Juvenile Justice to transfer records to Department of Corrections (2023)
content:
When a youthful offender is transferred to the Department of Corrections in accordance
   with this chapter, the Department of Juvenile Justice shall transfer a copy of all
   records relating to the youthful offender to the Department of Corrections.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.040. Certification petition
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.040. Certification petition
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.040. Certification petition (2023)
content:
A parent or other person exercising custodial control or supervision of a child, including
   a hospital or the state or any interested person, may seek to hospitalize a child
   who is mentally ill or has symptoms of mental illness by filing a petition for certification
   with the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.035. Rights of hospitalized child
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.035. Rights of hospitalized child
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.035. Rights of hospitalized child (2023)
content: (1)  A child hospitalized under this chapter shall have the following rights:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.070. Hearing procedure
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.070. Hearing procedure
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.070. Hearing procedure (2023)
content:
(1)  All hearings under this chapter shall be conducted in accordance with the Kentucky
      Rules of Criminal Procedure unless otherwise provided.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.020. Definitions for chapter
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.020. Definitions for chapter
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.020. Definitions for chapter (2023)
content: The definitions in KRS Chapter 600 shall apply to this chapter.  In addition, unless the context requires otherwise:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.060. Procedures upon filing petition; appointment of counsel
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.060. Procedures upon filing petition; appointment of counsel
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.060. Procedures upon filing petition; appointment of counsel (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon receipt of a petition for certification, the court shall appoint counsel
      from the Department of Public Advocacy to represent the child at every stage of the
      proceedings.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.090. Criteria for hospitalization
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.090. Criteria for hospitalization
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.090. Criteria for hospitalization (2023)
content:
The burden of proof at the certification and recertification hearings under this chapter
   shall be on the petitioner to show, by clear and convincing evidence, that:

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.080. Use of child's disclosures
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.080. Use of child's disclosures
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.080. Use of child's disclosures (2023)
content:
(1)  Disclosures made by a child during observation, diagnosis, or treatment shall
      be admissible during the certification hearing under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.100. Order after hearing
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.100. Order after hearing
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.100. Order after hearing (2023)
content:
(1)  Within three (3) days, exclusive of weekends and holidays, of the conclusion
      of the certification hearing, the court shall enter an order denying or granting the
      petition and shall state in writing the factual findings regarding criteria specified
      inKRS 645.090.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.105. Certification; forms; fees
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.105. Certification; forms; fees
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.105. Certification; forms; fees (2023)
content:
(1)  The certification referred to in this chapter shall be in the form prescribed
      by the department.  The certification shall state that the child has been examined by each of the qualified
      mental health professionals making the certification within twenty-four (24) hours,
      excluding weekends and holidays, of the date of their certification.  It shall state the facts and circumstances upon which the judgment of the qualified
      mental health professional is based and shall be sworn to before a notary or the clerk
      or judge of the court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.110. Recertification procedure
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.110. Recertification procedure
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.110. Recertification procedure (2023)
content:
(1)  If the petitioner or other interested person desires to continue a child's hospitalization
      beyond the initial sixty (60) days, he shall file a petition for recertification before
      the original sixty (60) days expire.  The procedures and rights specified inKRS 645.050to645.100apply to recertification petitions and hearings except as otherwise specified in
      this section.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.170. Hospital review committee; review of patient's individual treatment plan
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.170. Hospital review committee; review of patient's individual treatment plan
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.170. Hospital review committee; review of patient's individual treatment plan (2023)
content:
(1)  Every hospital which treats children under this chapter shall have a review committee
      of three (3) qualified mental health professionals appointed by the hospital director.  The review committee shall have the authority to review the appropriateness of a
      patient's individual treatment plan.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.180. Convalescent leave for involuntary patient; rehospitalization
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.180. Convalescent leave for involuntary patient; rehospitalization
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.180. Convalescent leave for involuntary patient; rehospitalization (2023)
content:
(1)  Upon notice to the court, an authorized staff physician may release an involuntary
      patient on convalescent leave not to exceed ninety (90) days.  The physician may authorize convalescent leave only if he concludes that the patient
      would not present a danger or a threat of danger to himself or others during such
      a leave.  Release on convalescent leave shall terminate the involuntary hospitalization order
      and shall include provisions for a jointly developed treatment plan by the hospital
      and by the provider of outpatient care who will provide follow-up care and the continual
      monitoring of the patient's condition by the provider.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.150. Prerequisite for involuntary hospitalization; discharge of voluntary patient; notice of discharge required
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.150. Prerequisite for involuntary hospitalization; discharge of voluntary patient; notice of discharge required
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.150. Prerequisite for involuntary hospitalization; discharge of voluntary patient; notice of discharge required (2023)
content:
(1)  A child hospitalized under this chapter shall receive necessary and appropriate
      treatment.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.130. Rights and duties of court-designated workers
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.130. Rights and duties of court-designated workers
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.130. Rights and duties of court-designated workers (2023)
content:
(1)  The Administrative Office of the Courts shall assign a court-designated worker,
      as described in KRS Chapters 600 and 605, to maintain contact with and perform other
      specific functions on behalf of each child involuntarily hospitalized under this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.210. Contesting of intent to leave
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.210. Contesting of intent to leave
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.210. Contesting of intent to leave (2023)
content:
(1)  After a notice of contest has been received, the hospital may continue the hospitalization
      on an involuntary basis until a hearing has been held and the court orders otherwise.  In no case may the child be held more than fifteen (15) days beyond the filing of
      the notice of contest, unless a certification hearing has been held within seven (7)
      days of the filing of the notice of contest.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.140. Jurisdictional matters
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.140. Jurisdictional matters
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.140. Jurisdictional matters (2023)
content:
(1)  The District Court may continue its jurisdiction over a hospitalized child for
      six (6) months beyond a child's eighteenth birthday for purposes of continuity of
      treatment.  At the conclusion of the six (6) months, the cabinet may initiate proceedings under
      KRS Chapter 202A.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.120. Emergency hospitalization
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.120. Emergency hospitalization
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.120. Emergency hospitalization (2023)
content:
(1)  If, as a result of mental illness, a child appears in need of immediate hospitalization
      for observation, diagnosis, or treatment, a peace officer or any interested person
      may either take the child to a hospital, mental health facility, or another less restrictive
      alternative or file a petition for emergency hospitalization.  Upon filing a petition, a peace officer may place a child up to twenty-four (24)
      hours, excluding weekends and holidays, in a hospital or mental health facility or
      another less restrictive alternative.  The peace officer shall notify the court designated worker of the child's placement.  Within twelve (12) hours, the peace officer shall, if no other party can be found,
      file a petition, unless the child has been taken to a hospital.  No child held under this section shall be held in a secure juvenile detention facility
      unless a status offense action or public offense action is also pending.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.230. Rights of child, parent
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.230. Rights of child, parent
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.230. Rights of child, parent (2023)
content:
(1)  The child, parent or other person exercising custodial control or supervision
      of a child hospitalized under this chapter shall be entitled to confer at regular
      intervals with the treating or admitting physician or a member of the child's treatment
      team concerning the child's condition, treatment, or diagnosis.  The hospital or other proponent of certification may request that the parent or
      other person exercising custodial control or supervision of a child be available for
      consultation and cooperation in connection with the treatment process and may seek
      a court order to require such cooperation.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.190. Child's right to file notice of intent to leave
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.190. Child's right to file notice of intent to leave
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.190. Child's right to file notice of intent to leave (2023)
content:
(1)  Any child who was admitted pursuant toKRS 645.030(1)(b) or (c)may give notice of intent to leave at any time.  The notice need not follow any specific form so long as it is written and the intent
      of the child can be discerned.  The notice may be written by the child, a court-designated worker, or any other
      adult having an interest in the welfare of the child, provided that it reflects the
      stated wishes of the child.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.200. Responsibilities of hospital after receipt of notice of intent to leave
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.200. Responsibilities of hospital after receipt of notice of intent to leave
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.200. Responsibilities of hospital after receipt of notice of intent to leave (2023)
content:
(1)  An authorized staff physician of the hospital shall discharge the child from
      the hospital within five (5) days, exclusive of holidays and weekends, after receipt
      of a child's notice of intent to leave, unless the hospital, the parent, or other
      person exercising custodial control or supervision files a notice of contest with
      the court within the five (5) day period.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.240. Procedures when child objects to being discharged
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.240. Procedures when child objects to being discharged
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.240. Procedures when child objects to being discharged (2023)
content:
(1)  A child admitted to a hospital pursuant toKRS 645.030may object to a discharge requested by his parent or other person exercising custodial
      control or supervision by stating in writing his objection and his desire to remain
      as a patient.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.220. Notice requirements
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.220. Notice requirements
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.220. Notice requirements (2023)
content:
(1)  If a child who is at least sixteen (16) years of age is voluntarily admitted
      to a hospital under this chapter, the hospital shall give notice within twenty-four
      (24) hours to the child's parents or other person exercising custodial control or
      supervision, including the state, if applicable.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.250. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.250. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.250. Authority to promulgate administrative regulations (2023)
content:
(1)  The cabinet may promulgate administrative regulations to implement the provisions
      of this chapter.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.260. Appeals
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.260. Appeals
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.260. Appeals (2023)
content:
Appeals from the final orders or judgments of the court made and entered in proceedings
   under this chapter shall be taken in the same manner as other appeals from District
   to Circuit Court.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.270. Duty of mental health professional to warn intended victim of patient's threat of violence
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.270. Duty of mental health professional to warn intended victim of patient's threat of violence
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.270. Duty of mental health professional to warn intended victim of patient's threat of violence (2023)
content:
(1)  No monetary liability and no cause of action shall arise against any mental health
      professional or person serving in a counselor role for failing to predict, warn or
      take precautions to provide protection from a patient's violent behavior, unless the
      patient has communicated to the mental health professional or person serving in a
      counselor role an actual threat of physical violence against a clearly identified
      or reasonably identified victim, or unless the patient has communicated to the mental
      health professional or other person serving in a counselor role an actual threat of
      some specific violent act.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.280. Place where child to be held
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.280. Place where child to be held
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.280. Place where child to be held (2023)
content:
(1)  No child held under the provisions of this chapter shall be held in a secure
      juvenile detention facility unless a status offense action or public offense action
      is also pending.  No peace officer or any other person shall bring a status offense action or a public
      offense action against a child who is mentally ill and in need of hospitalization
      pursuant to this chapter solely or primarily for the purpose of avoiding transporting
      the child to a hospital, mental health facility, or other less restrictive alternative.

path: Kentucky Revised Statutes›Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code›Chapter 645. Mental Health Act›KY REV ST 645.990. Penalty
title: KY Statutes › Kentucky Revised Statutes › Title LI. Unified Juvenile Code › Chapter 645. Mental Health Act › KY REV ST 645.990. Penalty
citation: KY Stat § KY REV ST 645.990. Penalty (2023)
content:
Any person who intentionally causes the unwarranted hospitalization of any individual
   under this chapter or the denial to any individual of any of the rights accorded to
   him under this chapter or the administrative regulations issued thereunder shall be
   guilty of a Class A misdemeanor.
